events.title: control: warp.get/warp.set, event.warp, the debug event family, debug.resources and debug.idle
events.message:
control: warp.get/warp.set, event.warp, the debug event family, debug.resources and debug.idle

A control-protocol client can now switch warp at runtime, and the guest
can through the uaelib trap. App::set_warp is the one place warp changes
for any reason other than a boot gate's own engage/finish: the hotkey and
menu, a client's warp.set, and the guest's warpmode() all land there.
Warp off is a complete action whoever asks (it drops a pending --run /
--warp-boot phase, releases any programmatic hold, and re-paces). Warp
on from a client or the guest records a hold that mutes live audio like
the boot gates do and keeps a gate's finish from re-pacing underneath
it; the manual toggle records no hold and keeps its audible behaviour.
One press of Cmd/Alt+W, power off, or the client disconnecting releases
a hold. A capture run is never re-paced, and a bridged physical drive
keeps the machine paced, which the reply's note reports.

The guest's request is drained once per committed frame in the burst
loop (breaking the burst so the new pacing applies at that frame) and
after frames retired outside it. The headless server, unpaced end to
end, accepts warp.set as a no-op with a note and reports the guest's
request as an event.

New surface: warp.get / warp.set {"on"} (source: none, manual, control,
guest, launch, boot, headless); `paced` and `warp` on status; event.warp,
sent without a subscription whenever warp changes for a reason other
than the client's own warp.set, delivered best effort so a full outbound
queue never disconnects the client; the `debug` event family
(event.debug, kind log or resource, with the device's drop count);
debug.resources and debug.idle (read-only, collectable); guest_idle_cck
on event.frame.
events.author: LinuxJedi

events.title: uaelib: WinUAE-compatible trap at $F0FF60 for guest warp, debug log and resources
events.message:
uaelib: WinUAE-compatible trap at $F0FF60 for guest warp, debug log and resources

WinUAE's boot ROM carries a service trap at rtarea+0xFF60 that guest
tools and cross-compiler templates call: uae-configuration, and the
vscode-amiga-debug template's warpmode(), KPrintF() and debug_*()
helpers, which test the first word at $F0FF60 for a JSR (0x4EB9) or the
A-line form (0xA00E) and call the address as a C function with the
function number first, result in D0. Copperline answers the same ABI at
the same address so that code works unchanged.

Copperline has no CPU trap hook, so the stub is 32 bytes of real 68k
code decoded by the CPU bus adapter next to Gayle: JSR to an inner
routine, MOVE.L A7 to a doorbell longword, MOVE.L of the host-latched
result into D0, RTS. The call is serviced inside the write that
completes the doorbell (a 68000 lands the high word first; the services
board's completes_long_reg rule), reading the arguments from the guest
stack at A7+8+4n through the CPU's own address mask. Only the function
number must be readable: trailing arguments beyond RAM read as 0, as a
caller with a short frame expects, rather than losing the call. A CDTV
extended ROM at $F00000 decodes first and hides the trap, as WinUAE's
rtarea relocation does there; $F00000 itself stays open bus.

Function 82 parses the "key value" line cfgfile_uaelib_modify would
(pairs, index -1, size 0 = NUL-terminated, out cleared) and latches only
`warp`; the template's cpu_speed and *_cycle_exact keys are accepted and
ignored, the core being always cycle-exact. Function 86 echoes the text
on stdout as a DBG: line (withheld while a run-ahead frame is
speculative, like Paula's serial sink) and queues it for the control
protocol. Function 88 keeps the template's resource registry (bitmaps,
palettes, copper lists from the 50-byte debug_resource struct) and turns
its idle markers into per-frame colour-clock accounting closed at
begin_new_beam_frame; overlay drawing and load/save are accepted no-ops.
Everything else returns 0.

The latches, pending warp request, bounded event queue, registry and
idle accounting are machine state in Bus (state version 73) so run-ahead
and rewind restore them with the guest that made them. `[emulation]
uaelib = false` leaves $F0FF60 floating; the launcher carries the key
across its round trip.

events.title: copperhf: M6 -- LSEG stress fixture, M6 probe, and three mounter fixes
events.message:
copperhf: M6 -- LSEG stress fixture, M6 probe, and three mounter fixes

The first real exercise of M3's FSHD/LSEG loader caught three
previously-unexercised mounter.c bugs, fixed at the site:

- Hunks were allocated lazily as each body record was reached, so a
  RELOC32/RELOC32SHORT legally targeting a LATER hunk always found
  segs[idx] NULL and failed the load. Every hunk is now allocated up
  front from the HUNK_HEADER size table, like real LoadSeg.
- The volume-name BSTR was not longword-padded, so any even-length
  partition name left the FileSysStartupMsg/DosEnvec that follow it
  odd-aligned -- an Address Error on 68000. M3's "DH0" dodged it by
  luck.
- ADNF_STARTPROC and the ConfigDev were passed for every partition;
  per expansion.doc both belong only to bootable ones (a non-bootable
  partition's handler starts on first reference).

guest/copperhf-test/gen_lsegfix.py generates lsegfix, a hand-crafted
248-byte three-hunk executable pinning the loader's edge cases byte-for-
byte: cross-hunk RELOC32 and a two-group RELOC32SHORT with its odd-word
pad, a DATA hunk whose header size exceeds its body (trailing-zero
truncation), and a BSS round trip -- its entry point folds three
relocated reads into magic 0x88911FD5 that only survives a fully correct
load. Because AmigaDOS starts a mounted DeviceNode's dn_SegList as a
real handler process on first reference, the fixture implements a
minimal DOS-packet loop and hands the magic back as a packet's Res2;
chftest_m6 verifies the FileSystem.resource entry, the seglist chain,
the magic via Lock("CHFM6:")'s IoErr(), and the DeviceNode patch, one
marker block each (blocks 512-515 of unit 0).

events.title: copperhf: M5 -- determinism and quiesce-on-save regression gates, docs
events.message:
copperhf: M5 -- determinism and quiesce-on-save regression gates, docs

tests/copperhf_m5.rs pins M5's two load-bearing properties against a real
AROS autoboot of the M3 RDSK/PART image (dense doorbell traffic: the
mounter's polled walk plus the OFS Startup-Sequence bootmark write):

- determinism_across_repeated_boots: the identical scenario, same image
  path reset to pristine bytes, fixed rtc_time seed (guest-clock
  timestamps in OFS metadata would otherwise leak host wall clock into
  the comparison), run twice -- the mid-boot save states and final
  screenshots must be byte-identical, with a structural bootmark check
  so a both-runs-never-booted pass cannot be vacuous.
- savestate_quiesce_and_resume: a state saved inside the busy boot-I/O
  window, resumed in a fresh process, must screenshot byte-identically
  to the uninterrupted run at the same absolute emulated time, and both
  runs must actually complete the boot.

docs/internals/copperhf.md gains the "Asynchronous I/O (M5)" section
(pipeline halves, determinism model, bounded-channel backpressure, the
browser build's threadless inline worker, quiesce-on-save) and the
updated milestone list.

events.title: copperhf: M5 -- asynchronous worker-thread I/O
events.message:
copperhf: M5 -- asynchronous worker-thread I/O

CHF_DOORBELL no longer executes a request inline. Doorbell time (emulation
thread) reads the IOStdReq, validates against board-cached unit state, and
copies write/SCSI payloads out of guest memory; a single FIFO worker
thread owning the backing files (Arc<Mutex<units>>, locked only per job)
does the real sector/CDB work; drain time (tick, emulation thread) copies
read data back in, writes io_Error/io_Actual, applies TD_EJECT's
media/counter bookkeeping, and pushes the completion.

Determinism is the invariant the whole shape hangs on: a request is due at
the first tick after its own doorbell write, and tick blocks on the
worker's result channel until everything already in flight has delivered
-- host disk speed costs wall-clock inside that block and can never move
which emulated tick a completion surfaces at. next_event_cck reports
in-flight work as immediately due so the sparse-wake scheduler always
reaches that tick. The doorbell-to-worker channel is bounded
(backpressure); deadlock-free because the worker never needs the emulation
thread to make progress.

Save states quiesce first: Emulator::save_state/save_state_bytes (now
&mut self, mirrored in the web crate's wrapper) drain the pipeline via
Bus::copperhf_quiesce before serializing, as do the CCP
copperhf.attach/copperhf.eject handlers before touching a unit -- a state
is always captured with nothing in flight (STATE_VERSION 71: the board
also gained a cached per-unit total_sectors). The browser build, which
has no threads, gets an inline-execution Worker variant with the same
FIFO contract.

events.title: review: redraw on the element's size, keep captures smooth, name the config file
events.message:
review: redraw on the element's size, keep captures smooth, name the config file

Copilot's review of the browser integer scaling (#614), three findings.

The layout redraw was keyed to the window's resize alone, but the
element changes size without one -- the CSS fullscreen fallback pinning
it to the viewport, the on-screen keyboard strip taking its share, the
shell's sidebar opening beside it -- and a paused or exactly reused
frame then left the backing store at its old size, CSS-stretched, so an
integer draw was no longer pixel-exact. A ResizeObserver on the canvas
now drives the same redraw, and the page's own fullscreen and keyboard
paths call it directly so they redraw at once rather than a frame later.

Screenshots were documented as untouched by the settings, but under
integer scaling a 60 Hz aperture presents at its own 428 woven rows and
the capture read that buffer. The capture wrapper that already drops a
drawn bezel around the buffer read drops integer scaling the same way,
so a capture keeps the smooth presentation's shape whatever the page
draws, as the desktop's captures keep the aspect's own shape whatever
its window draws.

The page fetches ./copperline.json; the guide called it config.json.
The shell hooks are also un-hidden explicitly on a capable bundle, so a
shell can ship #scaling and #autocrop hidden (the #devkeyboard pattern)
and never show a dead control ahead of the glue.
events.author: LinuxJedi

events.title: web: integer scaling and autocrop for the browser frontend
events.message:
web: integer scaling and autocrop for the browser frontend

The browser build stretched the presentation buffer over its 4:3
element and carried neither `[display] scaling = "integer"` nor the
autocrop presentation (#608). Both port onto the desktop's own
machinery rather than a JavaScript re-derivation.

The pure pieces move from window/present.rs into present_common.rs,
which the wasm build compiles: AutocropLatch, per_axis_fit and the
smooth fallback (now exact integer arithmetic, so a rect of the
viewport's own shape fills it to the pixel), and a new sub_rect_fit
holding the factors/destination core of display_src_layout. Two maps
follow the renderer's content envelope into the buffer the page draws:
FieldPlacement::content_rect onto the woven field, then
region_present_content_rect, the inverse of the deinterlacer's aperture
copy. buffer_layout answers a page's viewport with the rect to draw and
the whole-number factors, at the glass pixel shape read off the buffer
itself (buffer_glass_par: the page shows the buffer in a 4:3 element,
so a 668 x 540 PAL aperture states the desktop's 1.078 and an NTSC one
0.854). render_reusing_previous reports the fresh render's envelope
(ReuseRender) so the wrapper can latch it.

WebEmu gains set_scaling, set_autocrop, present_content_rect and
present_layout. The envelope is latched per frame in buffer pixels,
re-fed on an exactly reused frame so a static screen still lets a
smaller crop prove itself stable, and reset across a scan-geometry
change. Under integer scaling a 60 Hz aperture is presented at its own
woven rows rather than resampled onto the 50 Hz row count -- the
browser's equivalent of the desktop drawing its unresampled canvas --
so the factors carry every scan line as one exact block; a drawn bezel
suspends both modes, as on the desktop.

try.js draws the answer: the monitor passes take the picture sub-rect
through a u_src uniform mirroring crt.wgsl's src_rect (half-texel
clamp, whole texture by default), the 2D fallback scales a staging
canvas into a device-resolution store, pointer scaling follows the
layout, and fullscreen lets the element span the viewport while a mode
is on so a cropped picture can take a 16:9 screen's full height.
#scaling and #autocrop controls, remembered per browser and seeded from
copperline.json, hide on a bundle without present_layout.

events.title: copperhf: M4 -- guest-side NSD/change-interrupt stub and end-to-end probe
events.message:
copperhf: M4 -- guest-side NSD/change-interrupt stub and end-to-end probe

BeginIO now answers three commands entirely from the ROM stub, since
they need guest pointers or guest state the host cannot provide:
NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY (NSDeviceQueryResult filled from a ROM-resident
supported-command table), TD_ADDCHANGEINT (request held on a per-device
pending list under Disable()), and TD_REMCHANGEINT (removes the pending
add, matched by io_Data, and replies it exactly once -- also when a
caller reuses the very same request block). The INT2 server drains
CHF_IRQ_STATUS bit 1 by calling device.c's chf_drain_changes(), which
acks CHF_CHANGED_MASK at the board and Cause()s each pending change
interrupt whose unit the mask names; is_Data now carries the device
pointer, with dev_BoardBase's offset shared to the asm via
device_layout.h and a _Static_assert.

Two more hard-won toolchain findings documented in-source: recovering a
struct pointer by subtracting a field offset from the field's VALUE
(not its address) is nonsense arithmetic that only crashed the path
that needed it, and this GCC target silently ignores an __asm("a5")
parameter binding on an ordinary internal function (callee-saved
register), falling back to stack-passing -- so chf_drain_changes takes
its argument on the stack, pushed explicitly by int_handler.s.

guest/copperhf-test/chftest_m4 exercises the full surface over an AROS
autoboot (tests/copperhf_m4_guest.rs, marker block per subtest):
NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY, TD_CHANGENUM/CHANGESTATE/PROTSTATUS, TD_READ64,
HD_SCSICMD INQUIRY and READ CAPACITY(10), and the ADDCHANGEINT ->
TD_EJECT -> software-interrupt -> REMCHANGEINT story end to end.

events.title: copperhf: M4 -- TD64/NSD/HD_SCSICMD command coverage and disk-change host side
events.message:
copperhf: M4 -- TD64/NSD/HD_SCSICMD command coverage and disk-change host side

Protocol version 2 (copperhf_board.h): CHF_CHANGED_MASK/CHF_CHANGED_ACK
(per-unit media-change bits), CHF_UNIT_MEDIA (media present, distinct
from the now slot-configured CHF_UNIT_PRESENT so eject behaves like
pulling a disk from a still-attached drive), and CHF_IRQ_STATUS bit 1
gating INT2 alongside completions.

New host-side commands: TD_CHANGENUM/CHANGESTATE/PROTSTATUS/EJECT, the
TD64 family and its NSCMD twins (io_Actual is io_HighOffset on entry, no
4 GiB ceiling), and HD_SCSICMD answering CDBs against the unit's image
through src/scsi.rs::ScsiDisk (extended with READ/WRITE 12/16, READ
CAPACITY 16, MODE SENSE/SELECT 10, and a from_disk/sense_bytes reuse
surface), with SCSIF_AUTOSENSE sense fill and HFERR_BadStatus reported
in io_Error on a non-GOOD scsi_Status per scsi.device's contract. Plain
32-bit CMD_READ/WRITE/TD_FORMAT past 4 GiB now fail IOERR_BADADDRESS
(no wrap); I/O against a media-absent unit fails TDERR_DiskChanged.

Hot attach/detach: CCP methods copperhf.attach/copperhf.eject
(docs/debugger/control.md), sharing one path with the guest's TD_EJECT.
Boot-time config attach deliberately bumps neither the change counter
nor the changed mask -- an M1-M3 guest never acks the mask, so flagging
the initial attach latched CHF_IRQ_STATUS bit 1 forever and INT2-stormed
the whole boot; a unit that never changed also must read TD_CHANGENUM 0.

events.title: autocrop: crop programmable multisync scans through their own sync-anchored window
events.message:
autocrop: crop programmable multisync scans through their own sync-anchored window

Autocrop derived its envelope from the standard 15 kHz presentation and
suspended itself for programmable (VARBEAMEN) scans, so a DblPAL or
Multiscan Workbench, or a 31 kHz console, never got the crop-and-refit
(#607). The renderer's per-line display-window envelope was already
computed for those frames; only the presentation threw it away.

post_process_rendered_field now returns the FieldPlacement it applied --
a standard field's centring and recentring shifts, or a programmable
scan's sync-anchored column resample and the vertical window's skipped
and padded rows -- and FieldPlacement::content_rect follows the envelope
through it onto the presentation buffer. The programmable columns are
found by scanning the glass against the resamplers' own taps
(screenshot::stretch_rows_x_source, stretch_rows_x_window_source,
factored out of the resamplers), so a partly blended edge column counts
and the crop cannot disagree with the pixels; the deinterlacer's row
count says whether the placed rows were woven (LACE) or passed through at
native height. The renderer trims the envelope's edges by the
programmable blanking windows (VBSTRT/VBSTOP, HBSTRT/HBSTOP) and the
frame end, with the predicates apply_programmable_blanking paints with:
Kickstart leaves the display window open across the blank on these
modes, and those rows are black to the eye. canvas_content_rect folds a
35 ns canvas onto the canvas columns, so super-hi-res programmable scans
crop too.

App::display_canvas_src drops the programmable and canvas-width
suspensions (display_canvas_src_for is the same decision pure of the
live globals); a programmable scan keeps the uniform multiple under
per-axis integer scaling, since its rows are not woven pairs for a
per-line factor to step by, and a bezel or RTG scanout still suspends.
The autocrop latch resets across a scan-geometry change (programmable
flag, rows, width), the way the deinterlacer drops its weave history.
COPPERLINE_DIAG_AUTOCROP's layout line names the scan instead of the
two suspensions.

events.message:
review: prune the per-axis fit to the columns astride the ideal, and roll a failed canvas change back

Two findings from the #612 review. The fit scanned every column count at
every height, which a one-line autocrop rect on a large surface turns
into millions of candidates on every redraw and cursor move; at a fixed
height the shape is monotone in the count, so the two counts astride the
ideal are the only ones that can be the closest, and the tolerance band,
an interval around the ideal, holds one of them if it holds any. The
pruned fit is checked against the exhaustive rule over a grid of
surfaces, rects and shapes.

A canvas-height change whose texture resize failed left the new height
committed over the old, shorter texture, which the draw helpers slice by
the live height. resync_canvas_geometry now reports the failure without
touching anything else, and the pixel-aspect, scaling and bezel switches
put their setting back and re-plan for the canvas it went back to, as
the status-bar toggle already did.

events.title: scaling: draw the tv aspect per axis from the square canvas under integer scaling
events.message:
scaling: draw the tv aspect per axis from the square canvas under integer scaling

Integer scaling of the default tv aspect scaled a canvas already resampled
onto 537 rows for the 4:3 shape: crisp blocks of a resampled picture, with
square + integer the only pixel-exact pairing (#606). Integer scaling now
presents from the unresampled canvas under either aspect
(video::square_canvas), and under the tv aspect the scaler pass draws it
with a separate whole-number factor per axis -- surface pixels per hi-res
column and per field line -- chosen to approximate the shape of a
square-canvas pixel on the 4:3 glass, read back from the tv canvas's own
resample (glass_par: PAL 1.078, NTSC 0.854; the whole field over the glass
for full overscan). per_axis_fit takes the tallest fit whose shape is
within 11/10 of the glass's, then the closest, and the closest shape at
the largest size when none is inside the tolerance. Counting per field
line rather than per woven row is what reaches 4:5 on a 1080p display:
a non-interlaced line's two woven rows are identical, so an odd count per
line still lands as one exact block, and every display rect starts on a
woven pair, so the scaler's sample centres never sit on a line boundary.
Square + integer keeps its uniform multiple.

The window canvas (present_height) follows the rule; captures take the
aspect's own height (capture_height), so screenshots, recordings and
headless shots never change shape with a window setting. A bezel keeps
the tv canvas -- its opening resamples the whole glass -- and the bezel,
scaling and pixel-aspect toggles share one canvas-change path
(resync_canvas_geometry); the launcher adopts the bezel before the
scaling so the canvas moves at most once. DisplaySrc generalises the
autocrop sub-rect and the two modes compose: autocrop supplies the rect,
the fit the factors. COPPERLINE_DIAG_AUTOCROP names the mode, the factors
and the shape.

events.message:
copperhf: M3 -- boot-ROM RDSK/PART mounter with FSHD/LSEG loading

guest/copperhf/mounter.c walks each present unit's RDB at rt_Init time
over a polled doorbell/completion protocol (IRQ still disabled, so the
INT2 server never sees the mounter's portless requests), hand-builds a
DeviceNode + FileSysStartupMsg + DosEnvec per PART block (honoring
PBFF_NOMOUNT/PBFF_BOOTABLE), and adds it via AddBootNode on V36+ or the
hand-built eb_MountList BootNode / AddDosNode fallback on V34, mirroring
guest/services/handler.c's proven recipe. rdb_FileSysHeaderList is
walked too: a matching FSHD's LSEG chain is loaded through a minimal
streaming hunk loader (CODE/DATA/BSS, RELOC32 long and short forms,
SYMBOL/DEBUG skipped) into FileSystem.resource, created if absent, and
DeviceNodes are patched per fse_PatchFlags. entry.s's da_BootPoint now
boots dos.library on V34 instead of declining, same recipe as
guest/services/entry.s.

Two new hard-won toolchain pitfalls documented at the site: GCC's loop
idiom recognition emits memset/memcpy calls -nostdlib cannot link
(-fno-builtin-* / -fno-tree-loop-distribute-patterns), and strict
aliasing let -Os dead-store-eliminate the IORequest field writes behind
recast byte pointers outright -- the doorbell rang with io_Command
never written, verified by disassembly -- so those stores are volatile
now and the ROM builds with -fno-strict-aliasing.

events.title: A scrolling pass never puts the player in tranche B
events.message:
A scrolling pass never puts the player in tranche B

KC: the player judders when the screen scrolls. The trace showed the
position data clean - plyX, posX and slot 0's unit advancing in
lockstep - so it was temporal: the window-B repaint classes could
force the player's component into tranche B, and a tranche-B image is
one field behind the scroll. World-anchored, that is invisible on a
droid; the player is held against the screen frame by the view-follow,
so he oscillated centre-minus-a-step / centre at 25 Hz. The old "the
player is always in the window drawn first" line was this exact
guarantee, and the forcing had broken it - constantly, because the
tile tests ignored rows, so any door in the same columns forced him.

Both fixes live in the banks, no code-image cost. SprTileHit now
tests the tile's four char rows against the slot's padded row span
(row-blindness was harmless when all forcing went to tranche A; it
is not now). And SprScanCls flags a view-moved pass (mapHX/posY vs
oldHX/oldPosY, valid since ApplyMove has run) as bit 2 of sprCls[0];
SprAssignTr masks the class bits off satForce and refuses the split
when the forced-B component is the player's and the view moved.
Standing still keeps the split - recharging on a pad, the case the
window-B repaint was built for, lags no scroll.

Verified in jsbeeb: sprTr[0] never 1 while the view moves; 120 of
128 passes still split on a heavy diagonal leg through doors (5
refusals, drawn whole); timing histograms unchanged from step 4.
The branch-range fix in sat_asg is the player-refuse block pushing
sat_asgnext past 127.

events.title: review: WORDEQUAL is the comparator's live level, not a latch held until read
events.message:
review: WORDEQUAL is the comparator's live level, not a latch held until read

Paula's DSKBYTR bit 12 is the DSKSYNC comparator output itself: true for
the one cell in which the shift register equals DSKSYNC and gone once the
next cell shifts in, so a polling loop can miss a match and wait a
revolution for the next, as Copylock's does on real hardware. Only DSKBYT
is reset by a read; the DSKSYNC interrupt is the latched edge of the same
comparator and stays separate. Drop the event latch the register still
carried, and make the tests and the internals documentation say so,
including a match that has shifted out before the first read.

events.message:
The movement pipeline: keys and walls compute for the NEXT pass

Step 4 of the audit, the shape raster-timing.md already sketched:
ReadKeys/CalcSpeed/CheckWalls - and the ESCAPE test with them - leave
window A for the display period, sharing DroidsUpdate's overPhase
gate, and compute the speeds the NEXT pass's ApplyMove applies.
ApplyMove alone stays above the erase (the scroll depends on it), and
since it has already run when CheckWalls executes, the clip is taken
against exactly the position the next move starts from. Cost: one
pass (40 ms) of input latency, the pipeline the droid AI already
rides.

through it, and the pipelined speeds were clipped at a position a
transfer, a lift or a deck load may have moved the player away from.

the first ApplyMove of a game, so uninitialised speeds can never
apply on real hardware.

against ~13,100 - the level draw's latch budget nearly doubles to

it inside the first 8,192 cycles. The band remains the one tenant
that can overrun window A (~23% of band-crossing passes, by ~3k
where it was ~11k), and it is latch-bound like the columns.

full death-wash-highscore-title chain from its new home, split

events.title: floppy: frame DSKBYTR from the read shifter and model IPF cell-density profiles
events.message:
floppy: frame DSKBYTR from the read shifter and model IPF cell-density profiles

Rob Northen Copylock reads its key sector byte by byte through DSKBYTR:
it waits for WORDEQUAL, collects the bytes while counting how often it
polled between them, rejects the read unless the first two bytes are the
MFM of the sector's first data byte, then times a second sector against
the first and demands the few-per-cent difference the master put between
them. On an IPF both halves of that went wrong (issue #610, Lemmings
freezing black before the disk 2 prompt):

- DSKBYTR served bytes from the track's own byte grid, but Paula frames
  them with the bit counter a WORDSYNC match resets. Syncs on an IPF or
  flux track sit at any bit phase (this one at phase 1), so the bytes came
  out shifted and Copylock retried every revolution forever. Synthesised
  AmigaDOS tracks hid it because their syncs are word-aligned. DSKBYTR's
  byte, DSKBYT and WORDEQUAL now come from the read shifter, which also
  reframes on every WORDSYNC match with no transfer running: Copylock arms
  a zero-length read, which completes on arming, and relies on the
  free-running comparator from then on.

- The density models of an IPF track (IMGE density 3..9) decoded with
  uniform 2 us cells, so the timing check computed 0% and handed the game
  a wrong key: the disk 2 prompt appeared and the game crashed to garbage
  once disk 2 loaded. The decoder now emits the CAPS library's own
  profiles as per-mille cell-time spans (Copylock Amiga slows and speeds
  blocks 4-6 by -5.5/-0.5/+4.5% from the preceding gap through the block,
  the newer scheme blocks 0-2; Copylock ST, Speedlock and the Brierley
  models weight single blocks; the Brierley density-key model takes a bit
  per block from block 0's gap value), RawMfm carries them, and TrackRev
  scales each cell's clock by its run's weight. Uniform tracks keep the
  exact old arithmetic. Weak bits remain the one IPF modelling gap.

The DSKBYTR grid-position fields leave the floppy state and TrackRev gains
the profile, so the save-state version is bumped. Tests that pinned the
grid model move to hardware semantics; new ones cover off-grid sync
framing, Copylock's zero-length-arm idiom, the TrackRev density
arithmetic and the IPF profile generation.

Fixes #610.

events.title: Door repaints join the animated tiles in window B
events.message:
Door repaints join the animated tiles in window B

The second half of getting the level draw's tenants out of window A:
a moving door's tile repaint is a single-tile write exactly like the
recharge pad's, so it takes the same class-B path. DoorsUpdate's
STATE half stays in window A - it writes doorDef, which the same
pass's band and column draws read, and no buffer - and the repaint
half (du_draw, now DoorAnimPaint) runs from the window-B block on a
split pass, between tranche B's restore and its draw, with AnimPaint
as its tail so one call serves doors and tiles in both windows. On a
whole pass du_gate falls straight through and the old window-A order
holds. SprHitsDraw classes doors as bit 1 now; a sprite standing in
a moving doorway is forced into tranche B.

Columns do NOT move to window B, and the raster-timing step-3 sketch
that said they could is withdrawn in the docs: the CRTC start latched
at fire 1 shows the new viewport in the SAME field's display, so a
column drawn in window B would display one field of stale buffer at
the exposed edge - and deferring the latch instead makes the player
oscillate against the viewport by the scroll delta at 25 Hz. The
band and columns stay latch-bound in window A.

Verified in jsbeeb: the buffer oracle reads 0 of 10,240 against
RedrawAll (diagonal scroll, line=7, mapHX=21 odd, deck cleared by
CTRL+C, draws and restores NOPed per the docs/ram-pass.md recipe);
sprCls reads 2 for droids standing at moving doors and the split is
kept; doors and the pad animate cleanly. Walking diagonally through
a droid crowd, 128-pass histograms: tranche-A draws ending over the
display fall from the audit's 59% to 27%, tranche-B from 30% to
5.5%, split taken 127/128, exactly 25.0 Hz. What remains late is the
band + pass preamble against the fire-1 latch - the movement
pipeline (audit recommendation 4), not the repaint classes.

events.title: The animated tiles repaint in window B, not window A
events.message:
The animated tiles repaint in window B, not window A

The audit's corridor scenario showed ~29% of passes finishing the
tranche-A draw with the beam over the play area, and the recharge
pad's rotate pass was the recurring cost: AnimPaint in window A plus
its forcing of nearby sprites into tranche A.

The writers now carry a class: SprHitsDraw returns a byte (bit 0 the
window-A writers - band, columns, doors for now; bit 1 the animated
tiles) instead of a carry, and SprAssignTr forces a component to
tranche A on bit 0, to tranche B on bit 1, and refuses the split on
both - no tranche is safe under both windows' writers. On a split
pass AnimPaint bows out of window A (a gate at its head) and the
window-B block calls AnimPaintB between tranche B's restore and its
draw: the tiles land while every sprite that could be standing on
them is erased, and the draw's save picks them up. Whole passes keep
the old order.

AnimScanPass moves below the tranche-B block so window B paints the
list SprScanCls classified at the top of the pass, not a freshly
rebuilt one; its borrowed maprow is just as dead there, and a modal
arm skipping the rebuild costs nothing (the list is rebuilt from
scratch every normal pass). The main loop's two restore paths become
one - SprRestoreTr's argument is sprSplit minus one (0 = tranche A,
&FF = the whole pool) - which retires SprRestoreAll and pays for the
new call.

Verified in jsbeeb, player standing ON an animating recharge pad:
sprCls[0]=2 on rotate passes, the player forced into tranche B
(sprTr[0]=1) with the split kept, the pad animates under him with no
corruption - and the 128-pass histogram reads clean: every tranche-A
draw ends in state 0 (off-display), every tranche-B draw inside
window B, against 6/128 late with beam up to ~90 lines in before.

events.message:
paths: host data moves out of the hidden config tree and into Documents

~/Documents/Copperline on macOS and Linux,
%USERPROFILE%\Documents\Copperline on Windows -- somewhere a person
browsing their own files can find their saves, screenshots, recordings
and configs, rather than a dot-directory built for tools. Capitalised,
because the folder sits beside other applications' folders in Documents
and reads as a product name there, not a unix binary. Whichever of
USERPROFILE and HOME the machine defines names the home; XDG_CONFIG_HOME
and APPDATA are no longer consulted for the emulator, the old locations
were simply where host data used to live, and portable.txt keeps meaning
what it meant.

Player builds deliberately stay where they were: a published game is an
appliance whose data nobody browses, and every bought game planting its
id at the top of Documents would strew it with loose folders -- so an
overridden identity keeps the hidden per-user tree, one ~/.config/<id>
(%APPDATA%\<id>) per game.

events.title: ecs: give new ink a FREE SLOT instead of the nearest wrong one
events.message:
ecs: give new ink a FREE SLOT instead of the nearest wrong one

Reported while verifying #166: on ECS an event's first text line renders bright
cyan and the following lines render dim grey, near-illegible against the box.

Measured on the HEIRS innkeeper event (amiberry, ECS/68000): line 1 ink
#00bbbb, lines 2 and 3 #888888 against a #555544 box. The split is not
temporal, it is SPATIAL and lands exactly on a copper band boundary — line 1
sits in band 13, lines 2-3 in bands 14-15.

Cause: the per-band cut is computed from the surface as it stood, and drawing
text never marks it dirty, so anything drawn afterwards resolves through
remap_rect's absent-colour bucket — the nearest slot the band happens to own.
Band 13 owns a cyan slot only because the event PICTURE is cyan there. Bands
14-15 sit below the picture, never saw a cyan pixel, and resolve the same
glyphs to grey.

The existing remedy was explicitly a placeholder: ecs_ink_hold skips ONE
present in case a palette install is following, and its own comment says that
failing that the ink "paints on the NEXT present via the bucket fallback
exactly as before". The bucket fallback is the grey glyph.

★ And the band had room the whole time. Instrumenting the text-box bands says
they use 7 to 11 of their 32 slots — 21+ empty — while the glyph is forced onto
a slot 3675 away. So nothing needs re-quantising and nothing needs sacrificing:
hand the colour an EMPTY slot, fix the remap, and patch that slot's copper
word.

Writing a FREE slot's COLOR word is safe in a way a palette install is not
(#165): free means no used index maps to it, so no pixel on screen wears that
slot and changing its RGB cannot recolour the outgoing frame. Under
FRUA_PLANAR the band's draw-time coverage is dropped and its rows re-announced,
because rows a writer already stamped used the old remap for that index.

Per-band, because a colour absent here may be present one band down; and only
when the bucket is genuinely bad (ECS_INK_NEAR), so a glyph whose colour the
band already holds costs one distance test.

Result on the same event: all three lines now measure #00bbbb. The drive
adopts 6, 21, 3, 1, 1 slots at its re-band points.

Runtime knob video.cfg inkadopt=off restores the old behaviour for A/B.

All four targets build; 483 tests pass. ECS-only code — Falcon, TT, ST/STE and
AGA are untouched.

Not yet confirmed on hardware.

events.title: Keep the screen blanked until there is a picture on it
events.message:
Keep the screen blanked until there is a picture on it

KC: the 001 screen is cleared to the front end's colour and then changes
to the deck's text background. The palette wait added an hour ago was not
the whole of it -- between the rupture starting and the first screen
being drawn there is a second or more while the deck loads, and what the
display showed was IsBlank's cleared strip in whatever palette the front
end left, plus the panel as the bare white box FillPanel draws. KC:
"could actually just keep the screen blanked until the panel and the box
are drawn".

RuptAlign patches the IRQ's two unblank operands to R8_BLANK when it
starts the rupture; IsArm -- every IsStart screen's common tail -- and
BrRun's first page paint put them back to R8_ON. Both idempotent.

PATCHED OPERANDS, NOT A VARIABLE READ. One of the two is fire 2, which
has to land in horizontal blanking (T1_TUNE's whole business), and
LDA abs would move the write two cycles later. A patched immediate costs
nothing at either site; rvR8 and r2R8 label them.

HsEntry starts a rupture of its own and is unaffected -- the last screen
released the blank long before the game-over path reaches it.

Verified in jsbeeb: the title->001 seam is black end to end, the 001
arrives complete and correctly coloured, and the timed-out path still
reaches the briefing and on into a deck.

events.title: The rupture handover keeps a 312-line field
events.message:
The rupture handover keeps a 312-line field

KC caught it on b2 and photographed it (ref/beeb-paradroid-to-001-resync*
.png): the picture displaced downward mid-transition, which is a MISPLACED
field, not a wrong-length one -- exactly what a frame-length instrument
cannot see, and why jsbeeb read 39,93x throughout while b2 rolled.

The rupture's frame is three cycles with VSync 5 rows into the 13-row
tail, so a CRTC free-running in the tail's shape VSyncs every 104 lines.
Round two's aligned write started that cycle at line 64, so the next VSync
arrived at line 104 instead of 312. src/ruptalign.asm suppresses VSync
across the intermediate cycles and lets the first one the handler sees
arrive exactly one frame after the last:

    0     VSync of the last plain frame (row 31 of 39)
   64     that frame ends; a fresh one starts
  ~80     OSBYTE 19 + an 8-row spin land here; SetupRupture writes the tail
          shape and R7 = 255 goes straight over its R7
   64-168 cycle A    168-272 cycle B, R7 = TAIL_R7 written at ~240
  272-376 cycle C -- its row 5 is line 312. Three tail cycles ARE 312.

ROUND FOUR IS WHERE THAT LAST WRITE GOES. At ~180 it sat on cycle B's row
1, and whether that fires a VSync in B or only in C depends on the rule
this port measured -- R6/R7/R12/R13 take effect in the PREVIOUS cycle --
which the emulators disagree about. If it matches in B, VSync fires at
line 208 and again at 312: two bad fields where round two had one, which
is a picture displaced further, which is what KC saw. Past B's own row 5
at line 216 the two readings agree, so it goes in at ~240.

It lives in bank 5 because it wants ~50 bytes and no other bank has them;
ts_loads pages that bank in, the routine calls SetupRupture itself and
ends JMP PgData. Code image unchanged, PARBRF back to 18 bytes.

KC confirms it on b2. jsbeeb cannot see this class of fault at all.

events.title: The palette changes at fire 1, not wherever the main loop is
events.message:
The palette changes at fire 1, not wherever the main loop is

KC: "the top panel flickers (looks like a redraw)" going from the game
over static to Transmission Terminated. Nothing writes the panel's bytes
there -- GoWashStart put "Game over" up when the wash began, and IsStart
only parks the scroll, asks for the 16-row bottom edge and draws the page
in the strip. What changed was the ULA.

InfoCall's first act is SetTextPal, which ended in SetPalPlay: sixteen ULA
writes from main-loop code, wherever the raster happened to be. The panel
has its own palette, applied in exactly one place -- RuptVSync's
SetPalPanel, at VSync -- and it displays 64 to 96 scanlines later. A write
landing in that window left the panel in the DECK's palette for the rest
of the field: a one-frame flash across the top box that reads as a redraw.
About one transition in three, and worst at the game over, where the panel
is white and red and the wash is black and white.

So SetPalette builds palPlay and returns, and the next fire 1 makes it
live -- one field at the most, and at the one moment in the field that is
safe: fire 1 is at P+44, twelve scanlines after the panel's rows have
finished displaying. The IRQ's own write was never the problem.

Two screens have no rupture to apply it: SetupPlain's table already ends
with its own sixteen writes, and TiShow now calls SetPalPlay after
TiPaint. Everything else runs under the rupture.

Verified in jsbeeb, because a deferred palette could leave a screen in the
wrong colours: cold-boot title on its random deck palette, the 001 screen,
a deck, the wash's black and white, and the wash -> 999 transition stepped
a field at a time, panel intact in the field the palette changes in.

events.title: RuptAlign, second time: the rupture starts on a frame boundary
events.message:
RuptAlign, second time: the rupture starts on a frame boundary

Establishing the rupture costs three malformed fields, and they are a
phase problem: SetupRupture writes R4 = TAIL_R4 = 12 wherever the main
loop happens to be, and the plain frame is 39 rows, so the row counter is
usually PAST 12 and the 6845 runs on toward its wrap before the compare
matches. Frame lengths across the briefing exit, one field at a time:

  before   39,936  39,936 | 38,378  49,154  6,168 | 39,938  39,936
  after    39,936  39,936 | 39,939  39,936  39,936 | 39,936  39,936

RuptAlign waits for VSync with OSBYTE 19 and spins out the rest of the
frame -- 8 rows, 8,192 cycles, against a landing window of another 11
rows -- so the writes land in row 0 or 1 of a fresh frame where R4 = 12 is
ahead of the counter. ts_loads calls it immediately before SetupRupture.

THIS IS THE SECOND ATTEMPT. The first was reverted: KC judged it worse by
eye, but the blanks still leaked a row then, so a stripe of the play
buffer sat on screen through the whole seam and swamped it. With every
blank on R8 the alignment stands on its own.

Also measured on the way in and clean at 39,936: the 001 screen to deck
transition, where ReframeView swaps the bottom edge from 16 rows back to
15. What is visible there is the deck painting over the info screen for a
pass or two -- redraw cost, not sync.

It lives in PARBRF because it wants ~16 bytes of main RAM that need no
paging and the code image has seven; PARBRF is resident and valid on
every route into ts_loads, but NOT at HsEntry, which is why the call is
in ts_loads rather than inside SetupRupture. Code image 7 -> 4 bytes,
PARBRF 18 -> 2, which makes it the tightest region after the code image.

events.title: Every blank is R8, and the title is not watched being drawn
events.message:
Every blank is R8, and the title is not watched being drawn

R6 = 0 is not a blank: it leaks row 0, because the row counter is compared
at the END of a row. Measured twice today -- once in SetupMode, where the
leaked row was 512 bytes into the bank streams at DEPK_STREAM, and once in
SetupPlain, whose R12/R13 park on BUF_BASE and so put a stripe of the play
buffer on an otherwise black screen for the 3.7 s of the briefing exit and
the whole game-over seam. KC saw that as flicker at both.

So all four blanking points use R8_BLANK, the 6845's display-skew bits,
which gate the display enable itself: SetupMode, SetupPlain's table,
tiw_done and BrTimeout. The display comes back in exactly two places --
the rupture's IRQ, which writes R8 at fires 1-3 every field and covers
everything in the game, and the title, which has no rupture.

TiCRTC sets the title's shape but no longer unblanks. TiShow does, AFTER
TiPaint, so the RLE picture is painted into a dark screen and the logo
appears complete rather than a cell at a time (KC). Verified by breaking
inside TiPaint and screenshotting: black.

Costs nothing in the code image -- SetupMode's blank is the R1 write it
was already making, pointed at another register, and TiCRTC gave back the
ten bytes its R1 restore had cost PARTITL. code_end stays &2FF9. PARBRF
36 -> 18, PARTITL 37 -> 27, bank 4 unchanged.

Checked in jsbeeb over every path that could have come up black instead:
boot to title, the timeout into the briefing, the briefing exit into the
001 screen, a game, ESCAPE, the wash, the 999 page, and the high-score
entry -- the sharp one, because HsEntry displays on its own rupture
between two SetupPlains. Field lengths stay 39,93x throughout.

docs/raster-timing.md also records the teardown measurement (one 376-line
field), the three malformed fields at switch-on, and the RuptAlign
prototype that fixed those and was reverted as worse by eye.

events.title: The rupture is switched on next to the IRQ that drives it
events.message:
The rupture is switched on next to the IRQ that drives it

ts_loads put SetupRupture right after the IS_BLANK and then ran FillPanel
and three table builds before InstallIrq, so the CRTC sat in the tail
cycle's shape with nobody servicing it for the whole of them: a picture
at roughly double rate with no stable 50 Hz sync, which is the flicker KC
sees a TV do when the game takes the display over.

Measured on the boot path, breakpoints on SetupRupture and IrqHandler:

  SetupRupture -> first serviced IRQ   262,274 cycles -> 7,489
  frames painted in that window        14 -> 1

The JSR moved down to sit immediately before the JMP InstallIrq. Nothing
in between needs the rupture -- FillPanel writes &4A00, the others write
tables at &5400 and up, and none of it is displayed while the frame is
blank -- so the title's ordinary 312-line 50 Hz frame stands until the
instruction that hands the display over. Zero bytes.

Waiting for VSync before the switch was the other candidate and is not
done: it saves one frame where the reorder saves thirteen, and polling
CA1 costs ~15 bytes of a code image with seven. docs/raster-timing.md
records both, and the seams that are not in this class.

copperhf: M2 -- autoboot DiagArea ROM and the copperhf.device exec stub

The board now carries a 580-byte boot ROM (guest/copperhf/, built with the
dockerized cross-GCC; committed artifact in assets/copperhf/) served
read-only below the register block, with the DiagArea advertised via
autoconfig. The stub implements Open/Close/Expunge/BeginIO/AbortIO plus an
INT2 completion server: BeginIO clears IOF_QUICK and rings the doorbell,
the server drains COMPLETE_GET/ACK and ReplyMsg-s each request. No
partition mounter yet -- that is M3; a guest that knows the name can
OpenDevice("copperhf.device") and drive I/O.

Hard-won 68k lessons encoded in comments where they bit:
- MakeLibrary's word-displacement vector table needs same-file trampolines:
  cross-object `.short symA-symB` difference relocations are silently
  miscomputed by this toolchain's linker (and the table needs its -1
  terminator).
- An INTB_PORTS server may only trash D0/D1/A0/A1/A5/A6: parking the board
  base in A2 corrupted exec's server-chain iterator and address-errored
  the dispatcher on the first shared CIA interrupt of the boot. It lives
  in A5 now (scratch for the chain, preserved across ReplyMsg).

Verified: headless AROS boot reaches the normal insert-media screen with
"copperhf.device" InitResident-ed from the diag copy; full test suite,
clippy, fmt clean. New unit tests cover ROM serving, the read-only window,
and a DIAG_OFFSET/entry.s drift lock.

events.message:
Boot: the mode change goes after the banks, and nothing shows its loading

SetupMode was the first thing .start did, so VDU 22 blanked the screen and
the four bank streams then landed at DEPK_STREAM (&3200) inside a MODE 1
frame still pointed at &3000 -- the loads drew themselves. It runs after
BootBanks now: every load and every copy-up into sideways RAM happens in
the MOS's boot mode, where &3200 is not displayed. It still precedes
TitleSeq, whose artwork lands at &4000 under the clear VDU 22 performs.

That left TitleSeq's own *LOAD of PARTITL visible, so SetupMode leaves the

events.title: Console: the icons go back to even spacing, on a ladder of their own
events.message:
Console: the icons go back to even spacing, on a ladder of their own

KC: it is fine for the icons and the text to be offset. So the text
lines stay where they are and the icons return to 3/6/9/12 -- touching,
evenly spaced, the rows they had before the count lines.

They cannot share one ladder: an entry with two text lines needs a
four-row pitch, an icon is three rows, and four icons on a four-row
pitch from row 2 would put the last at 14 and write three rows past the
end of the buffer. Two ladders is legal because the two never collide --
icons in units 4-18, text from unit 24 -- and only the unit-type line
crosses the icon columns, which is why it keeps rows 0-1 and the first
icon starts at 3.

CON_ROW_ICON0..3 are new and the icon destinations derive from them;
consolesel.asm's CON_SEL* moved with them, and the ASSERTs that tie the
two together caught them, as they are meant to. There is an ASSERT on
the gaps being equal so this cannot drift back.

That is the second thing I called impossible in this layout and got
wrong, both times by applying an icon-to-icon or text-to-text rule
across the two. DECISION 5 says so.

Verified in jsbeeb: even icon column, text unmoved, and the selection
marker steps from the 001 to the database icon at the new rows.

events.title: chipset: pace pre-display sprite DMA with the beam, and fix the IPL pipe
events.message:
chipset: pace pre-display sprite DMA with the beam, and fix the IPL pipe

Two independent timing faults, both of which corrupted the same thing: the
vertical-blank sprite control-word fetch. Ghostown's Spooky Town paints its
credit-scroll background by multiplexing sprites 4-7 five times per line
from the Copper, so losing one channel drops five 16-pixel columns out of
every line -- black stripes flashing over the background.

Sprite DMA runs from the top of the field, above the render window, so the
lines from the sprite-DMA start (PAL $19) to the display start were
reconstructed by a replay in frame_capture.rs. That replay ran as one batch
at the display start, but `fetch_sprite_words` reads chip RAM as it is
*now*: a fetch modelled at line $19 actually sampled memory as of line $2C.
Software routinely rewrites its sprite descriptors from the vertical-blank
interrupt in between -- Spooky Town restores the old header and writes a new
one, immediately after the fetch it expects to have happened -- so the
replay latched image data instead of the descriptor. `poke_ctl` then took
vstart's bit 8 from that garbage and the channel's comparators pointed at
lines the beam never reaches for the rest of the field.

The replay is now paced by the beam: a slot-granular cursor
(`SpriteDmaReplayCursor`) advances as the beam passes each of a line's
sixteen sprite slots, with the frame's DMACON, SPRxPT and SPRxPOS/CTL
writes applied in between, so each fetch reads chip RAM at its own beam
time. The provisional live pass for pre-display lines is dropped: the
replay already owned those lines, and running both fetched them twice. The
cursor is serialized, so a state saved inside the pre-display window
resumes where it stopped. Both that cursor and the per-source interrupt
deadlines below change the serialized layout -- STATE_VERSION 71.

That left about one bad frame per second, with a second cause. The demo's
descriptor update is scheduled relative to the fetch and should enter at a
steady raster line; it jittered across v=2..36, and the frames where it
straddled the Copper's line-24 SPRxPT write moved the buffer while the
pointer stayed stale. Both faults were in the IPL recognition pipe:

  - The pipe extended an idle STOP nap. `idle_fast_forward_chunk` bounds a
    halted CPU's nap by the next device event, but nothing accounted for an
    interrupt already latched in INTREQ and merely hidden by the pipe. A
    halted CPU has nothing else to wake it, so the nap ran on to some
    unrelated event and the handler was entered a whole nap late -- tens of
    raster lines, not the five colour clocks the pipe is worth.
  - A single countdown was restarted by every newly raised source, so a
    later source stretched an earlier one's delay. Each source has its own
    path through the level encoder and now has its own deadline.

Handler entry is back within the pipe's own length, and 1600 consecutive
frames of the scene are clean on both OCS and ECS.

The two E-clock-phase-sensitive golden probes (`bltprobe-pace`,
`timing-test`) shift by one count, as timing-test/README.md describes for a
boot-timing change; re-blessed. Delivering interrupts on time also costs
about 8% of headless throughput, because the guest was previously
under-executing the ISR work it now runs.

events.title: ste: $FF820D is a HARDWARE difference, and the write is harmless — fix the comment
events.message:
ste: $FF820D is a HARDWARE difference, and the write is harmless — fix the comment

The comment above st_flip_super claimed only the hi/mid video-base bytes were
written, and that leaving $820D out 'keeps this correct on a plain ST too (no
$820D there)'. The code three lines below writes $820D. One of the two was
wrong; it was the comment.

Which one to fix needed measuring, on the configuration where it matters: a
plain ST with TOS 2.06 and an accelerator (Hatari --machine st --cpulevel 3
--cpuclock 32).

  - the write reaches the bus: 12 writes to ffff820d during boot, against 13
    each to ffff8201/ffff8203, so it is not dead code;
  - it raises no bus error. A full drive (boot, load, dungeon walk) took six
    bus errors, every one from the TOS ROM probing hardware it might not have
    (ffff8900 STE DMA sound, ffff8a00 blitter), and none from frua.

That is evidence rather than absence-of-evidence, because Hatari does model
this fault class on an ST — those ROM probes are exactly it, faulting and being
caught. The ST decodes the $FF82xx block coarsely and swallows the write. It
is harmless by construction too: pages are 256-byte aligned so the low byte is
0 on every flip, which is both its power-on value and the only value a plain
ST's fixed low byte can hold.

And it is a HARDWARE difference, not a TOS one (Compendium B.20: $FF820C
'Video Base Address Low' is STE-and-later silicon). Fitting TOS 2.06 to an ST
does not add the register; TOS 1.04 in an STE does not remove it.

Copilot's three findings on #604, all correct.

The saved default was validated -- filesystem checks included -- before
the launcher branch was even consulted, so a default whose floppy image

An automatic run also no longer overrides [emulation] power_on: pressing

nobody pressed it here -- the machine starts in the power state a

events.title: docs: the 020 build downgrades to ST graphics — run it on an accelerated ST
events.message:
docs: the 020 build downgrades to ST graphics — run it on an accelerated ST

The runtime backend choice was documented in one direction only (the 68000
build running on a Falcon/TT and picking their higher-colour path). It works
the other way too: dsp_detect reads the _VDO cookie, so the 020 Falcon/TT
binary detects ST hardware and downgrades itself to the same 16-colour ST-low
banded backend. The graphics follow the machine; only the CPU decides which
binary you can run.

That makes the Falcon/TT zip the right binary for an accelerated ST, which was
documented nowhere. Measured in the guest's own clock (FRUA_STEPPROF), one
dungeon step's render: stock ST 8MHz with the 68000 build = 155 ticks; ST with
an 030 at 32MHz running the 020 build = 9-13. Small sample, so the section
quotes the magnitude rather than the ratio.

Also records that no Hatari patch is needed to try it (--machine st --cpulevel
3 --cpuclock 32, with Hatari's own TOS 2.06/EmuTOS and 32MHz-max caveats), and
corrects a stale claim in the ST/STE entry: 'no version check in the code, so
earlier TOS may well work - nobody has tried' was wrong twice over.
plat_stram_alloc DOES gate Mxalloc on Sversion() and fall back to Malloc, and
TOS 1.04 has now been tried - a stock non-e ST boots and plays.

Stock-ST colour, measured rather than assumed: the STE 4-bit palette encoding
carries its extra bit in bit 3, so a plain ST reads a correct 3-bit
approximation for free - an ST frame uses only the even gun indices, the STE
frame uses the odd ones too. Costs colour count (15 distinct vs 23 in a walk
frame), not band seams: the mod-8 band-boundary test scores ST 5/20 and STE
4/20 against a chance baseline of ~2.5. It cannot get worse either, because
the collapse is deterministic - the 3-bit path can only merge colours, never
split them, and merging cannot create a seam.

events.title: floppy: latch the motor on the /SEL edge, and index the sync-word scan
events.message:
floppy: latch the motor on the /SEL edge, and index the sync-word scan

Two fixes to the drive model, both found booting Ghostown's Spooky Town
under Kickstart 1.3.

The motor latch. Every Amiga drive, the internal DF0 included, feeds /MTR
into a latch clocked by its own /SEL falling edge: the motor state changes
only at the instant the drive becomes selected, and the level of the MTR
line while it stays selected is ignored. That is why trackdisk.device and
the trackloaders deselect, set MTR, then reselect. DF0 was modelled as
level-sensitive instead, so a loader that restores a stale PRB shadow with
MTR high while the drive remains selected stopped the motor it had just
started. Spooky Town's motor-on routine writes $F9 (deselect), $71 (select
DF0, MTR low -- the latching edge), then writes back its shadow $F1 (still
selected, MTR high) before polling CIA-A /RDY, and so dead-spun at $C704EC
on a white boot screen. Turn-on now takes MTR low on either side of the
select edge; turn-off needs it high on both, the rule WinUAE and vAmiga
derived from hardware. External units keep running their drive-ID shift
register off the same edges.

Also mirror the /TRK0 sensor onto DF0's /RDY while its motor is off: the
internal mechanism has no drive-ID circuit to answer with, which is what
the external units use those cycles for.

The sync-word scan. `TrackRev::bits_until_sync` walked up to a whole
revolution one cell at a time -- about 101k iterations for a standard
AmigaDOS track. `Emulator::idle_fast_forward_chunk` calls it through
`next_sync_irq_cck` on every idle slice while a trackloader sits in STOP
waiting on DSKSYNC, so the scan ran thousands of times per track and
dominated the profile during loading. Each revolution now builds a lazy
index of the offsets where a 16-bit window matches the sync word, and the
query is a binary search plus a wrap fold. The index is derived state:
rebuilt on demand after a save-state load, replaced when DSKSYNC changes.
Spooky Town's 5s..10s loading window drops from 11s of host time to 1s,
which is what its audio underruns were.

events.title: input: one stamp per key — the accelerator beep is a DOUBLE DELIVERY (#11)
events.message:
input: one stamp per key — the accelerator beep is a DOUBLE DELIVERY (#11)

Reported from the Mega STe: [P]lay / [L]oad / [B]egin each WORK but beep every
time, "don't recall it doing that before".

The chime is jt1080, fired by L2d3e Phase 5's `else` arm when no DLItem claims
the key. That arm is faithful — the Mac beeps at a key nothing wants. What is
not faithful is that the port hands Phase 5 the SAME keystroke twice: the first
read claims the accelerator and opens a modal, the second finds no item with
that letter in the modal that just opened, and chimes. The beep was the engine
telling the truth about a key the port delivered twice.

Traced end to end on a Mega STe, one physical press:

  plat_kb_poll  = 9836      one poll
  kb_to_event   = 9836      one event
  l6dd0 STAMP   = 9836      stamp #1 -> jt1133 reads 'l' -> CLAIMED, opens Load
  jt1125 STAMP  = 108       stamp #2, no new poll and no new event
                            -> jt1133 reads 'l' -> UNCLAIMED -> jt1080

That also settles the open question in plat_kb_poll's own #132 comment, which
set out the discriminator and left it unanswered: two polls for one press would
be IKBD repeat or the test injector, one poll and two engine reads is ours. It
is one poll and two reads. The repo has been blaming the harness injector.

Cause is the TaskList #84 stash. l725c pops an event, pushes a copy to
g_evfifo so jt1125's consumers still see what the pump ate, AND routes it to
l6dd0 — which for a key stamps the pending slot (-818/-820). jt1125 later pops
the stashed copy and its port bridge stamps the same key again.

On the Mac the two paths cannot collide: jt1125 reads a separate IRQ-filled
buffer while L725c reads the Toolbox queue, so exactly one stamp lands per key
and jt1125 does not stamp at all. The bridge is a port addition for the single
shared queue, where whichever path reaches the event first consumes it. It was
right to add; it just has to know when the other path already ran.

Fix: jt1125 stamps only for an event it fetched ITSELF, not one popped from the
stash. That restores the Mac's one-stamp-per-key invariant. The event is still
RETURNED either way, so l2d3e Phase 1's movement routing is untouched — that
path reads the returned event, not the pending slot, and a walk drive confirms
it (party 10,8 -> 12,8, innkeeper event fires, text renders).

Measured A/B, same fixture, keys P L B, Mega STe under Hatari:

  HEAD   1 beep — 'p' stamped by l6dd0 then again by jt1125, second read
         unclaimed. Which key doubles is a race and moves run to run ('l' in
         an earlier run), which is consistent with a machine whose timing
         favours it beeping every time.
  fixed  0 beeps, one stamp and one read per key, all three claimed.

Falcon: 0 beeps after, and it never showed the letter double before — only the
shared Return case — which is why this read as Mega-STe-specific.

An unclaimed Return in the Hall still chimes. That is the faithful arm, not
this bug: nothing there has a Return shortcut.

Adds FRUA_BEEPTRACE (every beep source plus each Phase-5 key with its claim
result) and harmonises the FRUA_KEYDIAG caps to 400 across boot.c, events.c and
input.c — they were 60, and this bug is only visible by correlating stamps
ACROSS those layers, which a per-layer cap mismatch silently breaks.

All four targets build; 483 tests pass.

Not yet confirmed on the reporting hardware.

events.title: BUGS #12: the console opens mid-pass, and tranche B redraws over it
events.message:
BUGS #12: the console opens mid-pass, and tranche B redraws over it

Not the missing pool teardown the 2026-08-16 filing guessed. DoCharUnder
calls ConsoleEnter from below the main sprite draw and above the second
window's SprRestoreTr/SprDrawTr, so ConDraw paints the console and then
tranche B stamps the saved backgrounds and the droids back over it. The
modal arm that stops all sprite work is only reached next pass.

That also answers the open question in the entry: the bullets do not
keep updating behind the console. It is one pass's damage, left there.

ConMenuInit4 clears sprSplit -- three bytes, and the flag the tranche B
arm is gated on. SprSplitOK rewrites it on every pass that reaches the
draw, so nothing carries over.

Why the report named LASERS: the pool only splits when there is more
than one component of the overlap graph, and a droid standing next to
the player merges into the player's and goes to tranche A. A bullet
travels away from whatever fired it, so it is its own component and it
is what populates tranche B. Four scripted repro attempts with droids
beside the player all came out clean, which is consistent.

The visual repro was NOT reconstructed in the emulator and BUGS.md says
so plainly.

events.title: Console counts: the blank row, and the names' four-pixel left bearing
events.message:
Console counts: the blank row, and the names' four-pixel left bearing

The deck block moves down to row 10, which puts a blank row 9 between
the ship group and the deck group. I said that was impossible last
commit and it was not: only ICONS have to clear each other and only
TEXT LINES have to clear each other, so the alert icon at 13-15 sits
beside the deck's count at 12-13 quite happily. The ASSERTs are split
into an icon set and a text set so the rule is recorded rather than
re-derived wrongly.

The counts move one character right, to CON_COL_TEXT + 10. Measured in
the play buffer: at + 9 the digits and the names start on the same
character, but every capital in this font is inset four pixels -- an R
has no ink in the left unit of its first cell -- while a digit does
not, so the counts read four pixels left. Half a character would be
exact and pnCol cannot express it; a whole one is the nearest step and
lands four pixels the other way, as an indent. Count ink is now unit 44
against the name's 43.

events.title: Console counts: Alert to the top, aligned under the names, "1 droid"
events.message:
Console counts: Alert to the top, aligned under the names, "1 droid"

Four of KC's five follow-ups on the count lines.

The Alert LINE moves to the top beside entry 0's icon. Its own icon
could not come with it: the four icons are the menu's selection targets
and ConMenu4 walks conSel 0-3, so their rows have to ascend with conSel
or the marker jumps -- and conSel 0 is "leave", which the C64 puts
first. Three ASSERTs now hold that ordering. Entry 3 is the unlabelled
one now instead of entry 0.

The counts start at CON_COL_TEXT + 9, where the names begin: a label is
eight cells and ConTok's leading space is the ninth. That makes the
digits left-justified rather than blank-padded, so CnDigits4 drops the
leading zeros instead of blanking them.

The plural is a suffix CHARACTER in the shared block, 's' or a space,
not a flag: bank 6 prints it unconditionally because a branch is three
bytes it does not have. PnAscii maps a space to PN_SPACE and nothing
follows it on the line.

The fifth ask -- blank rows between the ship and deck groups -- is NOT
built and cannot be: entry 0's icon ends at row 4, the ship needs four
rows, so does the deck, and the alert icon then runs 13-15. Sixteen
exactly. DECISION 5 records the three ways to buy a gap and leaves the
choice to KC.

Bank 4 is down to 14 B and bank 6 to 7 B.

Verified in jsbeeb: 120/9 aligned under Paradroid and Repairs, and
"1 droid" above "9 droids" with shipNumDroids poked to 1.

events.title: copperhf: M1 -- board, [copperhf] config, and synchronous register protocol
events.message:
copperhf: M1 -- board, [copperhf] config, and synchronous register protocol

First milestone of copperhf.device (COPPERHF-DEVICE-PLAN.md), Copperline's
emulator-only hardfile controller in the spirit of WinUAE's uaehf.device: a
Zorro II board whose doorbell takes a guest IOStdReq pointer and whose host
side executes the request directly against the shared HardDriveImage layer,
so RDB and RDB-less images behave identically to [ide]/[scsi]/[lide].

- [copperhf] unit0..unit6 config section reusing the shared drive-descriptor
  shape; CD image paths rejected (hard disks only)
- CopperhfBoard: doorbell/completion-queue protocol with idempotent
  COMPLETE_GET + explicit ACK (torn-read-safe on the 16-bit Z2 bus),
  INT2 gated on IRQ_ENABLE, sector-streamed CMD_READ/WRITE/UPDATE/CLEAR,
  TD_FORMAT/TD_MOTOR/TD_GETGEOMETRY; I/O is synchronous in M1 (async in M5)
- guest/copperhf/copperhf_board.h: shared register-map source of truth for
  the M2 boot ROM/device stub
- wired into build_machine behind cfg.copperhf.enabled(); save states ride
  the generic BoardDevice path

events.title: Redux (5): the console counts the droids left, on the deck and the ship
events.message:
Redux (5): the console counts the droids left, on the deck and the ship

"Access granted." goes, as Redux does and KC agreed, and its two rows
plus the layout's two blanks pay for the two count lines. That is
exactly sixteen rows with nothing over, so the unit line returns to row
0 and layer-9 DECISION 17's row is spent again -- flagged, and the
icon-beside-the-unit-line alternative is still on the table.

The deck count is not drCount, which counts bullets and explosions and
would rise when something fired; the table is walked for real droids.
The ship count is shipNumDroids as it stands -- its seed of 1 is the
999, not the player.

Bank 4 counts and converts, bank 6 draws, and the answer crosses in
eight bytes of the PARAFNT block as finished ASCII: bank 6 had 39 bytes
and the divide belongs on the side with room. The word is the game's
own "droid" token plus an s.

CnCounts4 went into consolesel.asm first, in front of colourMap's
ALIGN, on the theory that the pad is free. The pad is spent: 200 bytes
there cost the bank 259, because past it the ALIGN rolls a page. Now
measured in DECISION 5, and in that file's warning.

Costs bank 4 115 B and bank 6 17 B; the code image is untouched.

Verified in jsbeeb: 120/9 on a nine-droid deck, then 111/0 after
CTRL+C cleared it.

events.title: Redux (4): the high-score entry starts where you left off
events.message:
Redux (4): the high-score entry starts where you left off

GetInitial began every initial at 'A', so a third set of initials meant
walking the alphabet from A three more times. hsPrev remembers what was
typed and HsGet seeds from it.

It belongs in hstable.asm for that file's own reason -- PARTITL is
reloaded from disc every title, so hsSelFor is back to its assembled
value each time, while bank 7 is never reloaded after boot. Compression
does not enter into it: a bank is ordinary RAM once unpacked. The three
bytes ride plandata's ALIGN pad, so bank 7 still ends at &BFF9 and the
code image is untouched.

hsSelFor is remembered rather than the filed table entry, and before it
is filed, so the next entry starts from what was typed and not from
whichever end of the table it landed in.

Verified in jsbeeb across both arms: DGZ entered on the low-score
screen, hsPrev read back 3/6/25, and the next game's HIGH-score screen
opened on D and seeded G -- through a reload of the overlay in between.

Layer-12 DECISION 4.

Suspending the crop under any CRT preset made autocrop inert for a

events.title: Redux (2): the deadlock does not reproduce, so it goes to the playtest log
events.message:
Redux (2): the deadlock does not reproduce, so it goes to the playtest log

A harness that stacks every droid on the player's own spawn, plus a
run-length counter on DrCollide's serviced pairs, over 60 s a deck.
The longest droid-droid contact was 35 passes on deck 0 and under 20
elsewhere; a stack of six disperses in seconds. Nothing saturated.

The mechanism is real all the same -- one pair a pass in a fixed order,
DrPause16 renewed on the higher slot, and drCollHit suppressing every
reversal until a pass finds no contact at all -- and the case the
harness cannot reach is the likely one: the player shepherding droids
into a dead end. So it is held open, not closed.

DECISION 3 records the mechanism, the harness recipe, the numbers and
the confound that made the first reading four times too high: a droid
leaning on the parked player wins the pair every pass. 12c now names
both this and DECISION 2 as things to watch for, with 1.4 s as the
baseline a jam has to beat to be news.

events.title: The briefing scroller parks the CRTC before it paints, so it stops hitching once a row
events.message:
The briefing scroller parks the CRTC before it paints, so it stops hitching once a row

KC saw it on real hardware and the rate was not the reason: sampled over
100 fields the scroll advances exactly 100 scanlines. What the display
gets is what the IRQ latches at fire 1, and across a row boundary that
read 7, 7, 1, 2 -- a field repeated and then two scanlines at once, six
times a second, with the average intact.

BrPaintRow is 35,850 cycles, measured against the User VIA's free-running
T1: ninety per cent of a field. br_scroll's SetCRTCStart came after it, so
on the one field in eight that paints a row the park missed the next
fire 1 entirely. Parking inside BrStep, as soon as line/scrollS/brTop are
complete and before the paint, puts it a few hundred cycles after fire 3
where it beats every latch; the paint still overruns into the next field
but invisibly, BrWaitField returning at once with fieldCount already
moved. No tearing: the row being painted is the staged brTop+15, below a
15-row window.

Verified at the same point in the travel -- iline now 3,4,5,6,7,0,1 with
pline tracking line on the wrap field where it used to lag -- and the
average re-checked over a second 100-field window.

The lesson is in the doc: position counters are not evidence about
smoothness, iline is.

events.title: The forced redraw gets its own DEBUG_REDRAW, so a release build cannot reach it
events.message:
The forced redraw gets its own DEBUG_REDRAW, so a release build cannot reach it

It was never gated -- the oracle is wanted on the ordinary build, so R was
simply always live -- and KC's call is that a debug key belongs under a
flag like the other four. DEBUG_REDRAW is DEV, so every dev build still
has CTRL+R; RELEASE loses the JSR and the fourteen bytes of bank 4 with
it, and the ASSERT DEBUG_ANY = 0 there is what proves it.

The flag's header carries the recipe rather than leaving it in CLAUDE.md
alone: what the oracle is for, that the diff has to cover odd mapHX,
non-zero line and diagonals, and that the player sprite vanishing while
the key is held is the tell that a build has it on.

!BOOT names it with the rest, so the banner now reads
"REM DEBUG: XFERWIN DECK KILL REDRAW" -- verified in jsbeeb, along with
CTRL+R still repainting the viewport in the dev build and both builds

events.title: CTRL+R on the briefing redefines the six controls, and the debug keys take CTRL
events.message:
CTRL+R on the briefing redefines the six controls, and the debug keys take CTRL

Z/X/K/M/L/SPACE become defaults in keyTab, and every one of the 36 places
that tested a control now goes through KeyDownIx and an index -- the same
two bytes the immediate was, which is what let the six sites in a code
image with six bytes left change at all. keyTab is those last six bytes:
no other main-RAM region is resident at all six moments a control is
tested, and PARTITL reads it directly because the font block that holds
KeyDownIx is not up at the first title of a cold boot.

The screen is bank 5, drawn through the briefing's own BrChar/BrCell, with
the panel left alone. ESCAPE abandons and restores; a key already taken
this run, or one the font cannot name, is refused; SHIFT and CTRL are
unreachable because the scan starts at &10, above the keyboard DIP links.
The chatter stops while it is up so the two beeps have voice 1 to
themselves -- the console menu step for a key taken, the collision bump
for one refused (the transfer's failure buzz was tried first: 2.5 s).

And with controls redefinable, R, C, W, [ and ] were a hazard -- bind LEFT
to R and every step repaints the viewport. All five want CTRL now, exiting
by the key-UP path so the press edge rearms. Moving the forced redraw's
test into bank 4 beside RedrawAll paid for it: the code image is back to
7 B free, bank 4 to 143.

Verified in jsbeeb, not by eye: the six rebound and read back, movement on
the new keys and nothing on Z, persistence across a game over and the
title, the high-score entry on PARTITL's direct path, chip writes counted
for the chatter and both beeps, and plain C against CTRL+C on the score.
