events.title: Flush the MOS's buffers before handing the IRQ back: it was playing the charset
events.message:
Flush the MOS's buffers before handing the IRQ back: it was playing the charset

KC heard a quiet sequence of rising notes after every game over, which
Q could not mute, pausing during the high-score entry and stopping only
when a real effect played.

&0400-&0C90 is the MODE 1 charset in reclaimed OS workspace. Inside it,
&0800-&08FF is the MOS's: &800-&83F sound workspace, &840-&87F the four
channel queues, &8C0-&8FF the envelope definitions. While we own IRQ1V
nothing reads any of it and the overlap is free -- which is why this has
never mattered. GoTitle calls UninstallIrq, the MOS's 100 Hz sound
driver wakes up, finds its queue pointers and buffers full of character
bitmaps, and plays them. The pitch sweeps because it is chewing through
glyph data; it is quiet because the attenuations it finds are 13-14.

Q could not touch it because Q sets sndVolume, and sndVolume only gates
OUR driver's writes. Any sound the mute cannot silence is not ours --
that mismatch is what identifies it.

Measured: after a muted game over, SndSilence had left all four
channels at attenuation 15, yet the chip read 14/13/-/14 with the tone
periods falling steadily (CH1 401 -> 146 -> 95, pitch rising). Zeroing
&0800-&087F stopped it instantly and restored all four to 15, which
pinned the cause. Sound suppression (OSBYTE &D2, the flag at &0262) did
NOT stop it: suppression gates new SOUND commands, not a queue already
draining.

Fix: OSBYTE &0F, X=0 -- flush every buffer -- BEFORE JSR UninstallIrq.
The ordering is the fix being airtight rather than nearly: our IRQ is
still installed there, so the MOS's sound IRQ is definitively not
running and cannot be halfway through draining a note while we reset
the pointers under it. After the uninstall there is a window between
its CLI and the flush where one garbage note can start. It costs a few
charset bytes, which do not matter -- BuildCharset repaints the set at
the next deck load and nothing between reads it.

Not caused by this day's work, though the Q mute is what exposed it.
Nothing in the volume, pause, transfer-button or keydown changes goes
near &0800, the charset's address, this seam or the MOS sound path. Not
bisected against an older build, so that is reasoning, not measurement.

Verified: silent through the death, game over and high-score entry, and
the briefing beyond plays its chatter normally.

The standing lesson is now in CLAUDE.md's memory map: the overlap is
safe only while we own the IRQ, so any future path that hands the
machine back must flush first. There is exactly one such seam today.

events.title: keydown reads the matrix directly: 243 cycles becomes 69
events.message:
keydown reads the matrix directly: 243 cycles becomes 69

Ported from thrust's test_inkey (BEEB/Repos/thrust/thrust.6502), which
is the canonical form of this. Port A is the slow bus, port B's low
nibble is an addressable latch choosing who listens ((value << 3) |
line), and line 3 is the keyboard's write-enable: drop it and the
hardware's free-running column scan stops, so the matrix can be driven
by hand. DDRA = &7F puts the internal key number out on PA0-PA6 and
leaves PA7 an input carrying the answer. One write, one read -- this
tests a key we NAME, so there is no iteration.

&FE4F and not &FE41: the no-handshake register. &FE41 strobes CA2.

Measured both ways, JSR to RTS inclusive: OSBYTE &81 = 243 cycles,
direct = 69. The OSBYTE figure was taken twice by independent routes
(the title loop's turn rate, and a DEBUG_TIME bracket round ReadKeys)
and they agree to a cycle. At ~12.5 key tests a pass that is ~2,175
cycles a pass, 2.7% of the budget -- four of those tests arrived this
afternoon, which is what made it worth doing.

THE RASTER WAS THE RISK, NOT THE SAVING. The sequence runs under
PHP/SEI/PLP so neither the MOS nor the sound driver (same port A, from
the IRQ) can interleave it: 26 masked cycles, twelve times a pass,
against a rupture whose T1 stages are deadline-driven. It costs them
nothing -- 25.0 Hz exactly before and after, rupture holding, boundary
clean while scrolling. NOT claimed: what the MOS masks for inside
OSBYTE &81, which was never measured.

The emulator showed the mechanism outright. Testing Z (IKN &61): key up
reads back &61, key down reads back &E1 -- the same seven bits we
wrote, with PA7 as the answer.

KNOCK-ON: TiWait's body WAS one OSBYTE, so the title loop is now 3.15x
faster (11,508 turns/s against 3,654). The volume gate goes back to
1-in-1024 (was rejected there at 3.6 Hz on the old build; it is 11.2 Hz
now, where the other two call sites sit), and the timeout into the
briefing falls 17.9 s -> 5.7 s. That is not a regression: the C64's is
256 frames, 5.1 s, and TiWait's header always claimed the wrap was "the
same order as the original's". KC to say if 18 s was preferred.

AND A TRAP IN DEBUG_TIME, now in its header: the bracket first reported
ReadKeys costing 2,903 cycles AFTER the conversion against 1,009
before. T1 free-runs from its latch, so the subtraction is modular
arithmetic only while the counter does not pass zero between the two
reads; when it does that pass contributes ~65,536 spurious ticks. The
excess was 1.96 x 65,536 exactly -- two wraps -- and the baseline had
none. The reload point drifts through the pass, so bad readings come in
consecutive runs, not at random. jsbeeb breakpoints DO fire now, so a
breakpoint pair and an elapsed_cycles difference is the honest tool for
anything short.

Verified through every path: title volume/mute and fire (MOS IRQ live
there, which is the harder case), movement and scrolling, P both ways,
SPACE transfer, [ deck hop.

events.title: SPACE as a second transfer button, and the redraw moves to R
events.message:
SPACE as a second transfer button, and the redraw moves to R

DECISION 12 in docs/layer-7-combat.md. An addition the C64 has no
equivalent of, and the reason is the keyboard: DoMoveMode ($31B9) has
one button to divide three ways, so it disambiguates by direction and
by time -- fire WITH a direction draws the weapon, fire with NONE
settles for eight passes and then enters transfer mode. On a joystick
that reads as intent. On a keyboard you must come to a stop, hold L and
wait a third of a second before touching a droid means anything, by
which time the droid has moved.

A dedicated button has nothing to disambiguate, so the settle is
SKIPPED rather than reproduced: SPACE puts moveMode at Transfer on the
next pass and holds it while the key is down, direction or no
direction. The fire route is untouched -- a second door into the same
room, not a change to the first. KC picked the semantics.

It forces the state AND the button, and both halves are needed:
mm_transfer holds moveMode at 0 only while fireDown is set and drops to
Mobile the moment it is not, so the mode alone would last one pass.
Setting fireDown is safe -- DoMoveMode is its only reader, and with the
mode already 0 the arm it lands in never calls DoFire, so holding SPACE
cannot shoot. Checked, not assumed.

Placement is forced three ways: below the L block (which writes
fireDown from scratch every pass), above DoMoveMode (which consumes
it), inside the overPhase guard (a corpse does not transfer). The
movement is untouched -- ReadKeys/CalcSpeed/ApplyMove have already run
by there, so ignoring the direction costs nothing and he enters
transfer mode mid-stride.

The forced RedrawAll moves SPACE -> R. It is the buffer-diff oracle
that CLAUDE.md's verification recipe and layer-3-scroll.md are written
around, so it could not just be dropped; R has been free since
DEBUG_RESTART went. The live instructions now say R; the historical
session records that mention SPACE are left as they were.

Verified in jsbeeb: SPACE from Mobile -> 0 in one pass, panel reads
"Transfer"; released -> &80; SPACE while walking -> 0 with
sprActive[7] still 0; the fire route unchanged (L with no direction
&80 -> 2, mmDelay 8 -> 6 over three passes -> 0, release -> &80); R
breaks on RedrawAll and SPACE runs ten passes without it.

Also recorded, because it cost half an hour: moveMode freezes wherever
it stood whenever a modal screen owns the machine, since all five modal
arms end the pass above the fire block. It looks exactly like a stuck
key. An unnoticed opening 001 info screen was the culprit.

events.title: v0.5.1: career depth (training, diary, records, youth) + AI shooting fidelity
events.message:
v0.5.1: career depth (training, diary, records, youth) + AI shooting fidelity

CAREER — the manager finally has levers, and the club has a memory.

* WEEKLY TRAINING (new). Pick a drill, an intensity and up to six players; the
  session is graded and slowly loads their skills. Modelled on FIFA 18's
  weekly graded session and CM 01/02's intensity dial, mapped onto SWOS's seven
  0..7 skills. Deterministic (CareerRng only) and completely skippable.
  Design + sources: docs/decisions/04-training-and-development.md
* YOUTH INTAKE DAY (plan #6). The academy's new players once a summer, each
  with a scouted RANGE rather than a number.
* CLUB DIARY (plan #7). One line per event across the whole career: signings,
  milestones, thrashings, runs, intakes, the board's verdict, the season's
  finish. Read-only by design — no unread counter, nothing to clear.
* APPEARANCES + GOALS and a CLUB RECORDS board (plan #8). New APP/GLS columns
  in the squad screen and an all-time appearance list that a sold player keeps
  his place in.

Three long-standing defects these screens exposed:

* every regular in every career was pinned at 100 fatigue — i.e. playing at
  FatigueModel.SkillPenalty's -2 tier for whole careers. Recovery between
  matches was FLAT and could never catch a big enough per-match gain; a flat
  rate cannot have an equilibrium below the cap. It now also sheds 35 % of the
  carried fatigue over a week's rest, and a pre-season divides it by five.
* the youth academy fell permanently silent after ~3 seasons: a club at the
  squad cap was given no intake at all.
* FormModel.FormSkillDelta had no caller outside a test. Form was computed,
  stored, displayed — and ignored by the match. It and the new sharpness now
  apply in CareerMatchTeam.ToPlayerRecord, capped at one SWOS level either way.

GAMEPLAY — closer to the original, and the CPU shoots straight.

* The AI no longer curves the ball away from goal. A port-only chase heuristic
  with no counterpart in the reference fired 25 410 of 30 000 ticks and
  overwrote the team-wide currentAllowedDirection from an arbitrary off-ball
  sprite. That value is also the AI's after-touch input, so it was bending
  every AI shot at random. Measured over five fixtures, shot-flight rotation
  against the rotation needed to steer toward goal: 53/39 toward/away with the
  heuristic on, 78/12 with it off. Ten fixtures scored 16 vs 13 goals, so the
  fidelity fix costs nothing.
* Spin direction now matches the asm. In the original D2 is ONE register, so
  the 769/129 write also seeds the low byte the spin sign test reads later.
  The port kept a separate d2Byte at 0, which made both teams always spin
  left; the real defaults are opposite spins per team.
* --swos-smoke prints shot-count, distance and curve telemetry so this class
  of question can be argued with numbers instead of impressions.

Also: version stamp (V0.5.1) in the bottom-left of every menu screen, read
from application/config/version so there is one place to bump it.

The browser career client is kept out of this repository. Main.cs reaches it
only through `partial void` hooks, so the tree compiles and runs without it.

events.title: Pause on P, in the shape DoPause is written in
events.message:
Pause on P, in the shape DoPause is written in

DoPause ($3B7C) ported. Called from ml_passend beside the volume keys,
which is where the C64 calls it from too -- GameLoop $13E6, ABOVE the
consoleState test, so the console, the transfer game and the lift are
all pausable.

DECISION 17: a blocking loop, not a flag the pass tests. The flag looks
tempting (the pass keeps drawing, so the picture stays alive for free)
but the pass has five modal arms that each end it at their own point,
so the flag would need honouring in six places and the console would
still answer its keys while "paused". A loop freezes all six by
standing in front of them, which is why the original is written this
way.

P both ways, KC's request. Resuming on fire -- which the manual offers
-- was dropped: it would fire the weapon on the way out, which is what
the C64's wait-for-release dance at $3BEB exists to prevent. clr-home's
quit has no port either; ESCAPE is always available and does it
properly.

The message costs almost nothing because the panel was already built
for it: PanelUpdate picks a mode word by index and repaints when a
shadow byte says the index moved, so "Pause" is a fifth pnTxtTab entry
and both the paint and the repaint fall out of the existing compare.
Five trailing spaces because Pause_txt has five. sndState 0 in and $12
out, as $3B8F/$3C0F. gameTick needs no save/restore -- it counts passes
and the pause happens inside one, so the C64's pair is a no-op here
rather than an omission.

DECISION 18: the picture freezes solid and the C64's does not -- its
loop keeps AnimateDroids and the font animation running, so the rotor
spins and the tiles cycle behind a frozen game. That needs the sprite
pool's window and tranche handling reproduced outside the main loop.
Recorded as wanted, not built.

AND A BUG THE FIRST BUILD HAD, worth the paragraph: WaitNextPass waits
for passF0 + FRAME_LOCK, stamped at the top of the pass we freeze in.
WaitUntilField's distance is signed and good for 127 fields either way;
its header said "2.5 seconds, and nothing here waits that long", true
until this routine existed. Measured: after a seven-second pause the
game came back and then did not move for two seconds. Two instructions
re-date passF0 on the way out, and the invariant is now stated at
WaitUntilField where the next person to block the pass will read it.

overPhase gates the whole routine: no pause under the death wash, where
the exit's sndState $12 would restart the sound mid-death.

Verified in jsbeeb: "Pause" in the mode field where "Mobile" was;
gameTick frozen across a seven-second hold; sndState 0 and all four
channels silent; the volume keys still stepping while frozen; P
restores the word, the sound and 25.0 Hz within 0.2 s; P held two
seconds during a death does not pause, and the death, game over and
high-score entry run through untouched. NOT exercised: pause with the
console, transfer or lift view up.

Cost: 93 B code image, 22 B bank 6, two state bytes.

events.title: Volume on the cursors, Q to mute, and the deck hop moves to [ ]
events.message:
Volume on the cursors, Q to mute, and the deck hop moves to [ ]

AdjustVolume ($0CB4) ported, and one of the few C64 routines this port
does not take verbatim. Kept: the 0-15 range, the clamp at both ends,
and the every-fourth-frame repeat, which lands on the same wall-clock
rate here by different arithmetic. Changed, all agreed with KC and
written up as DECISIONs 12-16 in docs/layer-11e-sound.md §9:

  - cursor UP/DOWN, not F5 and SHIFT-F5 -- nothing about ReadFKeys'
    direct matrix read survives the move to OSBYTE &81
  - it runs EVERYWHERE, not from TitleLoop alone: ml_passend (the point
    every modal arm converges on), BrWaitField and TiWait
  - Q mutes, which the C64 has no equivalent of. sndVolume 0 with the
    old level stashed, NOT sndState 0/$12 -- the briefing and GoTitle
    both write that byte and a mute flag hidden in it would fight them
  - no readout; the panel's text line is spoken for and the key is
    audible

Volume 0 is already total silence by construction, so the mute needs no
driver support -- but the attenuation clamp round nine deleted had to
come back first, in the C64's 6-byte form. 30 - level - sndVolume is
0-30 the moment the volume can be under 15, and unclamped it wraps into
the latch's channel bits. §8's costed 4-byte BCS snfv_off alternative
rejected on inspection: it skips the period write too, so a quiet voice
freezes its pitch and jumps when the volume comes back.

VolKeys is main RAM although the driver it steers is bank 4's:
everything it touches is main RAM, so it carries no paging contract and
every call site can use it from whatever bank is resting. Its three
bytes outlive a game, which is what makes muting at the silent title
mean something.

TiWait needed measuring rather than assuming. It is not field-locked --
its iteration count IS the timeout and the seed for the starting deck --
so the poll hangs off the tiLo carry. Measured in jsbeeb: 3,654
iterations a second idle, so the 16-bit wrap is a 17.9 s timeout and the
gate costs it under 1%; 6,720 a second with a key held, so the repeat
lands at 26 Hz. 1 in 1024 was tried first and gave 3.6 Hz, unusable.

The debug deck hop moves off the cursors to [ and ]. prevUp/prevDn keep
their names.

Verified in jsbeeb: steps and clamps at both ends at the title, in the
briefing and in play; the level survives title -> game; Q toggles once
across 13 held poll rounds; muted, the game runs with the driver live
and all four channels at attenuation 15, and Q in play brings the hum
back. The clamp caught in the act -- volume 2, snLevel 85, unclamped
would be 23, snChAtt reads 15. Pass rate unchanged at exactly 25.0 Hz.

Cost: 6 B bank 4 (51 -> 45), 98 B code image (&2D81 -> &2DE3), 3 B
PARBRF, 11 B PARTITL.

events.title: Intro lightning: real randomness, and a check grid that cannot strobe
events.message:
Intro lightning: real randomness, and a check grid that cannot strobe

KC saw near-constant lightning after the rate tweaks, and the cause was
that the trigger was never random: System VIA T1 runs the 100Hz tick,
20,000 cycles = exactly half a frame, so a vsync-locked read of &FE44
lands on the same T1 phase every time - a near-constant byte drifting
on interrupt jitter, passing EVERY 32-frame check whenever it drifted
under the threshold. The gate now uses an 8-bit Galois LFSR stepped
every frame, seeded from the timer at boot with its jitter folded in
at the check, so TRIG_PROB means what it says.

Trigger-logging in jsbeeb then showed a second effect: even with real
randomness, a geometric distribution on a 32-frame grid chains
minimum-spacing flashes (15 lit, 17 dark, four in a row). The check
grid is now 64 frames at 62.5%: the same ~2s mean, but flash starts
can never be closer than 1.28s. Measured 19 flashes in 41s at
64/128/192-frame intervals. The &FE44 fact is now in CLAUDE.md's
hardware list and docs/intro.md s7.

events.title: wonderboy: bg_scroll_blit at parity — sixteen straight-line bodies again
events.message:
wonderboy: bg_scroll_blit at parity — sixteen straight-line bodies again

bg_scroll_blit 148.8 K → 111.6 K cycles a call against the original's
105.3 K (x1.4 → x1.06; the variant body itself is 102.4 K exclusive vs
101.5 K). Frame 339.5 K → 328.4 K, 23.60 → 24.40 fps.

Reconstruction
- src/scroll.c: the column's seam split is a compile-time constant
  again (LONGWORDS_BEFORE_THE_SEAM), and DEFINE_COPY_VARIANT generates
  the sixteen routines names.txt names, bg_scroll_copy_x0..x15, each
  owning both halves of its blit as the original's does — one call per
  blit, entered by index through BG_SCROLL_COPY_BY_COLUMN. Column 0 is
  the shipped bytes instruction for instruction: thirty
  move.l (a0)+,(a1)+, addq.l #8,a0, lea 40(a1),a1, dbf; the seam
  columns keep the original's lea -128(a0),a0.
- include/scroll.h: copy_constant_run — a Duff-style fallthrough that
  folds to a straight run for any constant length ≤ 30 — serves the
  text box (22) and the stage tile row (2) as well; the runtime
  block/tail copier is retired.
- tools/recreate_kit/include/machine.h: CURSOR_BARRIER — the empty asm
  that keeps a walked cursor in an address register ("+a" on m68k):
  without it GCC folds postincrements into d16(An) moves (28 cycles)
  and lets the allocator park the cursor in a data register.
- atari/build.sh: scroll.c's -O3 reason re-measured (the bodies are
  level-independent; the queue/serve tier is +4.4 K a frame at -O2).

Verification
- make test 6,453 green; make guarded clean (10,043 runs); mutations:
  one longword too few/many (178/169 red across scroll, text, stage,
  game), column 3 given column 2's split (exactly its own case red),
  second half skipped (23 red). On target: m2, ownplay, floppy boot OK;
  WBOOT.ST 24,576 B free.

Docs
- STATUS.md "Performance", atari/README.md baseline; names.txt
  cmt 0x83b6 describes the generated bodies.

events.title: wonderboy: the frame under three vblanks — four levers and -O3 per unit
events.message:
wonderboy: the frame under three vblanks — four levers and -O3 per unit

12.20 → 23.60 fps; 656.7 K → 339.5 K cycles a frame, x1.06 the original
(320.5 K). Every frame is under four vblanks; most sit at two.

Reconstruction
- src/scroll.c: copy_longwords unrolled eight at a time under one dbf
  with a 4/2/1 tail; the seam split hoisted out of the scanline loop;
  an empty asm keeps the cursors opaque so GCC emits the postincrement
  pair (measured: it otherwise rewrites the run to d16(An) moves, and
  re-rolls a constant-trip loop). The wrap-back pointer is formed only
  for the columns that wrap — the guard that let -O3 unswitch the loop
  and put the frame under two vblanks. bg_scroll_blit 208.7 K → 148.8 K.
- src/sound.c: the VBL music tick addressed off the module base
  (d16(a3), 76 → 10 absolute constants), the channel tier off a record
  pointer, add_byte's carry from the byte wrap; the attenuation hoist
  licensed by a _Static_assert. vbl_handler 10,364 → 8,662 cycles/tick.
- src/blit.c: the off-image guard hoisted from the row to the whole
  blit (spans_in_image, fail-closed), the column loop unrolled so the
  width constant folds the window indices, the register file a local
  for the blit. blit_sprite_rows 74.2 K → 28.9 K a frame, x1.4 the
  original.

Build
- atari/build.sh compiles one object per unit: -O3 for the frame-loop
  cores (ipa-cp clones per width, hud_plot_digit 2,100 → 827 cycles),
  -O2 for behavior.c/rad.c/boot.c and the shim (16.8 KB for ~2 K cycles
  was the worst trade). WB.PRG 107 → 154 KB; boot floppy 27,648 B free.
  Both unit lists validated against the units built; the per-width
  clones asserted after the link. -flto fails the script's checks —

events.title: walk: render the step BEFORE its square's event fires (#163)
events.message:
walk: render the step BEFORE its square's event fires (#163)

Field report (Mega STe ATW800/2, 0.9.17-diag2): stepping onto a text
square printed the text at the bottom of the screen BEFORE the 3D view
drew the move — 'The Weary Wanderer.' landing while the view still
faced the caravan square. Structural, not timing: #90's deferred-render
optimization skips l1908's own jt312 (the Mac renders there), and
l63c0's replacement re-render runs only after the whole dispatch —
but jt297's GAP-1 block dispatches the square's event (l709e) INSIDE
the dispatch, so the event's text drew into a frame the step had never
reached. Invisible on a fast present; glaring on the ATW800/2 where a
full present is ~0.5 s of VME writes. The Mac order is
move-render-then-event (jt955's arm renders, THEN L41b2 dispatches).

Fix: hoist the cell-special read and flush the deferred render (jt312,
which presents) exactly when the step will do more than move — an
event will dispatch, or the sticky text box is about to clear.
Ordinary steps keep the #90 single-render path; only event steps pay
the second render, which is the frame the Mac drew anyway.

Verified in Hatari with an authored STICKY.DSN (sticky message,
confirm_mask=0, one step north of entry): enter -> view shows the move
and the text prints; standing -> text persists; leave -> box clears.
471 passed; 68000 + AGA + ECS build. Authoring trap re-confirmed while
setting it up: _hook's (col,row) vs the position box's ordering — hook
both readings when in doubt, one of them is silently a wall.

events.message:
titles: black the hardware CLUT while a title composes — each screen pops in whole

Field report (Mega STe ATW800/2, 0.9.17-diag1): every title screen showed
its seams — the previous screen recoloured by the incoming master
palette, the base image crawling in before its set palette landed (the
magenta 'defer' slots on screen = the pink frames), then the overlay
piece arriving as a second visible crawl. The cause is structural on a
hardware-palette screen with a slow present: a CLUT write recolours the
frame INSTANTLY while a full present is ~0.5 s of VME byte writes, so
NO ordering of "install palette" and "write pixels" is seam-free —
53e7a8b9's blit-then-commit only moved the flash.

New qd_palette_blackout(on) (hw-palette backends only, no-op on
quantisers): on=1 pushes an all-black CLUT and latches further
qd_set_palette forwards (the logical palette still accumulates); off
pushes the accumulated palette. l19d4 wraps each title's two-pass
composition in it — the rows land invisibly on a black screen and the
release pops the finished title in whole, with a short fade-to-black
between screens: the DOS/Mac presentation. The hw path also skips the
mid-body present (it would spend a second slow present on an invisible
intermediate); quantisers keep the Mac's two-present cadence unchanged.

Verified: Falcon title captures match the pre-change landmark hashes
frame for frame (quantiser path untouched, cycling alive); TT shows
each title whole and correctly coloured with black fades between, SSI
stars cycling on the hold; emulated ATW800/2 (xVDI) and AGA both boot

events.title: engine: the title logos cycle again — jt1066 phase A copied the wrong way
events.message:
engine: the title logos cycle again — jt1066 phase A copied the wrong way

The SSI stars and MicroMagic shimmer died in v0.9.7, when the jt919 title
roll replaced the port intro (the port intro ran its own cycle loop, so it
never depended on the engine tables). The chain was healthy until the
commit: jt993 read the title set's 3 cycle records (TITLE.CTL set 2 metric
[.,3,0,32,0,224,3,.]), jt1069 installed them into -3258 — and the very
next jt1066 wiped all three before jt1067 ever saw one come due.

Phase A of jt1066 is the third reversed-jt406 lift in this one subsystem
(after jt1067's rotate and jt1069's 0x756e install). The Mac pushes at
0x75e2-0x75ea are len 8, backup(-3354+i*8), live(-3258+i*8) — and by the
convention the 0x756e fix pinned (the push nearest the jsr is the SRC),
that is BlockMove(live, backup): the commit SAVES each flagged range.
The lift restored instead — from a backup jt1068 seeds to 12 empty
sentinels and nothing else writes — so every commit erased every fresh
range. The walk's fireplace only survived because dungeon_cycle_ensure
re-installs its ranges before every tick; the title roll has no such
guard, which is exactly the asymmetry that hid this for ten releases.

Bisected on release binaries (dense 0.6s captures, md5 runs): animated at
v0.9.6, dead from v0.9.7 — the jt919 commit's window, matching the user's
"some time after adding the music". With the copy righted, FRUA_CYCTRACE
(new, in-tree) shows the 3 ranges live and committing spans 176-191 +
208-239, and the SSI screen's frames all differ again; the UA wizard's
lightning alternates too. Menu and credits hashes are byte-identical to
the pre-fix build. 471 passed; 68000/STE titles render clean to the menu;
amiga AGA + ECS link.

events.title: nova: blitter-offloaded presents on the ATW800/2 — 43% less VME traffic
events.message:
nova: blitter-offloaded presents on the ATW800/2 — 43% less VME traffic

The Seurat 2D engine (regs at LUT+0x900; model measured against xVDI
20260730 on the hatari-et4000 emulation) copies card memory only, so
the CPU still crosses the bus once per doubled pixel — but the 2x row
duplication moves to the card: the full present's CPU writes each
doubled row once and one cmd-0x0003 blit per changed-row run copies
the even rows to the odd rows. The init clear (512,000 CPU byte
writes) becomes one cmd-0x0005 fill blit from a zero row parked past
the visible screen — xVDI's own desktop-fill idiom.

Measured on the emulated ATW800/2 (VME access counters at the same
boot-to-menu anchor): 2,778,599 -> 1,594,553 bus writes, -43%, menu
pixel-identical. Armed only after the LUT bind (same xVDI-cookie
hardware gate — a classic card bus-errors at these addresses);
video.cfg novablit=off opts out; a bounded status poll drops back to
CPU presents for the session if the engine ever fails to go idle.
The register model awaits confirmation on the real FPGA — novablit=off
is the field escape if the first hardware run misbehaves.

events.title: Fix (one) Hatari window mouse sync issue
events.message:
Fix (one) Hatari window mouse sync issue

If user moves mouse outside the window while mouse button is pressed,
SDL leave event comes only after mouse is released, and mouse coords
can be wildly outside the window area => constraint stored leave
coords (used for mouse location syncing on mouse enter) to the Hatari
window size.

This still leaves the issue with Atari borders and Hatari statusbar.
Host mouse can move over those, but Atari cursor cannot, so those also
cause mouse pointer to go out of sync a bit.  I don't see any good
solution for that, so it may be best just to tell users either to use

events.title: Layer 10: the transfer panel is the C64's again, layout and words
events.message:
Layer 10: the transfer panel is the C64's again, layout and words

KC read the original in the emulator and said the top panel was wrong -
it should keep the Paradroid logo in the middle and the score on the
right, both red, with only the left-hand text changing, and doubted our
win/lose/draw strings. Right on every count.

The C64's transfer messages are 13-byte strings beginning `2, 2` - column
2, row 2, the same eleven-cell mode-word field panel.asm already fills
with Mobile/Weapon/Transfer. The logo at cols 15-23 and the score at
30-37 are never touched:

  entry   Captured  ($69CB)  drawn at $22A0, Capture
  select  Colour 00 ($E6DB)  drawn at $E1F2, SubGameSelectSide
  play    Finish -99($69BE)  drawn at $20F9, xferDoCounter
  win     Complete  ($69FD)  drawn at $221D, FinishTransfer1
  loss    Burnt Out ($69F1)  drawn at $222F, FinishTransfer1
  tie     Deadlock  ($69A4)  drawn at $22D3, Capture's replay loop

The countdown is not a separate field at all - it is the last two bytes
of the left word's own string, which is why $20EF/$20F6 and $E1E4/$E1EB
write to +$A and +$B. Decoded from the raw bytes through
export_strings.py's C64->glyph map rather than trusting the annotator,
which mattered: there are TWO "Colour" strings, $69B1 plain for the
console and $E6DB with the digits built in.

Against that, the port blanked the whole line (XfTextClear walked 0 to
PN_COLS) and invented "transfer done", "transfer failed" and "short
circuit". XF_COL_MSG is 2 now with XF_MSG_CELLS 11, XfTextClear clears
only that field, XF_COL_TIME is 10 so the digits land on the field's last
pair, and "colour" and "finish -" are eight cells to put them there. The
words are the original's, in lowercase - XfGlyphAt is one cell a glyph
and the original's capitals are two, which is bank 6's PnGlyph and
unreachable from bank 7.

XfNum3 and XfSelectText are deleted. They were DECISION 7's substitute
for the sprites the port could not draw; DECISION 14 draws the real icons
on the board, where the original has them, so the stand-in has outlived
its reason - and deleting it paid for the new strings, leaving bank 7
where it was at 7 B of tail.

The ink was wrong too, and that was one byte: XfGlyphAt set
fontMask = &FF with a comment claiming it "never had an ink mask", so the
word drew black on the white panel. panel.asm has said THE MODE FIELD IS
RED, like the logo since Layer 9; it is PN_INK_RED now, the same ink
PnMode uses.

Verified in jsbeeb: "colour 93", then "finish -49", then "burnt out", all
red at column 2, with the logo and score standing in red throughout.
DECISION 6 is annotated where this supersedes it.

events.title: Layer 10: the droid number icons come back to the transfer board
events.message:
Layer 10: the droid number icons come back to the transfer board

KC played the transfer game and said the icons were missing. They were -
DECISION 7 dropped them in August for the panel line's two numbers. This
puts them back, and corrects what DECISION 7 said the original does.

WHAT THE C64 DRAWS. SubGameSelectSide puts two hardware sprites either
side of the board: sprite 7 with image $4F for the player ($E12B-$E14C)
and the target's with droidSprNum,X + $48 ($E14F-$E175). $48*64 = $5200,
the dynamic sprite area, so these are the LIVE droid sprites - rotor top
and bottom with the three-digit number between, what BuildDroidSprite
and AnimateDroids compose.

THEY DO NOT SLIDE, and DECISION 7's wording that they do was wrong -
KC's correction. $E1B5-$E1C7 writes plySpriteX/cpuSpriteX as one of two
values, 88 or 255, and $E1F5-$E213 pushes those at the sprite registers:
the icons SWAP SIDES when the stick changes its mind, each keeping its
own colour, so the colour names the droid and never the side.

Colour: the player's own yellow, the target black. The palette has no
white; magenta was the first cut for the target and KC changed it to
black, which is better against the blue, closer to the original (the
target sprite is literally black, $E165) and removes a wrinkle - yellow
and magenta are the LEFT and RIGHT side colours here, so a player on the
right saw their yellow icon over the magenta side and the two readings
disagreed. Black is not a side colour.

Position is the C64's: x=88 and x=255 are screen pixels 64 and 231 once
the 24-pixel border offset comes off, which is board columns 8 and 28,
rows 0-2. Both sit in blank spans of the three-row top block, so the
icons overlap no wire - KC's own observation, checked against xbTop - and
nothing repaints there: DoColumn walks only the twelve wire rows,
DrawCBar columns 19-20, DrawResult row 1 columns 19-20, DrawPulserCols
columns 1 and 38. Drawn at setup and again only on a real side change,
never during play. Blank rows write logical 0, the board's own
background, so a swap needs no separate clear.

src/xfericon.asm, AND ITS POSITION IN THE PARXFER BLOCK IS LOAD BEARING:
the consolesel.asm trick the other way round. The icons are 421 B against
126 B of ALIGN padding, so droidicon7.asm's 110 B and the state ride in
front and the code is assembled BEHIND plandata.asm's ALIGN, where it
costs its own size. Not theory - the first cut put it all in front and
overran the bank by 198 B. Fitting it took the split, a tighter swap test
in XfSelectTick (STX does not touch flags, so CPX's Z survives it) and
dropping a variable by deriving the second column as
XI_LCOL + XI_RCOL - xiCol.

XfIconPix is general over all four logical colours - build the logical-3
byte, then AND with the icon's mask - which is why turning the target
black cost two bytes there and gave six back at the call sites, XfIcons
now passing the mask straight in Y. Bank 7 ends at 9 B free, 2 of padding
and 7 of tail: the 154 B the glyph-pool pass found is spent, and anything
further in that bank needs its own pass.

export_droidicon.py still had the OUT7 path Layer 13d stopped using, so
the data came back with no tool work.

Verified in jsbeeb: 001 yellow left and 329 black right at setup;
pressing right swaps them, each keeping its colour, panel line agreeing;
a full game runs to its verdict with both icons untouched, which is the
no-repaint analysis confirmed live.

events.title: Layer 10: the board's three glyph sets become one pool - 154 B
events.message:
Layer 10: the board's three glyph sets become one pool - 154 B

KC wants the droid number icons the C64 puts either side of the transfer
board, and asked for a RAM pass to pay for them. This is the pass. It
found 154 bytes in bank 7 without touching a line of transliterated game
logic, because the waste was in generated artwork.

xferboard.asm shipped the 17 board characters three times over, once per
ownership set (DECISION 1). 13 of those 51 cells were duplicates - which
is DECISION 2 showing up in the data, since a character whose every
logical-3 pixel is STRUCTURAL is byte-identical in all three sets. The
five identical in all three are $00, $D0, $D1, $FB and $FC: the blank,
the two bus caps and the central bar's ends.

export_xfer.py now emits one pool of the 38 distinct glyphs plus a
51-byte xbSlot table, and the cell painter reaches the glyph through it:
xsGlyphOf gives 0..16, a new 4-byte xfSetOfs replaces xfSetLo/xfSetHi and
picks the set's run, xbSlot names the pool entry. Six more instructions
and ~8 cycles a repainted cell, against a pass with 12,000 spare. 816 B
of glyphs became 659; padding 228 -> 126 and tail 58 -> 314, so real free
space in bank 7 went 286 -> 440.

VERIFIED, AND NOT BY THE OBVIOUS METHOD. A before/after diff of the
10,240-byte play buffer showed 758 bytes differing, confined to the
twelve wire rows in the gate columns with the frame, buses and stock
identical. That is the RNG, not the glyphs: XfStart seeds from
USR_VIA_T1CL EOR fieldCount, and six extra instructions a cell shift the
cycle it samples on, so the gates land elsewhere. A before/after diff is
worthless for this change.

What proves it is an independent reconstruction - dump xsScr/xsCram and
rebuild the whole buffer on the host from export_xfer.mode1_char, the
PRE-dedup algorithm, through xfPenOf. All 10,240 bytes matched. The
exporter also asserts by construction that pool[slot[set][code]] is the
exact byte string the flat table held, for all 51 pairs.

Two corrections to the record while here. Bank 7's "58 B free" from
DECISION 13 was the TAIL figure and understated it badly: plandata.asm's
ALIGN &100 leaves padding that anything before that include rides for
free, so real free space was 286 B and the repeat filter cost 54 B, not
the 256 the tail move suggested. CLAUDE.md now says to quote the pair,
never the tail alone. And SPR_SAVE is &3E00, not the &3000 the memory
table implies - it moved up behind PARAFNT for Layer 11, and that cost
an hour of a wrong shadow-screen dump.

src/data/ is gitignored and build.ps1 does not run the exporters, so a
clean checkout now needs `python tools/export_xfer.py` before it builds.

events.title: nova: auto-switch the card to 640x400x256 for the game, restore on exit
events.message:
nova: auto-switch the card to 640x400x256 for the game, restore on exit

On a Nova/ATW800/2 the game now plays full-screen in the card's native
640x400x256 regardless of the desktop mode (big desktops left the game
in a corner; a TrueColor desktop meant no card at all), and QUIT hands
the desktop back exactly the mode it booted in.

The sanctioned interface: the driver's XCB block via the xVDI/NOVA
cookie — p_chres(RESOLUTION*, 0) at XCB+8, the same call XVDIMENU
makes. Three facts measured on the hatari-et4000 emulated card:
- p_chres is a REGISTER-ABI call (RESOLUTION* in A0, fll_ofst in D0,
  from XVDIMENU's own code) — a C stack call sets a garbage mode;
- vq_extnd still answers with the PRE-switch caps afterwards (the
  VDI's device info is not rebuilt at runtime), so the backend takes
  width/height/planes from the .BIB entry it just set;
- RESOLUTION entries are 86 bytes; match on mode byte +35 (2 = 256c)
  and the HDI/VDI display words +60/+68. The .BIB is read from the
  boot drive's AUTO folder; restore entry = the XCB's current index,
  verified against the live size, with a scan fallback.

Verified on the emulated ATW800/2: 1024x768x256 desktop -> game at
640x400x256 (menu clean, LUT bound) -> q/y quit -> desktop back at
1024x768. Classic NOVA-VDI (640x480): benign no-op, unchanged boot.
video.cfg novares=off opts out.

events.title: Layer 10: the transfer cursor gets a repeat delay for the keyboard
events.message:
Layer 10: the transfer cursor gets a repeat delay for the keyboard

KC played the subgame and said it was too fast and twitchy on keys
compared to the C64 joystick. The clock turned out to be innocent and
the input model guilty, so this is DECISION 13 - the only place the
port's controls deliberately leave the original.

The countdown is faithful and 2MHz never touches it. Mechanism is
verbatim: BCD xfTime from &99, decremented every other iteration the way
$20DA does it, then xfGrace = &55 iterations of grace. Measured in
jsbeeb at 79,886 cycles between consecutive XfPlayTick entries - 39.94
ms, exactly two fields, no overrun - against a body costing 67,550, so
7.92 s of countdown and 3.4 s of grace.

The C64 lands on the same 25 Hz by a different route. doSubGame gates
each half-turn on irqToggle, set by the raster chain at line 246 and
cleared at 118, and both waits are live - three of GameLoop's five
equivalents are nopped to D0 00 in the CE listing with a "!! remove"
beside them, and the subgame was left out of that. The gate is
work-dependent, so it was costed: a half-turn is ~21,000 cycles against
a 19,656-cycle PAL frame, so each takes its own frame. That half is an
estimate from the listing rather than a measurement - there is no C64
emulator here - and the doc says so.

Which leaves the input model, and it is the original's own.
xfer_DoMove ($1D75) is level-triggered, ReadKeys is a raw OSBYTE &81
scan, and one row per 40 ms crosses the twelve-wire bus in under half a
second. Fine on a self-centring stick where a flick fits inside one
iteration; impossible on keys, where the shortest honest tap is two or
three rows.

So XfGetMove's human arm - and only the human's, the CPU arm returns
above it - is edge-triggered with a hold-off: a new direction moves at
once and then waits four passes (160 ms), a held key repeats every two
(80 ms, 12.5 rows/s), a release re-arms the edge and a reversal counts
as a new direction. XfStart clears the state so a key still held from
the deck cannot eat the first row. Verified: a 120 ms tap moves one row,
a 200 ms hold two, an 800 ms hold nine, the countdown still ticks
99 -> 35 over 254 frames, and the game runs to its verdict clean. The
hold-off shipped at 240 ms first and KC asked for less.

The cost is out of proportion and is recorded as such: the filter is 54
bytes, but plandata.asm's ALIGN &100 had 27 bytes of padding spare, so
it rolled planInk to the next page and bank 7 went 314 B free to 58.
Recoverable by assembling the routine behind the ALIGN, at the price of
splitting it from XfGetMove; left as an open item because main RAM, not
bank 7, is the binding constraint. CLAUDE.md's bank-7 figures were stale
in two places - 314 B, and a "5,690 B reserved for the droid portrait
pool" that was wrong by two orders of magnitude - and are now current.

Not changed: the select countdown, which is the one real timing
deviation found. DelayScore(80) paces the original's at ~105 ms a tick
for ~11 s, where ours ticks every other pass for 7.92. Fire confirms
immediately either way, so it only shows if the player dithers, and
fixing it needs a mod-3 counter rather than the present AND #1.

events.title: Layer 15: the ship reset was missing the alert and the player's energy
events.message:
Layer 15: the ship reset was missing the alert and the player's energy

KC found a new ship starting on red alert. $1293 STA Alert is part of
_entership, and the port only zeroed alertLvl in CombatInit - which sits
ABOVE the T5 split, precisely because it also wipes the score. So a ship
transition inherited the last deck's alert, which after clearing a ship
is red by definition.

Auditing $1289-$12CD store by store, at KC's request, turned up a second
miss with the same cause: $12A7 sets the player's energy to 7 on entering
a new ship and the port carried the old ship's energy over. KC confirmed
porting it as it stands. droidType is NOT reset, on the C64 or here, so
the droid captured on the last ship comes with you - at 7 energy, against
whatever ceiling that droid has, because maxEnergy is genuinely untouched
at $12A5.

The other twelve stores were already right. Two needed checking rather
than trusting the annotated names: droidSprNum looked like it might be
maxEnergy, since $12A5 sets it and droidEnergy to 7 together, and $158F
shows it is not - it is the sprite number, which has no port meaning
because the player is slot 0 and drSprNum[0] is unused. And
ClearSubGameData sounds like it clears transfer state; $377E shows it
only zeroes the FindStrings index, which the port has no equivalent of.
The full table is in the layer doc as DECISION 7.

The alert reset joined EnterShip4's existing A = 0 run in bank 4; the
energy went into InfoHigh's ih_ship in main RAM, because bank 4 had three
bytes left and it needed five. DroidsInit deliberately leaves entry 0
alone, so after the call is as correct as inside it.

Paid for by two rewrites that are provable rather than clever, each a
LDA #n : STA where the branch immediately above has just tested the
flag's value: dbgdeck.asm's two latch sets became INC (+4 bank 4) and the
main loop's shipClear clear became DEC (+2 main RAM).

Verified in jsbeeb: alertLvl forced to &C0 reads 0 on the new ship;
energy 62 before and 7 after, with maxEnergy unchanged at 58; shipLevel 2
and a fresh 119-droid roster.

Bank 4 has 3 bytes free, main RAM 2.

write lands past the 1MB memory window and bus-errors (found by running

so its cookie now gates the probe; classic cards fall back to vs_color
cleanly (verified: menu up on the emulated card with no video.cfg).

events.title: Layer 15: the endgame - clearing a ship, and the next one
events.message:
Layer 15: the endgame - clearing a ship, and the next one

The port had no win condition and no ship progression at all: shipNumDroids
was maintained and never read, and GameStart fused the C64's two entry
points so its second half could not be reached. All five tasks land here.

T1/T3, the payouts. 500 for a deck (two AddScore 250, $17DF and $17E4, not
one call of 500 - AddScore takes a byte) with sndFx1 = $17, and 2,000 for a
ship as ten calls of 200, $1274-$127D. Both at DroidsUpdate's clear hook,
which is now all of $17DC rather than Layer 14's colour alone.

T2, leaving the deck. The C64 raises notInDeck, a shared "leave this loop"
flag the port has no equivalent of - it reaches the lift, the console and
the transfer by other means - so this is a dedicated shipClear byte, tested
in the main loop beside them and below the sprites, where the transfer's own
screens are and for the same reason: the page takes the play buffer over.

T4, ShowShipClear. $3816 is GotoHires, ClearGameScreen, ShowRobotType,
BuildIntroSprites, PrintTokenString - which is IsStart's is_st_norm path
instruction for instruction. So the screen is five table entries and a token
list and no drawing code. The list is SIXTEEN bytes, not the ten the scoping
note claimed: $6DCE is two sentences and the $FF is at $6DDD.

T5, the split. GameStart now writes shipLevel = 0 - $1255's own value, where
the port wrote 1 - and falls through into EnterShip4, whose first act is
NextLevel's INC at $129E. The split point is not a judgement call: above it
is what a new game needs and a new ship must not have, and the decisive
member of that set is CombatInit, which zeroes the score. Call it on a ship
transition and the 2,000 just awarded goes with everything else earned.
$1289 also falls into NewShipInfo at $12C7, so a new ship announces itself
on the screen the port already had.

Two pre-existing bugs fell out of building it.

export_strings.py stopped one string short, on the stated reasoning that
the C64 never prints its last. It does: string 248 is "awarded", the last
word of ShipClear_txt, and this screen is the first thing in the port to
ask for it. Token $F8 was landing on the sentinel. 248 -> 249 strings,
1542 -> 1549 bytes. Re-run export_strings.main() - the script has no
__main__ block and build.ps1 does not run the exporters.

And walking back onto a cleared deck re-ran the whole event - sound, colour
and another 500 points, every time. The C64 does not: $1388 tests what
InitDeckDroids placed and skips RunDroids outright when it placed nothing,
while $1395 runs InitColors regardless, which is why an already-clear deck
still shows the cleared floor. DroidsInit now assumes clear and lets the
first placement say otherwise, so a count of 1 makes DroidsUpdate's guard
return and the arm is never reached. It moved above ReframeView for that:
RedrawAll builds the palette and DroidsInit is what now decides the floor.

DEBUG_DECK's arm moved to bank 4 (src/dbgdeck.asm) to pay for the main-RAM
arm above - the trade dbgkill.asm made, one size up, and NOT in colourMap's
padding, where 69 more bytes would push the ALIGN past the page.

Verified in jsbeeb: the deck payout (score 0 -> 975 on a deck whose roster
predicts exactly 475 in kills plus 500); the screen in the C64's own words
with the player's droid; shipLevel 1 -> 2 with a fresh 119-droid roster and
the score carried, not reset; re-entry to a cleared deck leaving the score
at 975 with the floor still blue and no effect; and the relocated deck hop.

Main RAM and bank 4 both end with 2 bytes free.

events.title: Reconstruct the 1987 SSG renderer from the Amiga binary; add .dat support
events.message:
Reconstruct the 1987 SSG renderer from the Amiga binary; add .dat support

Recover the lost SSG (Scene Simulation Generator) renderer as C source in
ssg-src-authentic/, reverse-engineered from the original 1987 Amiga 68000
executable with Ghidra and validated byte-for-byte against the binary's
output under vamos. The reconstruction reproduces the binary's actual
behaviour rather than merely its images: bare rt-style names, single-
precision (FFP) math, an fscanf .dat reader built on the executable's own
recovered scanf grammar, a fixed up-front sphere allocation, and the
scanline-coherent screen-space-culling renderer (per-sphere projected
bounding boxes, per-scanline active lists, per-pixel column cull). Builds
as the ssg_authentic target with a ctest that checks it against the
captured original-binary renders.

Also add the runtime .dat parser for the modernized rt pipeline
(src/datparse.c) and PNG output (src/png.c); reverse-engineering notes;
blog posts (parts 3 and 4); Ghidra export scripts and validation tooling;
and the original-binary capture files used as the validation oracle.

events.title: wonderboy: blit register window — no libgcc modulo (4.75 → 9.45 fps)
events.message:
wonderboy: blit register window — no libgcc modulo (4.75 → 9.45 fps)

Reconstruction
- src/blit.c: mask_reg/plane_reg wrapped the 68000 register window with a
  `% WB_BLIT_SCRATCH_REGS`; -m68000 has no 32-bit divide, so each was a
  ~900-cycle __umodsi3 (→ __udivsi3 + __mulsi3) call — 856 per frame, 47%
  of the frame, from nine sites inlined into blit_row. Both now wrap with
  one conditional subtract (bit-identical for every reachable cell/plane);
  the cross-header bound the argument relies on is pinned by a
  _Static_assert (WB_BLIT_CELL_WORDS == WB_PLANES + 1).
- Measured with Hatari's CPU profiler: 1,646 K → 838 K cycles per frame,
  blit_row 42,000 → 8,807 cycles per call; the original runs 320 K/frame
  at a locked 25 fps.

Verification
- make test 6,417 green on a clean build; blit.o references no `si3`
  helper; mutations (swap the wrap comparison) go RED in test_blit.py.

Docs
- STATUS.md: "Performance" section with the measurement and the change.

events.title: Layer 14: a cleared deck's floor turns blue, and C to clear one
events.message:
Layer 14: a cleared deck's floor turns blue, and C to clear one

KC, 2026-08-24. When the deck holds nothing but the player, its
background goes blue.

The C64 does the same thing at a coarser grain: RunDroids ends its
compaction with STY numDeckDroids and, at a count of 1, runs a whole
deck-cleared event - InitColors, AddScore twice with 250, sndFx1 = $17,
and INC notInDeck when the ship is clear too. InitColors forces the
whole 12-slot record to ColorSets entry 7, which the listing itself
labels "7 - deck cleared", and its floor is C64 colour $B, dark grey.
MODE 1 has no grey, so blue is KC's substitution, and only the
background changes rather than all four logicals. Only the colour is
ported; the score, the sound and the ship-clear arm are Layer 15's, and
layer-14 DECISION 6 lists them as open.

deckClear is the test, not drCount, and that is a bug KC found rather
than a preference. LoadDeck runs ReframeView - which ends in RedrawAll,
which calls SetPalette - BEFORE DroidsInit, so arriving from a cleared
deck the palette was built while drCount was still 1 and the new deck
stayed blue with droids on it. LoadDeck now clears the flag first and
the compaction sets it, so the state cannot depend on the load order.
The C64 reads numDeckDroids directly and gets away with it because
InitColors is called from RunDroids, after the count is right.

The text palettes are exempt: palBase >= 64 is deckTextPal, whose
logical 0 is a legibility choice of its own (DECISION 4), not a floor.

DEBUG_KILL, ON, is the fourth debug flag that changes what the game
does: C kills every droid on the deck one at a time through
DrKillDroid, so the cleared floor can be reached without shooting a
deck empty. It drives the REAL kill path - explosion, sound, score,
alert, DrRemoveShip, sprite slot - so what it tests is the mechanism
and not a shortcut past it. It lives in src/dbgkill.asm, in bank 4
because DroidsUpdate calls it, and included before colours.asm so
colourMap's ALIGN padding absorbs it and the bank does not grow.

events.title: Layer 15: bank 4 gets 97 bytes back, from tables nothing read
events.message:
Layer 15: bank 4 gets 97 bytes back, from tables nothing read

The Layer 15 space pass. Bank 4 was 8 bytes on the fuel gauge and the
endgame's five tasks want about 50; it is now 105, with colourMap's 17
bytes of alignment padding untouched on top.

The saving is 112 bytes of per-deck tables that no longer had a reader.
Of the C64's eight tables at $F120 only deckDroids is read anywhere in
src/: deckOffsetLo/Hi indexed the RLE stream Layer 13d deleted;
deckY/deckX/deckHeight/deckWidth are the deck-plan geometry, of which
bank 7 has its own copy in sideview.asm because only one bank is visible
at a time; deckColour predates colours.asm's per-deck scheme table.
src/data/ is generated, so the change is in export_bbc.py, which carries
a comment saying how to put any of them back.

15 bytes went straight back out, and that is the part to remember.
Shifting bank 4 down by 112 pushed sound.asm's 38-byte voice-state block
across a page and broke ASSERT HI(snFreqLo) == HI(snPhase+1) - SndCopy's
stride-2 self-modified store steps the low byte only. That assert had no
padding behind it, so any bank-4 edit of the wrong size could break it.
It now has a conditional pad, at most 37 bytes and often none, so it
heals itself; the cost in this build is 15. A future bank-4 change can
therefore move the gauge by up to 37 bytes on its own - read it.

Verified as purely mechanical: both builds' listings reduced to a stream
of (mnemonic, addressing class) and diffed - 22,954 instructions, zero
differences. Main RAM, banks 5, 6 and 7 all end where they did.

In jsbeeb: boot, title, briefing, play; a diagonal scroll with the play
buffer diffed against a forced RedrawAll (SprDrawAll/SprDrawTr poked to
RTS), 0 diffs of 10,240; C clearing the deck; a deck hop; the console
opened from a console tile with all three pages drawn and closed through
entry 0; a lift ride to another deck; ESCAPE to game over, the high-score
entry, and round through the title to the briefing.

DEBUG_KILL was not turned off - the room was found elsewhere and its ~45
bytes stay in reserve. DEBUG_MAPGUARD no longer blows the one-page assert
but is still 19 bytes over bank 4; recorded, not chased.

events.title: ecs: CLUT-keyed RAM palette cache — the walk's per-step re-quant churn (A500)
events.message:
ecs: CLUT-keyed RAM palette cache — the walk's per-step re-quant churn (A500)

Field report: on the A500 the town walk drains and reloads its colours on
every step ('the CLUT keeps unloading/loading'). Measured on the inn
street route: SEVEN full re-bands in sixteen moves, each dragging a full
re-render — the walk's wall-set CLUTs alternate between a handful of
palettes, and the only cache (the disk one) keys on clut+FRAME hash,
which can never hit mid-walk.

This is the ST's st_pcache ported: six RAM entries keyed on the CLUT
alone (hash + full 768-byte verify, MRU). A hit skips the cut entirely
and carries the two guards the ST proved out: indices the cached cut
never saw are re-pointed at their nearest per-band slot (no falling
through the absent-colour bucketing), and when the restored remaps equal
the live ones the planes on screen stay valid — palettes-only, no
force-full, no epoch reset. Fresh cuts and exact disk hits both store.
video.cfg clutcache=off opts out. ~59 KB of BSS.

Same route on the cache build: 3 fresh cuts (first-ever CLUTs only),
3 RAM hits, and the user's exact video shots — the brown door, the
innkeeper event — render correct in emulation.

events.title: Layer 9: the panel's mode word is red, like the logo and the score
events.message:
Layer 9: the panel's mode word is red, like the logo and the score

KC: "the text on the left hand side of the top panel should be red, same
as the paradroid logo and the score in the rest of the panel."

The original says so directly. LevelColors ($2844) fills six rows of
colour RAM with bgColor and then overwrites rows 2 and 3, COLUMNS 2 TO
37, with $F2 -- low nibble 2, red:

  2853  LDA #$F2
  2855  LDY #35
  2857  STA $D852,Y      ; $D800 + 82  = row 2, col 2
  285A  STA $D87A,Y      ; $D800 + 122 = row 3, col 2
  285E  BPL _1           ; 36 cells, cols 2-37

The status line's fields are the mode word at col 2, the logo at 15-23
and the score at 30-37 -- all inside cols 2-37, so all three are red on
the C64. We had the logo and the score right and the mode word in
PN_INK_TEXT.

Three routines write that field and two needed changing:

  PnStr (bank 6)       Mobile/Weapon/Transfer/Console and PnBriefing's
                       "Briefing" -- PN_INK_RED after PnAt, which resets
                       the ink: the same two lines the logo and the
                       score already had.

  DbPanelStr (bank 7)  the droid database's "More" and "Console" --
                       DbGlyph's ink is now the variable dbInk, so the
                       PAGE keeps DB_INK white and only the panel field
                       takes DB_INK_PN red. DbPanelStr puts it back.

  XfGlyphAt (bank 7)   the transfer game's verdict messages at col 4 --
                       LEFT ALONE. A different screen with its own
                       palette, and not what was asked for.

Cost: 5 bytes of bank 6, which is down to 4 free, and ~14 of bank 7's
314.

Verified in the panel buffer rather than from a screenshot: the mode
word, the logo and the score all come out logical 2 and nothing else --
71, 55 and 8 bytes with the high plane set and ZERO in any other plane.
Checked on both "Mobile" and "Console".

The icon selection was re-checked on the ct_back path at the same time:
returning from the database with conSel = 1, the ship icon is white and
the other three black, drawn once.

NOT verified: the droid database's own "More", written on its page 3.
Its sibling "Console" write shares the changed path, but page 3 was not
reached in the emulator.

events.title: Layer 9: the console selection is the icon's colour, as the C64's is
events.message:
Layer 9: the console selection is the icon's colour, as the C64's is

KC: "on the c64 the menu option is just indicated by changing the icon
colour, not with a selection marker." Correct -- the white bar was ours.

conWaitInput ($2C63) writes SpriteColor $F1 -- VIC colour 1, white -- to
the newly selected sprite and puts $FF back on the one it left, taking
that from the sprite table's own field at $6B94+9 (colour 15, light
grey); WrSpriteState ($09B7) STAs the byte into $D027,Y. Nothing else
marks the selection.

Black and white here, because MODE 1 has no grey. KC was shown a 2x2
dither for a real grey, the deck's highlight, and black, and took black:
the same KIND of change as the original's, a brightness step, taken to
its ends. Layer-9 DECISION 18.

A TRANSFORM, NOT A SECOND COPY. An icon is two-colour, so its shape
lives entirely in the LOW nibble of every byte; the high nibble is 0 for
logical 1 and a copy of the low for logical 3, and one patched AND
chooses. Neither bank 6 nor main RAM had room for black artwork.

THE COLOUR IS CHOSEN BEFORE THE DRAW.  KC, on the first build: "the
icons all appear white before then becoming black. when returning to the
menu the icon should be drawn in the correct colour once." Visibly true
-- ConIcons is the SECOND thing ConDraw does and the recolour ran after
every line of text. So ConIconInk4 now fills conInkT (four bytes of main
RAM: &F0 selected, &00 the rest) before anything is plotted, and
ConIcons/ConDroid load it into csn_mask per icon. Main RAM because
conSel is bank 4's and bank 6 cannot read it -- the same reason PN_TABS
and pmShip exist.

ConSprNib was restructured to pay for that in a bank with 16 bytes: its
three stores now share one csn_put that takes a four-pixel pattern in a
low nibble and builds the high plane from it -- the SAME transform
ConIconSel4 uses, so the draw path and the in-place path agree by
construction. That deleted conNib3 (sixteen n*&11 entries, now computed)
and made conDblHi/conDblLo patterns rather than finished bytes. Net cost
to bank 6: 7 bytes.

The in-place transform stays for menu STEPS, which redraw nothing. Only
the two after-redraw paths lost their post-draw call.

WHERE THE SPACE CAME FROM. ConIconSel4 is ~80 bytes and bank 4 had TWO;
the first build overshot by 38. colourMap is ALIGN &100 with 162 bytes of
padding in front of it -- and DELETING THAT ALIGN RECOVERS NOTHING, tried
and measured: tiledefs.asm aligns next and pads by the same amount, and
the bank still ended at &BFFE. The padding is a hole, and a hole only
pays if you put something in it. So the routine is src/consolesel.asm,
INCLUDEd between chardata.asm and colours.asm -- anywhere before that
ALIGN will do, because the pad then shrinks by exactly what was added and
the page boundary does not move. It cannot live in colours.asm: src/data/
is generated. CLAUDE.md now carries the rule, and the 162-byte limit past
which the ALIGN rounds to the next page and costs 256 at a stroke.

Bank 4: 2 bytes free -> 45. Bank 6: 16 -> 9. Main RAM: 6 -> 3.

Verified in the buffer, stepping through the draw itself: mid-ConIcons
and before a single character of text, ship 27 bytes of its final 46 and
deck and alert complete, every byte black and zero white; next dump, 001
white at its full 76 and the others black at 46/160/92. After a step to
conSel = 1, 001/deck/alert every non-zero byte at high = 0 and ship every
one at high = low -- zero malformed bytes, counts unchanged. The marker
column is clear on all four rows.

Two stale comments fixed: console.asm claimed the icons and the marker
were "logical colour 1, white on every deck". The buffer says the icons
were logical 3, and Layer 14 made logical 1 black.

events.message:
Layer 9: the console menu moves down one row

KC: the play area has been sixteen rows since 2026-08-21 and the console

CON_ROW_UNIT/ACC/SHIP/DECK/ALERT: 0, 2, 5, 8, 11 -> 1, 3, 6, 9, 12.
Constants only, so it costs nothing.

WHERE THE C64 PUTS IT. ClearGameScreen ($2BA5) fills 17 rows from $4940
-- $4800 + 320, so screen row 8 -- at 40 bytes a row (FillCRAM $0A52).
So the console area is screen rows 8-24 and ConsoleMain's five lines, at
screen rows 10/12/15/18/21, are console rows 2, 4, 7, 10 and 13.

We are therefore still ONE row above the original, not level with it.

its icon on 13-15, filling the area exactly); KC was shown both layouts
and chose one row. Both console.asm and layer-9 DECISION 17 now say so,
and say not to "correct" it to two without asking -- the derivation above
makes two look obviously right, and it is not what was asked for.

drift apart:

  - the four icon destinations          console.asm, were 2/5/8/11
  - the marker bar CON_MARK0-3          droid.asm, were 3/6/9/12

events.title: Layer 14: the logo screen gets its emboss back, and a random boot deck
events.message:
Layer 14: the logo screen gets its emboss back, and a random boot deck

The C64 logo screen is embossed and ours was one flat colour.

WHY. The screen is hires (Irq1 $2922 writes $D016 = $C8, bit 4 clear), so
a cell is the shared background plus one foreground colour -- and
ShowTitle $2879 makes a SECOND pass over the same 1,000 codes, writing
$D800 from CharColor $0800. Colour is a property of the character CODE,
not of the cell: CharColor's high nibble is a fixed slot and
NewCharColors $3577 patches the low nibble per deck. Slot is artwork,
physical is palette -- the split this port already has.

Matching all 1,000 cells of Title_dat against ref/c64-logo-screen.png on
a fitted grid, the whole screen is five slots:

  slot 0  484 cells  (162,142,229)  code $00, blank        -> logical 0
  slot 9  247 cells  (241,238,251)  white highlights, TL   -> logical 3
  slot 7  249 cells  (100, 79,180)  violet shadows, BR     -> logical 1
  slot 4   17 cells  ( 23, 15, 61)  BY ANDREW / BRAYBROOK  -> logical 1
  slot E    3 cells  green          the three blobs        -> logical 2

The highlight and its shadow are about three character cells apart and
never share one, so none of it needs per-pixel colour. export_title.py
bakes each slot's logical colour into the 36 glyphs (SLOT_LOGICAL) and
that is the whole change: title.asm is still 1,140 bytes, TiCell is
untouched, the RLE stream is untouched. Supersedes layer-11 DECISION 9.

The four fixed slot roles ARE the four tones the logo wants, so the only
substitution is slot E's green taking the deck highlight.

THE RANDOM BOOT DECK (KC). The front end inherits the last deck's
palette, and at a cold boot there is no such deck. It ran on the OS's
MODE 1 default -- logical 0 black, logical 1 red -- which INVERTS a fresh
emboss: the shadow strokes came out brighter than the background they sit
under. Seen in jsbeeb. Any deck palette has the relationship the artwork
wants.

TiBootPal (src/title.asm, so in PARTITL) takes the TEXT palette, not the
play one: that is what the game-over path arrives on, since InfoCall runs
SetTextPal before every front-end screen, so boot and the loop back now
agree. It also dodges decks 0, 5 and 9, whose logical 0 IS white and
would swallow the white highlights.

It absorbed main.asm's boot seed -- the deck and the LFSR seed are the
same sample of the same free-running counter. bootPal, an assembled 1 in
main RAM, keeps it to a cold boot; it cannot live in PARTITL, which is
reloaded from disc on every title and would bring it back set. And it
pages bank 4 itself: boot's last act before TitleSeq is UnpackBankIn on
SWRAM_XFER, so SWRAM_DATA is not the resting state on arrival.

Net -4 bytes of main RAM: the code image ends at &2FFA, 6 bytes free, up
from 2. PARTITL spent 32 of its 89. Bank 4 unchanged.

Verified in jsbeeb: cold boot lands on deck 11 (bootPal 0, deck 11,
palette [4,0,5,7]) -- blue ground, white highlights top-left, black
shadows bottom-right, dark panel lettering, magenta blobs, the same
relationships as the C64 reference. NOT yet seen on the game-over path,
where the inherited palette comes from a deck actually played.

events.title: annotate.py: the annotated listing was missing 43% of the original's data
events.message:
annotate.py: the annotated listing was missing 43% of the original's data

Looking up CharColor ($0800) in paradroid_ce_annotated.asm returned 76
bytes. The table is 256, and paradroid_ce.lst has all of it.

get_content split the line on tabs and returned the FIRST non-hex field.
IDA lays a .BYTE operand list out in tab-separated column groups, so
every group but the first was dropped -- and because dropping one shifts
everything after it, the bytes that survived sat at the WRONG OFFSETS.
CharColor[$16] returned a real-looking byte from a different entry rather
than nothing. Truncation announces itself eventually; misalignment does
not, and the annotated listing is what this project reads the C64
original -- its specification -- out of.

Measured by the new tools/verify_annotation.py, which re-extracts every
.BYTE block from both files and diffs them per address:

                                   before    after
  .BYTE bytes in paradroid_ce.lst  49,537   49,537
  present in the annotated copy    21,405   49,420
  blocks truncated                    295        0
  blocks whose values disagree         96        0

Two details each cost a build: DATA_DIRECTIVE_RE needs its \b (a mangled
one compiled to a literal backspace and matched nothing), and the rejoin
must not insert a comma when the directive itself ends a field -- ".BYTE,"
broke the \.BYTE\s extraction and re-truncated eight blocks.

The remaining 117 bytes are zero page, where annotate.py deliberately
emits `name = $XX`: the address survives and the assembled initial value
does not. The tool reports those separately and passes. Read zero-page
initial values from paradroid_ce.lst.

The exporters in tools/ all parse the raw listing, so src/data/ was never
affected -- confirmed, not assumed.

events.title: Merge Layer 14's first pass: the floor dither and the text palettes
events.message:
Merge Layer 14's first pass: the floor dither and the text palettes

The deck floor at half intensity — logical 0 dithered 2x2 with logical 1,
which is black on every deck — because the BBC palette is fully saturated
where the C64's is not. It costs nothing in the main loop: the pattern is
baked into the charset at deck load, from inside BuildCharset's own
character walk, and the parity falls out of the byte index.

It turned out to add a FIFTH TONE to a four-colour mode, and decks 0, 5
and 9 spend it: white dithered to the grey their C64 floor actually is.
That made 'four distinct physical colours' the wrong rule, and both
places that enforced it now test four distinct TONES.

Dithering the static screens' backgrounds was tried and reverted — it
cost the text's readability. They take a solid per-deck background
instead, deckTextPal, which is deckPalette with logical 0 replaced and
sits 64 bytes along so one offset picks between them. The deck plan is
the exception: it is a picture of the deck, so it keeps the deck's own
colours. Every switch runs before the draw it belongs to.

Bank 4 came out of it 22 bytes better off than it went in, then spent
most of that again; main RAM and bank 4 both end at 2 bytes free.

docs/layer-14-visual.md carries the four decisions and the numbers.

events.title: Layer 14: set the palette before the screen, not after it
events.message:
Layer 14: set the palette before the screen, not after it

KC: all four switches ran after their draw, so every screen was painted
in the outgoing palette and only corrected once finished — a visible
wrong-coloured pass on every transition.

Each moved to the routine that DECIDES the transition rather than the one
that completes it: ConMenuInit4 for the console open (and ConsoleEnter
now calls it first), ConMenu4's deck arm for the plan, ConPageKeys4's
leave arm for the way back, and InfoCall before it pages bank 7. The way
back to the deck was already right — RedrawAll sets it before its own
draw.

Three of the four are tail calls on arms that already ended in RTS, so
they cost two bytes each rather than three, and ConMarker4 gave three
back when the call left it.

ConsoleEnter calling ConMenuInit4 first is a reorder of game code, and it
is safe because that routine only writes flags — conSel and the key edges
— which nothing in ConsoleOpen reads; the marker is still drawn after.

SetPalette and SetTextPal now preserve X, because InfoCall calls one
before paging and IsEntry takes its selector in X. SetPalPlay clobbers X
too, so the save outlives it: the routine ends in JSR SetPalPlay and an
RTS rather than the JMP it used to. Five bytes, and it removes the trap
that had already caught this once.

Verified in jsbeeb: the 001 screen is drawn in its text palette from the
first frame. Main RAM and bank 4 are both at 2 bytes free.

KC's hand-picked text-screen backgrounds did not appear in a rebuild,
and the reason was not the reader: build.ps1 does not run export_bbc.py,
so src/data/colours.asm was simply the old one. That is deliberate for
the exporters whose input is the C64 listing — it is supplied locally
rather than checked in — and it is fine for a CODE change. It is a trap
for a DATA one: tools/deck_palettes.json is hand-edited in the lab, and
a build after editing it silently used the old palettes with nothing to
say why.

So compare the two timestamps and throw, naming the command to run. Both
files have to exist for the check to fire, so a tree without the listing
is unaffected until it edits the JSON — at which point stopping is
exactly right, because its build would otherwise be wrong.

events.message:
installer: ask for the engine disk BACK before exiting — the 'ENDIF/ELSE missing' error

A500 field report: at the end of a floppy install the launcher window
showed an Installer-language-looking error ('MISSING END or ELIF') right
where it asked for ECS disk 1 again. The real parser complaining is the
AmigaDOS SHELL: the Workbench  launcher is streamed line by line
FROM the engine floppy, and every line after the Installer/instdisk step
is read after the disk swaps — the CD RAM: fix (ef94721e) cured the
working-directory half but not the script-streaming half. When the
re-read goes wrong the shell loses its IF nesting: 'ENDIF/ELSE missing'.

Fix in both install routes, using each one's own well-tested prompt:
the Installer LISP script ends with an (askdisk) for the engine volume
(OpenUA-AGA / OpenUA-ECS-1), and instdisk's Amiga floppy path prints
'put the engine disk back, press RETURN' before exiting. With the script
disk back in the drive, every remaining launcher line reads cleanly and
the window closes itself.

Ships with the next media build - the 0.9.15 ADFs still carry the old
script.

events.title: engine+ste+ecs: the v0.9.7 title regression — palettes commit before the blits, and a replaced CLUT re-quantises eagerly
events.message:
engine+ste+ecs: the v0.9.7 title regression — palettes commit before the blits, and a replaced CLUT re-quantises eagerly

Field report + archaeology: the titles 'displayed perfectly a few versions
ago'. Verified — v0.9.6's are clean; v0.9.7's are not. 87251793 (v0.9.7)
replaced the port's hand-written intro (which pre-installed each screen's
palette) with the engine's own jt919/l19d4 sequence, whose Mac order is
blit-then-commit. On the Mac that whole body runs inside a frame; the
planar backends stamp the visible planes AS the blit runs (seconds at
8 MHz), so each title rendered quantised under the PREVIOUS screen's
palette — the yellow wizard and candy-striped credits. The DOS original
(DOSBox, 0.35 s sampling) shows every title fully-formed and correct, so
this was never faithful in effect.

Three-part fix, verified frame-by-frame in Hatari (STE, real-time):
- l19d4 commits each picture's palette BEFORE its blits (the Mac's net
  frame; the original tail commits skip via the CLUT-unchanged guard),
  and holds presents across the compose (qd_present_hold).
- st/ecs_clut_major_change(): a wholesale CLUT replacement (>=64 entries
  moved clearly) vetoes the registers-only repalette — the split
  heuristic cannot see 'everything moved' — and re-quantises EAGERLY at
  install time, so draw-time stamps after the commit use the new cut.
  Same total cost: the present's CLUT-unchanged guard then skips the
  re-band this replaces; the walk's CLUT alternation stays on the
  palette cache.
- Chunky backends (Falcon/TT/Nova) get the ordering fix for free: the
  commit-first order removes their draw-vs-install colour flash too.

Wizard + Forgotten Realms + credits now compose and settle in their own
colours; settled frames match v0.9.6's.

events.title: nova: row-diffed present + long writes — the slow card text; name the >8bpp fallback
events.message:
nova: row-diffed present + long writes — the slow card text; name the >8bpp fallback

Field report (Mega STe + ATW800/2): text crawled in Nova mode while
normal ST mode was fine. A full qd_present rewrote all 512,000 card
bytes over the VME bus with per-byte writes, and every glyph update
triggers one. Two-part fix: a shadow of the last-delivered frame makes
the full present write only rows whose bytes changed (compares run in
local RAM, an unchanged screen costs zero bus traffic), and the doubling
loop now emits one aligned LONG per two source pixels instead of four
byte stores — a quarter of the transactions for rows that do write.
novadiff=off in video.cfg restores the old behaviour for A/B.

Also: a card found at 16bpp+ was silently handed back to the ST backend,
reading as a probe failure in the field. Our present writes raw 8-bit
indices, so >8bpp genuinely cannot work — but now DBG.LOG says the card
was FOUND and asks for the desktop to be set to 256 colours.

events.title: engine: the plate cache keys on the label TEXT, not just its pointer — the treasure bar drew POOL over EXIT
events.message:
engine: the plate cache keys on the label TEXT, not just its pointer — the treasure bar drew POOL over EXIT

A1200/ECS real-hardware report: on the treasure screen, SHARE the platinum
then TAKE the ring and the command bar shows POOL where EXIT belongs;
clicking that "POOL" presses (and acts as) EXIT. Reproduced identically on
the Falcon — shared-code, not ECS.

The A/B convicted the command-button plate cache (#138-#141): with
FRUA_NOPLATECACHE the re-laid bar is correct (VIEW POOL EXIT); with the
cache it replays VIEW TAKE POOL. The cache key was (label POINTER, count,
top, left, state) — but a bar re-layout rebuilds its label strings in the
SAME pool slots, so the slot that held "TAKE" now holds "POOL" at the same
address and position, and the stale plate replays. The pressed repaint
misses (state bit differs), which is why the clicked button flashed its
true label — the tell that convicted stale pixels over stale logic.

Fix: a djb2 hash of the label C string (capped at 32 bytes) joins the key;
find and capture both carry it. A reused slot with new text now misses and
repaints; identical text still hits, so the 82->23-tick bar win is intact.
Verified: the exact repro (beginplay -> entry chain -> s,t,t) renders
VIEW POOL EXIT with the cache ON, matching the no-cache control frame.
