events.title: Move the picture 4 rows down the tube
events.message:
Move the picture 4 rows down the tube

The set locks to VSync and counts down from it, so moving VSync EARLIER
in our frame moves the picture DOWN. Nothing else changes: the frame is
still 312 scanlines and the three cycles are untouched, and all that
moves is how the 120 scanlines of blanking are split between the front
porch (picture bottom -> VSync) and the back porch (VSync -> panel top).
It was 80/40 and the picture sat high with the black stacked under it;
it is 48/72 now, both still far beyond PAL's ~5 and ~25.

FRAME_DROP_ROWS is that number in character rows. KC, 2026-08-21: four.
TAIL_R7 becomes 8 - FRAME_DROP_ROWS, so VSync moves from P+272 to P+240.
T1_I1 is derived from the same constant, because the T1 chain is
restarted at VSync and every fire in the frame is measured from it -
shift one without the other and the whole rupture lands 32 scanlines
into the wrong part of the frame.

R7 = 255 had to move from fire 1 to RuptVSync, and this is the part that
was found by building it rather than by reasoning about it. Fire 1 is at
P+44, row 5 of the 7-row panel cycle, so R7 held the tail's value for
the first five rows of every frame - harmless only because that value
was 8, which a 7-row cycle can never reach. At 4 the panel cycle reaches
it at P+32 and fires a VSync of its own, which re-enters RuptVSync
mid-frame, restarts T1 and zeroes ruptState. Fire 1 then never runs, the
play cycle is never set up or unblanked, and the play area is BLACK with
the panel alone on a rolling picture. R7 belongs to the previous cycle,
which for the panel is the tail, and that is where it now is.

The title did NOT move: it runs under SetupMode's ordinary MODE 1 frame,
not the rupture, and matching it is not a matter of dropping its R7 -
that frame has only two rows of blanking between the end of the display
and VSync. It would mean drawing the artwork lower in its own
framebuffer. Recorded in docs/layer-3-scroll.md, not done.

Verified in jsbeeb: boot, the 001 page, gameplay, ESCAPE, the wash and
the game-over seam back to the title. The picture is 32 scanlines lower
and steady, with no roll and nothing lost off either edge.

  asserted from bytes) plus a negative control. rte pops a 6-byte

events.title: Every non-gameplay screen shows all 16 rows
events.message:
Every non-gameplay screen shows all 16 rows

The play area displays sixteen rows and only fifteen are visible: the
sixteenth carries the smooth scroll's sub-row fraction, and the R8 blank
at fire 3 is all that hides it. With the scroll flattened - which every
screen that takes the buffer over does first - that row is real buffer.
The transfer board, the lift's deck select and the deck plan already
showed it, via T1_I3X; the console and its three pages, the four
information screens and the game over's wash now do too. KC, 2026-08-21.

The PORTED pages move down one row onto the C64's own. Its screen area
is rows 9-24 and it puts the database's name line at row 10 and the
content at 12, 14 ... 22 - buffer rows 1 and 3, 5 ... 13. At fifteen
rows the page had to start at row 0 and every line came out one row
high. DB_LINE_ROW0 carries the missing row into dbLineLo/Hi and
DB_IMG_ROW follows it, so the portrait moves with the text; the
information screens and the game-over page ride on the same table. The
console main screen does NOT move - KC's rule is to plot from the top
row, and the top row is still row 0.

Set on entry, restored in ONE place. The four instructions used to be
copied into each screen's exit - three of them in bank 4, which had
three bytes free - and the deck plan's had to be undone by the console's
own the moment the page closed. ReframeView is where every path back to
the deck goes through, so the restore lives there and
ConDeckEnter4/ConDeckExit4 are gone. Bank 4: 3 bytes free -> 60.

Only the high byte is a variable, and structurally so: the two intervals
differ by one character row, a row is 8 scanlines and a scanline is
SL = 64 ticks, so the difference is &200 exactly. t1i3Lo is now a
constant the rupture reads and nobody writes, with an ASSERT to keep it
true. That halved all six sites, which mattered - the main-RAM code
image had FOUR bytes left, not the 47 CLAUDE.md and PLAN.md claimed, and
writing both bytes in ReframeView took it to zero. Both documents' RAM
figures are now measured ones.

ConClear and DbClear grow to PLAY_ROWS: they cleared fifteen because the
last row was never shown, and leaving them would have put a strip of the
deck along the bottom of every console screen. The wash needed no such
change - GoWashRow has always run X = 0-15, because the C64's fills its
whole screen area.

Verified in jsbeeb, not just built: console main, database browser,
stats page, deck plan and the close, reached by walking to a console on
deck 2; and ESCAPE -> explosion -> wash -> 999 page -> title -> new game
-> the 001 page. t1i3Hi reads &1F on every screen and &1D again the
moment ReframeView runs, and the bottom row is clean everywhere.

doc/Debug-version.md documents the lot, and it was already in the tree

events.title: ESCAPE self-destructs and ends the game; DEBUG_RESTART is gone
events.message:
ESCAPE self-destructs and ends the game; DEBUG_RESTART is gone

A way out of a game, and the port's own: the C64 has no equivalent, its
only abort being the RUN/STOP DoPause reads, which pauses. KC asked for
one and it is a game feature, not a debug key.

It kills the player AS A 001, whatever he was riding. CbCheckDeath's
$144D arm already says a captured droid falls back to a 001 and a 001
has nothing to fall back on, so forcing drType to 0 alongside drEnergy
is how "end the game" is spelled in that language - and the explosion,
the sound, the wash, the 999 page and the title all follow with nothing
else added.

It sits BELOW the four modal arms, unlike the R it replaces. R was above
them so a restart could be reached from the console, the lift view or
the transfer; a player-facing quit wants the opposite, because those
states have their own way out and a half-finished transfer applying its
outcome to a player who is already dead is a tangle with no reason to
exist.

ESCAPE is made an ordinary key with OSBYTE 229,1 in GameStartInfo.
Without it the MOS raises an escape CONDITION on the same press, and the
next filing-system call - GoTitle's own *LOADs, on the way out of the
game ESCAPE just ended - fails with Escape.

DEBUG_RESTART is removed entirely: the flag, the key, the loop block,
DEBUG_ANY3 and the !BOOT line, which now reads XFERWIN DECK. ESCAPE
tests Layer 11a's boot split better than R did, because it reaches
GameStart the long way round rather than jumping to it.

Verified in jsbeeb: press, explosion, wash, the 999 page, the title -
and the title's loads run clean, which is the OSBYTE working.

events.title: NuLA: a plan for the VideoNuLA build, as a separate deliverable
events.message:
NuLA: a plan for the VideoNuLA build, as a separate deliverable

Scroll and colour are the two the hardware fixes: control code 2 makes
the horizontal step 1 px instead of 4, which is the whole reason
CAM_TOPSPD is 8 rather than the C64's 7, and the 4096-colour palette
removes the nearest-BBC-hue approximation while leaving the four-colour
merge exactly where it is. Both land in the display path — the buffer,
the blitter and the tile data are untouched.

Costed against the port as it stands: the colour path comes out SMALLER
and faster than the &FE21 machinery it replaces (logical palette mode,
8 writes a swap instead of 16), and pays for the two zero-page bytes the
scroll offset needs. Attribute mode is parked, with reasons.

Verified rather than recalled: b2 implements the full register set
(m_scroll_offset, m_blanking_counter, m_direct_palette, the attribute
emitters), b-em likewise, and jsbeeb parses every control code and
renders only the palette — so the MCP cannot see the headline feature.
b2's HTTP API was driven end to end: peek returns &1100 byte-identical
to PARA on the disc, poke round-trips into RAM, poke does NOT reach the
I/O bus on the build to hand.

Nothing is built. Ships as a second executable on the same disc (10 of
31 catalogue slots used, 40K of 200K), chosen by KC's runtime detection.

events.title: Note for later: time the rupture switch so the TV keeps its lock
events.message:
Note for later: time the rupture switch so the TV keeps its lock

SetupRupture rewrites R4, R5, R6 and R7 from SetupMode's plain 39-row
frame to the three-cycle shape wherever the CPU happens to be, and a
television needs several fields to pull vertical sync back - so the way
into a game, and the way back after a game over, rolls for a moment.

Recorded as an open item in PLAN.md and, with the constraints it has to
respect, in docs/layer-3-scroll.md: switch on a field boundary rather
than mid-frame, order the writes so every intermediate state is still a
legal 312-line frame, and/or blank across the change. R6/R7/R12/R13
belong to the cycle before they fire, R5 must stay away from a cycle
boundary, and R7 must not sit at TAIL_R7 during a filing-system call.

Nothing measured yet; it wants the emulator and then real hardware,
since a TV's tolerance is what is being tuned.

events.title: Layer 11d: blank the strip before the rupture can show the title
events.message:
Layer 11d: blank the strip before the rupture can show the title

The title's framebuffer is &4000-&7E7F and the play buffer sits inside
it. TitleSeq rebuilds the panel and the &5400 tables over their share of
that ground, but nothing owns &5800-&7FFF until something draws there -
and now that the 001 screen holds LoadDeck's redraw back, that is not
until the page is printed. In between, SetupRupture starts displaying
the strip, and what it displayed was the title, smeared.

So TitleSeq blanks it on the way past, immediately before SetupRupture
and after PageLowIn. It is DbClear through a third IsEntry door, because
DbClear is already exactly this and there is no room in main RAM for a
second clear; the page calls it again a moment later, which costs 60,000
cycles once.

IsBlank sets infoAct to $FF as well. lowbss is SKIPped rather than
loaded, so at this point in the boot that byte has never been written,
and a garbage 0 would send InfoCall's continuation into ReframeView
before there is a deck to draw.

Verified from a cold boot: black behind the panel, then the page, then
the deck when the page is dismissed.

events.title: Layer 11e: the transfer time-up posts ONCE, and fades - $20DA exactly
events.message:
Layer 11e: the transfer time-up posts ONCE, and fades - $20DA exactly

KC nailed it from the sound alone: the C64 time-up fades out where
ours held. The listing agrees - xferDoCounter ($20DA) exits early when
the count is ALREADY zero ($20E0 BEQ), so the $1B post at $2104 fires
exactly once, on the tick the countdown reaches zero. One zipper
instance, 16 gated ticks, then a ~3 s release fade while it keeps
descending: went-on-for-a-long-time WITH the volume fade, precisely.

Stage 3 had restructured the routine with the post in the already-zero
arm - reposting every other pass at full volume: no fade, and the wrap
screaming. The previous commit's alarm substitution treated the
symptom; this restores the C64's own control flow, post included, and
reverts the alarm.

Also captured the transfer-entry pair against theory: both zips hit
the chip tick-for-tick on the C64 arithmetic (fx $1B 3676 down to 244
Hz, fx 9 3571 down to 197, detuned as designed), so the entry-pitch
question is timbre or memory, not data - awaiting KC's A/B against the
real thing.

events.title: Layer 11e: the transfer time-up stops screaming
events.message:
Layer 11e: the transfer time-up stops screaming

KC found the game-completion sound a bit intense, and the diagnosis is
a genuine cadence deviation: the C64 re-posts fx $1B every 50 Hz
frame, restarting the zipper every tick and PINNING it to its
first-tick frequency - a steady ~240 Hz urgent drone. Our repost runs
at pass rate, every 4 ticks, which lets the zipper wrap mod 65536 and
puts a 3.6 kHz scream tick in every fragment.

A 50 Hz sequencer cannot be pinned from 25 Hz code, and fx $1B data is
untouchable (its full zipper is the transfer-entry siren, signed off),
so the time-up posts fx 8 - the alarm - which at this cadence plays as
a near-steady ~490 Hz warble: the C64 character, an octave up. Zero
bytes, bank 7. An exact-240 Hz custom record is the 11-byte
alternative, noted in the source.

events.title: Layer 11e: effect end is a cut, not a tail - as ResetVoice has it
events.message:
Layer 11e: effect end is a cut, not a tail - as ResetVoice has it

The held note after the explosion was the release draining past the
sequencer end with the frequency frozen - a 0.6 s constant-pitch fade
the C64 never plays. ResetVoice ($0678) writes the TEST bit then a
control byte of zero: NO waveform selected, an instant cut the moment
an effect ends. The port now matches: effect end zeroes the level with
no envelope step on the way out, and idle voices run nothing at all.
The only release that sounds is a mid-effect gate expiry - which is
the C64 semantics exactly, and is what shapes the explosion: the fade
runs THROUGH the sweep, then chops dead on the final tick.

Byte-neutral (bank 4 stays at 0 free). Captured in jsbeeb: CH3 fades
0 through 8 across the sweep and ends on a single atten=15 write at
tick 40, with nothing after it.

Layer 11e: an unowned noise channel is silenced

The droid explosion tail was fading correctly - the capture showed its
release stepping through attenuation 7..12 - until the deck hum, which
shares voice 2, re-posted: a tone effect taking over the owner voice
releases noise ownership, and with no owner nothing ever wrote channel

events.title: Layer 11e: the sub-floor mute is the volume, not the period
events.message:
Layer 11e: the sub-floor mute is the volume, not the period

KC heard a click at the hum start on two accurate emulators. The wiki
sn76489 page explains it in its sample-playback section: every
attenuation setting shifts the chip output DC offset, and that offset
IS how PCM playback works on this chip - so writing N=1 (ultrasonic,
tonally silent) while the envelope stepped the volume was a one-sample
PCM pop. A mute on this chip must hold the VOLUME at 15.

SndConv now returns the mute in carry (set = sub-floor on a
MUTE_SUBFLOOR instrument; no period produced at all) and the flush
routes BCS into its existing silent-voice path - attenuation 15,
period untouched. Unmuting writes the period before the volume, so the
tone re-enters cleanly. Captured: the hum cycle is now sweep, one
atten=15 at the reset tick, period-then-atten=10 on the way back, and
the muted opening writes nothing whatever - no DC step exists to hear.
Bank 4: 1 byte free.

events.title: Layer 11e: the hum stays a tone; its sub-floor mutes to N=1 instead
events.message:
Layer 11e: the hum stays a tone; its sub-floor mutes to N=1 instead

KC reverted the periodic-noise hum - the tone version was right, only
the opening drone was wrong. The wiki sn76489 page supplied the proper
tool: period 1 is a 125 kHz square, out of audible range and stripped
by the LM324N, so a MUTE_SUBFLOOR instrument flag (bit 6) sends the
hum instrument sub-floor clamps to N=1 instead of the audible N=1023.
The hum now fades in as its sweep crosses the floor, with a one-tick
articulation gap at each segment reset - no drone. Effects that live
entirely below the floor (the disruptor) keep the 1023 buzz: the flag
would silence them outright. Never period 0 - undocumented on this
chip. The periodic-noise machinery stays in history (dd108a2) for
stage 4.

Planning the fix surfaced a real driver bug: SndConv counted its
shifts in X, and the flush picks the write channel from X after
converting, so every IN-RANGE voice-1 tone effect had been landing on
channel 0. The hum escaped only because its clamped path skips the
shift loops. Counters moved to snTm2; the capture now shows the hum
cycle (N 940 down to 569, one N=1 mute tick, repeat) entirely on
channel 1. Paid for by collapsing the SndTick init head to its one
surviving state value and merging the clamp/mute exit - bank 4 back
to 3 bytes free.

the control byte from them - a change that made the driver smaller,
which mattered at 3 bytes free. A periodic fundamental of tone/15 sits
within 6% of the white-noise scale, so one conversion path serves both.

clocked), tone 2 sweeping periods 30-75 through the hum cycle, CH3 at
the hum sustain attenuation, no 1023 clamp anywhere. The other five

events.message:
Layer 11e stage 2: the SN76489 driver, alive in the IRQ

src/sound.asm (1,018 B, bank 4): a transliteration of the C64 Sound
($0500) game-FX path - request pickup with the disruptor priority bit,
the mod-65536 slide sequencer with bounce and reset segments, a linear
ADSR envelope stepped at 50 Hz, latest-wins noise ownership, and a
diffed chip flush over the stage-0 write primitive with DDRA/ORA saved
once per burst. IrqHandler pages bank 4 in around SndTick via ROMSHAD
and restores what it found - the one sanctioned breach of the bank
rule, recorded in CLAUDE.md. Requests are four main-RAM bytes so every
bank can trigger a sound with a plain STA.

The 629 bytes bank 4 was short came from three places, KC choosing the
first: chardata bitmaps now ship ZX0-packed (1,096 -> 640, unpacked
into the idle sprite save areas at deck load, an 8-byte lampSrc cache
serving the alert lamp live re-colours; charRemap leads the file so its
ALIGN is free), the never-used chain byte and the three deferred
chatter records are gone, and the frequency table halved to 64 midpoint
entries. Bank 4 ends &BFB2 - 78 free - and the build prints the gauge.

Verified in jsbeeb: title, first deck and a DEBUG_DECK hop all render
from the packed charset; effect $12 poked into sndFx1 plays the droid
explosion exactly as the data says (N 263 sweeping to 487, 8-tick gate,
4-per-tick release). One bug found by the first capture and fixed: the
sub-2048 clamp shortcut flattened noise voices; they now pre-scale x16
saturating. Tick costs measured over the shim: 475 idle, 1,161 active,
2,425 on the start tick - all inside the 10,700-cycle VSync gap.

events.title: Layer 11e stage 1: export_sound.py, and the wrap discovery
events.message:
Layer 11e stage 1: export_sound.py, and the wrap discovery

The exporter reads the $C610 effect records and $EAA0 instruments out of
paradroid_ce.lst (hard-failing on unfilled ranges), and emits 700 B of
generated data: 31 records at 12 bytes, 12 instruments converted from SID
ADSR to 50 Hz envelope steps, and a 128-entry frequency-to-period table.
tools/output/sound_dump.txt simulates each effect's actual trajectory for
review.

The simulation changed the design: slides run mod 65536 and the zipper
effects (fx5 wraps 39 times, fx9 every 8 ticks) depend on the wrap, so
records stay in SID-frequency space VERBATIM minus the pulse bytes and
the driver converts at chip-write time through the table - more faithful
than the planned period-space fit, at the cost of 256 B and ~60 cycles.

Also out of the dump: the per-deck hum survives (7% sub-floor), but six
tone effects - the disruptor at 100% - sit below the SN tone floor and
are stage 4's review list. Bank 4 is now estimated 150-300 B over; the

events.title: Pack the deck maps with ZX0, and retire the level RLE entirely
events.message:
Pack the deck maps with ZX0, and retire the level RLE entirely

Layer 13d, task 4, approved by KC. Rather than compressing the C64's
RLE streams, export_bbc.py now decodes each deck offline — BuildLevel's
exact old semantics, including decks 1 and 2 legitimately running past
their stream into the next deck's data — and ZX0-compresses the decoded
1,024-byte maps. That compresses better than RLE-then-LZ, needs no
scratch anywhere (Zx0Unpack writes straight into the tile map), and
deletes the RLE format from the port: BuildLevel is pointer setup plus
a tail call, and the console's deck plan walks the tile map in place —
main RAM, static after BuildLevel, readable from bank 7 — instead of
decoding a 512-byte staged copy, so ConDeckEnter4 keeps only its t1i3
work. The decoded maps are byte-identical to the C64's; only the
packaging changed.

tools/zx0.py is a line-for-line Python port of Einar Saukas' reference
compressor (BSD-3, github.com/einar-saukas/ZX0) in its default mode —
forwards, interlaced Elias gamma, inverted new-offset-MSB — with its
own decompressor, and every emitted stream round-trips at export time.
src/zx0depack.asm is the 6502 side, written from the reference
compressor's source rather than a recalled depacker.

leveldata's 3,503 bytes become deckPack's 2,183 plus ~230 of depacker:
bank 4 goes from 12 bytes free to 1,161 — the resting-state bank, where
every future gameplay byte has to live.

Verified in jsbeeb: all 16 decks unpacked through a BuildLevel
trampoline and diffed against the offline decode — 16 x 1,024 bytes,
zero mismatches — plus a normal boot playing on its decompressed deck.
The deck plan page still wants an in-game play-check.

Layer 13d, task 3, reversing layer-11's [DECISION 3] with KC: the
48 x 84 portrait IS ported, because the costing that deferred it was
wrong on both ends. Only the LEFT column of BuildIntroSprites' 2 x 4
sprite grid is stored (the right is MirrorSprite's at runtime, ours as
theirs), the 24 records share their images, and the unique pool is 63
sprites = 4,032 bytes of the C64's own data — not 6 K, and never 24 K,
because a multicolour pair is exactly two MODE 1 pixels and PoDraw
expands at draw time the way FontCell expands the font.

multicolour->MODE 1 tables into bank 7; portrait.asm composes them —

the C64's sprite X=40/Y=144 translated: buffer rows 2-12, units 4-15.
The rotor-and-digits stand-in and droidicon7.asm are deleted; DbImage
is now a guard (repaint only when the type or a clear demands it) in
front of PoDraw.

events.title: Give the title back to the disc, and let a game over reach it
events.message:
Give the title back to the disc, and let a game over reach it

Layer 13d, task 1. The title screen leaves bank 7 and becomes the
PARTITL disc overlay again — [DECISION 6] of layer-11 restored —
assembled at &3000 over PARAFNT's ground and loaded by TitleSeq, which
boot and the new game-over seam now share: load the title, show it,
reload PARAFNT and PARALOW over it, rebuild everything the title's
framebuffer sat on, raise the rupture, take the IRQ back.

GoTick7 ends a game with GoTitle instead of JMP GameStart:
UninstallIrq, SetupMode, RestoreDfsWs, TitleSeq, GameStart. Two things
made that survivable, both measured in jsbeeb rather than recalled:

- InstallIrq now saves the MOS's System VIA IER, ACR and T1 latches
  before clobbering them, and UninstallIrq hands them back — the
  rupture rewrites the latches every field and the MOS's 100 Hz events
  (keyboard scan, clock, disc timeouts) run off what it left there.

- The low overlay buries DFS's workspace at &0E00-&10FF AND the MOS's
  extended vector table at &0D9F (under lowcode2) — the route DFS 1.2's
  FILEV takes into its ROM — so any filing call after PageLowIn jumps
  through game code and dies; *DISC does not recover it. SaveDfsWs
  snapshots both spans (912 B) into bank 6 right before PageLowIn, and
  GoTitle restores them byte for byte before its loads.

The snapshot lives in bank 6, NOT bank 5 as the session plan first
said: the approved "sideview to bank 5" move turned out unbuildable
(sideview.asm is the lift screen's data, read by bank-7 code through
xfer.asm's shared machinery), so the same bank-7 bytes were freed by
rehoming the snapshot instead, leaving bank 5 whole for the flicker.

Verified in jsbeeb over two consecutive game overs: boot -> title ->
game -> death as a 001 -> wash -> title -> fire -> new game.

events.title: amiga/ecs: never paint a screen the palette cannot show (the boot's garbage frames)
events.message:
amiga/ecs: never paint a screen the palette cannot show (the boot's garbage frames)

The user watched the ECS boot on a real desktop: the title sequence rendered as
black with one garbled strip for over a minute. Traced (FRUA_ECSTRACE, new): the
title sequence draws each screen's art and PRESENTS before installing its
palette, so the incremental present converts the new art through the PREVIOUS
screen's bands -- wrong-palette garbage, held on screen for the full length of
the following re-band, twice per title screen.

The backend already detects exactly this condition -- e_new_ink >= 4 schedules a
re-quant -- but only after painting the garbage. Now the incremental branch
pre-scans the announced rows first, and at >= 8 pixels of ink the current bands
cannot show it HOLDS: keeps the announcements pending, shows the last complete
frame, and lets the palette install that follows take the full-render path with
the real palette. The garbage is never painted.

  ! RENDERING IMMEDIATELY IS ALSO WRONG, and it was tried first: re-band and
    render in this present, so nothing depends on a follow-up present ever
    coming. Measured on the boot: the re-quant runs against the CLUT AS IT
    STANDS, which is exactly what is stale -- it painted the whole SSI screen in
    well-quantised garbage and added a 9.5 s re-band per title. No quantiser can
    fix indices whose CLUT entries have not arrived.

  ! ONE HOLD, NEVER TWO. The legitimate new-ink case -- art whose CLUT entries
    are fine but missed the last quant (an event portrait) -- must still paint.
    A second consecutive present with no palette change paints via the bucket
    fallback exactly as before, one modal-loop pass later. A full render also
    clears the hold, so nothing can stick.

A/B on ONE binary (video.cfg inkhold=off; the Amiga side never had a video.cfg
reader, so this adds the ST/Nova contract to ecs_init):
    on:  40 frames -- black, SSI correct, MICRO MAGIC silver (bucket fallback,
         by design), gold on its install. No garbage frame.
    off: config line confirmed, zero holds -- SSI in blue/black wrong-palette
         garbage for ~20 s, a red-striped second flavour after the next draw.
         The user's symptom, reproduced on demand.

Also: FRUA_ECSTRACE (present/flip/render tracing behind FRUA_AMIGAPROF, with an
#error guard for the missing dependency), and the profiler dump now fires on
FULL presents too. Note for anyone reading the traces: the rl clock starts when
the VBL server installs, LATE in the AmigaOS boot, so rl timestamps sit ~60-90 s
behind capture wall time.

All five configs build; 471 passed, 6 skipped.

events.title: quantize: the nearest-remap's multiplies cost the ECS boot 35 seconds — b7d628ba was priced on one backend
events.message:
quantize: the nearest-remap's multiplies cost the ECS boot 35 seconds — b7d628ba was priced on one backend

The user booted the ECS build on a real desktop and saw the title sequence as a
single bar with a smear for over a minute. Frame-by-frame capture confirmed it:
~70 seconds of one strip of the SSI screen on black, then everything at once.

Attribution (new apecs timers): 8 full presents in the boot at ~12.2 s each,
86% of it ecs_reband -- 16.8 s per re-band, five of them. Three theories fell
before the right one: unannounced dirty rows (the DIRTYCHECK police reads 0),
per-row conversion cost (that number divided whole-screen render time by an
incremental row counter), and then the real thing:

b7d628ba put the nearest-colour remap into quantize.h scoring candidates with
2L*dr*dr + 5L*dg*dg + 1L*db*db -- three 32-bit multiplies, which a plain 68000
turns into ~200-cycle __mulsi3 calls. The header is SHARED, and it was priced
on the ST, where #139 had already collapsed 25 band cuts to 1-3 group cuts:
+2.9%, measured, honest -- for the ST. The Amiga ECS still cuts all 25 BANDS,
so the same change cost it twenty-five-fold. The build sweep compiled the Amiga
targets all along; compiling is not pricing.

The same expression sits in TWO loops: the present-colour remap and the
absent-colour 4x8x4 bucket table (128 buckets x ntot per band -- the bigger
one; fixing the remap alone bought 5%). A 512-byte square table makes both
shifts and adds. The VALUE is identical, so palettes, remaps and every rendered
frame are bit-for-bit unchanged -- verified on 11 captured title/menu frames
(qband output identical before and after).

Measured on the ECS boot, same drive: re-band 16.8 s -> 9.5 s (-44%), full
presents 97.9 s -> 62.4 s (-36%).

Also in this commit:
 - QUANT_PROF: opt-in phase timers in quant_banded (zero-cost when off).
   Host attribution (qprof, sum-check 97%): buckets 40.8%, cut 29.8%,
   remap 12.8%, keep 9.4%, hist 4.2%. No single free win remains; the rest
   of the 9.5 s is inherent per-band work, and reducing it is the measured
   group-count trade-off (qband: N=5 keeps 65-87% of per-band fidelity at
   1/5 the cuts, but 4 of 11 title screens genuinely need per-band cuts).
 - apecs timers for reband/remap/c2p, the quant phase dump, and the dump now
   fires on FULL presents too -- it hung off the rect path alone, and a boot
   issues no rect presents, so three successive runs printed nothing while
   the counters incremented.
 - tools/quant/qband (per-band vs one-cut error + band divergence) and
   qprof (host phase attribution with the sum check).

★ Traps paid for here, recorded in the comments: a timer bracket must close on
exactly the paths its open ran on (two bugs: a close outside its open's branch
added the absolute clock per skipped band; a close 90 lines BEFORE its open);
and validate the instrument where iteration is cheap -- two emulator runs at
five minutes each went to bracket bugs the host reproduces in one second.

docs: the ECS row of the #148 audit is code-derived — six live attempts never reached the walk

Recording this as unverified rather than letting the code argument pass as an
observation. Six attempts to drive the ECS build to a dungeon walk in amiberry all

    from the host for "menu: modal up" reports "not yet" long after the menu is up.

    park the drive on ADD A CHARACTER with the party half-seated.
  - amiberry drops keystrokes: attempt 5 reached the hall, attempt 6 with the same
    script lost the Escape and four `b` retries went nowhere.

events.title: docs: audit the other backends for #61's hazard — the ST was the only one exposed
events.message:
docs: audit the other backends for #61's hazard — the ST was the only one exposed

The shape is not "does it have a viewport" but "is anything written to the display
whose content is NOT in the shared chunky surface", because then any copy from the
draw-time plane buffer erases it.

Checked all six. The TT's t_dt and its c2p both derive from g_chunky; ECS and AGA
draw a SOFTWARE cursor that the shim composites into the chunky surface (#64 retired
AGA's sprite cursor, so plat_cursor_active() returns 0 there too); the Falcon is
chunky-native; ST-High and Nova register no draw-time target at all. Only the ST
renders anything into a separate buffer, and dsp_viewport_scratch is registered by
exactly one backend.

That is structural, not luck: ADR-0016's writers stamp planes AND record the chunky
index, so s_chunky stays the source of truth and the plane buffer is a cache that can
always be rebuilt from it. The ST viewport is the sole exception.

Also records that the ST's own coverage is complete -- both incremental arms (BLiTTER
and CPU memcpy) share the hook because it sits before the s_use_blt branch, and the
force-full was already covered by #61 -- and the one piece of deliberate slack:
st_vp_touched tests rows only, so a rect present entirely right of the viewport
re-arms a repaint it does not need. That is 5-7 composites per ~1500 presents, i.e.
optimising 0.09%, and the s_dt paths rebuild whole rows where a column test would
always be true anyway.

events.title: platform: repaint the viewport after a copy that crossed its rows (ST/STE, #148)
events.message:
platform: repaint the viewport after a copy that crossed its rows (ST/STE, #148)

The ST/STE lost the BOTTOM NINE ROWS of the first-person view -- game rows
103..111 came out fully black, the floor's nearest band simply missing -- while
the Falcon rendered the identical frame, same cell and same in-game minute,
complete. It shipped, and it was in every affected walk frame.

The viewport deliberately does not live in s_chunky (ADR-0016 B2): that is what
keeps the roster and chrome on its scanlines static so the row-diff can skip
them. So s_chunky's viewport hole is BLACK -- measured, 0 of 88 columns non-zero
against 88 of 88 in the scratch -- and s_dt, built from s_chunky, carries the
hole too. st_dt_present_full then copies runs of rows from s_dt into the pages,
erasing the viewport's share of every row it touches. A row is only rebuilt when
it CHANGES, which is why the damage is a band and not the whole pane: rows
24..102 are static chrome beside a constant hole, while the compass and the
coordinate/clock box sit at rows ~103..125 and the clock ticks. It stops at 111
because rows 112+ have no viewport to erase.

★ #61 ALREADY FOUND THIS AND FIXED HALF OF IT. Its comment sits in the
force-full branch of the same function -- "this just rewrote BOTH pages from
s_dt, which does not carry the composited viewport (the composite writes the
PAGE, not s_dt). Both pages owe it again." The incremental run copy, which is
the walk's common path, never got the same treatment. This is that treatment.

st_vp_touched() re-arms s_vp_owe when a written span crosses the viewport's
rows, so the st_vp_composite() that already follows every present repaints
instead of returning early. s_vp_have, not s_vp_active: the scratch and the
stamped planes both persist after the commit is consumed, which is what makes
the repaint possible.

★ THE HOOK GOES ON THE COPY, NOT THE BUILD. Hooking st_dt_build_row was tried
first and left one of three drives still showing the band: s_dt PERSISTS with
the hole in it, so a row built once can be re-copied on any later present with
no build to notice. The copy is the event that damages the page.

★ AND AN EARLIER ATTEMPT HOOKED st_blit_rows ALONE AND MEASURED NO EFFECT,
which read as a refutation and was not: CPU68K=68000 implies FRUA_PLANAR, so the
ST's full present goes through st_dt_present_full and never calls st_blit_rows.
The hook was on a path the walk does not take. Both writers are covered now.

ST/STE ONLY: display_ste.c is the sole backend that calls
planar_viewport_register, so every other target (Falcon, TT, Amiga AGA/ECS,
Nova) renders the view straight into the shared surface and has no separate
buffer for a copy to erase. No Amiga counterpart is needed.

A/B on ONE binary, video.cfg `vprepair=off` restoring the shipped behaviour,
three drives per arm at staggered key counts:

events.title: docs: #148 — nine black rows in the ST's 3D view, and the twelve instruments that missed it
events.message:
docs: #148 — nine black rows in the ST's 3D view, and the twelve instruments that missed it

Found by the user in a screenshot taken during the #139 A/B. Game rows 103..111 of
the viewport are fully black on the ST/STE; the Falcon renders the identical frame
-- same cell, same in-game minute, checked at a legible crop -- complete. It ships,
and it is in every affected walk frame.

The cause is still OPEN. This section is mostly about instrument design, because
that is where the cost was: twelve experiments, each individually reasonable, most
of them measuring something other than what I thought.

Eliminated, each by a live A/B: the draw-time viewport writer (vpplanar=off
reproduces), the whole ADR-0016 writer half (PLANAR=0 reproduces), the raster split
(vpbands=off reproduces -- and that arm has ONE palette frame-wide), the engine's
pane placement (Falcon shares it and is clean), the engine's render into the scratch
(poisoning the buffer shows 0 unwritten rows of 88), the composite (a self-triggering
scan on both present hooks never sees a blank row), and a blit clobbering viewport
rows (re-arming s_vp_owe in st_blit_rows changes nothing).

Six stages measure healthy and the output is still wrong, so one of them answers a
question nobody asked. Two live leads are recorded: the composite's own stamp does
not survive to the screen (slot 15 forced across the whole rect in every page leaves
no trace), and the ST/Falcon fork at dsp_viewport_scratch() -- NULL on the Falcon, so
the engine renders straight into the chunky surface, while planar_viewport_register()
runs unconditionally in st_init so NEITHER vpplanar=off NOR PLANAR=0 crosses it.
Every elimination above stayed on the same side of that fork.

The traps are the point, and all were paid for:
  - st_present is the FULL present; the walk presents by RECT.
  - st_present_rect's B2.2 fast path returns early for a rect inside the viewport --
    the walk's own present -- so a hook at that function's tail is DEAD CODE there.
    Measured: 0 calls.
  - st_vp_composite fires ~once per walk STEP, not per present; a probe gated on
    composite #400 never fires.
  - "are the planes zero" is the WRONG QUESTION -- they always hold real non-zero
    slots on the black rows. Five probes tested it and all reported healthy.
  - the defect is VIEW-dependent (cell 12,5), so a fixed-count trigger samples
    whichever frame is up; self-trigger, and require a PARTIAL band or a one-shot
    latches on the legitimate before-the-first-composite state.
  - a QDUMP capture cannot tell a drawn row from a stale one.
  - silence and a reading of zero are identical in DBG.LOG -- print the call count.
  - verify the screenshot geometry: the image is at (96,58), not (0,0).

events.title: Add live screen viewer (VS Code webview + streaming port) and a Manic Miner example
events.message:
Add live screen viewer (VS Code webview + streaming port) and a Manic Miner example

zxspectrum/server/screen_stream.py is a third independent asyncio TCP
server, structurally identical to dap.py's: it pushes the live display as
length-prefixed PNG frames to any connected client (10fps), no different
in kind from DAP/MCP and with no VS-Code-specific code in it. Frames are
read via engine.machine.render_screen() directly rather than through the
engine's command queue -- a run() in progress occupies the actor loop for
its entire duration, so a queued read sat unserved (and the live view
visibly froze) until it stopped; this bypass is the same pattern dap.py's
_read_memory_sync already uses for exactly this reason.

vscode-extension/ moves the project's debugger-type registration in-repo
and adds real code for the first time: extension.js bridges the raw
stream into a webview panel (a webview can't open a raw socket itself),
auto-opens on debug session start, and auto-reconnects if the server
restarts.

core/snapshot.py gains write_sna(), the field-for-field inverse of the
existing parse_sna(), needed to package scripts/build_manicminer.py's
output (SkoolKit's Manic Miner disassembly, assembled with sjasmplus) into
a loadable .sna. Verified live end to end, including sending real
keypresses over MCP to get from the title screen into gameplay. Given the
same copyright treatment as the ROM: game_disassembly/ and
.manicminer-disassembly-src/ are gitignored, only the build script is

events.title: Give the drawing its window back, and let the split survive scrolling
events.message:
Give the drawing its window back, and let the split survive scrolling

KC reported the flicker back, worst on the enemy droids, and suspected
the collision work and the animated tiles had eaten the budget. Both
halves were right. Measured with a zero-byte harness -- breakpoints on
the JSR sites plus elapsed_cycles -- because DEBUG_TIME did not build.

On the LIGHTEST pass the game can have (one sprite, no level draw) the
sprite draw already finished 1,572 cycles past the 24,576-cycle window,
and 16,888 of that window went on work that writes no pixels. AnimTick
alone was 10,060 and found nothing. Every further sprite is +5,182, and
enemy droids are drawn after the player, so they are the ones still
missing when the beam arrives.

PHASE 1 -- empty the window of work that draws nothing.
AnimScan and AnimLamp move below the draw and fill the list for the NEXT
pass; AnimTick keeps only the charset rotation, 10,060 -> 1,558. Same
one-pass pipeline the droid AI took. DoScore and CbDisruptor move to
ml_afterdraw, immediately above ml_passend -- the one point every arm of
the pass converges on -- so they still run with a modal state up, which
is what put them at the top of the pass in the first place.

PHASE 2 -- the split is what prevents flicker, and it was refused on
every pass the player moves. The global vetoes are replaced by a local
test: each writer is one-dimensional (a band is full width, a column
full height, a door and an animated tile are single tiles), so any
overlap component holding a sprite under one of them is FORCED into
tranche A, the tranche already erased while the level draw runs. Spans
are padded by eight, a pass's scroll, because a tranche-B sprite's saved
background was taken last pass. DoRedraws is no longer skipped on a
split pass -- it had to be unskipped, or the deck stops scrolling.

The decision outgrew the eleven bytes the code image had left, so it is
src/sprsplit.asm in BANK 6 behind a bridge on PanelTick's pattern. Every
byte it reads is outside bank 4. The code image goes 11 free -> 323, and
DEBUG_RASTER, DEBUG_DRAW and DEBUG_TIME assemble again; RASTER has been
run and draws its bands correctly.

Measured scrolling diagonally with a 302 on screen: tranche A finishes
2,959 cycles inside the window and sprTr puts the player in A and the
droid in B. Buffer oracle against RedrawAll: 0 of 10,240.

Two instrument fixes came out of it. DEBUG_DECK puts the cursor deck hop
behind a flag. And DEBUG_DRAW's magenta band had no close after the draw
-- it ran on through the droid AI, the panel and the WaitWindowB idle,
reporting 20,000 cycles of display work as sprite work and reaching into
the play area on every pass. It broke when Step 1 moved DroidsUpdate
below the draw. Magenta now ends at the draw and the display-period work
has a red band of its own.

events.title: platform: reuse a palette already cut for this CLUT (ST/STE, #139)
events.message:
platform: reuse a palette already cut for this CLUT (ST/STE, #139)

"Pin the palette" turns out to mean CACHE it, because the walk is not one scene
whose palette drifts -- it is a handful of scenes alternating.

A 300-key HEIRS drive: 14,336 presents, 85 re-bands, of which the new-ink
overflow path accounts for 11. The other 74 are qd_set_palette. The #142 comment
in this file asserted the opposite ("s_dirty is never set that way during it"),
which is why the task had been aimed at INK_MAX; that comment is corrected here
rather than left to mislead the next reader. Across the 76 play-phase re-bands
there are 18 distinct CLUTs and 58 land on one already cut. The backend does
remember a CLUT -- s_clut_banded -- but it remembers exactly ONE, and one is the
wrong number for an alternation. Measured LRU hit rate by size:

    1: 0%   2: 2%   3: 2%   4: 53%   6: 65%   8: 73%   13: 76%

Nothing until four, because the cycle is walk -> cleared viewport -> walk ->
event picture. ST_PCACHE is 8: two thirds of the ceiling for ~20 KB.

Fidelity, priced offline over the 58 repeats (tools/quant/qpin): viewport +7.9%,
everything outside it -3.7% -- a fresh cut on a frame whose viewport just filled
with a portrait re-partitions the roster panel too, and a cached cut does not.
On screen, an A/B on one binary differs in game rows 24..111 and NOWHERE else:
0 of 7,680 pixels above the viewport band, 0 of 28,160 below, all of it speckle
across textured granite. The roster text's histogram is identical across arms.

Time, one binary, video.cfg palcache=off selecting the arm, RNG pinned, 150 keys:

    in-present   56,893 -> 63,033 t200      band branch  16,455 -> 20,636
    the cut alone 3,156 -> 6,768 (-54%)     slot align      328 -> 329 (control)

  ! QUOTE -6.6%, NOT -11.1%. The band branch is the only part the cache touches
    and it is 4,181 of the 6,140 saved; the rest is run-to-run variation (54 vs
    57 re-bands, 2176 vs 2144 presents -- key injection against emulator
    wall-clock is not deterministic even with the seed pinned).

  ! AND THE FORCE-FULL SURVIVES. The hope was that a restored palette would be
    likelier to clear st_align_group with no USED index moving slot, skipping the
    whole-frame rebuild. It is not: FORCE-FULL moved -5.2% and no-skew fired 0
    times against 1. Coming back to CLUT A after a re-band on CLUT B, the
    alignment permutes A's palette to match B's numbering, so A's used indices
    land where they were only by luck. At 14,480 t200 the rebuild is still ~23%
    of in-present on the walk, and nothing here touches it.

Also recorded: 40% of the walk's re-bands quantise a BLACK viewport (the engine
clears, presents, then draws; reband-on-stale is 0, so this is not the
lazy-chunky hazard), and keying the cache on the used subset of the CLUT instead
of all 768 bytes buys nothing -- 18 classes either way, so #139's q12/q13
anecdote does not generalise.

All five configs build; 471 passed, 6 skipped.

events.title: tools/quant: price a pinned palette, and drive a walk long enough to price it
events.message:
tools/quant: price a pinned palette, and drive a walk long enough to price it

#139's next step was blocked on data: only 2 of the 14 QDUMP captures were
dungeon walks, and they were near-identical, so "one fixed palette across many
walk screens" could not be measured at all. #147's headless route makes a wider
drive cheap, so this adds one.

st_walkcap.sh is st_profile.sh's drive minus the profiler: boot, beginplay, the
HEIRS entry-event chain, then arrows until the capture budget is spent. During
the walk the re-band trigger is the new-ink overflow path, so every re-band a
walk causes is by construction a frame the current palette does not cover --
which is exactly the frame a pinned palette would have to survive. Walk far
enough and the per-re-band dump IS the dataset. ST_MACHINE lets the same drive
ask a chunky backend the same question as a planar one.

qpin scores each captured frame three ways: re-cut fresh (what ships), the
palette cut on the first frame carrying this CLUT (what a cache serves), and one
cut over every frame carrying it (the best fixed palette that colour space
admits).

  ! IT COMPARES ONLY WITHIN ONE CLUT, AND THE FIRST CUT OF THIS TOOL DID NOT.
    Pinning every frame to frame 0's palette reported a 25x error, which is not
    a fidelity result -- the walk's CLUT moves, so that is one colour space
    scored against another's palette. A pin can only mean "reuse the palette we
    already cut FOR THIS CLUT".

It also reports the LRU hit rate by cache size over the re-band order, which is
what sizes a fix; the distinct-CLUT count does not, because what matters is how
far apart a CLUT's uses are.

events.title: docs: what SSI shipped on the Amiga, and how not to measure it
events.message:
docs: what SSI shipped on the Amiga, and how not to measure it

Curse of the Azure Bonds (Amiga, 1991) on a plain A500, against our ECS build
on the same corridor.

NO COPPER SPLIT: COLOR00 is one value — black — down the entire frame, title
screen and corridor alike. Same instrument that caught our own 25-band border
striping. SSI used a single palette.

THEY DID ENRICH THE AMIGA OVER THE ST, about 1.5x: same corridor, 10 colours
whole-screen / 8 in the viewport on the ST against 15 / 11 on the Amiga, and
the extra entries are shading rather than new hues — two dark blues where the
ST had one, three teals where it had one, two browns where it had one.

AGAINST OURS the budget is a tie and the spending is opposite: 15 genuine
colours for them, 16 for us, but theirs goes on chroma (teal chrome, cyan text,
green, brown door) and ours on a nine-step grey ramp, because our corridor is
quantised photographic stone and our chrome is a granite texture. Different art
pipelines, not better or worse.

★ AND A MEASUREMENT TRAP WORTH MORE THAN THE FINDINGS: amiberry's default
capture BLENDS (gfx_linemode=double2 plus a lores->hires upsample). A panel
that is flat by construction — our own ECS HUD — read as 30 distinct colours in
a 40x40 crop, and a whole frame as 4086. Any colour count off a default capture
measures the scaler. The fix is exact-pixel config keys (kept in a SEPARATE
openua-ecs-exact.uae, because the run-amiga-port skill's click coordinates
assume the 720x568 window) plus a filter to genuine palette entries: 4 bits per
gun means every channel of a real colour is a multiple of 17, and a population
floor clears the residue.

The first version of that filter kept pixels in a flat run of >= 3 instead,
which is biased against a TEXTURED image and in favour of a flat one — exactly
backwards for this comparison. It scored us 14 and them 10; the population
floor scores us 16 and them 15.

Also records a question about our own build: 16 colours frame-wide against 11
per scanline, with 25 independent band palettes available, suggests the ECS
split is buying little on a tonally uniform screen. Hypothesis, not finding —
the population floor could be hiding band-local colours.

events.title: ecs: the copper's 25 palettes striped the border, and had all along
events.message:
ecs: the copper's 25 palettes striped the border, and had all along

COLOR00 is the Amiga's border as well as playfield colour 0. DIW is exactly
320x200, so every scanline of the overscan shows it — and the copper rewrites
all 32 registers, COLOR00 included, at each of the 25 band boundaries. Twenty-
five independent cuts put twenty-five different colours there.

Measured down one column of the left overscan on a boot frame: 21 distinct
colours in 28 runs, changing every 8 scanlines, one of them pure white. After
the fix: 3 and 4 for the whole column, and across the display rows themselves
1 and 1 — a single colour, on the title sequence and on the main menu.

This shipped with the per-band copper palette and nothing caught it, for the
same reason the ST version went unnoticed for a day: every check looked at the
320x200 image, where there is nothing wrong. The ST hit the identical bug when
its raster split landed (f93795be) and its three bands flattered it — this is
the same shape with twenty-five.

ecs_unify_border() mirrors st_unify_border: pick the slot nearest band 0's slot
0, permute it into position 0 (palette and remap together, so no pixel changes
meaning), set its RGB to band 0's exactly. Matching band 0 rather than forcing
black is deliberate — uniform is the requirement, and band 0's colour is what
the border had before the split existed. ecs_repalette gets the no-permute half:
its premise is that slot numbering does not move, so it forces the copper WORD
alone, which it needs because the slot reps are per band and each band would
otherwise re-derive its own slot 0 and stripe again on the fast path.

AGA is unaffected — 256 colours, one palette, no band split.

MEMORY

  of the regions that were full. Main RAM is now 77 bytes in five
  pieces, and docs/memory-map.md says where the sound driver's will have
  to come from.

DEFECTS
  BUGS.md #17: four debug flags were silently pushing the code image
  past &3000, because CLEAR FONT_ADDR releases beebasm's overwrite check
  over exactly the range an overrun lands in. GUARD FONT_ADDR now catches
  it during assembly. The readouts moved to bank 6 so VSYNC, POS and
  ENERGY build again, and off the status box's black corner so they can

Bring README, PLAN and make.sh up to date

README: the sprite pool is eight, not seven, and the front paragraph now
says what the last two days added -- droids killing each other, the
disruptor, the turning recharge pads and the ALERT lamps. The "or

not a bug in what you just wrote. CLAUDE.md gets the same rule and
dbgpanel.asm's home.

DEBUG_VSYNC's own header still claimed it cost 117 bytes of main RAM, that

events.title: GUARD the code image, and move the debug readouts into bank 6
events.message:
GUARD the code image, and move the debug readouts into bank 6

KC: DEBUG_VSYNC corrupts the player sprite and the frame digit is
illegible. It was not the debug code -- it was that the flag adds 143
bytes to a code image with eleven spare, and NOTHING SAID SO. `CLEAR
FONT_ADDR, ...` releases beebasm's overwrite check over exactly the
range an over-long image spills into, so `PARA` shipped with its tail
sitting on the front of the text font; `*RUN PARA` scribbled on PARAFNT
and the PARAFNT load scribbled back over the code. The only bound in the
file was `code_end <= SPR_SAVE`, right when the font lived at &3C00 and
3,584 bytes too slack since.

So, KC's suggestion: GUARD FONT_ADDR, which fires during assembly at the
instruction that crosses the line and names the routine rather than a
total at the end, plus the ASSERT to match.

DbgFrameCount, DbgPosOut, DbgEnergyOut, the shared 4x5 digit font and
DbgHexDigit/DbgHexByte move to src/dbgpanel.asm, in bank 6 beside the
panel code they draw over -- the right home, not merely a free one.
Their shims are in lowcode2. DbgEnergyOut's droid type and energy are in
bank 4 and cannot be read with bank 6 paged, so its shim mirrors them
first. DbgSetBg and DbgDeckBg stay resident and must: the blitter calls
them with a sprite bank in.

VSYNC, POS and ENERGY now each build and run -- verified in jsbeeb, the
panel reads FF 11 FF 88 FF, the digit 2, two fields a pass, sprites
intact.

RASTER (59 over), DRAW (83), TIME (154), MAPGUARD (1 K of bank 4) and
POS+ENERGY still do not fit. All of them were silently corrupting the
build before today and all of them now fail it instead. They are the RAM
situation rather than the debug code, and RASTER's and DRAW's
instrumentation cannot move to a bank at all -- the interrupt and the
blitter call it. main.asm's debug header now carries the table of which
flags build, and BUGS.md #17 the whole story.

events.title: Handle WebGL context loss/restore in the Emscripten CRT shader path
events.message:
Handle WebGL context loss/restore in the Emscripten CRT shader path

Mobile Chrome (Pixel 8a observed) drops the WebGL context under GPU
memory pressure more readily than desktop. With no handler, the
default webglcontextlost behaviour never restores the context, so the
canvas goes black forever while audio and game logic keep running on
unrelated threads. Install lost/restored listeners (preventDefault on
loss to allow restore) and recreate the program/vbo/texture -- which
don't survive a context loss even though the context handle does -- on
restore.

events.title: Fix Pixel 8a canvas blackout: gate glitch hash/sin() chain on u_glitch
events.message:
Fix Pixel 8a canvas blackout: gate glitch hash/sin() chain on u_glitch

A live u_glitch uniform (vs. compile-time const 0.0) stops the compiler
folding away chq_hash()'s sin() call, so it runs every frame even with
glitch disabled. mediump sin() on this GPU can return NaN, and NaN
survives "* u_glitch" regardless of value. On the tile-based renderer
this corrupted the whole canvas to the clear colour, matching every
symptom seen (no GL error, no context loss). Root cause isolated by
on-device bisection of each uniform between const and real.

Fix: skip the hash/sin() chain entirely unless u_glitch > 0.0 (a
uniform, not varying, branch -- no divergence cost). Applied to all
three shader variants (GLES, MSL, SPIR-V) to keep their math in sync.
Zero effect under default params (glitch = 0.0 in both presets).

events.title: ste: the raster split banded the BORDER, and cropping hid it (#139)
events.message:
ste: the raster split banded the BORDER, and cropping hid it (#139)

Colour register 0 is what the ST shows in the border, and with a raster split
every group gets a turn at it. Three independent cuts put three different
colours there, so the border grew a horizontal band exactly as tall as the
viewport: measured on the left border strip, #555544 above and below against
#555555 inside.

Every check so far had cropped to the 320x200 image, where there is nothing
wrong — the AE comparisons, the montages, the colour counts. It was found by
looking at a full screenshot while checking the combat and town screens.

st_unify_border(): in each later group, find the slot nearest group 0's slot 0,
permute it into position 0 (palette and remap together, so no pixel changes
meaning), then set its RGB to group 0's exactly. The permutation is free; the
assignment costs a little fidelity for whatever indices live in that slot, and
buys a border that is one colour. Re-measured after the fix: #555544 at all
three sample heights, on three consecutive walk frames.

st_repalette passes may_permute = 0. That path's premise is that slot numbering
does not move, so the planes already on screen stay valid and no force-full is
needed; permuting there would renumber slots behind those planes, which is the
"brown chrome" failure. It still needs the RGB assignment, because the slot
reps are per group and each group would otherwise re-derive its own slot 0 and
band the border again on the fast path.

Also drops the `g == 0` gate on the alignment's position-0 claim, which was
written when only band 0's palette reached the border.

SCREENS CHECKED with vpbands=on, 33 re-bands over two drives: three groups only
ever on screens that commit a viewport. Boot, title and the main menu stay at
one group and are unchanged. The dungeon walk (24-27 colours), three different
town/BIGPIC event screens and the treasure/XP screen all render correctly with
a uniform border.

COMBAT IS NOT VERIFIED. It could not be reached headlessly: the CBTSND/CBTAUTO/
CBTPLAY harness (#74) bus-errors during boot on the ST build — with vpbands OFF
as well, so it is not this change — CBTSND alone boots but its `k` hotkey does
nothing from the walk (the letter-key hit-test eats bare letters there), and the
HEIRS slot-A chain resolves its combat faster than a 2 s sampling interval
catches. By construction it should stay at one group, since st_group_layout
requires s_vp_active and combat does not render the viewport, but that is
reasoning rather than measurement and is recorded as such.

AE=0 with vpbands off against the build before this change.

wonderboy: batch 41 phase D — the honest stop before 62/62

Measurement, not reconstruction (0 C changes, +4 cases, suite 5,855):
- THE ROW DID NOT FLIP, and the blocker is measured on the original's own
  code: $a4a (walk) and $a4e (weapon) are ADJACENT bsr's, so the frame
  alone must supply player_weapon_fire's entry X — two seeds differing in
  two record bytes leave BYTE-IDENTICAL memory at $a4e and then diverge at
  exactly one address ($b449, the shot count, $03 vs $04; the diff set is
  now ASSERTED, not prose, and the assertion is the one form that catches a
  seeded second divergence — equality, not membership). Identical memory
  in, one byte out: the difference travels in a CPU flag the oracle does
  not report. The overlap_mask_exit_extend treatment claimed for $1260 is
  refuted. PHASE E = threading the walk's exit X (probes $10a2/$1170 +
  $ec8), then the flip.
- Phase C's cost list was short, not wrong: it enumerated the batteries the
  flip would move, never the routine the flip would write. Annotated.
- $a38 body read off raw bytes (# ctx off): nine bsr's, tst.w d7/bmi.w,
  guards tst.w $6ef0.l (abs.LONG) and tst.w $a32.w (abs.WORD) — both
  fixed globals, not the record.
- cmt 0x6ef0 was wrong in both directions: EIGHT operand sites and FOUR
  readers, not three and one; the frame's own fall guard was among the
  missed. THE REAL AXIS IS ROUTINE COVERAGE, not encoding — the old plate
  enumerated one site per routine it had read and stated the total as
  image-wide (the encoding story was refuted three ways from the bytes;
  a lesson's mechanism must be what actually happened, second false
  mechanism caught this phase).

events.title: ste: Timer B fires on group boundaries, not band boundaries (#139)
events.message:
ste: Timer B fires on group boundaries, not band boundaries (#139)

The raster-split viewport palette cost +18.5% on the dungeon phase, and almost
all of it was Timer B firing 25 times a frame when only TWO of those boundaries
are a real palette change. A fast exit for the unchanged ones was tried first
and measured 807 cycles/fire against 771 for the full handler — entry and exit
are the whole bill at that cadence — so it was reverted (3929e850) and the timer
is reprogrammed per fire instead.

    presents   off      25 fires   2 fires
        16    13814      13814     13649
        32    19980      19949     19851
        48    23580      24216     23535

Marginal over the dungeon phase (32 -> 48): +18.5% becomes +2.3%. The rendered
frame is AE=0 against the 25-fire version — the split lands on exactly the same
scanlines — and AE=0 with vpbands off against the build before this change.

MFP68901 event-count mode: a write to TBDR while the timer RUNS sets the data
register only, so a written interval takes effect one fire later. Each descriptor
carries both halves — `expect`, the counter's reload while this fire runs (the
spin waits for the counter to drop below it, and that used to be the constant
ST_RPB), and `next`, the interval to program now for the fire after the next one.
The last live fire programs 255, which cannot underflow inside 200 display lines,
so the frame ends quiet and the VBL re-phases from scratch. Trailing sentinels
make a request latched while masked and serviced late (#91) install the last
group's colours again rather than walk off the table.

The variable compare needed a scratch register, so the palette loads into d0-d6
and a1 rather than d0-d7 — still eight registers and 32 bytes, and moveml's
register order is fixed, so the load and the store agree.

st_prof_tbcost is disarmed and says why: it armed Timer B by force, which worked
when the cadence was fixed regardless of content, but forcing it on a uniform
screen now arms a timer with nothing scheduled and would report the cost of an
idle timer as the cost of the split. The wall-clock fixture A/B above replaces
it — one binary, vpbands on vs off.

Still default-off, but no longer for cost: it has only been exercised on the
dungeon walk (the only screen that commits a viewport, so the only screen where
s_ngrp is ever 3), and the one-line-early fire plus the spin is timing-sensitive
in a way Hatari may not reproduce exactly. The gate is a real-hardware check.

events.title: ste: the viewport gets its own palette, on the raster split (#139)
events.message:
ste: the viewport gets its own palette, on the raster split (#139)

ADR-0016 B1 collapsed the ST's per-band palettes into ONE cut replicated to
every band, because per-band palettes produced the #40 seams — a flat panel
spanning a boundary in stripes. That holds for boundaries chosen by arithmetic.
It does not hold for a boundary placed exactly where the content changes, and
the dungeon screen has two: the top and bottom edges of the viewport. Split
there and the 3D view stops sharing its sixteen slots with the roster text and
the granite chrome.

Measured with tools/quant/qvp on the captured walk frames, against the true CLUT
colour of every pixel:

                        viewport   whole screen
    one group             392.5        155.0
    three groups          232.5        107.2      -41% / -31%

and the second walk capture agrees (395.7 -> 245.3, 161.0 -> 106.9). BOTH halves
improve: the chrome is not paying for the split, because it was the chrome's own
colours crowding the viewport out. On screen the night sky goes from near-black
to blue and the frame carries 24 distinct colours instead of 16.

Cost, matched present counts, same binary, only the runtime knob differing:

    presents   wall ticks off   on
        16         13814      13814
        32         19980      19949
        48         23580      24216

Identical through the boot (no viewport yet, so both run one group), +2.7% by
48. The MARGINAL cost over the dungeon phase alone is +18.5%, which is the
honest number — the split only exists on dungeon screens.

So it ships DEFAULT OFF, behind `vpbands=on` in video.cfg. Runtime, not
compile-time: one binary has to hold both arms or an A/B is comparing two
builds, which has misled this port before.

The band count is the RASTER RESOLUTION, not the palette count. ST_NBANDS goes
10 -> 25 because the viewport is at y=24 and 88 tall, so 24/112/200 are all
multiples of 8 and 20-row bands cannot express those edges. Groups (s_ngrp,
s_grp_b0) are runs of bands sharing one cut, and every band inside a group holds
an identical copy — so a tile straddling a band boundary within a group still
bakes the right slots, and `band = y * nbands / h` is untouched in the c2p and
in every draw-time writer in the engine. s_ngrp == 1 is byte-identical to the
old path: the same scripted walk gives AE=0 against the pre-change build.

Almost all of the 18.5% is Timer B: the handler now fires 25 times a frame where
only two boundaries are a real change. A fast exit for unchanged bands was
written and MEASURED — 807 cycles a fire against 771 for the full handler, i.e.
no change, because entry and exit are the whole bill at this cadence. It was
reverted rather than shipped: complexity in an IPL-6 handler for a measured
zero. The lever is fewer fires (a variable TBDR, twice a frame), and that lives
in the spin test, which is the one place in this file with a documented deadlock
(#91). Recorded in docs/planar-plan.md as the open item.

Also fixes a guard that could not fire: the no-force-full test read
s_have_prev_pal, which st_reband sets to 1 a few lines above it, so the
no-predecessor arm was dead and the first re-band compared against an all-zero
previous remap. It forced a rebuild anyway — index 0 is almost never slot 0 in a
fresh cut — but by luck, not by construction. It tests `first` now.

events.title: quant: the remap was the CUT'S BOXES, not the nearest colour (#139)
events.message:
quant: the remap was the CUT'S BOXES, not the nearest colour (#139)

quant_banded built a good palette and then labelled the pixels with the
median-cut BOX each colour fell in. A box is not the entry nearest to its
contents: the split that separated two colours happened before either box had
its final representative, so a colour could sit closer to a neighbouring box's
entry than to its own. Measured on the QDUMP captures, same palette both ways,
against the true CLUT colour of every pixel:

    frame                 box      nearest
    SSI logo             889.1      324.3    -64%
    Forgotten Realms     589.0      378.2    -36%
    UNLIMITED ADVENTURES 1481.3     401.1    -73%
    dungeon walk          198.3     155.0    -22%
    dungeon walk (2)      252.8     161.0    -36%

and inside the 3D viewport alone, 692.6 -> 392.5 on the walk frame.

Visible, not just numeric: the SSI logo's red gradient had a PURPLE wash across
its top-left corner and the UNLIMITED ADVENTURES title had black blotches down
its edges. Both are gone. Rendered through the shipping header by the new
tools/quant/qrender, and confirmed on a live STE walk.

The search runs only over the colours the band actually contains (m of them,
ntot entries each), because those are the ones on screen; absent colours keep
the 4x8x4 bucket table. That is why this costs m*ntot and not 256*ntot, and it
is what makes it affordable: measured on the STE at matched checkpoints of the
same scripted walk — identical reband counts, so the comparison is honest —

    presents  rebands   band t200 old   new
        16       10         3675       3795
        32       15         4582       4713
        48       17         5250       5400

+2.9% on the re-band, about 44 ms of an 8MHz walk, for the fidelity above.
Exact-preservation is untouched: the reserved slots are applied AFTER the
search, so a kept colour still lands on its own slot.

tools: qvp prices a dedicated viewport palette against the shipping whole-frame
cut (this is where the 8-colour question from Curse of the Azure Bonds gets
answered), and qrender prints the picture rather than the number — build it
against two revisions of quantize.h and you have a before/after with no
emulator. quantize.h is now a Makefile dependency; without it an edit left
every tool reporting the OLD numbers.

Also untracks four .ppm renders that dd228b1d committed by mistake. They are
320x200 frame buffers of FRUA title art — exactly what this task's own note
says never to commit — and *.ppm is now ignored.

events.title: tools: qstable — price the stable-palette designs, and the guard that looked exact
events.message:
tools: qstable — price the stable-palette designs, and the guard that looked exact

Next step on #139 was "build the stable palette". Measuring first changed what it
should be, and then caught the obvious cheap version being WRONG.

★ A STABLE PALETTE IS NOT FREE. qstable quantises through the engine's own
quant_banded and scores every pixel against its true CLUT colour, over five
captured frames that share one CLUT:

    ST  16 col   A per-frame 750.0   B CLUT-only 1575.1 (+110%)   C union 1076.5 (+44%)
    ECS 32 col   A per-frame 200.7   B CLUT-only  966.7 (+382%)   C union  331.9 (+65%)

B derives the palette from the 256 CLUT entries alone; C from the union of a
scene's content weighted by summed populations, which models an ART-derived
palette. Even C costs 44% more error. That is the argument #139 says has to be
made before an engine change, and it says: not like this.

★ AND THE CAPTURES SHOWED SOMETHING BETTER. The walk's CLUT changes at nearly
every re-band, so there is little reuse to exploit — but of 13 re-bands, TWO
changed no colour that was on screen at all. One moved 225 of 256 entries and not
one of them was drawn. Each of those cost the full ~364 t200 re-band (quant + used
scan + whole-frame FORCE-FULL), about 1.8 s of ST time, to produce an identical
frame. The shipping guard cannot see it: it is an exact memcmp over all 768 bytes.

★ THE FIX THAT LOOKED EXACT IS UNSOUND, AND THE SCREENSHOT CAUGHT IT. Comparing
only s_used_idx entries, snapped to the hardware's bits, seemed pixel-identical by
construction — and skips jumped 2 -> 7. The frame came back with a BROWN sky
instead of blue. s_used_idx is filled by the used-index scan INSIDE st_reband, so
at guard time it describes the LAST re-band's frame, not this one: anything drawn
since whose colour moved is invisible to the test and renders through the old
mapping. Reverted; the engine is untouched by this commit.

For a future attempt the guard needs a used set that is current at DECISION time.
Candidates: pair it with s_dt_new_ink == 0 (nothing unseen drawn since the last
scan) — plausible but it fired 7 times here and still went wrong, so verify before
trusting; or maintain s_used_idx incrementally as rows are built rather than
rebuilding it per re-band, which also attacks the 82 t200 scan (b59a2781).

qstable is committed with the tools; the engine change is not.

make test 471 passed.

events.title: Port the collision matrix, friendly fire, and the disruptor
events.message:
Port the collision matrix, friendly fire, and the disruptor

CollisionType ($6D6D) and DoCollision2 ($1B51) replace the two
hard-coded arms the port has carried since Layer 6 -- reverse the first
droid, pause the second. That was the table's $08 entry and nothing
else, which is why droid-versus-droid worked and everything else in the
matrix was missing. The table ships whole, all thirty-two bytes: a
transcription is faithful by construction and a trimmed one is faithful
until the first thing it gets wrong. The player's own collisions are
still separate, because $1A43 branches to _ply_droid before
DoCollision2 is ever reached; his bullet is too, because ours is slot 7
with no droid-table entry and DrBulletHit already handles it.

What the table turns on: EnemyFireEnemy ($1BF6), so a droid's shot and
a droid's EXPLOSION both hurt whatever else they touch, for
2 * (40 - type) of the target's own weakness -- and FreeSpriteTmp2, so
the shot is spent when it lands.

The disruptor is weapon 3, and it is an area effect rather than a
bullet: everything the player can see takes that same damage at once,
and the firer takes energy + type - shipLevel - $20 unless its type is
on DisruptorImmune. Only the 711 and the 742 carry one and both are
immune, which is what makes them worth taking. It runs for four
iterations; the sweep is the first and the flash is the rest.

[DECISION, agreed with KC] THE SCREEN SHAKE IS NOT PORTED. $23A3 jitters
the VIC's fine-scroll registers for three frames; our play strip is
exactly sixteen rows inside one hardware wrap, so a vertical jitter
fetches rows that were never drawn and a horizontal one shows a column
the incremental draw has not written.

The flash is an OVERRIDE, not a saved-and-restored palette. Writing
palPlay looked right until the console opened mid-burst: the transfer
game and the lift view both save palPlay and install their own, so a
flash caught by one of them would be restored later as the deck's
colour. SetPalPlay forces logical 0's four entries white after the
table instead, stores nothing, and a modal screen ends the burst.

Space: main RAM had 90 free bytes and the disruptor wanted 245, so this
also claims &0D60-&0DEF -- Econet and mouse workspace and the extended
vector table -- as the low overlay's second chunk, one file and two
copies, with the NMI workspace and the ROM private-workspace bytes left
alone. LUTs moved to &54C0 and three droid arrays to &0C90 to buy bank 4
back the room its half of the matrix needed.

Verified in jsbeeb: a disruptor kills a visible 123 for 72, costs the
player 64 -> 31 by the original's own arithmetic, pays the score, flashes
for three passes and puts the deck's colour back; an explosion parked on
a droid kills it through the matrix; the pass is still exactly two
fields.

events.title: Reclaim &0E00 for code, and animate the recharger and the alert lamp
events.message:
Reclaim &0E00 for code, and animate the recharger and the alert lamp

Main RAM was down to 48 free bytes and bank 4 to 10, and the two banks
that have room are both paged out during play. &0E00-&10FF is DFS's
shared workspace, live only while the filing system is, and dead from
the last *LOAD on -- the same argument the charset at &0400 already
rests on, one page up. So PARALOW is a sixth disc file, staged clear of
the font and copied down after every other load, and lowbss.asm puts its
mutable state in the 112 bytes at &0C90. Page &0D is deliberately left
alone: the NMI handler, the extended vector table and the sideways ROMs'
private-workspace bytes all live there.

THE ORDER IS THE WHOLE TRICK. PageLowIn writes the workspace DFS is
using, so it has to come after the last filing-system call, and PARAFNT
owns the staging address -- so PARALOW loads last and stages on the
panel. Done the other way round the next *LOAD hangs in the 8271 poll.

DrawDoorTile's body moved there as DrawTileCells, parameterised by a
definition and a list of cells, because the two new features want
exactly what a door wanted: repaint a tile that changed while the view
stood still. That is 200 bytes back out of the code image as well.

The recharger is AnimAllInsideFont ($38C4): rotate characters 76-79
inside the charset every other iteration. Ours needs a repaint after it,
because the charset is not the screen's source here -- AnimScan walks
the eleven visible tile columns for tile 20 and AnimPaint redraws the
eight cells that hold those characters. Rotating the CHARSET rather than
the map's codes is what keeps every draw path agreeing, RedrawAll
included. ChrAnimData1's other group, characters 122-125, is not ported:
no tile references it, so it is not in the 137-character export.

The alert lamp is BUGS.md #13, and MODE 1 has no fourth colour to give
it -- see the [DECISION] in lowcode.asm. Character $16 gets its own
logical instead: black, the deck's highlight, white, and white blinking.

Verified in jsbeeb: the four characters rotate one step every second
pass; a pad poked into the map paints, animates, and agrees with
RedrawAll; the lamp rebuilds and repaints at each threshold.

events.title: tools: graduate the quantiser analysis tools, with a way to feed them
events.message:
tools: graduate the quantiser analysis tools, with a way to feed them

#139 cites qfid/qpre/qdither as available tooling. They were in a scratchpad, and
two things were wrong with that.

★ THEY DID NOT BUILD AGAINST main. All three passed a tenth argument to
quant_banded — a band_used out-param that does not exist in platform/include/
quantize.h. It was declared, passed and never read in any of them, so dropping it
is lossless, but a future session would have hit the error and had to work out why.

★ AND THEY HAD NO INPUTS. The frames were captured ad-hoc in an earlier session
and nothing in the tree produces them, which is the difference between a tool
existing and a tool being usable. So -DFRUA_QDUMP now writes the quantiser's own
inputs at each re-band: the 320x200 index surface and the 768-byte CLUT exactly as
quant_banded is about to see them, viewport overlay included (qsrc is s_shadow
when a viewport is committed). Verified end to end — captured a real walk frame
and ran all three on it.

The point of these tools is that they #include the ENGINE'S quantize.h rather than
re-implementing it, so a number is comparable to what the machine renders.
tools/quantsim.py median-cuts an RGB image directly and models an IDEALISED
per-pixel dither; it measures a different pipeline and overstates what is
shippable. The README says so, along with two traps: MSE RISES with any dither
(judge by eye), and the ST runs nbands = 1 today, so multi-band numbers describe a
configuration that is not shipping.

★ AND RUNNING THEM CONTRADICTS #139's OWN CLAIM. The task states that weighting
the cut by AREA (box choice, split point, representative) "is now in". It is not:
quantize.h builds its cut list from PRESENCE — `if (cnt[i] && !kept[i])`, each
colour once, no population — and uses cnt[] only for the exact-slot reservation.
qpre on a captured walk frame: A shipping 252.8, B population-weighted 230.9,
C B+diffusion 594.3. So that 8.7% is an AVAILABLE win, not a banked one.

Both discrepancies point the same way: the earlier work lived in a variant of
quantize.h that never landed, and the task was written up from its results. #139
corrected accordingly.

Captures are frame buffers of copyrighted art — the README says never commit one;
they land in the git-ignored gamedata dir. Shipping binary carries 0 QDUMP strings.

make test 471 passed; ST 68000, ST QDUMP, Atari 020, Amiga AGA and Amiga ECS clean.

Refs #139, #138.
