events.title: Fix screen hover tooltip CCK/plane-address accuracy
events.message:
Fix screen hover tooltip CCK/plane-address accuracy

CCK was derived by snapping to the nearest matching BPL1 DMA-fetch
event, so it only appeared where bitplane DMA happened to land on
that exact word (blank over background/border) and jumped in
word-sized (~8 CCK) steps instead of tracking the hovered column
exactly. It's now computed directly from the hovered canvas-x via
the same beam-position formula computeSlotFromBeamPosition already
uses, so it's always present and exact.

Plane addresses now come from a new per-pixel PixelSnapshot.planeAddr
array, populated inline in decodeScreenPixels' existing per-pixel bit
decode (which already resolves BPLCON1 scroll and per-plane DDF
margin correctly), instead of a separate word-index guess in
computeHoverExtra. That guess didn't account for scroll delay
extending the display past a line's nominal fetch-window width, so
the last few scrolled-in pixels of a line showed no address/colour
info at all. Fixed by extending decodeScreenPixels' per-line decode
width by that line's own BPLCON1 delay, mirroring the existing
head-side margin-word compensation at the tail.

events.title: Redesign blit-region highlight to compute chip addresses directly
events.message:
Redesign blit-region highlight to compute chip addresses directly

Replaces the old fetch-time cursor/marking approach (which required
mirroring custom.c's own fetch-timing internals and drifted out of
sync at region edges) with a draw-time lookup: bvis_project now
derives the chip-RAM word a displayed pixel came from directly from
a per-line snapshot of each plane's bitplane pointer, fetch mode, and
real fetched-word count, then queries the blitter write-tap for that
exact address.

Fixes several edge-alignment bugs found along the way: DDFSTRT/DDFSTOP
region-width clamping using a direct per-plane fetch counter instead of
an unreliable display-side counter, and BPLCON1 scroll-delay handling
for the read side (using the clean toscr_delay_shifter source rather
than the SPEEDUP-contaminated toscr_delay_adjusted).

Rebuilds puae.wasm/puae.js from the updated libretro-uae submodule.

events.title: joust: verify the ctx name map — 73/75 confirmed, 37 renamed, +1 function
events.message:
joust: verify the ctx name map — 73/75 confirmed, 37 renamed, +1 function

The 56 '# ctx' names (behaviour-inferred, never body-read) are now
verdicts: 73 of 75 functions CONFIRMED from the 68000 asm (Ghidra
renders most register-argument routines as bare 'return;', so
tools/prg_dis.py disassembly was the evidence surface, not decomp.c
alone), 37 RENAMED with recorded evidence, 2 honestly still ctx
(sprite-render questions that extract_graphics.py would settle).

Headline: the whole 'graphics/input' cluster around 0x10a56 was the
SOUND DRIVER — set_color_lvl is play_sound (XBIOS Dosound via a
priority-gated sound_table), read_key_flag is snd_poll_done (Giaccess
mixer poll), init_gfx is snd_tone_sweep, wait_vsync is read_joysticks
(IKBD interrogate 0x16 — nothing waits on vblank), poll_key is
poll_quit_key (Ctrl-C: silence PSG, save HIGH.SCO, restore, Pterm).
Root cause is a broken XBIOS table in the SHARED trap-annotate tools
(decimal opcode numbers entered as hex: 0x20 labelled Supexec is
actually Dosound, 0x1f/0x18/0x21 likewise, 0x19 Ikbdws + 0x1c Giaccess
missing) — fixed in tools/ in the next commit, not here.

Other substantive renames: the egg lifecycle family (update_eggs +
erase/draw/physics — 'alloc_object' allocated nothing), spawn_wave is
update_pterodactyl (4-slot table, edge entry, mouth-only kill),
advance_scroll is rng_advance (walks the program image as an RNG),
count_objects_and_pad is a frame-time equaliser, the troll draw/erase
pair was swapped, raise_floor/paint_floor_row/dissolve_platforms are
the wave-transition world morphing. Two stubs were real (fill-pattern
builder, sprite-base select); screen_to_pos is dead code with a broken
x reconstruction (x22 vs x16). Untagged-name correction:
xbios_setcolor -> flash_hiscore_color. Var fixes: p1_x/p2_x pointed at
y; num_players is players_alive; screen_left/right are platform-0's
ground x range.

Map now documents the 0x4e-byte object record (incl. the egg
sub-record and ASCII score digits), the flags-word bit map, platform /
spawn / message / sound table formats: vars 26 -> 95, cmts 21 -> 76,
75/75 exported clean.

Leads recorded in README: make_fill_pattern's four byte-identical
btst/or blocks look like a possible depack_gamex.py LZSS over-repeat
(a live Hatari dump would settle it); ghidra_proj project.prp OWNER
was stale (ganneheim -> geogeo, gitignored file, buggyboy's has the
same issue).

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: retire the standalone HUD demo
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: retire the standalone HUD demo

The demo (render/atari/main.c + build.sh + run.sh -> HUD.PRG) was the
pre-game HUD-only on-target pin. It stopped linking when hud.c grew
calls into events.c (fixing the link set cascades ~15 symbols — most of
the game), its HUD.PRG was a stale Jul-21 binary whose MATCH validated
stale code, and the full game + frame-0 golden harness has long
superseded everything it proved. Retired rather than repaired.

Removed: main.c, build.sh, run.sh (git rm); stale HUD.PRG / hud.bin /
hud_fixture.h / golden.bin / palette.bin artifacts (untracked; backed up
in the session scratchpad).

Surgery, with the dependency evidence:
- golden.bin/palette.bin were demo-only: written only by
  gen_hud_fixture.main() (invoked only by build.sh), read only as
  verify_frame's DEFAULTS — the sole live caller (run_golden.py) passes
  explicit per-leg paths. Generation removed with the demo.
- gen_hud_fixture.py stays as a pure capture library (gen_game_fixture
  imports its asset/palette baking; Makefile GATE_DEPS lists it as a
  dependency source) — main()/CONTROLS gone, __main__ exits with a
  pointer. Now-misnamed; rename deferred as it ripples through 4 files.
- run_hatari.py is now explicitly a library module: demo main() gone,
  __main__ exits with a pointer to run_golden.py; verify_frame paths
  are required args; the needs_data opt-out existed only for HUD.PRG
  (all six call sites resolved True) so staging is unconditional —
  behaviour-identical for every live caller.
- Docs: render/atari/README.md reframed around the game + golden
  harness with a one-paragraph history of the demo; PORTING.md step 7
  and docs/binary-formats.md's verify example now cite run_golden.py.

Pins: BUGGYBOY.PRG byte-identical (133cae22..addbd); make test 730;
goldens st+ste MATCH; run_ste_selftest MATCH (covers the needs_data
removal); all runner modules import clean; disk/ = the trio.

Noted, not touched: .claude/settings.json carries a now-dead permission
entry for run_hatari.py-as-a-command (user-owned settings).

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: readability sweep — name the remaining magic literals
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: readability sweep — name the remaining magic literals

Zero-cost by construction and by pin: #define/enum introduction, literal
-> name substitution and comment fixes only — BUGGYBOY.PRG is
BYTE-IDENTICAL to the pre-sweep build (sha256 133cae22..addbd, re-hashed
after every file), make test 730, STE sweep 5,624/0, goldens 5/5.

Reconstruction (naming only, no values changed):
- sound.c/sound.h — the user-named priority: the note-stream command
  bytes 0x80..0x8c are now the SND_OP_* opcode family (REST, FLAGS_CLEAR,
  PORTAMENTO, GLIDE_DOWN/UP, LOOP, VIBRATO, SET_BIT1, END_TUNE, SET_F13,
  SET_BIT12, SET_R6_SRC, ENV_HOLD), each grounded in its handler +
  recreate reference + docs/sound.md; unrecovered musical intents keep
  the offset+role convention (SET_BIT1/SET_BIT12 say so). Plus
  SND_FLAG_ON, SND_VC_NOTE_HOLD, SND_MOD_RESTART/VALUE_MASK,
  SND_EG_PHASE_MASK, and a separate VC_EF_* vocabulary for SND_VC_ENV_FLG
  (borrowing VC_F_* would have asserted a shared vocabulary the driver
  doesn't have). A typedef compile-time assert pins the family to the
  dispatch window (SND_OP_REST == SND_CMD_LO, ENV_HOLD == +12) so a
  renumbered opcode cannot compile silently.
- results.c (LEG_*), events.c (FX_* block offsets + flag masks),
  object_list.c, object.c, road.c (reused road_const.h names), flow.c,
  gameplay.c, blitter_sweep.c (SWEEP_LOG_MAX), hud.c, assets.c, blit.c,
  player.c.
- Deferrals closed: object.c's duplicate COL_ALIGN + OBJ_ROAD_START_OFF
  now come from blit_const.h / scroll_const.h; BLT_ENDMASK_ALL applied in
  blitter_selftest.c; crash-lock literal duplicated across
  events.c/player.c hoisted to game.h (RM_CRASH_LOCK_SPIN/_SLOW).

Review gate (high) caught five false comment claims the hash could not:
the endmask2 absolute (blitter_skew puts a colour fill there), the
results.c divider side/target, blit.c's 'no second copy' claim, the
SND_TUNE_ON 0xff aliasing SND_TEMPO_ACC (load-bearing arithmetic, not
just 'nonzero'), and an SND_OP_ENV_HOLD comment claiming unconditionally
what only the shipped tune data guarantees (now honestly unpinned in a
comment: 0x8c always precedes a note in SND_CONST).

Deliberately unnamed: byte extractions (& 0xff), dbf sentinels,
geometry.c's nibble fixed-point masks (function comment covers them),
psg_regs/psg_src table values. Still open (recorded in PERF30): 0xfff8
has three legitimate names; results.c's NUM_MAX_CELLS_M1 duplicate.

Docs: docs/sound.md gained the opcode table; PERF30 A3 dedup deferral
marked closed.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: C5 slice 2 — HUD dashboard composite on the blitter
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: C5 slice 2 — HUD dashboard composite on the blitter

Route (byte-exact, fourth blitter route, second table-less one):
- src/blitter_dash.c: 8-pass AND/OR cookie-cut of the phase-7 dashboard
  composite — 4x LOP=AND from each group's mask word, 4x LOP=OR from
  {ink_a, ink_b, ink_b, ink_c}; x_count 8 groups x y_count 40 rows,
  src/dst pitch both 104. THE finding: ARENA_ROW_STRIDE ==
  SCREEN_ROW_BYTES (static-asserted), so the chip reads the LIVE per-leg
  art IN PLACE — no materialised stream, no invalidation, +16 B BSS, and
  the mid-leg probe_collision word mutation cannot go stale. Poke-batched
  (36 register writes vs blit_run's 136), ONE Supexec, shared-bus restart
  loop (HOG A/B: only ~0.5 ms better, declined per the slice-1 policy;
  GAME_DASH_HOG=1 knob). Bound on the blitter probe alone.
- include/dash_const.h: ONE home for the dashboard geometry — collapses
  DASHBOARD_DST (hud.c literal), DASH_ROWS/GROUPS (independent copies in
  plane.h AND events.c), ARENA_ROW_STRIDE and RM_DASH_SRC_OFF (events.c +
  results.c); game_main.c pins the adapter-baked ARENA_DASH_SRC_OFF equal
  by static assert.
- The census's 7-pass refinement is algebraically WRONG (planes 1/2 share
  ink_b but not background: ROAD_TOP_FILL puts 0x0000 vs 0xFFFF under
  them) — shipped as CAUGHT sweep mutation 14 instead of code. It passes
  on the all-opaque baked atlas (14/16 catches): a baked-art-only pin
  would have blessed it — the dash_pristine trap, now a measurement.

Cadence (leg 0): STE gate 99.25 -> 97.75 ms (-1.5%), drive 90.72 ->
89.80 (-1.0%); ST bit-identical at the gate, drive delta is tick-phase
noise (draw_frame cycle-identical under Musashi). Realized saving is
~half the census projection (isolated-loop vs in-frame measurement gap;
flagged honestly in BLIT_STE_SPEC §17 rather than repeating ~3.3 ms).

Harness:
- src/blitter_sweep.c + run_ste_sweep.py: dashboard section — CPU vs
  blitter over all 5 legs' REAL live art (init_leg_dash +
  draw_leg_labels + a marker-stepped variant) + baked atlas +
  all-transparent extremes, over seeded-LCG and top-fill backgrounds
  (a uniform background hid mutation 14 — vacuity hole closed); a
  distinct-art hash count (must be 8) pins the staging itself.
- Mutations 11-14 (LOP swap / x_count+1 / y_inc short / p2-copy) all
  CAUGHT, 1-10 unregressed; per-route positive mutation selectors.
- game_main.c + run_cadence.py: dash routed/declined counters
  (201/251 routed, 0 declined); VBLS_PER_FRAME_HEADROOM 12 -> 16 +
  CELL_TIMEOUT_S so the stock-ST gate cell completes (slice-1 deferral).
- Pins: make test 730; sweep 5,624/0-XOR; goldens x5 st + x5 ste at
  default AND --memsize 1; A/B 0-mismatch; 1 MB STE all four routes
  bound, free TPA 184,188.

Memory: +16 B BSS -> 1 MB STE margin 9,564 -> 9,548 B.

Docs: BLIT_STE_SPEC §17 (+ §7 item 1 closed measured-NO-GO: CLIP is
0.225 ms/frame, objshift2 issues zero clip calls in real play; §14 muluw
note closed NO-GO on size: 0.028 ms for 5,120 B of margin); PERF30 C5
slice-2 note + census closures; README/STATUS: draw_hud is 19.06 ms on
LIVE art, not 16.27 — the published number was measured on the baked
opaque atlas (baked-vs-live footnote added).

Known honest gaps (named in §17/STATUS): the odd-address tripwire is
structurally unreachable (like slice 1's); the 24-bit address truncation
predates all four routes; the boot bind is evidenced only by the cadence
route counters.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: C5 slice 1 — road fine-scroll on the blitter
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: C5 slice 1 — road fine-scroll on the blitter

Docs-only. Both binaries re-measured at HEAD on the same instrument
(Musashi, identical staged gate frame — the original reproduces Part 0
to the cycle: 880,376 cyc / 110.05 ms):

  stage           original   remaster   ratio
  render_road       26.19      28.85    1.10x
  object tree       57.34      62.93    1.10x
  scroll blit       11.80      12.06    1.02x
  draw_hud          12.29      16.27    1.32x (incl. the concurrent
                                       dash-memcpy revert — the mini-map
                                       is transparent; correctness won)
  TOTAL draw_frame 110.05     123.98    1.127x
  remaster on STE (estimate, bridged by the same-build render-clock
  ratio 0.808): ~100.1 ms = ~0.91x the original — the first
  configuration where the port beats the hand-written original,
  at byte-identical pixels. The original never touches the blitter
  (verified: zero FFFF8Axx refs), so 110.05 is its STE number too.

Memory: the ORIGINAL's resident extent read from its own main —
48,632 B program (text carries globals + stack; data=0 bss=0) + one
Malloc of exactly 388,616 B (the same number the remaster's arena
models) = 437,248 B TPA held, 469,248 incl. the TOS-owned second
screen (physbase_tbl[4] IS buf_aux — it allocates only one screen of
its own). START.PRG's hard-coded 0x77000 scratch pins a 512 KB ST
design target (medium-high confidence): the earlier '512 KB was not
enough' claim in §15 was unsupported and is corrected — the remaster
needs 1 MB (as required); the original was likely a 512 KB title.
A 512 KB remaster would be a separate ~270 KB campaign.

Reconstruction: two measurement-first moves take the shipping footprint
1,132,000 -> 707,840 B, under the measured 1 MB TPA (EmuTOS 905,448 B,
TOS 1.04 940,906 — Malloc(-1) probe at --memsize 1).

(1) The 2x128 KB SCREEN_OVERDRAW tails were sized to folklore: the reach
census (tools/reach_census.py + reach_probe.c, 5,240 composed + 4,000
forced-branch + 305 staged frames, all legs/scenes) measured the TRUE max
write past the visible 32,000 bytes at 8 BYTES (render_road; every object
engine stays below 32,000; nothing ever draws below the screen — the
off-screen cull idea is moot, both family predicates are horizontal).
Tail -> 0x1000 (512x margin; 36,096 keeps the 256-alignment), -253,952 B,
SCREEN_TAIL_LIVE(8) names the legitimate prefix. Standing guards so the
number can never rot into folklore again: the host suite canaries the
whole tail on every compared composed frame (mutation-checked: +0x800
draw reddens 16 tests), trace builds scan the full 4,088-byte tail per
present on target (mutation-checked: 100 presents trip), adapter.py
regex-reads both constants from game_main.c (one source of truth), and a
new 32-case below-screen sweep section pins the chip path against the
tail (all sweep comparisons now span screen + tail).

(2) skew_table + objsh2_cache (170,432 B) leave BSS: placed into the free
TPA above BSS at boot only when the blitter binds. os.s _start captures
the basepage and initial SP; rm_blit_bind_all computes the window
(base = align(p_bbase+p_blen), ceiling = min(p_hitpa, SP) - 16 KB stack
margin), memsets the block, hands out pointers. No Mshrink/Malloc — the
shell owns the TPA, the same 'ample RAM' the original relied on. The
unplaced state is TOTALLY safe: skew route starts latched-full, objsh2
declines on a null cache at its single entry, both flushes are null-safe
total functions, and the sweep consumes the bind result and reports a
clean DECLINE (verified via GAME_FORCE_NO_BLITTER) instead of crashing.

Harness: run_golden/run_ste_golden take --memsize (validated; arg wins
over RM_MEMSIZE); census/sweep pin themselves to 4 MB (CENSUS.PRG alone
is 1.4 MB); the reach census + dispatch sweep drivers land in tools/ so
the 8-byte number stays reproducible; blit.c's RM_HOST_ASSERT moved after
the clip test (fully-left-clipped no-write blits no longer abort the
host — the old code formed the wild pointer before checking).

Result: a 1 MB ST fits with +197 KB spare; a 1 MB STE fits WITH the
blitter tables placed (route live, 14,092 B spare above the stack margin
— the thin-margin watch item, observable via the cadence 'free TPA bytes'
counter). NEW STANDING PIN: goldens x5 st + x5 ste at --memsize 1, next
to x5 + x5 at default. make test 730 (host canary live); sweep 4,968
cases 0-XOR; A/B 0-mismatch; cadence in noise (105.47 / 97.34 ms), 0

claim (§8/§11/§12/§14); PERF30 C4 slice-10 note.

buggyboy/remaster: C4 slice 9 — colour engine routed via the skew table: GO

Reconstruction: the shipping STE build routes rm_blit_objshift's BASE
family through a 128-entry no-eviction first-sight table (sprite key +
src arena pointer; rows grow on demand — prefix-stable, so a grown entry
is byte-identical) behind a boot-bound rm_blit_objshift_fn, mirroring the
objshift2 pattern (static CPU-asm default, no NULL window; seam in
object_list.c). -DRM_STE_OBJSH_ROUTE and its glue are deleted; the
pre-shift path and its 219 KB cache leave the shipping link (sweep-only,
still pinning the pre-shift recipe). Poke batching: blit_skew_begin owns
per-blit invariants incl. X_COUNT (latch-reloaded per line,
sweep-verified), passes grouped 4 AND then ORs — 42 register writes per
6-pass blit vs blit_run's 102; src_addr must re-poke (the chip walks it).
Shared blit_start_and_wait gives the HOG policy one owner;
rm_blit_bind_all / rm_blit_flush_all enumerate the engines once.

dumps sprite-key set contents and the runner unions legs 0-4 — converged
per-leg sets are 78/75/79/98/79 but the cross-leg union is EXACTLY 128,
the table capacity, zero headroom. start_leg() flushes (live set <= 98,
~30 spare, warm-up = the measured cold-table drive); a saturation latch
retires the route to the pixel-identical CPU hybrid on overflow instead
of scanning 128 probes per blit forever.

full-decline / latched-decline / flush-rearm; declined cases must leave
the framebuffer untouched then complete byte-exactly on the CPU) with the
NOGROW mutation caught only by it; cadence tail gets a magic+count header

(-19.2% vs stock ST), STE drive 99.22 -> 97.18 ms (-2.5% vs stock, NO
regression — slice 4's 9%-hit failure inverted to 90% table hits); ST

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: C4 slice 8 — hardware-skew colour recipe proven byte-exact
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: C4 slice 8 — hardware-skew colour recipe proven byte-exact

Reconstruction: src/blitter_skew.c blits the colour engine's BASE family
from UNSHIFTED, colour-independent bitmaps (M = ~(A|B|C)&D, planes A/B/C,
D&~M pre-folded) with skew = fine_x and NO FXSR/NFSR — the one polluted
source read per line lands exactly in the bits endmask1 = 0xFFFF>>k /
endmask3 = ~(0xFFFF>>k) already block, src_y_inc = 0 spans the packed row,
and the colour fill rides in the OR-pass endmasks (dst |= src & e), so the
bitmaps are colour-independent for arbitrary fills and a zero plane skips
its pass (game blits average 6 passes; fills verified binary over all
legs). Public seam pre-built for the slice-2 table: ObjshSkewBitmaps +
materialise-into-entry + blit-from-entry, with the scratch-backed wrapper
as the swept entry point.

Harness: the sweep runs THREE grids (objshift2 / pre-shift / skew) —
4800 cases, 0 mismatch (720 + 704 + 704 handled); non-vacuity is gated by
C-emitted expected-BASE counts in a self-describing report tail (a
forced-decline build fails loudly — verified); --mutate all catches all 5
recipe mutations (704/704/643/660/297 failing skew cases) with the other
grids skipped and clean; the bench checks the handled flag, times the blit
passes in isolation (the old subtract-two-totals estimate was an 8x-low
artifact), and adds a game-realistic binary-fill variant. Makefile: the
skew file joins STE_SRC (host .so exclusion — the missed line broke the
host link) and GATE_DEPS. objsh_is_base is shared (blitter.h) by the
census and skew paths; OBJSH_PLANES / OBJSH_MAX_ROWS hoisted to
blit_const.h as the single source; signed per-row source walk kept
host-safe (blit.c's form).

Cost (Hatari, swept shape base_cells 2 x 32 rows): materialise 13,520 cyc;
passes 16,680 synthetic / 12,920 game fill; CPU asm 33,960 — 0.78x with
per-call materialise, 0.38x from a table. Hatari's blitter timing is a
model, not cycle-exact hardware (recorded in §13).

Docs: BLIT_STE_SPEC §13 (calibrated register recipe + pins + caveats,
supersedes §11's 3264-case figure); PERF30 C4 slice-8 note.

clip-test dedup in blitter_objshift.c, the SYS_HZ200 -Warray-bounds

The Memotech hardware UI collapsed all five separately-fetched firmware ROMs

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: make the MTX FDX floppy a hardware option

The FDX floppy subsystem was always fitted. Add a 'Floppy (FDX)' hardware
toggle (default on): unchecking removes drives B:/C:, empties the FDX Disk
BASIC ROM socket (page 5 reads 0xFF), and hides the FDX ROM slot in the pane.
CP/M boots from floppy, so it force-fits the subsystem — mirroring how it
already force-fits the 80-column display.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: wire up MTX TEXT transcription (screen OCR)

The MTX shares the TMS9918 VDP with the MSX but never exposed the OCR text
overlay: the descriptor omitted the 'text' status LED and MtxFrameProbe had no
transcribe driver, so the status bar showed no TEXT indicator and transcription
never ran. Add the 'text' LED, MtxMachine.ocrScreenStyled/blankCells (reusing
the shared TMS9918 name-table OCR), and a MtxTranscribeDriver. Transcription is
skipped while the FDX 80-column board is showing, since it already renders
crisp text.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: character-intent typing for the MTX keyboard

The MTX arranges symbols unlike a PC ('=' is Shift+'-', ':' and '_' sit on
their own keys) and KEY_MAP had no browser code for the ':'/'*' [5,5] and '_'
[7,5] keys at all, so ':' was untypeable. Drive the matrix from the typed
character (event.key) using the MTX BASIC ROM key legend, forcing the Shift
cell to match the character rather than the physical Shift key, so a PC key's
legend 'just works'. The MCP type tool sends literal characters for the MTX
instead of Spectrum symbol-shift chords.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: MTX BASIC listing parser for the BASIC pane

MtxFrameProbe exposed no panes provider, so the BASIC Listing pane was always
empty on the MTX. Add a detokeniser for MTX BASIC's crunched program format
(program at CPU 0x4000; per line [length][line#][tokens][0xFF]); token tables
transcribed from the BASIC ROM keyword tables, and LIST spacing (statement
keywords spaced, operators inline, REM verbatim) validated against a real
RAM-dump capture. Wire it to panes.basicListing.

in-race mini-map source art at buf_c+0x11c20 is byte-identical between

original's g_draw_hud does; the whole dash_pristine machinery removed

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: marker-decay divergence — suspect refuted, effect localised
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: marker-decay divergence — suspect refuted, effect localised

The 2-of-27 composed-frame divergence on the armed-decay drive was recorded
with a prime suspect: the harness re-serializing the dispatcher grid every
frame where the shell only does so on a course advance. That is NOT it -
gating the store on the wrap flag leaves the count at exactly 2.

A marker_off sweep localises it instead (frame 0, leg 0, whole-framebuffer
diff vs g_draw_frame): no decay armed = 0; low pad = 109 bytes at rows
118-136; row 0 byte 8 = 263 at rows 143-167; byte 0xc = 528 at the same rows;
bytes 0 / 0x18 and row 1 byte 4 = 0. So the effect tracks the decay column and
only some columns diverge.

Two conclusions:
- The low-pad row is RESIDUAL #2, confirmed empirically. That offset is
  RoadPose.seg_data[12] in the original, so the reference zeroes a far
  road-slope byte while the port writes into inert pad - and rows 118-136 is
  exactly the horizon band. It was documented from a source read; it is now
  measured.
- The rest is still unexplained, and the obvious explanation is ruled out: for
  marker_off 0x10 every decay write lands inside the grid, and the candidate's
  and reference's grids are BYTE-IDENTICAL after both prefixes run (verified
  directly), yet 263 framebuffer bytes differ. The cause is therefore
  downstream of the flag bytes the dispatcher reads. Next step is to bisect
  the draw stages on a diverging offset, not to theorise further.

The test keeps seeding 0x10 - one of the diverging cases - on purpose.

No code change; suite unchanged at 727.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: draw the name-entry alphabet in the results differential
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: draw the name-entry alphabet in the results differential

The results screen was ALREADY byte-compared against recreate across every
mode, rank and leg (test_results_screen_matches) - and still missed the black
box, purely on DATA: the default hi-score table's names are "...", so the
name-entry alphabet never reached the glyph blitter from there. The draw was
covered; the character set was not.

Two windows of the table's initials fields now tile 'A'..'`' (the top one
ending ON the delete sentinel), drawn and byte-compared. Mutation-verified:
restoring FONT_BYTES = 0x600 reddens exactly the window that draws '`' (23
bytes) and leaves the other green - i.e. this test catches the shipped bug
directly, which nothing else did.

Review fixes folded in (both were real holes in the first cut):
- The window guard was a tautology: "the last window ends at the top char" is
  true by construction of NAME_WINDOWS. Now asserts GAP-FREENESS, which is
  the property that can actually break (a smaller table silently leaves a
  hole in the middle of the alphabet).
- `footprint > 0` cannot show the alphabet was drawn: both sides read the same
  seeded table, and the initials are ~250 bytes of a ~9600-byte footprint
  dominated by the background fill, so a screen that never blitted the last
  row would agree with the reference and pass. (results.c's RS_MAX_ROWS is not
  pinned to HS_ROWS, so that is reachable.) The test now changes ONLY the
  window's top character and requires the REFERENCE output to move, proving
  the row carrying it is really blitted. Sensitivity-verified: aiming that
  probe at a row the screen does not draw fails the assertion.

Docs: two coverage traps generalised in PORTING.md - a differential can be
pinned on the wrong DATA (ask which values the fixture contains, not just
which paths run), and mutation testing lies when the edit preserves file size
(Python validates .pyc on mtime+size, so a same-length constant edit applied
and reverted within one filesystem second can leave the MUTATED bytecode in
place; it also baked a truncated fixture_font, which the shipped-fixture
assertion caught).

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: hoist the prefix asset binding into shared code
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: hoist the prefix asset binding into shared code

The play-test bugs were not "does the shell compile" (that is the build gate,
69a6332) but "does the shell wire the arenas the way the original did".
`make test` cannot answer that by compiling game_main.c for the host - it is
full of TOS seams. The answer is to move each binding DECISION into shared
code the shell AND the harness both call, so a wrong decision is wrong on
both sides and the composed-frame differential sees it.

rm_bind_gobj_prefix_assets (src/gameplay.c, declared in game.h) now owns the
whole GobjPrefixAssets bundle - the one where every alias in this port lives:
- marker_recs = rm_ring_decay_base(ring_st): the decay arena IS the object
  dispatcher's flag grid (this is the alias whose absence left a kicked
  roadside object writing to a dead buffer, animating nothing).
- anim_color = the HUD's fuel-mask table.
- the two buf_a anim-word mirrors, at RM_GOBJ_ANIM_MIRROR{1,2}_OFF, moved
  from render/atari/game_frame.h into game.h so there is one definition.

Callers now: game_main.c, equiv._ComposedScene, and equiv.compare_gobj_prefix.
The three const table pointers stay the caller's to resolve, since only it
knows its own base - the shell walks its obj-low blob, the harness points into
the 68k image, and they agree because OBJ_LOW_BASE + OBJ_LOW_X == A_X by
construction (gen_game_fixture.py's low()).

Why this is the real fix: the harness now EXECUTES the shell's binding code
instead of re-implementing it. Mutation-verified - dropping the bias inside
the binder fails four tests, where before the harness had its own (also
wrong) binding and saw nothing.

Pins:
- test_game_fixture asserts the shell binds through the binder AND pins the
  ARGUMENTS: anim_color is a pass-through, so a shell handing the prefix a
  private colour buffer would otherwise "use the binder" while silently
  breaking the fuel-mask alias on hardware (mutation-verified).
- The two mirror offsets are pinned game.h <-> adapter.py across the language
  boundary, like the ring-block geometry.

Review fixes folded in: zero-init the shell's bundle so it matches the
ctypes-zeroed harness struct if a field is ever added; drop game_main.c's now
empty game_frame.h include; correct that header's banner (one bench-only
constant left, and a note that a real shell wants rm_ring_decay_base); name
the macros in the struct's field comments instead of repeating their values.

Scope, honestly: the OTHER bundles (HudAssets most of all) carry their offsets
in the GENERATED game_fixture.h, which src/ would have to include to bind
them - pulling every baked array into the host .so. Hoisting those needs
gen_game_fixture.py split into a defines header and an arrays header. Until
then, bind bundle-by-bundle, starting with whichever holds an alias.

make test 723 passed; make gate clean both ways; make golden 5/5 MATCH.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: harness gap #2 — the on-target build is a test gate
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: harness gap #2 — the on-target build is a test gate

`make test` compiled the game shell for NOBODY: render/atari/game_main.c
(1721 lines - every asset binding, the frame loop, every TOS seam) is in
neither the host .so (SRC is src/*.c) nor bench.elf (bench_build.sh links a
17-file src/ subset), and four more src/ files (frame/flow/intermission/
results) are in the host .so but not in bench.elf. build_game.sh compiled
all of them; nothing in the gate ever RAN it. A shell that did not compile
therefore reached origin TWICE in one session with the suite green.

Gate:
- `make test` now depends on GATE.PRG + GATEMEAS.PRG: full cross-compile +
  link + .PRG wrap. Two builds because src/blitter_{selftest,sweep,census}.c
  compile only under their own measurement flags; those three combine into
  one extra build, so between them every .c in the project is covered
  (src/render.c excepted - a dead Phase-A stub linked by neither).
- Both go through build_game.sh rather than restating its flags; a third
  copy of the cross flags is exactly the drift the gate exists to catch.
  Gate-only .PRG names + GAME_NO_STAGE=1 so the shipping BUGGYBOY.PRG and
  the Hatari drive are never touched.
- `make golden` promotes the Hatari end-to-end (5 legs, ~20 s) to a named
  target for pre-promotion runs. Verified: 5/5 MATCH, which also confirms
  today's four play-test fixes on a 68000.
- Mutation-verified: a typo'd constant in game_main.c now fails `make test`
  at the build step, before pytest runs.

Incrementality (the trap adding the gate exposed):
- build_game.sh and bench_build.sh re-run gen_sound_fixture.py
  unconditionally, so build/sound_data.h's mtime bumped every build and
  every target depending on it was out of date the moment it finished.
  bench.elf had been rebuilding on every `make test` for exactly this
  reason, unnoticed. Fixed at the root: fixture_lib.write_if_changed()
  skips identical writes, used by all three generators. `make test` on an
  unchanged tree now rebuilds nothing (~21 s, same as before the gate).
- The first attempt (order-only prerequisites) was reverted: it "worked"
  only by dropping the rebuild coverage that made the dependency worth
  declaring. Caught by the pre-commit review.
- GATE_DEPS declares what a script-built target easily under-declares: the
  generators, the harness modules the fixture is baked from (test/adapter.py
  bakes the asset windows - an adapter change is what shipped the truncated
  font fixture), and render/atari/*.h, which neither existing wildcard
  covered. An under-declared gate certifies a binary it did not rebuild.
- Order-only chain serialises the three m68k builds (they share fixed-name
  intermediates in render/atari/build/, so `make -j` could wrap one build's
  .bin into another's .PRG - a green gate that validated nothing). `golden`
  joins the chain since run_golden.py shells out to the same script.

Scope, honestly: this catches "the shell does not compile / does not link".
It would NOT have caught any of the four play-test bugs - those were valid
C. Executing the shell's bindings host-side stays the job of hoisting them
into shared code (rm_draw_frame, then the ring/decay geometry in game.h).

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: close harness gap #1 — shared ring/decay aliasing
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: close harness gap #1 — shared ring/decay aliasing

REPAIRS THE BUILD: dcafb21 committed game_main.c's use of
RM_RING_ST_BLOCK_BYTES / RM_RING_DECAY_BIAS / rm_ring_decay_base without
the include/game.h that defines them, so the m68k game build did not
compile at that commit. This lands the header half.

Harness gap #1 was: the marker-decay binding lives in game_main.c, which
`make test` never compiles, so the fix for the missing kicked-object
animation shipped pinned only by reading. Closed not by compiling the shell
host-side but by removing the opportunity to disagree.

- The aliasing geometry moved OUT of the shell into include/game.h:
  RM_RING_DECAY_BIAS / RM_RING_DECAY_SPILL / RM_RING_ST_BLOCK_BYTES and
  rm_ring_decay_base(). One definition of "the dispatcher's grid and the
  prefix's decay arena are ONE padded block".
- equiv._ComposedScene had been binding marker_recs into the image while its
  own dispatcher read a private unpadded ring_st - the harness independently
  reproducing the shell's bug, which is exactly why the composed differential
  was blind to it. It now allocates the same padded block.

Pins (all mutation-verified):
- test_marker_decay_writes_reach_the_dispatcher_grid: the decay's walked
  marker must arrive in the grid THROUGH THE POINTER THE DISPATCHER IS GIVEN
  and make that slot word negative (what triggers the SPECIAL pass). Asserted
  via scene.ring_st, not the test's own block - reading the block let the bias
  cancel out of the arithmetic and passed with the grid mis-based.
- A directed armed-decay drive (no free drive kicks an object).
- test_game_fixture: the shell's own allocation (game_main.c is never
  compiled by make test, so without this a build that drops the bias stays
  green), game.h's RM_RING_ST_BLOCK_BYTES macro BODY (dropping a term would
  otherwise pass), and the seed constants against MARKER_DECAY_ARM /
  GOBJ_MARKER_STRIDE.
- bench_main.c: a note that its separated arenas are deliberate and must not
  be copied into a real shell.

What it caught immediately: with the arenas correctly aliased the composed
frame still diverges on 2 of 27 sampled frames of the decay drive. That is
EXPOSED by the fix, not caused by it - bound separately the same drive
diverged on 25 of 27, i.e. the old harness was noise. Asserted as an exact
count rather than xfail'd: a binary xfail cannot tell "still failing for the
documented reason" from "failing because someone unbound the arenas" (under
the bias mutation the drive goes to 27 of 27 and an xfail stays green).
Prime suspect is a harness artifact - the composed scene re-serializes the
grid every frame while the shell and the original only do so on a course
advance. Recorded in STATUS.md, unresolved.

Docs: PORTING.md gains the closure and the rule it generalises (when two
subsystems must see the same bytes, the aliasing geometry belongs in shared
code, not in each caller); STATUS.md records the gap, the pins and the
divergence.

buggyboy/remaster: C4 slice 3 — objshift2 collapses on the STE (-12% gate)

The profiling decomposition (timing-only NOMAT/NOBLIT builds on the
objshift2-dense gate frame) found slice 2's flat result exactly: the
per-frame materialise = +3.0 vbl (the entire cost); the blitter passes
are ~free; per-blit Supexec never blocked the win.

without enumerating sprite layouts. 128 slots x ~2.75 KB = 356 KB BSS
(honest minimum: 1 MB STE; tunable to 178 KB for 512 KB).

Measured (free-run, vbl/present): leg-0 gate 8.22 -> 7.22-7.28, leg-4
gate 8.23 -> 7.23 (~-12%, not a leg-0 artifact); driving frames ~flat
(slow sprites already hit).

Also: mkprg.py reloc fix - filter abs_fixups to allocated sections; the
STE binary's .debug_line relocs collided with .text offsets and broke the

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: C4 slice 2 — objshift2 routed through the blitter, byte-exact
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: C4 slice 2 — objshift2 routed through the blitter, byte-exact

Recipe: pre-shift + skew=0 (deliberate - the aligned recipe is the proven
one; hardware FXSR/NFSR/endmask edge semantics deferred as a RAM optim,
not a correctness path). Per column the fine-x straddle is materialised
into interleaved mask/data bitmaps; the blit is 2 passes total (AND all
planes / OR all planes, negative y-inc walking up). LEFT/RIGHT clip
families stay on the CPU asm engine (pinned hybrid; the family decision
runs in user mode so clips never pay the Supexec). Routed via a macro
override in object_list.c under GAME_STE (kept out of game.h - concurrent
session owns it). Scratch cost 2.7 KB static.

Pins: run_ste_sweep.py 1728 cases (widths x 16 fine-x x 12 columns x rows;
720 BASE blitter-drawn, 0 mismatch; mutation fails 601); STE goldens x5
with the blitter live; stock-vs-STE A/B 0-mismatch x10 frames; stock
goldens x5; stock .PRG byte-neutral (hash-proven); make test green.

HONEST perf finding (PERF30 note): cadence is FLAT (stock 6.61 vs STE
6.65 vbl/present) - the per-blit materialiser redoes the fine-x shift +
mask build the CPU does, so only the framebuffer RMW is offloaded. The
collapse is a DATA change: slice 3 = boot-time pre-shift tables from the
static sprite sheet -> 2 blits over static data, no per-frame materialise.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: fix 4 shell-binding bugs found by play-test
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: fix 4 shell-binding bugs found by play-test

Two visible faults were reported ("no animation when the buggy kicks a
roadside object"; "a black box for the character during high-score name
entry"). Both were the same class, and sweeping for that class found two
more. NONE was in src/ - every ported core stays byte-exact. All four sat
in the layer `make test` does not compile (render/atari/game_main.c) or in
the fixture windows it consumes, where the harness builds its own bindings
instead of the shell's, so the suite was green and the game was wrong.

Fixes:
- marker-decay arena: GobjPrefixAssets.marker_recs pointed at a private BSS
  block while the dispatcher read ring_st. In the original both are the one
  grid at A_obj_markers (decay base = grid - 8), so the kicked-object
  animation wrote nowhere; the object still vanished and still scored, which
  is why it read as "the animation is missing". ring_st is now a padded
  block and the prefix gets the biased base.
- font window: FONT_BYTES was 0x600, one glyph short of the name-entry
  delete sentinel '`' (0x60). On target the blitter read the next fixture as
  glyph pixels, and an all-zero (mask, ink) row REPLACES the cell with
  colour 0 - the black box. Now one derived FONT_BYTES; the duplicate
  FONT_GLYPH_BYTES is gone.
- live globals frozen: objlist.bonus_timer / p24_flag were derived once in
  start_leg, so the 5-flag bonus window never clamped an object type and the
  p24 gate never re-read the checkpoint-bumped score digit. Both refreshed
  in rm_draw_frame, where the original reads them.
- aliased global split: 0x18d12 is rev_reload AND lean_frame, so the poke at
  both its sites restarts the lean overlay. It had been skipped on the
  reasoning that "no compared surface reads lean_frame" - false,
  draw_buggy_hi reads it every frame. Now PlayerState.lean_frame_reload ->
  rm_apply_player -> SpriteState.lean_frame.

Harness (the reason these hid):
- equiv._ComposedScene no longer REPRODUCES the shell's staleness for
  bonus_timer / p24_flag - reproducing a bug on both sides is exactly what
  stops a differential from seeing it.
- test_composed_frame: directed bonus-window drive (no free drive opens the
  window). test_player: both rev_reload poke sites. test_game_fixture: the
  font window derived from flow.c's HS_CHAR_DEL + the glyph stride pinned to
  text.h across the language boundary + the shipped fixture length, and the
  marker-decay padding pinned to the addresses and the prefix walk.
- test_text now fuzzes up to the top glyph instead of stopping one short.
- All mutation-verified: each fix's removal reddens its own test and no other.

Docs:
- PORTING.md: "The shell-binding trap" - the four defects, the generalised
  rules, and the alias sweep over addrs.h (4 addresses carry two names; only
  0x18d12 was broken).
- STATUS.md: the fix table plus two honest residuals on the decay wire (the
  clears do not survive a course advance since ring_st is a derived mirror;
  the low pad is seg_data[12] in the original, not filler).
- names.txt: the dual role at 0x18d12.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: C1 — vsync-locked presentation cadence (pixel-faithful)
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: C1 — vsync-locked presentation cadence (pixel-faithful)

Shell-only (game_main.c): a free-running 50 Hz vbl_count (bumped in the VBL
sound pump before its early-outs) + present_wait_boundary() quantize every
Setscreen flip onto a fixed 2-vblank grid - presents land 2/4/6... vblanks
apart (25/12.5/8.3 fps steps) instead of free-running.

Measured (249-present headless autodrive): baseline 5/6/7/8-vblank jitter
(39% odd-span) collapses to 6x153 + 8x93 (0.8% odd, instrument artifact);
mean 6.59 -> 6.99 vbl (the cost of rounding heavy frames up). Honest notes
in PERF30: the deliverable is the LOCK, not 25 fps compute (2-vblank
presents need <40 ms frames); tearing never existed (Setscreen latches at
vblank) - the fix is pacing jitter.

Wait = plain Vsync (services the pump + IKBD); vbl_count single-writer/
single-reader, no lock; liveness fenced by ordering (install before first

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: SOUND slice 3 — the game ships WITH sound on target
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: SOUND slice 3 — the game ships WITH sound on target

Shell (render/atari):
- vbl_sound: the 50 Hz VBL pump — when vbl_enable is RUNNING and no trigger
  mutation is in flight, writes rm_refresh's YM2149 (reg,val) stream to
  0xffff8800/02; parked = silence, exactly the original's parked vector.
  Installed as _vblqueue[0] PRESERVING the displaced TOS entries (TOS's
  per-VBL Dosound stepper drives the beeps), via one Supexec; conterm
  cleared (TOS key-click). Symmetric UNINSTALL on the quit path restores
  SYS_VBLQUEUE/SYS_NVBLS so Pterm can't leave TOS jumping into freed TPA.
- Real XBIOS Dosound over the baked lists (sound_dosound.h, split from
  sound_data.h so the shell doesn't carry SND_CONST); unconditional in
  game_main.c so a dropped -DRM_SOUND_TARGET fails at link, not mutely.
- race_start_countdown: stop_music(BEEP)x3 + GO, 51 Vsyncs apiece
  (wait_vbl_set_offset @0x102ee), at race entry like main @0x10226.
- op_wait_music_off: spin on rm_sound_music_on polling FRESH input per
  Vsync — skippable at name entry (0x25bc), NOT at game over (0x2406);
  Crawio key drain at the tail (0x25de). os.s gains Dosound + Supexec.

Reentrancy (the VBL races the main line on one SoundState):
- A nesting-counter lock — the shell runs user mode, so no SR mask; the
  pump skips one inaudible frame when a mutation is in flight. The lock
  lives INSIDE the multi-store primitives (rm_turnoff/rm_egoff/
  rm_inittune/rm_initfx) so no call site can forget it; rm_stop_music
  keeps a sequence-level bracket (nesting is why a counter beats a bool).
  rm_sound_lock/unlock carry compiler barriers so -flto can't reorder the
  publish; contract documented in sound.h. No-ops on host/bench builds —
  the differential .so is behavior-identical.
- SND_PSG_WRITES_MAX pins the shell cap to the driver's max emit
  (asserted per frame in test_sound_rm).

Proof:
- Hatari --trace psg_write (FLOWSND autodrive): countdown = reg13=0x00 x4
  from Dosound per leg start; engine idle = reg13=0x0e repeating from
  Dosound; 10k+ music writes (regs 0-0xc) from the REFRESH pump. The
  GAME_FLOW_AUTO loop still closes; run_golden.py MATCH on all 5 legs
  (sound is off-image); make test 690 green, host untouched.
- Honest scope (STATUS): the trace proves the right registers get the
  right values; audio QUALITY (timbre/pitch/tempo) is by-ear only —
  awaiting a play-test. Perf ledger records the pump tax (~2.3 ms/frame
  in-race, ~4.8 ms under a tune, 1.6-3.3% of the frame; all-regs dump is
  faithfulness-required; rm_refresh a future hand-asm candidate).

buggyboy/remaster: PERF30 A2 measured sizing — the naive design is dead, objshift2 is the prize

Instrumented all three fine-x engines over composed 600-frame drives on all
five legs, recording DISTINCT source bytes per engine (spans overcount):
- objshift2 (the 56 ms fixed pass) reads only 3.0 KB of LEG-INVARIANT sprite
  data and re-shifts it 3,240x per leg — the ideal pre-shift target: a
  boot-time full pix+mask table is ~98 KB compacted.
- objshift (42.8 ms post-A1) reads 8.8 KB mostly shared across legs; full
  table ~360 KB — memory-marginal; masks-only ~72 KB.
- The naive '16 phases of every roadside sprite' is dead: ~458 KB compacted,
  ~1.4 MB offset-preserving. The rm_scroll_prebuild precedent does NOT
  transfer cleanly (its 16-bit offset-preserving window can't hold the 32-bit
  straddled masked form).
- RAM verdict: objshift2-full fits a 1 MB ST beside the 389 KB arena +
  screens; BOTH full does not; on 512 KB only masks-only objshift2 (~49 KB)
  fits. A real pre-shift build implies a 1 MB machine.
- Correctness constraint recorded: objshift's per-call colour fill applies
  AFTER the shift — tables must store pre-colour pix + rotated mask, keeping
  the per-plane &-fill and the RMW at blit time.

Proposals only — no blitter code changed (instrumentation reverted).
Implementation scoped: objshift2 full pre-shift first (boot-time build,
equivalence test per the test_mode2_scroll_prebuild pattern), then
objshift masks-only or fold into A3.

events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: PERF30 Part 0 — the ORIGINAL binary measured; baseline corrected

The perf baseline was the GCC-compiled recon, never the original's hand-asm.
Measured three ways (the original's draw_frame @0x12e22 on the cycle-accurate
Musashi over the bench's staged frames; the live PRG in cycle-exact Hatari via
flip cadence; per-stage spot-checks):
- Original: 110 ms gate (9.1 fps), 82.8 ms median (12.1 fps), p90 101 ms;

  20 fps' impression (light screens + object-free stretches), not the race.
- The remaster is currently 1.83x SLOWER than the original (201 vs 110 ms
  gate) — STATUS's 'beats the original' claim was vs the recon and is
  corrected. The original's asm is ~2x the compiled C exactly where the
  fight is (object tree 0.49x, render_road 0.51x); blit_road_scroll is the
  one stage already at original parity (the pre-rotation win — a plain-copy
  stage; the masked object blitters cannot repeat it).

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: joystick support — the shell parses IKBD packets
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: joystick support — the shell parses IKBD packets

Reconstruction:
- The shell's IKBD ISR (os.s) is now a packet parser: headers 0xF6..0xFF get
  their payload length from a protocol table; ONLY the final byte of a 0xFD
  both-sticks report (joystick 1, the ST game port) is stored to joy_state —
  every other payload is swallowed, so packet bytes can never corrupt the
  scancode arrays. kbd_install pins the IKBD into joystick interrogation mode
  (0x15) alongside mouse-off, so only interrogate replies arrive; read_input
  sends the original's per-frame 0x16 interrogate (read_joystick @0x12110) via
  Ikbdws — the raw ACIA poke the arcade port used bus-errors from user mode
  (found by the flow trace, PC=0x1b150), a supervisor/user difference the
  original never faced.
- Priority merge mirrors recreate input.c:32 exactly: stick bits (0x8f mask)
  win; keyboard arrows/space are the fallback only when the stick is idle.
  F1-F5/R/Esc/Q stay keyboard-only, as in the original. The stick drives the
  race, leg-select nav/fire, and name entry through the one shared input word.
- Gotcha paid for once, now assembler-enforced: os.s .bss must stay even-sized
  (tos.ld SUBALIGN(1) packs downstream globals directly after) — a trailing
  .even replaces the hand pad; the odd-size case address-errored at boot.

Harness:
- 532 tests green; BUGGYBOY.PRG builds; golden MATCH (input is never polled
  before the frame-0 dump); GAME_FLOW_AUTO trace 19 records, unchanged — its
  race loop drives the interrogate + ISR every frame, pinning no-hang /
  no-bus-error / no keyboard corruption. STATED HONESTLY: the headless reply is
  all-zero, so the joystick DECODE path is verified only by the manual
  stick-in-hand run (hatari --joy1 keys); joy_state is sticky on a lost reply
  by design, mirroring the original's async joyvec.

Docs:
- STATUS.md joystick row + scoped coverage note; PORTING.md (user-mode ACIA
  gotcha, .bss .even rule); README controls gain the joystick mapping.

wall time no longer moves with the collected-item count. Surfaced by the
flow-slice-B review's efficiency angle (measured, not assumed).

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: port game_update §12's course object/marker ring
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: port game_update §12's course object/marker ring

Section 12 scrolls one grid of 0x20-byte rows, one row per distance band, and
refills the far end from the next packed course record. RoadPose.seg_data was
already row -1 of that grid; this ports rows 0..13 as CourseRing.

The consequence that mattered: each band's marker word is a live course value,
not the baked table it was modelled as. build_road_geometry stamps it into the
HIGH (flag) word of every control long the band covers -- render_road's
blit-variant bits plus the EDGE_* shoulder flags §10 reads back. Freezing that
column froze the road's flags after the first frame. The road half-width is the
control long's LOW word and never came from here, despite the original's
road_width_src name.

Reconstruction:
- CourseRing/CourseRow (include/game.h); EDGE_* hoisted out of player.c, since
  the ring is where those flags are born.
- rm_road_course_advance gains the ring: scroll, refill (select mask -> type
  codes, animation-run expansion, marker fixups, the slot-1 -> slot-13 echo),
  and the no-record age path.
- rm_build_road_geometry takes the ring instead of RoadSource.width_src, so a
  live input can no longer be mistaken for a table it is safe to snapshot once.

Harness:
- compare_leg_drive stops handing the road control table over: it is now a
  compared result, and the ring is compared band by band. The drives hand over
  exactly one thing (the crash arming) instead of two.
- test_course_ring.py: bands 0-11 byte-exact over free-running 600-frame drives
  x 3 scripts x legs 0-4, plus a pin test for the C/Python constant mirrors.

Coverage, found by mutation rather than by reading:
- Branch counters must derive from the record consumed, not the band produced.
  525 of the 554 animation codes re-select the slots the expansion writes and
  overwrite them with the same bytes, so deleting the whole expansion left the

- Two branches a leg start cannot reach are pinned by seeding read_pos onto a

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: latch IKBD key presses so short taps are not dropped
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: latch IKBD key presses so short taps are not dropped

The demo polls held-key state once per frame, and a frame here costs ~84 ms
(~12 fps). A tap shorter than that had its make AND break both arrive between
two polls, so key_down[] was already back to 0 when the loop read it and the
press vanished. Esc typically needed three presses to quit.

Fix
- os.s: the IKBD handler now also sets key_hit[scancode] on a MAKE. Unlike
  key_down it is never cleared by the break — only by the C that consumes it,
  so no press can be missed between polls. The handler saves d1/a1 as well as
  d0/a0 now that it writes them (save and restore lists verified to match).
- demo_main.c: take_key_hit() consumes the latch. Momentary keys (Esc, Q, R)
  read it; held keys (arrows, Space) keep reading key_down[], which is what
  steering and throttle actually want. R therefore becomes edge-triggered:
  one restart per press instead of repeating while held.

Instrumentation (same commit: it is what diagnosed the bug, and two hunks in
main() interleave it with the fix, so splitting would leave a commit that does
not build)
- -DDEMO_TRACE=N logs per-frame course state (read_pos, row_ctr, speed, rpm,
  collision_lock, hud_crash_timer, view_wrapped) so a headless drive can show
  whether the course actually advances on-target.
- -DDEMO_KEYLOG plus -Wa,--defsym,KBD_RAWLOG=1 logs every raw byte the ACIA
  delivered, in arrival order, before it is read as a scancode. That log is
  what proved the fault: three Esc presses (01 81 | 01 81 | 01), only the last
  honoured, with no stray packet bytes anywhere in the stream. It also refuted
  the earlier theory that mouse/joystick packets were corrupting key_down[].

Not verified in play: the latch is diagnosed and reasoned from the captured
byte stream, but no interactive run has confirmed Esc/Q/R since. make test does
not reach on-target input, so no automated check covers it.
events.author: Geoffrey Anneheim

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: port the crash / auto-steer script (game_update §6)
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: port the crash / auto-steer script (game_update §6)

Reconstruction
- src/player.c: port §6, the crash / auto-steer script. While collision_lock is
  armed it replays a canned crash out of crash_anim_tbl, one 8-byte record per
  frame (body pose, optional rpm override, animation frame, curve kick, marker),
  stepping its own cursor until a terminal record hands the controls back. The
  armed curve window that cuts a crash short when you are shoved back onto the
  road is included.
- Plus the crash-adjacent branches the script needs to be reachable and correct:
  §5's spin lean override, §7's RM_IN_COAST down-step and the rev limiter the
  script is allowed to break, §9's steer-from-centre + steer_delta + curve_freeze,
  and §10's spin arming and the clamp gate a crash stands down.
- include/game.h: PlayerState grows the script's state; PlayerAssets grows
  crash_anim_tbl. The precondition weakens from "no crash in progress" to "no
  event pending" — the script now handles a crash rather than excluding it.

Harness
- test/test_leg_drive.py + equiv.compare_leg_drive: a FREE-RUNNING leg drive from
  init_leg with no warmup. The candidate is seeded once and then drives itself
  (physics, course advance, geometry, scroll feedback), so drift accumulates
  instead of being erased per frame the way compare_player_drive erases it.
  600 frames x 4 input scripts x legs 0/1/4: up to 204 crash frames and 20
  control handoffs per drive, with the off-road push reached on leg 4.
- Exactly two things are handed over, both counted: the single frame recreate
  arms a crash (detected on the 0 -> nonzero edge of an event-owned global), and
  the road control table, whose marker rows stream from §12's unported ring and

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: fix the defects the workflow code review found
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: fix the defects the workflow code review found

Max-effort review of 674505e..HEAD returned 11 findings. Three CONFIRMED ones
contradicted claims made in the previous commits' messages, so those are called
out first.

Correctness:
- run_hatari.py staged COURSES.DAT/GRAPHICS.GRA for EVERY .PRG, but only
  build_demo.sh copies them and disk/ is gitignored — so `build.sh &&
  run_hatari.py` (the documented HUD flow) died on a clean checkout. The earlier
  "HUD.PRG MATCH" passed only because disk/ was already populated by a demo
  build. Now staged per-.PRG, and verified by emptying disk/ first.
- The GRAPHICS.GRA guard had a header-sized floor and no real protection: a file
  truncated ANYWHERE past the header sailed through, and rle_decode had no output
  bound, so it walked out of the arena. The prior commit claimed this was
  "verified on Hatari" — the test only truncated BELOW the floor, which the floor
  caught for the wrong reason. Bound the decoder itself at both ends and return
  false; a size check at the call site cannot do this job, since a file of any
  length can carry an unterminated stream.
- Fread's count (0x3f500) exceeded the arena's remaining room by 37 KB, so an
  over-long file overran the block before any validation ran. Replaced with
  RM_GFX_READ_MAX, derived from the arena geometry.
- read_file accepted handle 0. GEMDOS reserves 0/1/2 and never returns them from
  Fopen; handle 0 is the exact failure os.s's own new comment documents, and it
  makes Fread read the keyboard. Now `<= 0`.
- assets_load.py bounded COURSES.DAT's copy but not GRAPHICS.GRA's, so an
  over-long file memmoved past the ctypes block and corrupted the CPython heap.

Harness:
- test/test_assets_bounds.py — new. Malformed-input cases including the mid-file
  truncation the old test missed, each asserting a trailing canary survives.
- test_python_constants_match_assets_h pins assets_load.py's 8 mirrored
  constants against include/assets.h by parsing it (CLAUDE.md §5). It caught its
  own regex bug on first run.
- Replaced test_region_matches_recreate, which could not fail unless the
  whole-arena compare already had, with a first-difference report naming the
  region and phase.
- LIBREMASTER was spelled out in three test modules; hoisted into adapter.py.

Docs:
- shim.c claimed "byte for byte as before". Not true: across a TU boundary GCC
  can no longer inline memset at the call site, so demo_main.c's per-frame frame
  clear is now an out-of-line call. The benched cores are unaffected, which is
  why the bench counts did not move — but "identical code" was the wrong claim.
- Recorded why src_end, not dst_end, is the bound that fires: the decode runs in
  place with dst below src, so a runaway stream overwrites its own input first.
  Measured with the output bound removed (211068 of 256000 bytes used).
- README: the Cconws diagnostic is invisible under headless Hatari; the only
  symptom a script sees is a missing SCREEN.BIN.
- build_demo.sh CORES wrapped to the 160-char limit.

Verification: 296 host tests green, DEMO.PRG and HUD.PRG MATCH, HUD flow
verified with disk/ emptied, bench unchanged (0.76x).

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: keep the file-I/O trap wrappers together and first
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: keep the file-I/O trap wrappers together and first

Adding Fopen/Fread for the asset load wedged Cconws between Fread and Fwrite,
splitting the file-I/O block. That block being contiguous and immediately after
_start is not cosmetic: putting other wrappers ahead of or between them made
Hatari's GEMDOS-HD hand back handle 0 (stdin) from Fopen in a large .PRG, so
Fread read the keyboard and the graphics unpack spun forever waiting for an end
marker it would never see. Diagnosing that cost a long session in recreate's
game_os.s, whose layout this file mirrors.

Move Cconws down with the other console wrappers and record the rule in the
header comment so the next wrapper does not re-break it.

The demo happened to work either way at its current size — the original failure
was size-correlated — so this removes a latent trap rather than fixing a live
one. DEMO.PRG and HUD.PRG both still MATCH, and the truncated-asset guard still
refuses bad files.
events.author: Geoffrey Anneheim

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: shared libc shim + code-review fixes
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: shared libc shim + code-review fixes

Runs the pre-commit review gate over the shim extraction and over the two asset
commits it was skipped on (74e0ff1, 9e1d222).

Reconstruction:
- render/atari/shim.c — main.c, demo_main.c and bench_main.c each carried their
  own byte-identical memset/memcpy (and, since the loader, memmove). One file
  now, linked by all three, beside the shim_include/string.h that declares them.
  Its header comment states the cost honestly: these loops are NOT free (a
  32000-byte frame clear per frame, ~450 KB through the boot-time unpack) and
  neither shows up in tools/bench.py, so a long-word version is an open item.
- demo_main.c — read_file now returns Fread's count and load_assets checks it.
  The RLE decoder trusts its stream to be terminated, so a truncated or wrong
  GRAPHICS.GRA walked the decode off the end of the arena; COURSES.DAT is read
  with a count equal to its exact size so a short read is definitive, and
  GRAPHICS.GRA is floored at RM_GFX_FILE_MIN (assets.h). Verified on Hatari:
  truncating either file is refused with a message naming it, intact files run.

Harness:
- assets_load.py — RmArena was mirrored as a bare 6-pointer array, so adding a
  field to the C struct would have rm_arena_init write past the buffer. Now a
  ctypes.Structure with named fields, as adapter.py does everywhere else.
- bench.py — assert the arena fits the Musashi image; a slice-assign past the
  end silently GROWS the bytearray and shifts the stack/sentinel layout.
- test_assets.py — module-scoped fixtures (the unpack ran 4x) and named region
  spans instead of bare hex lengths.

Docs:
- render/atari/README.md — shim row, and the asset-load failure behaviour where
  a user would meet it; reflowed to the 160-char limit.
- gen_demo_fixture.py — staged_image's docstring now states the arena swap,
  which bench.py also depends on.

Verification: 291 host tests green, DEMO.PRG and HUD.PRG both MATCH, and the
bench's instruction counts are bit-identical to before the refactor
(4021 / 42781 / 7435 / 17385), so the extraction changed no generated code.

Deferred:
- Long-word memset/memcpy for the frame clear and the unpack's block slides.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: DEMO.PRG loads the data files instead of baking them
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: DEMO.PRG loads the data files instead of baking them

The on-target demo now reads COURSES.DAT + GRAPHICS.GRA over GEMDOS at boot
and unpacks them with src/assets.c, so the road texture, the scroll playfield,
the course stream, the object record arena and every sprite are read from the
game's own files. ~413 KB of baked asset arrays are gone (demo_fixture.h:
28530 -> 2702 lines; DEMO.PRG text is 68 KB). run_demo.py still prints MATCH:
byte-identical to recreate's ported pipeline on a real 68000.

Reconstruction:
- demo_main.c — a BSS arena, read_file/load_assets over Fopen/Fread, and every
  asset pointer rebound to an arena region; memmove for the unpack's block
  slides.
- os.s — Fopen / Fread / Cconws wrappers (Cconws names a missing data file
  instead of failing silently).

Harness:
- test/assets_load.py — one shared "load both files through remaster's own
  loader" helper, used by test_assets.py and the fixture generator so the
  compared arenas cannot drift apart.
- gen_demo_fixture.py now bakes only non-file content and emits ARENA_* offsets
  instead; it stages a freshly-loaded arena into the reference image so golden
  and the demo render from identical assets. Measured: 347 of the arena's
  388616 bytes differ after 60 staged frames, and exactly one reaches the
  framebuffer — a bit the running game clears in its own dashboard graphic,
  which returns once the system that writes it is ported.
- gen_hud_fixture.py — from_arena=True drops the three graphics-file tables and
  keeps dsp_table's original (absolute) offsets. The HUD-only demo is unchanged
  and still MATCHes.
- bench_main.c / bench.py — Musashi has no filesystem, so bench.py writes the
  unpacked arena straight into the .bss block and runs bench_stage_assets before
  each measured call, keeping the wrappers zero-work. Numbers unchanged (0.76x).

Deferred:
- The three on-target mains each redefine the freestanding memset/memcpy(/memmove);
  a shared shim.c would collapse that, but it is out of scope here.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: drive the demo with the ported physics — playable buggy
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: drive the demo with the ported physics — playable buggy

The demo's ad-hoc throttle/steer feel is replaced by rm_player_update, so
the buggy behaves like the original's: the rev model with its limiter, the
lean and wheel frames following the steering, the road curvature the steer
table integrates, the edge clamp and off-road push, and the course
advancing on the view wrap (at the speed you are actually travelling)
rather than off a made-up distance accumulator. The HUD's speed and clock
are live.

Demo
- demo_main.c: game_update-then-draw frame order; apply_player fans the
  physics outputs to the render structs (each one a shared global in the
  original); R restarts the leg from the baked start state.
- Held-key input: GEMDOS only reports presses, and driving needs several
  keys held at once, so the demo takes the IKBD ACIA interrupt (os.s
  kbd_isr) after switching mouse and joystick reporting off, and restores
  both on exit. The first-frame dump happens before the install, so the
  headless MATCH run never depends on it.
- DEMO_AUTODRIVE=N debug flag: scripted input + a dump after N frames, so
  the whole loop can be checked headlessly instead of only frame 0.
- gen_demo_fixture.py: bake the physics table offsets and start state, and
  every road edge bank (a live drive re-picks the bank each frame).

Verified
- run_demo.py still MATCHes: the first frame is byte-identical to
  recreate's whole ported pipeline on a real 68000.
- A 150-frame DEMO_AUTODRIVE run drives on-target: course advanced, road
  geometry changed, HUD clock ticked, speed held down by the curve clamp
  while cornering.

Docs
- render/atari/README.md: the demo is now the playable one — loop order,
  the IKBD held-key mechanism, both debug flags, and what is still not
  modelled (crash script, collision, events, section 12's object ring).
- PORTING.md: Phase B has started + how porting a gameplay function
  differs from a render one (scalar equivalence, staging artefacts,
  excluding frames where an unported system engages).

events.title: Add opt-in buffered playback and fix jitter-driven double-ticking
events.message:
Add opt-in buffered playback and fix jitter-driven double-ticking

Adds a launch-config-only bufferFrames option that runs the emulator
ahead of what's displayed, smoothing occasional slow-tick jank at the
cost of latency (never active during interactive debugging). Also
fixes the actual root cause behind most "slow frame" reports in normal
playback: routine tick-worker timer jitter occasionally nudging the
due-frame count two ticks ahead, forcing a back-to-back double-tick
that both busts the frame budget and silently drops one of the two
frames. Normal-mode catch-up now runs at most one tick per callback for
small backlogs, reserving full fast catch-up for genuine stalls.

Diagnostics reworked accordingly: per-tick (not just per-callback)
overrun averaging, a distinct counter for genuine-stall multi-tick
callbacks, and an aggregate achieved-fps report — with the exploratory
checkpoint/heap-sampling logging from investigating this removed now
that the real cause is confirmed and fixed.

events.title: Build the wasm module with -O3 and ThinLTO
events.message:
Build the wasm module with -O3 and ThinLTO

puae_debug.c, the grafted libretro-common/zlib/7zip deps, and the final
link were building at -O2 while libretro-uae's own core already used
-O3 by its Makefile's default — bumped to match. Also enables ThinLTO
across all three build stages (including a change to the libretro-uae
submodule's Makefile) so the final link can inline across object
boundaries, e.g. puae_debug_instructionHook into newcpu.c's per-
instruction dispatch loop.

Together, a measured ~2.8% reduction in average per-tick cost, with no
correctness regressions (full wasm test suite still passes). Confirmed
this doesn't fully explain a separately-observed ~14ms/tick cost in
real use, which further investigation traced to the actual cost of
cycle-exact emulation for DMA/graphics-heavy content, not anything
addressable here.

events.title: Render the PUAE canvas via WebGL, add jerky-playback diagnostics
events.message:
Render the PUAE canvas via WebGL, add jerky-playback diagnostics

The 2D canvas path needed two full-framebuffer copies per tick (wasm
heap -> ImageData -> canvas backing store, since Chrome rejects an
ImageData backed directly by wasm memory). WebGL uploads straight from
a view into wasm memory via texSubImage2D, cutting that to one copy,
with context-loss recovery since that's a real risk on weak/software
GPUs. Verified pixel-identical against the old renderer's output.

Also adds frame-budget overrun logging (aggregated to at most once a
second, since logging every overrun individually was itself expensive
enough to worsen the stutter it was meant to diagnose) and per-checkpoint
capture time/heap-size logging, both reported through a "PUAE
Performance" output channel so they're visible without needing the
webview's DevTools open — attaching DevTools was itself found to distort
these very measurements.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: on-target demo draws the full object pipeline
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: on-target demo draws the full object pipeline

The interactive DEMO.PRG now runs remaster's WHOLE Phase-A render pipeline on a
real 68000 — road + ground + foreground sprite + roadside object list + scaled
object + player buggy + HUD — and its first frame is byte-identical to
recreate's g_build_road_geometry + g_render_road + g_blit_road_scroll +
g_draw_game_objects + g_draw_hud (run_demo.py prints MATCH). Arrow keys still
steer live.

Demo:
- demo_main.c sequences the draw_game_objects tree in recreate's order (prefix,
  ground, fg sprite, pass 1, draw_object, pass 2, then the fixed pass + buggy
  ordered by the view) and keeps the object state in step with the live pose.
- gen_demo_fixture.py bakes the object arenas (buf_a records, the buf_c
  sprite/graphics arena, and the STATIC+bss table blob the dispatcher reads)
  plus the object/sprite/ground/prefix scalars, and adds g_draw_game_objects to
  the golden pipeline.

Aliased globals the split model has to reproduce (each caused a real on-target
diff, all documented in render/atari/README.md):
- anim_color == fuel_mask (0x17f08): the prefix's animated colour IS the HUD's
  phase-6a fuel mask -> one mutable buffer shared by both.
- obj_xoff_tbl == road_width_tbl + 2 (0x18f26): the dispatcher's x-offset table
  is the freshly built control table -> rebound to `ctrl` each frame.
- ground_view_off == obj_scan_off (0x18c58): one value (view_flags * 0xdd).

Also: ObjListCtx.px must be rebound to the frame's buffer each frame (we
alternate two screen buffers) — it was left NULL, so every object-list pixel
was written to address 0 instead of the screen; that was the last 1103-byte
under-draw. Screen buffers carry a SCREEN_OVERDRAW tail because
draw_game_objects writes off-screen sprite fragments well past the visible
32000 bytes.

Harness:
- DEMO_EXTRA_CFLAGS + DEMO_DUMP_STAGE cut the frame short after a chosen stage,
  so a headless run bisects an on-target divergence to one stage (that is how
  the NULL px was found: stages 0-2 matched, pass 1 carried the whole diff).

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: blit_road_scroll fast top fill -> matches hand-asm
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: blit_road_scroll fast top fill -> matches hand-asm

Profiling the pre-rotated blit showed the 13 KB constant top fill (the plane
pattern above the road band) was ~78% of the remaining cost, and GCC compiled it
to move.l #imm,(a0) (operand refetched every store, 20 cyc) in an indexed loop.

- src/scroll.c: fill via a post-increment pointer unrolled 8x, with the constant
  laundered into a register (asm barrier, no-op on host) so the stores are
  move.l dN,(a0) (12 cyc). blit_road_scroll 19.33 -> 11.98 ms (0.36x recon, ~1.02x
  the original hand-asm — the full 2.84x gap is now closed). Byte-identical.
- test/test_scroll.py: cover all 5 legs (was 0/2/4) — 40 cases, all byte-exact.
- STATUS.md: perf table (pipeline ~84 ms; remaster 0.76x recon).

Verified: full host suite 142/142; demo still MATCHes on the 68000.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: optimize blit_road_scroll via pre-rotated playfield
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: optimize blit_road_scroll via pre-rotated playfield

blit_road_scroll was the worst C-vs-asm ratio (2.84x the original): recreate
rotates every plane-word every frame (20x20x4 = 1600 variable-count rol.l). Since
the fine shift is constant across a frame and the playfield is static per leg, we
precompute instead.

- src/scroll.c: rm_scroll_prebuild() builds the 16 fine-shift pre-rotated copies of
  the playfield once (copy 0 == the raw playfield, which the edge seam reuses for
  its masked wrap blend); rm_blit_road_scroll() now plain-copies contiguous columns
  from copy[shift] — no per-word rotate. 33.55 -> 19.33 ms on the 68000 (0.58x the
  recon, ~1.64x the original, down from 2.84x). Byte-identical to the verified core.
- include/game.h: rm_scroll_prebuild decl + RM_SCROLL_SHIFTS/RM_SCROLL_WINDOW; the
  blit's 3rd arg is now the pre-rotated buffer.
- test/adapter.py, equiv.py: prebuild then blit in compare_scroll (24 cases still
  byte-exact vs recreate's rotate-based g_blit_road_scroll).
- render/atari/{bench_main.c,demo_main.c}: prebuild once, blit from it; bench measures
  the per-frame blit (prebuild is prep). Demo still MATCHes on the 68000.
- tools/bench.py: prep the scroll blit with bench_scroll_prebuild.
- STATUS.md: perf table updated (pipeline ~92 ms; remaster 0.83x recon overall).

events.title: Persist duplicateOfPrevious through .puaeprofile save/load
events.message:
Persist duplicateOfPrevious through .puaeprofile save/load

The duplicate-frame flag (b3d99bd, "Flag duplicate frames") only ever
lived on FrameCapture -- extension-host-only, in-memory -- not on
RawCapture, the thing that actually gets serialized. The later
multi-frame save/load rewrite (d693f4d) rebuilds FrameCapture[] fresh
from RawCapture[] on every load, with nothing to set the flag again, so
it silently vanished on any save->reload regardless of whether the
underlying detection worked live.

Moved duplicateOfPrevious onto RawCapture itself, so it's carried
through save/load for free the same way every other raw-capture field
already is, instead of needing separate persistence wiring that's easy
to forget (as just happened). Added it to the .puaeprofile format's
per-frame frameMeta (renamed from frameImages, since it's no longer
image-only) and patched the two checked-in fixtures' embedded JSON to
match the field rename.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: demo at -O2, double-buffered (no tear, no shift)
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: demo at -O2, double-buffered (no tear, no shift)

Two on-target fixes to the interactive demo:
- build_demo.sh: -Os -> -O2 (matching recon) so the blit primitives inline; this
  ~halves the render cost (see tools/bench.py). The single-frame output is
  unchanged (still MATCHes golden on the 68000).
- demo_main.c: double-buffer the display. The old single-buffer memcpy to the live
  screen every frame tore badly at ~10 fps; now we render off-screen and flip the
  video base at the vblank via Setscreen. The two buffers are aligned to 256 bytes
  at RUNTIME (the ST shifter only uses the high/mid base bytes, so a non-256-aligned
  base is rounded down -> the image shifted); link-time alignment wasn't enough
  because the GEMDOS load base needn't be 256-aligned.
- os.s: add Cconis (non-blocking key poll), Vsync, and Setscreen trap wrappers.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: per-function 68000 cycle bench vs recon (+ machine model)
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: per-function 68000 cycle bench vs recon (+ machine model)

Adds a cycle-accurate perf comparison of the remaster render cores against
recreate's recon, both cross-compiled to m68k and run under Musashi on the SAME
staged leg-1 frame.

- tools/bench.py: loads bench.elf (remaster) + recon game.elf, runs each stage via
  emu.run_bench, prints instructions/cycles/ms and the remaster/recon ratio; also
  benches g_render_road_machine (the byte-exact register/goto model).
- render/atari/bench_main.c + bench_build.sh: zero-work bench_<fn> entry wrappers

  at -O2 (matching recon).

  the bench measure the identical frame (else frame content skews the ratios).
- STATUS.md: perf section with results.

Findings: remaster is 0.96x the recon overall — on par or ahead per stage —
render_road 0.91x, and 0.89x vs the machine model (GCC optimises the native-pointer
C better than the hand-threaded transcription). The earlier "2x slow" was purely
-Os not inlining the blit primitives; -O2 fixes it. Remaining gap is algorithmic.
