events.title: buggyboy/remaster: make the demo auto-run so driving is visible
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: make the demo auto-run so driving is visible

Fixes the interactive demo: Up/Down did nothing visible and Left/Right drifted.
Root cause — leg 1 starts flat (seg_data all -2 for ~25 steps) and the baked
scroll_speed was 0, so a single course-advance per keypress produced no motion.

Now the demo auto-runs, paced by the vertical blank, with non-blocking input:
- speed (Up/Down = throttle/brake) both scrolls the road band (feeds
  blit_road_scroll's scroll_speed) and advances the course via a distance
  accumulator, so the road visibly streams forward at any speed.
- steering (Left/Right) adds a gentler CURVE_STEP up to CURVE_MAX and
  self-centres by CURVE_DECAY each frame, so it no longer over-drifts.
- os.s: add Cconis (non-blocking key poll) + Vsync (XBIOS 37) trap wrappers.

Verified: per-frame framebuffer diff is nonzero every frame while driving (road
band scrolls + hills advance); the first frame (speed 0) still MATCHes golden on
the 68000, and the HUD-only demo still MATCHes (shared os.s).

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: extract plane.h cell ops (fill / and / overlay)
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: extract plane.h cell ops (fill / and / overlay)

The HUD repeated three two-line patterns that all operate on one ST "cell" (the
two plane-longs at `a` and `a`+4), differing only in the transform: plain fill,
AND-with-mask, and masked overlay. The overlay was moreover identical to text.c's
blit_row. Collapse all of them into a shared plane.h:

  cell_fill(px, at, lo, hi)                  -> wr32 both halves
  cell_and(px, at, mask)                     -> AND both halves
  cell_overlay(px, at, mask, ink, lo, hi)    -> (bg & mask) | (ink & fill)

Every 2-line write pair in hud.c is now one named op; text.c's blit_row is gone
(uses cell_overlay). No behavior change (pure refactor) — full suite 30 green.
events.author: ganneheim

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: take Framebuffer* in the render primitives
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: take Framebuffer* in the render primitives

The dst buffer was uint8_t *px — the same type as the font/string/asset
pointers, so nothing stopped a wrong pointer being passed as the framebuffer.
Take Framebuffer* instead: the type now says exactly what it is, and the
compiler rejects passing an asset buffer as the draw target. (A bare pointer
typedef would read nicely but give no such safety — it converts freely to/from
any uint8_t*.) rm_glyph_run + the HUD phase functions take Framebuffer*; the
one-word leaf helpers (blit_row, overlay_word) stay raw addresses.

test_text binds the first arg as POINTER(Framebuffer) to match. Full suite 30
green (pure type change; codegen identical).

events.title: S34+S35: case-insensitive asset lookup, Android touch fixes, Amiga sound repair
events.message:
S34+S35: case-insensitive asset lookup, Android touch fixes, Amiga sound repair

Case-sensitive filesystems (Linux, Android, R36S) never found SWOS files whose
capitalisation differed from our hardcoded literals, so the game reported "no
data" even when the files were in the right folder. Windows dev machines cannot
reproduce it. DataPaths gains ResolveFile/ResolveDir (exact case first, then a
case-insensitive probe returning the real path); every SWOS data lookup now goes
through it: the boot gate, TEAM.* enumeration, the grafs atlases, pitch variants,
charset, CD cue/img resolution and the .RAW sample index.

Amiga in-match sound had never been play-tested and was wrong three ways, all
verified by decoding SFX.SNG against the original 68k:
  - a goal played instrument 36, which in the original is only ever the
    near-miss "ooooh"; goals and misses were literally the same sound. Goals,
    penalties and full time now play the song-6 roar (instr 28 + 27).
  - the crowd bed ran at 8000 Hz instead of 16574 Hz, over an octave low on the
    quietest sample in the bank, so there was effectively no crowd.
  - the module's volume ramp was ignored, so reactions ended on a hot sample and
    were audibly chopped; the decay is now baked into the PCM.
Full time was silent on Amiga (win/lose/draw samples are PC-only).

Android had two inescapable dead ends: pausing hid the touch overlay while
nothing on a touch device could emit ui_cancel, and the full-time screen waited
on a keyboard-only ui_accept. The pad now stays up while paused (icon quits,
fire resumes) and every fire tap raises a discrete accept. Menu touch zones use
the bare bar instead of the match grace strip, which had been swallowing the
option rows' arrows and flipping the options page instead of changing a value.

Import/UX:
  - BOTH floppies are required: SFX.IN2 lives on disk 1, so "only disk 2 is
    used" was wrong and cost users all Amiga sound. Wording corrected, and the
    importer no longer short-circuits on graphics alone, so adding the missing
    disk later actually completes the import (bank probe invalidated after).
  - SOUND option always toggles instead of silently refusing an unavailable
    choice, and boot auto-selects a source that exists.
  - First-run screen prints on-screen diagnostics (searched paths, .adf counts,
    storage reachability, which of graphics/teams is missing) so reports from
    Android and handhelds are actionable.

Android storage: extraction output moves to the app-private dir; the public drop
folder stays in Download/OpenSWOS. Android export presets sign with the Godot
keystore so release exports are installable.

GFX_Promo/ (111 MB of personal media) added to .gitignore.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

buggyboy/remaster: port glyph blitter (text_body)

a character pair packs into one 4-plane cell (char1 -> high byte of the
(mask,ink) words, char2 -> low byte), ink masked by the two colour planes.

byte-exact, not just coverage): recreate exports g_draw_hud_bar and
g_draw_hud_gauge0, which both hit this body — 960 fuzz cases (8 chunks x 2
modes x 60), random strings/offsets/fills/backgrounds, incl. the char2==0
last-cell glyph-0x2f substitution. test parametrized by chunk for xdist.

cursor chaining + draw_dashboard + buf_c before it lands.

events.title: buggyboy: cycle-accurate per-frame benchmark (original vs recon)
events.message:
buggyboy: cycle-accurate per-frame benchmark (original vs recon)

Measure the in-race pipeline's 68000 cost under Musashi, no Hatari needed,
to quantify why the reconstruction runs slower on a stock ST.

Harness:
- shim: tally each instruction's cycles (osh_num_cycles); add trap-free
  osh_run_bench to run our cross-compiled m68k recon functions (their OS-trap
  vectors sit inside the recon .text, so osh_run's vector install would corrupt
  them). emu: expose `cycles`, add run_bench.
- tools/bench_frame.py + `make bench`: stage a real mid-race frame, then time
  each pipeline function twice — the original machine code (emu.run) and the
  recon cross-compiled to m68k (game.elf, the BUGGY.PRG code, via run_bench).

Finding (stable across legs/frames): recon is ~2.1x slower than the original.
draw_game_objects + render_road dominate absolute cost; blit_road_scroll has
the worst efficiency gap (~2.8x, a move.l (a1)+,(a0)+ copy GCC doesn't match).
A compiler-efficiency gap, not an algorithmic regression (behaviour is verified
byte-identical). hatari --cpuclock 16 covers it.

Docs:
- README: Benchmarking section.

Tests:
- test_game_update_real_course.py stages the real leg-N COURSES.DAT
  (render_screen._prepared_image + oracle init_leg, so both sides start
  byte-identical), forces a section-12 course advance each frame, and diffs

  offsets, fx_block_2e byte-vs-word). Parametrized (leg, chunk) for xdist;

events.title: Fix severe profiler multi-frame capture slowdown
events.message:
Fix severe profiler multi-frame capture slowdown

Two compounding issues made multi-frame captures take 40+ seconds
instead of a few: DMA/copper/snapshot buffers were transferred across
the webview<->extension-host postMessage bridge as raw Uint8Array,
which gets flattened into a slow per-element array-like instead of a
single primitive value like base64 does, and trimToProgramRoot/
applyContextReuse called the expensive syntheticLabel lookup
uncached, dominating per-frame model-build time.

Also delays arming debug_dma/debug_copper recording until the
frame-boundary hook fires, instead of during the throwaway alignment
frame, avoiding wasted recording work during capture start.

events.title: Address code-review findings on the profiler frame-alignment fix
events.message:
Address code-review findings on the profiler frame-alignment fix

A review of the three prior commits (flame-graph anchor fix + frame
alignment fix) surfaced 8 findings, all addressed:

Correctness:
- Guard against a single throwaway retro_run() call crossing more than one
  true frame boundary: a new g_wprofMarkersAllowed flag (set only after the
  throwaway call returns) prevents a second crossing from emitting a
  spurious inter-frame marker that would zero g_wprofRegEnabled and lose
  register-trace data for the whole capture.
- buildSampleSlots' anchor search now requires a candidate's next few
  samples to also resolve nearby before accepting it, instead of trusting
  the single earliest match unconditionally — guards against an isolated
  coincidental same-address occurrence (e.g. a shared subroutine an
  interrupt handler also calls) winning over the genuine start.
- wasm_profile_emit_frame_marker now returns whether it actually wrote the
  marker; the caller's emitted-count only advances on success, instead of
  drifting from the buffer's real contents when it's nearly full.

Efficiency:
- g_wprofActive now stays 0 until the precise true-vsync boundary fires
  (not armed-then-rewound), so the throwaway alignment frame does none of
  instrHook's stack-walk/register-snapshot work for data that would just
  be discarded.
- The anchor-candidate search resolves all 32 candidates in one shared
  O(N) pass over the DMA grid instead of 32 independent O(N) scans.

Cleanup:
- Extracted wasm_profile_reset_counters(), shared between
  wasm_profile_prepare() and the boundary hook.
- Extracted wasm_profile_on_frame_boundary() as its own function, keeping
  profiler-capture bookkeeping structurally separate from
  puae_debug_frame_boundary_notify()'s original replay/stepBackFrame
  purpose.

Verified: single-frame and 4-frame captures both show every frame's
CPU-sample anchor exactly matching its DMA grid's true start (vpos 0),
register data still correctly present for frame 0 in both cases. Full
suite (801 unit tests, wasm integration tests including stepBackFrame,
lint) passes.

events.title: Fix profiler frame-boundary markers misaligned for frame 1+ in multi-frame captures
events.message:
Fix profiler frame-boundary markers misaligned for frame 1+ in multi-frame captures

The previous fix (5b9dab5) only corrected frame 0's start: it rewound the
CPU-sample buffer to the true vsync via puae_debug_frame_boundary_notify(),
but the markers separating frame 0/1, 1/2, etc. were still inserted by
frontend_shim.c right after each retro_run() call returned — the same
few-scanlines-late point that made frame 0 imprecise before. That
misattributed each subsequent frame's first few lines to the *previous*
frame's tail (and over-extended that previous frame by the same amount),
reintroducing a small CPU/DMA misalignment on every frame after the first.

Now markers are emitted from the same precise per-vsync hook as the frame 0
reset, tracking how many of them (numFrames - 1) are still owed.

Verified directly: in a fresh 4-frame capture, every frame's CPU-sample
anchor now exactly matches its own DMA grid's true start (vpos 0) — frames
1-3 previously showed a ~0.6% (vpos 1) discrepancy. Full test suite (800
unit tests, wasm integration tests including stepBackFrame/rewind which
share the modified hook, lint) passes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: Fix CPU profiler still missing ~1% of instructions at each frame's start
events.message:
Fix CPU profiler still missing ~1% of instructions at each frame's start

The previous frame-alignment fix armed recording synchronously right after
a "priming" retro_run() call returned, but retro_run() only returns once
the CPU execution loop notices the libretro_frame_end flag — confirmed via
direct instrumentation to happen a few scanlines *after* the true vsync
(vpos wrapping to 0), not at it. So recording was still arming a few lines
late, silently dropping genuinely-executed instructions at the very start
of every capture.

Now: arm recording immediately (at whatever imprecise raster position),
run one throwaway partial frame, and let puae_debug_frame_boundary_notify()
— an existing hook that already fires with exact precision at the true
vsync (previously only used by rewind/stepBack) — rewind the CPU-sample
buffer right at that boundary, discarding whatever accumulated before it.
The DMA/copper grids needed no equivalent change; their own double-buffer
toggle already happens automatically at that same precise point.

Verified directly: "first CPU code fetch anywhere in the grid" now lands
at exactly vpos 0 (was vpos 3) across multiple capture-timing offsets, and
the flame graph's real anchor position improved from ~0.96% to ~0.05% of
the frame. Full test suite (800 unit tests, wasm integration tests
including stepBackFrame/rewind, lint) passes.

events.title: Fix CPU profiler flame graph showing a spurious gap at frame start
events.message:
Fix CPU profiler flame graph showing a spurious gap at frame start

buildSampleSlots (columns.ts) anchored sample 0 to its own address via an
unbounded scan of the whole DMA grid. When that instruction's own fetch was
invisible in the grid (already retired before the very next fetch landed),
the search would latch onto a much-later same-address loop revisit instead
of the true start, rendering a large false gap at the left of the flame
graph for any program with a long-running per-iteration loop. Fixed by
anchoring on whichever of the first ~32 samples resolves earliest in the
grid instead.

Also aligns capture start to the true frame boundary before CPU/DMA
recording arms (wasm_profile_start), so frame 0 always starts at the
raster origin rather than wherever the CPU happened to be when Capture
was invoked.

events.title: Save/load every frame of a multi-frame profiler capture, not just frame 0
events.message:
Save/load every frame of a multi-frame profiler capture, not just frame 0

Saving a .puaeprofile only ever persisted ProfilerManager.getLastRaw()'s
single frame, and the file editor always posted a one-element frames
array -- so reopening a saved multi-frame capture could never show more
than one frame, regardless of how many were actually captured.

.puaeprofile now stores every frame (section names prefixed "f0:",
"f1:", ...; per-frame thumbnail/full-frame JPEG dimensions). No backward
compatibility with the old single-frame layout -- this extension isn't
published, so there's nothing to preserve; decode requires the current
format outright.

ProfilerManager.getLastRaw() -> getAllRaw() (RawCapture[]); saveProfile()
persists them all. On load, profileLoader.ts rebuilds every frame via a
new buildFramesFromCaptures(), extracted from ProfilerManager.capture()'s
live multi-frame loop so both paths share one implementation: frame 0
keeps its real disassembly, later frames reweight it, exactly as a live
capture already does. combineFrames() (the all-frames combined model)
and buildFrameRangeModel() (shift-click sub-range selection) are
similarly extracted and now shared between a live session and a loaded
file -- a loaded multi-frame document's filmstrip behaves identically to
a live capture's, including range selection, which previously could
never even be reached in the file editor (frames.length was always 1).

Regenerated the replay fixtures against the real captured bytes (using
puae/kick34005.A500, now available locally): migrated template.puaeprofile
to the new format in place, and built a new template-multiframe.puaeprofile
(two frames of genuine captured profile/DMA/copper data) with replay
coverage for independent per-frame decode and the combined model.

events.title: Preserve real aspect ratio in multi-frame profiler filmstrip thumbnails
events.message:
Preserve real aspect ratio in multi-frame profiler filmstrip thumbnails

wasm_profile_save_thumbnail() downscaled each frame into a fixed 160x100
buffer using independent x/y scale factors, stretching whatever the real
framebuffer's aspect ratio is (~320x256, ~1.25:1 for a typical PAL screen)
to fill that box's 1.6:1 shape -- squashing every multi-frame capture's
filmstrip thumbnails. The single-frame capture path (getFramebuffer in
rpc.ts) already computed its thumbnail size from the real aspect ratio,
so this was a batch-path-only regression relative to that.

Since every frame in one capture shares a single screen resolution (the
same assumption g_wprofFullFrames already relies on), the actual
thumbnail size (g_wprofThumbW/H) is now computed once from frame 0 by
scaling uniformly (one factor for both axes) to fit within a
WASM_THUMB_MAX_W x WASM_THUMB_MAX_H bound -- that bound now just caps
storage, it isn't the stored shape. wasm_profile_get_thumb_w()/_h() and
the per-frame pointer stride report the real per-capture size, which
rpc.ts already queries once and applies to every frame. No JS changes
needed: the filmstrip CSS already renders each thumbnail at its own
intrinsic aspect ratio (height: 52px; width: auto).

events.title: Fix stale pre-AGA BusOwner ordinals in the thumbnail DMA usage bar
events.message:
Fix stale pre-AGA BusOwner ordinals in the thumbnail DMA usage bar

computeDmaBar (the little stacked bar drawn under each profiler filmstrip
thumbnail) classified DMA cells by hardcoded BusOwner ordinal ranges that
predate AGA support. Adding BPL7/BPL8 shifted SPRITE0-7/COPPER/BLITTER/
BLOCKED up by 2 (see BusOwner's comment in profilerTypes.ts), but this one
classifier was never updated to match, unlike every other BusOwner
consumer in the codebase.

Concretely: BLITTER (25) matched none of the stale ranges and fell into
the near-transparent idle bucket, so the blitter never showed a bar at
all. COPPER (24) was silently merged into the CPU bucket, SPRITE6/7
(22/23) were mislabeled as Copper/Blitter-colored segments, and BPL7/BPL8
(14/15) were miscounted as sprites.

Switched the classification to reference the BusOwner enum directly
instead of magic numbers, so it can't drift out of sync again.

events.title: Scale the CPU profile buffer per frame, not once for the whole multi-frame capture
events.message:
Scale the CPU profile buffer per frame, not once for the whole multi-frame capture

g_wprofBuf held the entire multi-frame capture's decoded-instruction
stream in one fixed-size static array, reset once per capture rather
than per frame. 76438d8 cut its cap 4x (4MB/~174k samples -> 1MB/~43k
samples) reasoning only about a single frame's worst case, but the
cap is actually shared across all N frames of a multi-frame capture:
once busy frames exhausted it partway through, later samples AND the
frame-boundary markers themselves were silently dropped, so a 10-frame
capture could come back as 6 frames, with the frame where the cap hit
missing its CPU data entirely.

g_wprofBuf is now allocated per capture in wasm_profile_prepare(numFrames)
at numFrames * WASM_PROFILE_BUF_WORDS_PER_FRAME -- one frame's worth of
headroom for every frame actually requested, matching the existing
per-frame allocation pattern already used for the DMA/copper/full-frame
buffers in frontend_shim.c. Single-frame captures are unaffected (same
1MB/frame budget as before).

events.title: buggyboy: inline the screen-fill cell copy (snappy leg-select menu)
events.message:
buggyboy: inline the screen-fill cell copy (snappy leg-select menu)

screen_fill_span/_rect copied each 8-byte colour cell with a memcpy call, so a
full-screen fill was ~1900 jsr-memcpy calls (3 stack pushes + cleanup each),
every frame. draw_leg_results full-screen-clears on every leg-select frame, so
this dominated the menu's frame time and made arrow-key stepping sluggish (the
3-frame auto-repeat felt slow at the depressed frame rate).

Copy the cell inline as two longwords via the be32/wr32 accessors (native move.l
on the 68000, byte-order-safe on the little-endian test host). The inner loop is
now two move.l per cell, no call. Speeds up every fill (menu, results, HUD,
race backgrounds). All 253 differential tests stay byte-identical; verified on
Hatari: leg-select is now as snappy as the original.

events.title: buggyboy: fix Crawio wrapper reading high word of its arg (F-keys, ESC)
events.message:
buggyboy: fix Crawio wrapper reading high word of its arg (F-keys, ESC)

The Crawio wrapper did `move.w 4(%sp)` to fetch its `short w` argument, but the
C ABI passes `short` in a 4-byte slot — on big-endian m68k the value sits in the
LOW word (6(%sp)), so it read the high word (0x0000) instead of 0x00ff. GEMDOS
Crawio(0) writes a NUL char and returns 0, so every console poll silently did
nothing: leg-select F1-F5 (console scancode) and the in-race ESC-to-quit both
went through it and were dead. Read the longword and push its low word, the same
idiom Fcreate/Fopen already use. Verified on Hatari: F1 starts a leg, ESC quits.
events.author: ganneheim

events.title: buggyboy: make the on-target PRG run at ~ST speed (native-endian access)
events.message:
buggyboy: make the on-target PRG run at ~ST speed (native-endian access)

The playable PRG ran ~4x too slow on a stock 8 MHz ST — menu and race alike,
independent of render_road. Root cause: the big-endian image accessors
(be16/be32/wr16/wr32 in machine.h) compiled to a byte-by-byte lsl-#8 shuffle
on EVERY multi-byte access in every draw/blit routine. Those helpers exist to
preserve the 68000's byte order on the little-endian test host, but the m68k
target is itself big-endian, so there they are just aligned move.w/move.l.

Fixes (PRG-only; the differential harness is untouched — 253 tests still green):
- machine.h: #if __BYTE_ORDER__ == __ORDER_BIG_ENDIAN__ -> native aligned
  load/store on-target; keep the byte assembly on the little-endian host so the
  verified behaviour is byte-identical. Kills the shuffle (PRG ~40% smaller).
- game_build.sh: -O2 (was -Os) + -fno-tree-loop-distribute-patterns (stop GCC
  turning the hand-written mem* loops into self-calls).
- game_main.c: long-word memcpy/memset when aligned.

Also fixes the apparent screen-shift, which was frame-overrun tearing: with the
frame back inside the 20 ms vblank budget, flip_screen latches cleanly.

Tooling:
- oracle shim/emu: expose osh_num_insns() — per-run instruction count for
  perf profiling (read-only, additive; how render_road/menu costs were measured).

Docs: render/atari/README Performance note (endian gotcha + --cpuclock), and a
machine.h pointer in recreate/README.

events.title: buggyboy: playable PRG shim + toolchain fixes (boots, loads, unpacks on ST)
events.message:
buggyboy: playable PRG shim + toolchain fixes (boots, loads, unpacks on ST)

Builds the whole verified reconstruction into a runnable GEMDOS .PRG (game_main.c
game loop + game_os.s traps/hardware), extending the static-screen render/atari path.
Now boots on real TOS in Hatari, loads COURSES.DAT/GRAPHICS.GRA (handle 64), and
completes g_unpack_graphics on-target. Remaining: a hang in the in-race render frame
loop (tracked next).

Reconstruction:
- game_main.c: mirrors decomp.c main() — user-mode file load + unpack, then Super()
  for the hardware phase; strong overrides of the (now weak) no-op boundary glue
  (g_flip_screen video-base flip, g_wait_vbl_set_offset, g_xbios_setpalette,
  g_set_rez/read_joystick/install_handlers IKBD path, g_load_graphics); VBL sound
  driver via _vblqueue; SMOKE build (-DSMOKE=N) for headless framebuffer verification.
- game_os.s: GEMDOS/XBIOS wrappers + IKBD joystick-packet handler. File-I/O wrappers
  MUST precede the control wrappers or Hatari GEMDOS-HD returns handle 0 (stdin).
- src/screen.c, src/road.c: mark g_flip_screen / g_wait_vbl_set_offset BB_WEAK so the
  PRG can override them; harness .so keeps one definition (253 tests still green).

Harness/toolchain:
- tos.ld: ALIGN(256) before .bss + .bss (NOLOAD) SUBALIGN(1) so a 256-aligned image
  symbol can't push .bss past text+data (was silently corrupting BSS on-target).
- mkprg.py: pad text to _bss_start so GEMDOS places BSS exactly after text+data.
- game_build.sh / game_run.sh / game_smoke.py: build, GUI run, headless verify.

Docs:

events.message:
fix(settings): Reset All wipes all storage, not just known keys

Reset settings > All only re-applied defaults to the enumerated setting
keys; it never cleared cached ROM images (IndexedDB rom-<model>), ROM
label keys, saved media, or any unknown/stale key. A corrupt cached ROM
was therefore un-clearable from the UI and could hang a machine at boot.

Add factoryReset() which clears the whole localStorage and deletes the
entire IndexedDB database, then reload after it so the app rebuilds from
defaults and re-fetches ROMs from the CDN. Guarded by a confirm() since
it also drops saved disks/tapes/snapshots.

events.title: buggyboy: add COURSES.DAT course editor + verified road/game viewers
events.message:
buggyboy: add COURSES.DAT course editor + verified road/game viewers

A new projects/buggyboy/editor/ toolkit to decode, edit and visualise
COURSES.DAT, built on the verified reconstruction (libbuggyboy.so).

Decode / edit (stdlib only):
- course_format.py  file<->memory map + 8-byte record decoder (constants
  mirrored from the verified C, each tagged with its source symbol)
- course_file.py    patch-in-place editor: markers, mask, control(rows/slope),
  scroll table, dashboard track pixels; backup-on-save, lossless round-trip
- roadprofile.py    decode the road elevation profile (segment slope + rows)
  and the roadside-object slots from the record stream
- decode_course.py  CLI stream/scroll/marker dump

Findings (empirical, pinned by tests): each 8-byte record = 15-bit select
mask + control (rows = (b&0xf8)>>3, slope = (b&7)-3) + marker word (bit15 =
event; runs = continuous features). Elevation is in the file; the horizontal
curve is runtime steering state (not in the file).

Visualise (drives the verified cores via ctypes):
- tui.py       curses editor: record browser, live dashboard-map paint,
  road elevation profile w/ live slope edit, PNG + live in-terminal 3rd-person
- roadview.py  render_road -> PNG/ASCII; GameSession drives init_leg +
  game_update + draw_frame (the whole verified game)
- roadwin.py   playable pygame window: held keys -> game_update/draw_frame,
  authentic road + object sprites + buggy + HUD (real pixels)

test_roundtrip.py: 14 tests (identity + edit round-trips, map/profile decode,
render pipeline); optional pygame/.so tests skip cleanly when absent.

from the real entry via a staged abort; the Phase-A/B/D counter
arithmetic by mid-function entry + checkpoints; the phase-step return
codes asserted directly (the image diff can't see them). The unbounded

events.title: buggyboy: reconstruct + verify game_update @ 0x1110e (89/91)
events.message:
buggyboy: reconstruct + verify game_update @ 0x1110e (89/91)

The per-frame in-race game-logic driver — the root of the three remaining
orchestrators (intermission + init_playfield both call it). No OS traps and it
returns each frame, so it verifies run-to-rts against the Musashi oracle despite
being the largest single function (2452 bytes, ~50 state globals + 7 tables).

Reconstruction (src/game_update.c, sections mirror the decomp)
- 1-11 (common path): pending-marker gate + engine-sound; input; fire ->
  dashboard-variant anim; bonus-time countdown; lean-anim + spin overrides;
  crash/auto-steer script vs live steering; engine-RPM/speed model + EGFREQ;
  scroll speed + view-flags wrap; wheel position + lean; road-curve integration,
  edge clamp, off-road crash; then build_road_geometry + return.
- 12 (course advance, view-wrap frames): collision probe, road_seg_data +
  road_curve_tbl shuffles, packed course-record unpack (control-code expansion),
  sprite-mode dispatch (scroll/palette), fx-block rebuild, event-jump-table
  dispatch, and the checkpoint/collision/score markers.
- gu_dispatch_event: table-driven event-jump-table dispatch to the evt_* family
  (evt_flag_gate alt entries; score-message groups A/B/C with per-entry gate +
  delta -> add_score + play_event_tune(8); checkpoint counters).

Test (test/test_game_update.py, ~580 cases; poison off — game_update is a
stateful RMW function, so the plain whole-image diff is the correct check)
- common-path fuzz (400); course else/pull/modes/crash/course fuzz; event

events.title: Fix TypeError crash on an incomplete bit-op source line
events.message:
Fix TypeError crash on an incomplete bit-op source line

instructionAttrs's bit-op (bchg/bset/bclr/btst) branch accessed
parsed.operands[1].value with only an optional-chain guard on
`operands` itself, not on index 1. parseLine explicitly tolerates
incomplete lines (its own docstring says so, for "as you type"
editing), so a bit-op with only one operand entered so far (e.g.
"btst d0" before the destination operand is typed) has
operands.length === 1, and indexing [1] reads undefined --
.value then throws. Reachable during normal editing, not a rare
edge case. Added the missing guard and a regression test.

events.title: Fix disassemble() returning more rows than requested, and other bugs
events.message:
Fix disassemble() returning more rows than requested, and other bugs

- disassemble() violated the DAP disassemble contract (must return
  exactly `count` rows): when a negative instructionOffset needed
  padding rows for addresses before available memory, the code pushed
  the padding AND then still sliced `count` more instructions,
  returning count+paddingCount rows instead of count. Reachable via
  ordinary UI scrolling near the start of available memory, not an
  edge case. Also capped padding itself at `count` for the case where
  the negative offset alone would need more padding than the whole
  request budget.
- MAX_BYTES_PER_INSTRUCTION was 8, but 68k's true worst case is 10
  bytes (e.g. MOVE.L $12345678.L,$12345678.L -- long-absolute source
  and destination, not rare in code addressing hardware registers
  directly). Undersizing it could under-fetch the backward-estimate
  buffer and fail to find baseAddress in the decoded output at all.
- Padding rows carried a placeholder addr:0, which is a meaningful
  Amiga address (reset SP/PC vectors) -- if the source map has any
  entry covering it, a padding row (meant to represent unavailable
  data) could get a plausible-but-bogus symbol/location attached.
  Skip the source-map lookup for padding rows specifically.

An existing test asserted the old buggy row-count behavior as
correct; fixed it to match the DAP contract and added a case for the
padding-exceeds-count edge.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: grahambates

events.title: Fix breakpoint/watchpoint tracking corruption on emulator-call failure
events.message:
Fix breakpoint/watchpoint tracking corruption on emulator-call failure

Every "set breakpoints" method (source, instruction, function, data,
temp) pushed its new tracking entry into the corresponding array/map
BEFORE the await that arms it in the emulator, with no rollback on
failure. A failed setBreakpoint/setWatchpoint/setRegisterWatch call
(e.g. a transient RPC error) left a phantom entry permanently tracked:
invisible to the DAP client (never in any removal loop), unremovable,
and able to misroute a later real breakpoint/hit at the same address
through the wrong code path.

Also: setInstructionBreakpoints and setFunctionBreakpoints had no
try/catch at all, so a single failed setBreakpoint call aborted the
whole batch instead of reporting that one breakpoint as unverified.
The custom-chipset-register data breakpoint path (one DAP variable
that can need two underlying watchpoints at different addresses) now
rolls back the first watchpoint if the second fails, instead of
leaving it live in the emulator but untracked. Every removal loop
(source/instruction/function/data/register-watch) now catches each
individual removal failure so one bad removal doesn't abort the
array/map reset that follows it, leaving later entries stuck in a
"removed on the emulator side but still tracked" state.

buggyboy: reconstruct + verify object-sprite helper family @ 0x14620

Reconstruction (object-type sprite-draw helpers; not among the original 91 —
part of the draw_object_list handler block):
- draw_obj_sprite_hi @ 0x14620 (60 bytes) — derives blit geometry from a
  per-object descriptor record (A2) + view_flags, sets the per-row stride/mode
  word at blit_mode (0x18cb0), and calls the verified blit_objshift; models the
  68000 movem D3/D5 -> D0/D4 register rename around the call.
- draw_obj_handler_dbl @ 0x1465c (8 bytes) — colour-preserving double draw
  (mode 8 then the 0xa8 tail), sharing draw_obj_sprite_hi + draw_obj_blit_tail.
- draw_obj_handler_lo @ 0x14664 (18 bytes) — dst = A6 + 0x3ac0, src += a
  per-parity record word, single 0xa8 tail.
- draw_obj_blit_tail @ 0x14676 — shared tail (mode 0xa8, then blit_objshift).
- Corrected the generated spec: the blit runs with A0 = the (-xoff,+voff)
  scanline base (movea.l a0,a2 leaves A0), and A2/dst-top is restored to A0

events.title: Fix unbounded growth of VariablesManager's handle maps
events.message:
Fix unbounded growth of VariablesManager's handle maps

variableHandles/locationHandles and their backing context maps
(localsContextByRef/structPtrByRef/arrayByRef) were created once per
session and never pruned -- every getScopes() call (once per stop) and
every struct/array/pointer expansion added entries with nothing ever
removing them, growing unbounded over a long debug session. Per the
DAP spec a variablesReference is only valid until the next stop event
(VS Code always re-fetches rather than reusing a stale one), so
there's no reason to keep them past that point -- added
VariablesManager.reset() and call it from stackTraceRequest (called
once per stop), alongside the adapter's own existing analogous
frameIdToPc.clear().

events.message:
Cap .puaeprofile decompressed size against a gzip bomb

decodeCapture's gunzipSync had no output-size limit, even though a
.puaeprofile is loaded from disk and may not have been created by the
current user. gzip's compression ratio is effectively unbounded, so a
crafted few-KB file could expand to gigabytes before any of the
existing manifest/section bounds checks got a chance to run. Passes
maxOutputLength (generous relative to any real capture, which tops out
around a few MB) so an oversized payload throws cleanly instead --
already caught by profileEditorProvider.ts's existing try/catch around

events.title: Fix cache-invalidation race on concurrent reads during a mutating RPC
events.message:
Fix cache-invalidation race on concurrent reads during a mutating RPC

Every mutating method (pause/run/step*/jump/setRegister/pokeCustom*)
invalidated the CPU-info/custom-register cache before sending its RPC,
but not after. A getCpuInfo()/getAllCustomRegisters() call already in
flight when a mutation starts can resolve after the pre-mutation
invalidation, repopulating the cache with pre-mutation data with
nothing left to invalidate it again -- serving stale register values
to every subsequent read until an unrelated mutation happens to race
favorably. Added a second invalidation in a `finally` once each
mutating RPC resolves.

events.title: Fix DWARF5 header parsing masking truncation, and two hang risks
events.message:
Fix DWARF5 header parsing masking truncation, and two hang risks

parseLineNumberProgram used `elfBuffer[offset++] || default` for
several DWARF5-only header fields (address_size, segment_selector_size,
maximum_operations_per_instruction, directory/file_entry_format_count).
`||` fires whenever the read is out-of-bounds too (elfBuffer[offset]
reads back `undefined` on a truncated buffer), silently substituting a
fabricated default and letting parsing continue past the real end of
the section with made-up header values -- inconsistent with the rest
of the function, which already throws on an out-of-bounds read for
minimumInstructionLength/lineRange/opcodeBase. Replaced with a
readU8-or-throw helper.

While in the same function: the DWARF2-4 directory/file-name loops
(`while (elfBuffer[offset] !== 0)`) had no bounds check in their own
condition -- once offset ran past a truncated buffer, elfBuffer[offset]
reads back `undefined` forever (never `0`) and readString on an
out-of-bounds offset returns a 0-length string rather than throwing,
so the loop would spin forever. Added an explicit offset < length
check.

Also added a depth cap to parseDIE's recursion: a corrupted abbreviation
table with no real null-DIE terminators could otherwise nest recursion
deep enough to hit a stack-overflow RangeError instead of a clean parse
error.

events.title: Fix silent data corruption and crash risks in debug-info parsers
events.message:
Fix silent data corruption and crash risks in debug-info parsers

- dwarfParser.ts readULEB128/readSLEB128: replace `|=`/`<<` (which
  coerce to 32-bit ints and wrap mod 32 once shift exceeds 31, i.e. a
  5+ byte encoding / values >= 2^28) with plain arithmetic, which stays
  exact up to JS's 2^53 safe-integer range. Previously any oversized
  length/offset field in a corrupted DWARF section silently produced a
  wrong (possibly negative) decoded value instead of erroring or
  decoding correctly.
- amigaHunkParser.ts BufferReader.readString: stop spreading a
  charCodes array into String.fromCharCode(...charCodes) -- `length`
  is an unbounded file-supplied field (HUNK_SYMBOL name length,
  HUNK_DEBUG LINE filename length), and a large enough one throws
  "RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded" instead of a clean
  parse error. Reads the string directly off the buffer instead.
- amigaHunkParser.ts parseHeader: the `tableSize < 0 || ... < 0`
  validation was dead code (readLong() is always unsigned); replaced
  with the real invariant (lastHunk < firstHunk), which previously
  produced a silently-empty hunk table instead of an error.
- amigaHunkParser.ts parseDebug (LINE format): validate the derived
  line-entry count is a non-negative even number before looping,
  instead of silently under-reading and desyncing the reader for every
  subsequent block in the hunk.

events.title: Fix missing error handling on Continue/Pause and stuck stepping state on failure
events.message:
Fix missing error handling on Continue/Pause and stuck stepping state on failure

continueRequest/pauseRequest/customRequest had no try/catch, unlike every
other DAP request handler -- a rejected emulator.run()/pause() call left
the request promise rejecting with no response ever sent, so Continue/
Pause appeared to just hang in the UI instead of surfacing an error.
Wired them to the already-defined but unused CONTINUE_ERROR/PAUSE_ERROR
codes.

Separately, every place that sets `this.stepping`/`this.isRunning` before
an awaited stepInto()/run() call left those flags stuck true if the call
rejected, since a failed step produces no "stopped" state message to
reset them via the normal handleStep()/handleStop() path. The next
unrelated stop (e.g. a real breakpoint hit while running) would then be
misrouted through handleStep() instead of handleStop(), silently
discarding the real stop reason. Reset the flags in a local catch before
rethrowing at each of the three call sites (stepInRequest,
doInstructionStepOver, and handleStep's line-granularity retry).

The 6px glyph extractor leaves bits 1-0 (the inter-character gap) blank, but the
inverted font sets them, so inverse-video glyphs missed by 2 bits/line — past the
match tolerance. Mask the glyph comparison to the 6 significant bits (0xFC) so
inverse video matches; normal text is unaffected (its gap bits are already 0).

events.title: fix(einstein): detect OCR font offset per MOS version; blank cells to backdrop
events.message:
fix(einstein): detect OCR font offset per MOS version; blank cells to backdrop

The font offset differs between MOS versions (1.2 @ 0x106D, 1.21 @ 0x107A). The
CDN-hosted ROM is 1.2, so the hardcoded 1.21 offset made the OCR match against
the wrong glyphs (punctuation especially). Detect the font offset at runtime
(findFontOffset scans for the blank space glyph + plausible letter/punctuation
pixel counts) and cache it per ROM.

Also: the TEXT overlay's cell-blanking filled matched cells with palette[0]
(black) when the cell background was colour 0 (transparent). On the TMS9918A a
transparent pixel shows the backdrop, so resolve colour-0 fg/bg to the backdrop
(R7 low nibble) — matched cells now blank to the real paper colour (e.g. blue).

Recover the Einstein's screen text by extracting each character from VRAM and

The system font is 6 wide × 8 high drawn at a 6px pitch, so glyphs straddle the
VDP's 8px pattern cells — the OCR reconstructs the pixels and reads 6px-wide
glyphs at that pitch (which line up bit-for-bit with the font's top 6 bits).

events.title: Fix cross-platform path-key matching in source/profiler lookups
events.message:
Fix cross-platform path-key matching in source/profiler lookups

SourceMap, ProfilerCodeLensProvider, and ProfilerLineDecorationProvider
keyed file paths with the platform-native path.normalize(), which only
treats a host's own separator as a path separator. On a POSIX host that
left "C:\proj\a.c" and "c:/proj/A.C" as distinct keys instead of the
same file, breaking lookups whenever debug info carries Windows-style
paths (this project's toolchain runs via WSL from a Windows checkout)
on a non-Windows dev machine. Switched all three to path.win32.normalize,
which always treats both separators as equivalent regardless of
process.platform.

events.title: fix(einstein): don't alias I/O ports A6/A7 — XtalDOS 1.31 boots
events.message:
fix(einstein): don't alias I/O ports A6/A7 — XtalDOS 1.31 boots

The port decoder masked the address with & 0x3F, so 0x40-0xFF aliased onto the
0x00-0x3F device block (e.g. 0x48/0x49 -> the VDP at 0x08/0x09). XtalDOS 1.31
writes to 0x48/0x49, which corrupted the VDP mode register (R0 0x02 -> 0x60,
flipping Graphics II to Graphics I) and blanked the screen. Games don't touch
those ports, so they were unaffected.

The on-board devices decode at 0x00-0x3F with A6=A7=0; add a guard so ports with
A6/A7 set are unmapped. XtalDOS 1.31 (einstein-xbas.dsk) now boots to its ◇:
prompt in Graphics II; MOS and XtalDOS 1.11 still render correctly.

events.title: feat(einstein): Z80 CTC clock-chain for real interrupts
events.message:
feat(einstein): Z80 CTC clock-chain for real interrupts

Implement the CTC's periodic-interrupt path per MAME's Einstein wiring: channels
0-2 are clocked at 2MHz (inputClockDivide from the 4MHz CPU feed) and each
channel's zero-count can be chained to another's trigger. Wire channel 2's ZC to
channel 3's trigger (zc2 -> trg3); channel 3 is the interrupt source, serviced in
IM 2. This drives the ~50Hz/RTC ticks software (BASIC, cursor blink) expects.
Verified the MOS sign-on and XtalDOS boot still render correctly with the chain
active.

events.title: feat(einstein): disk support — boots Xtal DOS from .dsk
events.message:
feat(einstein): disk support — boots Xtal DOS from .dsk

Einstein disk images are Extended CPC DSK (40 trk, 10x512 sectors, IDs read
from the track headers), so the existing parseDSK/parseFloppyImage handles them.
Route .dsk/.hfe/.scp through machine.loadDisk in emulator.ts (loadFile,
loadDiskToUnit, loadableExtensions), and call fdc.tickFrame() each frame.

Fix the drive-select latch (port 0x23) per MAME's drsel_w: one-hot drive select
on bits 0-3 (0x01 = drive 0), side on bit 4, no motor/density bit.

WD179x: add an opt-in Type I BUSY pulse (pulseBusy). The MOS polls the WD1770
for BUSY to *set* (command-accepted handshake) before waiting for it to clear;
the previous instant-completion model never asserted BUSY, so RESTORE timed out
and the boot aborted. The flag defaults off (so the +D/Beta instant-completion
model is unchanged) and the Einstein enables it. Verified against the real MOS
1.21 + a system .dsk: Ctrl-BREAK now loads the boot tracks and chains into
TATUNG/XtalDOS 1.11 (its drive prompt renders).

UI: show the Drives pane for the Einstein (drive A:/B: = WD1770 units 0/1) and
hide the Mouse pane (the Einstein has no mouse).

events.title: fix(einstein): correct CTC interrupt wiring; verified real MOS 1.21 boot
events.message:
fix(einstein): correct CTC interrupt wiring; verified real MOS 1.21 boot

MAME confirms the TMS9929A VDP interrupt is NOT wired to the CPU on the TC-01:
the VDP vblank only sets a status flag the MOS polls, while CPU interrupts come
from the Z80 CTC (2MHz-clocked, ch2->ch3 chain) and the keyboard. Remove the
incorrect VDP->ctc.trigger(0) routing; keep the pollable VDP vblank flag and the
timer-driven CTC path (advanced by ctc.addCycles). Full CTC clock-chain fidelity
(baud, RTC tick, cursor blink) is a follow-up — the MOS monitor runs by polling.

Retarget the interrupt integration test to a CTC timer channel (the real path).

Verified against the genuine MOS 1.21 ROM (CRC a746eeb6) headlessly: boots
pixel-correct to the '*** EINSTEIN *** / TATUNG/Xtal MOS 1.21 / Ready >' monitor
prompt, and typed keystrokes echo and are processed through the AY keyboard.

events.title: Anchor flame-graph CPU columns to their real DMA slot
events.message:
Anchor flame-graph CPU columns to their real DMA slot

CPU boxes were positioned by cycle-cost fraction (timeOffset/duration),
while the DMA/blitter bands use the DMA grid's own slot index — two
independent clocks with different origins. The cycle-cost timeline only
starts counting from the first sampled (in-program) instruction of the
capture, silently dropping any real time spent in interrupts/OS calls
before that point, so CPU boxes drifted from where the DMA/blit bands
(correctly) place the same instant — most visibly at the first blit of
a frame.

Instead, match each sample's PC against the grid's own CPU instruction-
fetch cells (owner==CPU, DMA_CODE flag) to recover its true slot, walking
both streams in execution order. Falls back to the old cycle-fraction
estimate when there's no DMA data to anchor to.

events.title: feat(disk): SuperCard Pro (.scp) flux images with weak-sector fidelity
events.message:
feat(disk): SuperCard Pro (.scp) flux images with weak-sector fidelity

Add read-only .scp support for the +3/CPC (uPD765A) and Beta Disk / +D
(WD179x). SCP is a flux format one layer below HFE: a software data separator
(PLL) recovers MFM bit-cells from the raw flux timings, which are then fed to
the existing decodeHfeTrack decoder verbatim (cells → sectors).

The point of flux over HFE is copy-protection fidelity: all revolutions are
decoded and a sector whose data varies across revolutions is attached as a weak
DskSector.copies[] (which the uPD765A already picks from at random).

Track mapping derives the cylinder step as the gcd of gaps between present
tracks — a 3" 40-cyl disk is stored at even physical slots 0,2,..,84 with odd
slots absent — so cyl = (track - start) / step. Wired like .hfe: parseFloppyImage
content-detection (works at every mount site incl. ZIPs), the Beta/+D load and
restore paths, media-manager + mcp/loader dispatch, and the drive pickers.

Validated against the greaseweazle oracle: Dark-Side decodes 360/360 sectors
byte-identical to its .hfe; Amstrad-Bundle surfaces 3 genuine weak sectors the
single-revolution HFE cannot. Real protected +3 games (Dark Side, Double Dragon
II) boot to a bit-identical framebuffer from .scp vs .hfe.

events.title: feat(beta): Beta Disk / TR-DOS support (WD1793, TRD/SCL/HFE)
events.message:
feat(beta): Beta Disk / TR-DOS support (WD1793, TRD/SCL/HFE)

Add the Beta Disk interface (TR-DOS) for the 48K/128K/+2, alongside the
existing +D. Refactor the +D's WD1772 into a shared WD179x base class with
WD1772 and WD1793 subclasses (the base defaults are the +D's behaviour, so
WD1772 stays byte-identical). The WD1793 differs only in status bit 7
(NOT-READY vs MOTOR-ON), a 16-sector format, and exposed INTRQ/DRQ.

BetaDisk peripheral uses the Beta 128 auto-paging model: the 16KB TR-DOS ROM
maps in on an M1 fetch in 0x3D00-0x3DFF (while the 48K BASIC ROM is active)
and out at >= 0x4000. Ports 0x1F/0x3F/0x5F/0x7F/0xFF match Fuse beta.c, gated
on pagedIn so 0xFF never steals the keyboard. System register (0xFF): drive
b0-1, HLT b3, side b4 (inverted -- bit set = side 0), density b5, no reset bit.

New TRD and SCL parsers build the shared DskImage (geometry from the disk-info
sector; truncated images padded); HFE works via the existing decoder. Mutually
exclusive with the +D / Interface 1; reuses the C/D drive-state signals
(relabelled A:/B:), separate persistence keys and settings flag. MCP betadisk
tool + .trd/.scl loader dispatch. ROM hosted at trdos.rom.

events.title: feat(hfe): support creating a new blank HFE disk
events.message:
feat(hfe): support creating a new blank HFE disk

Add a from-scratch MFM track encoder so a brand-new blank disk can be
created as a track-level HFE image, not just a DSK. encodeHfeTrack lays
down the standard IBM System 34 double-density track (index mark, per
sector sync/A1/IDAM/CHRN+CRC/gap2/DAM/data/CRC/gap3) using the same clock
rule as the existing write-back path, so createBlankHfe/attachHfeBitstream
produce an image that decodes byte-identically to the DSK blank, saves as
.hfe, and round-trips writes through serializeHFE.

Wire it into the UI: the +3/CPC new-disk menu gains DSK/HFE submenus for
every format, and the +D drives gain a blank-800K-HFE option
(insertBlankPlusDDisk now takes an asHfe flag).

events.message:
buggyboy: IKBD memory model + verify read_joystick (60/91)

Phase 1 of the input-oracle work (HARNESS.md). read_joystick busy-waits the IKBD
6850 ACIA's TDRE bit at $fffffc00 then sends the 0x16 joystick-interrogate command;
under the oracle it used to spin forever because reads above the 1 MiB image returned
0, so the bit was never set.

- oracle/shim.c: model IKBD_STATUS ($fffc00 on the 24-bit bus) as always TDRE-ready,
  so the wait loop terminates. The command write to IKBD_DATA lands above the image
  and is dropped by the existing bounds check (no capture needed — input state is
  scripted as an image global, see HARNESS.md), so read_joystick has no image effect.
- src/os.c: g_read_joystick — no-op glue (like xbios_setscreen).
- test/test_input.py: run-to-rts, empty whole-image diff (reaching rts is the check).

events.title: feat(hfe): HFE write-back — save a mutated HFE back to HFE
events.message:
feat(hfe): HFE write-back — save a mutated HFE back to HFE

serializeHFE() re-encodes writes into a copy of the retained bitstream
rather than rebuilding tracks from scratch: decodeHfeTrack now records
each sector's data-field bit position (HfeBitstream.layout), and save
splices only the sectors whose data actually changed back into the
cells (payload + recomputed CRC, over the same cell span so gaps/marks
stay put). Unwritten fields — including protection tracks with odd
gaps, deleted marks or deliberately bad CRCs — are preserved verbatim;
an unwritten disk round-trips identically.

saveDisk / savePlusDDisk write .hfe (via serializeHFE) for HFE-sourced
disks and .dsk/.mgt otherwise. The FDC cores are untouched — writes go
through the existing writeBackSector into the decoded track, and
reconciliation into the bitstream happens only at save time, so the
uPD765A/WD1772 stay free of any HFE-format knowledge.

Verified on real disks: identity round-trip and full protection
preservation on Three-Inch-Loader and Alkatraz titles, with a written
sector reading back exactly. Not covered: formatting/creating a new HFE
(no prior layout) — a follow-up if wanted.

events.title: feat(hfe): native HFE disk support for +3 and CPC via the uPD765A
events.message:
feat(hfe): native HFE disk support for +3 and CPC via the uPD765A

Decode the HFE (HxC) raw MFM bit-cell stream directly the way hardware
does — A1 (0x4489) sync hunt, IDAM/DAM, CRC-16-CCITT, circular track —
into the existing sector-level DskTrack the FDC already consumes. The
HFE bitstream is retained as the disk's identity (new optional
DskImage.bitstream); no DSK file is produced and the DSK code path is
never involved. parseFloppyImage() content-detects HFE vs DSK, so .hfe
and .dsk both work at every uPD765A mount/restore site, incl. inside
ZIPs. Scope: HFE v1 (HXCPICFE), ISO/IBM MFM; v3 is rejected clearly.
The +D/WD1772 is intentionally left for a follow-up.

Decoder fidelity (validated byte-for-byte against hxcfe's own HFE->DSK
conversion of ~48 real greaseweazle dumps, incl. Speedlock/Alkatraz/
Three-Inch-Loader/CPC-format; HFE-vs-DSK boots are framebuffer-identical
on a real +3): reject bad-CRC IDAMs (kill false syncs), cap each data
field at the next sync (a bogus giant-N sector can't swallow the track),
accept 1-3 A1 preamble marks (worn disks emit 2).

Wired: emulator load/route/restore, media-manager, loadableExtensions,
DrivePane picker, drag hint, mcp/loader. New tests build an independent
MFM/HFE encoder from spec and cover the edge cases above.

events.message:
buggyboy: run the reconstructed leg-results screen on a real 68000 (Hatari)

Cross-compile the same C cores to a GEMDOS .PRG and run them under Hatari with a
real TOS ROM; a headless run confirms the on-target framebuffer is byte-identical
to the host render (render_screen.py) — the reconstruction is correct compiled and
executed on an independent 68000, not just against the Musashi oracle.

The cores are unchanged: they compute image+offset and never dereference an
absolute address baked into the binary, so they are position-independent where it
matters. The 1 MiB game image lives in BSS (no Malloc); mkprg.py builds the GEMDOS
reloc table from the ELF's R_68K_32 fixups (ld --emit-relocs).

events.title: recreate: add attribution (poison) pass to catch coincidental passes (#3)
events.message:
recreate: add attribution (poison) pass to catch coincidental passes (#3)

The plain diff proves final-image equivalence, so a candidate can pass by
coincidence: it never writes a byte the oracle wrote, but that byte already
held the oracle's value (an output landing in a zeroed/base region). Add an
opt-in attribution pass that removes the coincidence.

  - harness._attribution_check: re-run both cores on a copy of the input
    where every oracle-written byte is poisoned (its normal final value,
    inverted). A byte the candidate fails to write stays canary instead of
    matching, so the omission surfaces. Gated on differential(poison=True)
    and only after the plain pass is clean (safe for leaf functions;
    poisoning a control-steering output could perturb a complex run).
  - test_poison_catches_coincidental_write: a stub writing 0x00 over a
    zeroed byte with a do-nothing candidate passes the plain diff but is
    caught with poison=True (proves the guard fires).
  - Enable poison on the leaf tests whose outputs aren't pre-seeded:
    add_score edge cases (score_str HUD digits) and the screen fills
    (zeroed draw buffer). README notes the pass.

events.title: recreate: cross-validate Musashi against a real 68000 (ISA conformance, #5)
events.message:
recreate: cross-validate Musashi against a real 68000 (ISA conformance, #5)

The differential suite proves each function matches Musashi; this certifies
Musashi itself against an independent, hardware-validated 68000 (Hatari's
WinUAE core), so "verified against Musashi" means "verified against a real
68000" for the instruction mix BuggyBoy uses.

  - oracle/isa_conformance.py: 277 self-contained, position-independent
    instruction snippets (inputs = immediates, flags captured with move sr
    immediately after the tested op, result saved via (a5)+). Runs the
    identical bytes on Musashi (emu.run) and real TOS (headless Hatari) and
    compares result + defined CCR bits. Classes: byte/word/long memory RMW
    (the class Unicorn mis-handled), asr/lsr/lsl/rox/ro, ext, movea.w,
    muls/mulu/divs/divu, add/sub/addx/subx, cmp.b+Scc, swap/neg.
  - tos_probe.py: extract run_tos_program() (reused by both harnesses).
  - test/test_isa_vs_tos.py: skips without Hatari/TOS; else asserts 277/277.

Result: all 277 match. The only core divergence found was N/Z after a
DIVS/DIVU overflow, which the 68000 PRM defines as *undefined* — so it is
excluded from the CCR comparison (result and the defined V flag still agree).

events.title: recreate: vet diff exclude bands against the oracle's stack extent (#6)
events.message:
recreate: vet diff exclude bands against the oracle's stack extent (#6)

An exclude band suspends the byte-for-byte guarantee for its range, so a
band that dropped a real (non-stack) divergence would pass silently. Vet
every band before use:

  - oracle (shim.c) now tracks the deepest stack pointer reached (min_a7),
    exposed via emu.run's out_regs.
  - _vet_exclude_bands (A) requires the band to extend past min_a7 — a band
    entirely below where A7 descended cannot be stack; (D) rejects a named
    global (names.txt) sitting *below* min_a7 — provably not stack.

Verifying it surfaced a real subtlety: _start relocates its stack across
trace_pc@0x1b040, so a naive "reject any named global" is wrong — a global
the stack sits *over* is legitimately reused as scratch. The check allows
named globals at/above min_a7 and only refuses ones below it. Empirically
the _start band's below-stack bytes are untouched, so it stays sound.

test_exclude_band_guards pins all three cases (A fires, D fires, reuse ok).

events.title: recreate: widen screen + blit fuzz to the register-masking edges
events.message:
recreate: widen screen + blit fuzz to the register-masking edges

The fill and blit tests only fed small, clean values, so the word-vs-long
register handling was asserted by construction (& 0xffff in the test), never
verified against the oracle. The disassembly shows these are word ops:
fill uses lsl.w #3 (colour) + sign-extended adda.w (offset) + dbf (count);
the blit glue takes width/x/row_offset/rows as int16/uint16. So the high 16
bits must be ignored and the colour offset sign-extends (0x1000<<3 = 0x8000).

  - harness.hi_garbage(rng, low_word): pack a low word with random high bits;
    shared by both tests (one definition, not copied).
  - test_screen: full-range colour + high-garbage counts/offsets in the fuzz,
    plus test_register_masking pinning the lsl.w/dbf/adda.w edges (colour
    sign flip, high word ignored) with explicit values.
  - test_blit: splat random high bits on the four word registers (width, x,
    row_offset, rows) while a6/fills stay full 32-bit.

Verified against the asm first (no wider domain that would diverge); all green.
Other suites left as-is: test_road already targets 16-bit overflow, test_events
enumerates discrete branches, test_graphics feeds random source to the shifts.

events.message:
recreate: widen add_score fuzz to the full byte domain

The score fuzz only exercised ASCII digits (0x30..0x39), leaving the
signed-carry edge untested. The disassembly shows the per-digit carry is
a signed cmp.b/bpl against '9' with a manual sub.b #10 (no BCD/decimal-
adjust op anywhere in the binary), so the reconstruction's
(int8_t)('9' - digit) < 0 should hold for every byte, not just digits.

  - test_fuzz now draws full-range bytes (0..255) for score and delta;
    score/delta live in fixed 6-byte buffers, so any value is memory-safe.
  - test_boundary_bytes pins the carry decision at each digit position for
    bytes straddling the flip (0x39/0x3a), the int8 sign boundary
    (0x7f/0x80), the blank-walk char (0x30), and the extremes, plus
    add.l/.w wraparound cases.

events.title: recreate: cross-check the OS trap model against real TOS (headless Hatari)
events.message:
recreate: cross-check the OS trap model against real TOS (headless Hatari)

Anchor the deterministic shim (shim.c + os.h) to a genuine TOS ROM so its
hand-modeled semantics are validated against real hardware, not just
asserted.

Harness:
  - oracle/tos_probe.py assembles a small GEMDOS program that runs Malloc,
    Getrez and a sequence of Freads, writes a fixed-layout record to a
    GEMDOS drive, and Pterm0s. It auto-runs headless under Hatari (SDL
    dummy video, --fast-forward) and reads the record back from the host
    dir — no debugger/breakpoint/load-address needed. Mshrink prologue so
    Malloc has a free pool.
  - test/test_os_vs_tos.py compares the capture to the shim: exact-value
    calls (Getrez low-res, Fread bytes + cursor/EOF counts) must match to
    the byte; Malloc's machine-dependent address is checked as the
    invariant the shim also honors (even-aligned, non-overlapping, odd
    size rounded up to even). Skips when Hatari or a TOS ROM is absent
    (the ROM isn't redistributable).

Docs:
  - README OS-trap section documents the two test layers.
  - docs/tos-os-calls.md adds the reusable headless-Hatari technique.
events.author: ganneheim

events.title: recreate: pin the OS trap model's semantics with shim-contract tests
events.message:
recreate: pin the OS trap model's semantics with shim-contract tests

The existing OS tests validate the reconstructed wrappers through the
differential harness but never stress the shim's own semantics at the
edges. Add five tests that drive tiny hand-assembled 68k stubs through
the oracle to pin shim.c + os.h directly:

  - Malloc bump-allocation + odd-size rounding to even
  - Fread cursor advance, partial read at EOF, zero past EOF
  - Fopen reopen rewinds the cursor
  - Fread on a closed handle is rejected (emu.run raises, not silently served)
  - Fopen of an unstaged file is rejected

A regression in these semantics now fails here instead of silently
inside a caller's differential test.

events.title: buggyboy-sound: add C64 SID transcode of the YM2149 stream
events.message:
buggyboy-sound: add C64 SID transcode of the YM2149 stream

Play BuggyBoy's tunes and effects on a Commodore 64 SID (reSID-fp /
pyresidfp) by transcoding the same per-frame YM register stream the
existing renderer captures. `sound_player.py --synth sid` writes
out/sound/*_sid.wav beside the YM references.

Mapping: YM square -> SID 50% pulse; YM noise -> SID noise, clocked from
the YM noise rate (SID clocks its LFSR from the voice frequency, so using
the stale tone period would silence noise FX); per-channel YM volume and
hardware envelope -> per-voice software amplitude scaling (SID has no
per-voice volume, and this stands in for YM's hardware-envelope "buzz").
Output is AC-coupled and faded in to mimic the real C64 and drop reSID's
reset transient. The envelope AM advances by the samples reSID actually
emits per frame, so it stays aligned to the audio with no drift.

Faithful port of the ST arrangement/timing in SID timbre; not a re-scored
native C64 tune.

events.title: Fix CPU profiler hang/timeout on 68020/030 and fast-RAM captures
events.message:
Fix CPU profiler hang/timeout on 68020/030 and fast-RAM captures

Chases four compounding issues, most severe last: raw TypedArrays sent
over the webview<->extension postMessage bridge get flattened into slow
per-element array-likes (~800ms/MB), so getProfileData/getProfileRegs
now ship base64 strings instead; 68020/030's cycle-exact accounting lets
far more instructions retire per profiled frame than other CPU models
for the same program, so the profile/register buffer caps are now much
tighter; the render loop's wall-clock-based frame pacing could accrue an
unbounded "catch up" backlog after a long synchronous capture call, now
capped; and the emulator was resuming free-running immediately after
wasm_profile_start() returned, competing with the RPC queue throughout
the whole data-retrieval sequence — now the capture explicitly pauses
first and only resumes afterward if it was actually running before.

events.title: fix(resume): reliable refresh resume — sync snapshot save + correct +3 ROM
events.message:
fix(resume): reliable refresh resume — sync snapshot save + correct +3 ROM

Two bugs broke 'resume where you left off' on page refresh:

1. saveHMRState ran in a beforeunload handler but awaited an async
   CompressionStream deflate, so the localStorage write usually never
   completed before teardown — leaving a stale snapshot. Added a synchronous,
   uncompressed SZX writer (saveSZXSync) and made saveHMRState fully sync.

2. restoreHMRState restored the +2A/+3 ROM page with the plain-128K formula
   ((7FFD>>4)&1), ignoring the high ROM bit in 1FFD bit 2. A +3 game using
   ROM 3 resumed into ROM 1, freezing its ROM-dependent interrupt routine
   (silent music, frozen colour/border effects) while input still worked.
   Centralised the bank/ROM restore in a shared applySZXPaging() used by both
   the resume path and the file-load path so they can't drift again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: feat(debug): step into the interrupt handler when the CPU is halted
events.message:
feat(debug): step into the interrupt handler when the CPU is halted

Single-stepping called cpu.step() directly, which never asserts the maskable
interrupt (that only fires at the frame boundary in runFrame). On a HALT the
step just refetched the NOP forever — only R advanced — so the interrupt
service routine was unreachable from the debugger. stepInto/stepOver now
synthesise the frame interrupt when the CPU is halted with interrupts enabled,
landing PC on the first ISR instruction. DI HALTs (waiting on NMI) still spin.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

a4091: emulate 53C710 SCSI loopback pins

The ncr7xx SCSI pin test drives the output latches and reads them back through the bus input registers in loopback mode. Model the A4091 loopback path for SBDL, SBCL, and SSTAT1, and add the missing SOCL write latch.

SCNTL1.ADB now latches instead of aborting the setup write, allowing the loopback reads to observe the driven SODL and SOCL state.

events.title: lsi53c710: reject illegal group-3 SCRIPTS opcodes
events.message:
lsi53c710: reject illegal group-3 SCRIPTS opcodes

The 53C710 only supports Memory Move in SCRIPTS group 3. Opcodes with reserved bits set, including the 53C810+ Load/Store-register forms, should raise DSTAT.IID instead of being executed.

This prevents garbage fetched from non-responding addresses from causing stray DMA or register accesses during the ncr7xx bus access test.

events.title: Replace deprecated noweb toolchain with self-contained weave.py
events.message:
Replace deprecated noweb toolchain with self-contained weave.py

Recent TeX Live releases no longer ship the noweb LaTeX package, and the
noweave/notangle command-line tools are effectively deprecated. Convert the
build to a self-contained Python weaver/tangler plus a vendored noweb.sty,
mirroring the approach used by ali_baba_reveng.

- Add weave.py: a standalone noweb weaver + tangler (stdlib only). It weaves
  main.nw into main.tex using the noweb macros, and tangles the <<*>> root
  chunk into assembly. Adapted for Lode Runner's richer chunk names
  ([[quoted code]], spaces, operators), the zero-indent chunk-use semantics
  the old ignore_preuse_text.py filter provided, and multi-line [[...]] quotes.

events.title: Fix Multiface crash on Return after a second NMI press
events.message:
Fix Multiface crash on Return after a second NMI press

pressButton() called cpu.nmi() unconditionally, but a real Z80 NMI is
non-maskable — it fires even while the CPU is mid-ROM. Pressing the
button again before "Return" pushed a second return address onto the
game's stack and clobbered IFF2 (nmi() sets iff2 = iff1, and iff1 was
already false from the first NMI). The MF ROM's "Return" only unwinds
one level, so the leftover stack entry got popped and jumped to later
— after the ROM had already paged itself back out — running whatever
happened to be at that address in the game's own memory.

pressButton() is now a no-op while already pagedIn. Real hardware has
no legitimate use for a second press before the first session ends.

events.title: Fix Multiface hang: pageOut must not disarm the interface mid-session
events.message:
Fix Multiface hang: pageOut must not disarm the interface mid-session

f399b80 made MF128/MF3 ports invisible until the NMI button arms them,
but also cleared the armed latch on every pageOut(). Real Multiface
ROMs page out and back in many times per session as part of normal
operation (e.g. the MF3 menu borrows the underlying ROM's
HALT/keyboard-scan idle loop by paging out, then must page itself back
in once a key is pressed). With the latch cleared on that first
internal page-out, the follow-up page-in was silently ignored and the
machine hung — reproduced live: pressing NMI on a +3 reached the menu,
but the ROM's own idle-loop page-out immediately disarmed it, ,so it
could never page back in to handle the keypress.

armed now only clears on reset(), matching what the original finding
actually required (invisible before the button is ever pressed) without
assuming an incorrect auto-disarm-on-return semantic.
events.author: damieng

events.title: Fix tape playback "correcting" the trailing checksum byte
events.message:
Fix tape playback "correcting" the trailing checksum byte

buildRawData always recomputed the XOR checksum from flag+payload,
even though the parser had the genuine on-tape byte available and
discarded it. This silently "fixed" deliberately-bad checksums — a
common protection technique on Spectrum tapes, not just CPC/CDT
(whose data blocks carry their own CRCs and already had this handled
via an opt-in rawDataBlocks flag).

parseTAP and parseTZX (standard/turbo blocks) now always attach the
verbatim on-tape bytes via DataBlock.rawBytes, which playback already
preferred over buildRawData when present. Since Spectrum tapes now get
the same treatment as CPC/CDT, the rawDataBlocks option is no longer
meaningful and is removed along with its call sites.
events.author: damieng

events.title: Fix .z80 snapshots dropping AY state and ignoring +3 port 0x1FFD
events.message:
Fix .z80 snapshots dropping AY state and ignoring +3 port 0x1FFD

The saver wrote 0 for both the AY selected-register byte and the 16
AY register-content bytes (mislabeled "reserved"), so any .z80 saved
from a 128K/+2/+2A/+3 machine always came back with AY registers
reset — 128K .z80s loaded with garbled music. Neither side handled
the 55-byte v3 extended header's port 0x1FFD byte at all, so +3
snapshots taken in an all-RAM CP/M configuration reloaded with ROM
paging instead and crashed immediately.

loadZ80 now reads the AY selected register + 16 register bytes
(byte 38, bytes 39-54) and, for +2A/+3-class memory, the 1FFD byte
(byte 86, only present in the 55-byte header) — applying specialPaging
and the correct 4-ROM-page select the same way the existing SZX flow
already does. saveZ80 takes optional ayRegs/ayCurrentReg parameters
(mirroring saveSZX) and writes a 55-byte header with hwMode=7 when the
memory is +2A/+3-class, adding the 1FFD byte; 128K/+2 keeps the
54-byte header unchanged. media-manager.ts's .z80 branch now restores
AY state after load, mirroring its existing SZX branch.
events.author: damieng

events.title: Fix four uPD765A FDC spec deviations
events.message:
Fix four uPD765A FDC spec deviations

- Overrun (ST1.OR) now correctly sets ST0 IC=01 (abnormal termination).
  It previously left ST0 as normal completion, even though the CPU
  genuinely failed to service the data register in time.

- Multi-track (MT) reads restart the sector count at literal sector 1
  on the new side after a head switch, not the command's original
  starting R — the two only coincided by accident on disks that start
  numbering at 1. Removes the now-unused exStartR field.

- SK (Skip) is now honoured on Read Data/Read Deleted Data: a sector
  whose address-mark type doesn't match the command is skipped
  entirely (not transferred, not a termination point) and the search
  continues to the next sector, instead of always behaving as SK=0
  (read the mismatched sector and terminate after it).

- Duplicate sector IDs (deliberate on copy-protected tracks) now
  resolve to the first physical occurrence instead of the last —
  matching real hardware, where the FDC stops at whichever copy the
  head reaches first during rotation and can't see ahead to a later
  duplicate.
events.author: damieng

events.title: Fix AMX mouse firing PIO interrupts with interrupts never enabled
events.message:
Fix AMX mouse firing PIO interrupts with interrupts never enabled

pioControlWrite parsed the interrupt-control word's mask-follow bit
(D4) but never looked at D7, the actual Interrupt Enable flip-flop.
A real Z80 PIO powers up with interrupts disabled; here moving the
mouse under any IM2 program vectored through the interrupt table
regardless, crashing programs that never armed interrupts (or armed
with an uninitialised/still-zero vector table entry).

Tracks per-port intEnabledA/intEnabledB (set from D7 of the interrupt
control word, cleared on reset) and gates interruptWithVector on it in
drainMovement. Direction latches (dirX/dirY) still update every step
regardless — those reflect direct hardware lines, not the interrupt
path — so polled-mode software is unaffected.
events.author: damieng

events.title: Fix Multiface 128/3 paging ports being live before the button is pressed
events.message:
Fix Multiface 128/3 paging ports being live before the button is pressed

MF128/MF3 decoded their page-in/page-out ports (0xBF/0x3F) and the
0x7F3F/0x1F3F latch readback unconditionally. Real MF128/MF3 hardware
gates those ports behind a latch armed only by the button's NMI, so
they stay invisible until invoked — otherwise any stray IN on those
(very common) port numbers during normal gameplay pages the MF ROM in
mid-game. MF1's narrower bit-mask decode has no such latch on real
hardware and is unaffected.

Adds a `armed` flag to Multiface: set by pressButton, cleared on
page-out (and reset), and consulted by the MF128/MF3 port checks in
io-ports.ts.
events.author: damieng

events.title: Fix +2A/+3 wrongly exposing the Ferranti floating bus
events.message:
Fix +2A/+3 wrongly exposing the Ferranti floating bus

Unattached I/O ports fell through to Contention.floatingBusRead
unconditionally, returning live VRAM bytes on every model. Real
hardware only floats the bus this way on the Ferranti ULA (48K/16K/
128K/+2); the Amstrad gate array (+2A/+3) drives unattached ports to
0xFF instead, which is why Arkanoid hangs on a real +3.

Adds a hasFloatingBus flag to MachineVariant (true for Ferranti
variants, false for Amstrad) and gates the floating-bus read in
io-ports.ts on it.
events.author: damieng

events.title: Fix redundant DD/FD prefix chains costing 8T, double-bumping R, and being interruptible
events.message:
Fix redundant DD/FD prefix chains costing 8T, double-bumping R, and being interruptible

A repeated prefix byte (e.g. DD DD 23) rewound PC and returned to
step(), letting the frame loop re-fetch that byte as a fresh top-level
instruction. That double-counted the byte's M1 cycle (8T instead of
4T), incremented R twice for one fetch, and — because control returned
to the frame loop between prefix bytes — let a pending interrupt be
accepted mid-chain, which real Z80 blocks for the whole prefix stream.

Fix: continue the chain in place by calling into executeDD/executeFD
directly instead of returning, so a run of prefixes resolves within a
single step() call, matching hardware.
events.author: damieng

events.title: Fix AY noise LFSR running at twice the hardware rate
events.message:
Fix AY noise LFSR running at twice the hardware rate

The noise generator shared the same /8 master-clock tick as the tone
and envelope generators, so it shifted every 8*NP master cycles.
Real AY-3-8910/YM2149 hardware has an extra /2 prescaler ahead of the
noise counter, shifting every 16*NP cycles. All noise-based sound was
an octave too bright.
events.author: damieng

events.title: Make MCP parseAddr reject invalid addresses instead of returning NaN
events.message:
Make MCP parseAddr reject invalid addresses instead of returning NaN

parseInt on a typo'd symbol name or non-hex garbage returned NaN, and
NaN & 0xFFFF is 0 — so write_memory silently wrote to address 0x0000,
read_memory dumped 0x0000, set_register set PC=0 and echoed "PC = NaN",
and breakpoints were registered at addresses that could never hit.

parseAddr now validates the hex digits (for plain, 0x- and $-prefixed
forms alike) and throws a descriptive error, which the MCP SDK returns
to the client as a proper tool error. Symbol resolution and the
identifier-shaped-hex fallback (`face`) are unchanged.

events.title: Fix swapped Kempston mouse left/right buttons
events.message:
Fix swapped Kempston mouse left/right buttons

The Spectrum button map put DOM left on bit 0 and right on bit 1, but
the Kempston mouse button port 0xFADF is D0 = right, D1 = left,
D2 = middle (active low) — confirmed against FUSE (ui_mouse_button maps
left to bit 1 and right to bit 0) and the WoS hardware ports reference.
Every left/right click in Kempston-mouse software was inverted. The
previous mapping (and its test) came from a since-vanished reference
page that had the two bits backwards.

The CPC's explicit map already had the correct layout, so only its
"swaps vs the Spectrum" comments needed correcting.

events.title: Fix crash chaining consecutive TZX Direct Recording blocks
events.message:
Fix crash chaining consecutive TZX Direct Recording blocks

When a Direct Recording block ended with pause=0, advanceDirect()
called beginBlock() for the next block and then unconditionally nulled
directData. If the next block was also a Direct Recording block (the
normal way long sampled recordings are split), beginDirectBlock() had
just installed its data — the null clobbered it and the next advance()
threw "Cannot read properties of null" at the block boundary.

Clear directData before the hand-over instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: Fix FDC format flag surviving an aborted FORMAT_TRACK
events.message:
Fix FDC format flag surviving an aborted FORMAT_TRACK

exFormatting was only cleared by finishFormat(), so a FORMAT_TRACK
terminated early — by the MSR overrun path or by a machine reset —
left the flag stuck. The next ordinary WRITE_DATA completion was then
misrouted into finishFormat(), which reinterpreted the written sector
bytes as C/H/R/N ID tuples and rebuilt (destroyed) the current track
in the disk image.

Clear the flag in finishExecution(), the choke point every execution-
phase termination passes through, and in reset(), which bypasses it.

events.title: qt: let Cmd+Q close the launcher on macOS

The launcher runs as a modal QDialog::exec() with no application event

internally, but macOS disables the auto-generated application menu (and
its Cmd+Q) while a modal session is active, so Cmd+Q was swallowed by
the OS and never closed the dialog. Bind QKeySequence::Quit directly on
the dialog so it is handled inside the modal loop, mirroring Escape.

od-unix: preserve Qt runtime config on restart

launcher from the loaded config when one is available. Remove the
temporary snapshot after the restarted frontend has consumed it.
