events.title: cmake: own the qemu-uae plugin provisioning
events.message:
cmake: own the qemu-uae plugin provisioning

The mandatory qemu-uae.so plugin was only buildable from a sibling
qemu-uae source tree; distro builds without one configured fine, built
fine, and then failed at install time when the install rule referenced
the never-built plugin (GitHub issue #6). Both CI workflows carried
their own duplicated checkout/build/strip plumbing for the
uae-ppc-plugin builder instead.

Resolve the plugin at configure time, in order: prebuilt
WINUAE_QEMU_UAE_PLUGIN_FILE, the sibling qemu-uae source tree, an
uae-ppc-plugin builder checkout (WINUAE_QEMU_UAE_BUILDER_DIR, default
sibling; WINUAE_QEMU_UAE_QEMU_TARBALL feeds it a local QEMU tarball for
offline distribution builds), or a build-time clone of the builder
(WINUAE_QEMU_UAE_BUILDER_FETCH, default ON). When nothing applies the
configure fails with the list of options. On Linux the plugin target is
part of the default build so plain build+install flows always bundle
the plugin.

Drive the builder through an OUTPUT-based custom command so repeated
`all` builds and CPack preinstall do not rerun the external builder once
qemu-uae.so is already present.

The Ubuntu and macOS workflows drop their manual plugin build steps and
pass the builder checkout to CMake; stripping moved into the builder
wrapper script.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: od-unix: add Scale2x GLSL scaler to the shader pipeline
events.message:
od-unix: add Scale2x GLSL scaler to the shader pipeline

The Filter page's filter selector only offered "None" (GitHub issue
#4): the generic gfx_filter config option cannot carry named shaders
outside the Windows Direct3D path, and the Unix GL presenter had no
scaler stage.

Carry the selection as a new unix.gfx_shader target option (parsed and
saved in od-unix/config.cpp, no generic code changes) and implement
Scale2x/EPX as a stage in the GL presenter's fragment shader, selected
through a uniform. The scaler forces nearest-neighbour sampling, runs
before the color/scanline/noise stages, and applies to the emulation
frame only, leaving the status line untouched. The launcher's Filter
selector offers Scale2x when the shader pipeline is available, and the
value round-trips through the config (covered by the roundtrip smoke).
events.author: reinauer

events.title: Fix snapshot load applying to a destroyed machine after model auto-switch
events.message:
Fix snapshot load applying to a destroyed machine after model auto-switch

ensure128kROM() destroys the current machine and creates a new one, but
applySnapshot kept using its captured spectrum parameter afterwards:
stop/reset/load/start all hit the destroyed instance, and start() fully
resurrected it — two frame loops, two AudioContexts, and two renderers
fighting over the same canvas whenever a 128K snapshot was dropped on a
48K machine.

ensure128kROM now returns the machine in service ({spectrum, model}) or
null, and applySnapshot re-binds to it before touching anything. The
refreshed model also fixes the SZX path applying 128K-style paging when
the upgrade actually produced a +2A/+3 (port 1FFD ROM bits were dropped).

events.title: od-unix: mirror Windows GUI option gating in Qt launcher
events.message:
od-unix: mirror Windows GUI option gating in Qt launcher

Bring the Qt launcher's control enablement to parity with the Windows
GUI's enable_for_*dlg/values_from_cpudlg logic, with the constraining
option always acting as master:

- Gate Z3 Fast, Z3 Chip, processor slot RAM and Z3 mapping mode by the
  24-bit addressing checkbox (enable_for_memorydlg). Previously a 68000
  could be combined with Z3 RAM and the config booted with it.
- Stop force-unchecking 24-bit addressing when a Z3 RTG board is
  selected, and stop writing cpu_24bit_addressing=false into the config
  whenever a Z3 RTG board is present.
- Apply CPU selection side effects: 68000/68010 force 24-bit addressing
  on, 68030+ force it off; FPU selection is remapped on user-driven CPU
  changes (external to internal at 68040+, internal to 68881 below,
  None on 68000/68010 with More compatible or memory cycle-exact).
- Enable FPU radios per Windows rules; block JIT while an MMU is
  selected; disable More compatible under memory cycle-exact; disable
  the CPU speed slider under full cycle-exact; gate the CPU frequency
  controls.
- Chipset page: clear and disable Wait for Blitter under Immediate
  Blitter or memory cycle-exact with 68000/68010; force NKRO on for UAE
  and A2000-8039 keyboard modes; disable the DMA/memory cycle-exact
  checkbox below 68020.
- Advanced chipset page: disable all manual controls while Compatible
  Settings is checked (enable_for_chipsetdlg2); 1M chip jumper also
  requires 512 KB chip RAM.
- Display page: disable resolution and line-mode controls while
  autoresolution is active, keep interlaced modes tied to the line-mode
  split, gate VGA autoswitch by hires or better with line doubling, and
  disable frame skipping under memory cycle-exact.
- Re-run all gating after loading a configuration file.

The sound page and accelerator board controls already follow the same
Windows gating rules, so leave them unchanged.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: Fix EI interrupt shadow: run one instruction after EI before accepting INT
events.message:
Fix EI interrupt shadow: run one instruction after EI before accepting INT

The frame loop cleared cpu.eiDelay unconditionally after every step,
including the step that executed EI itself, so a pending frame INT was
accepted between EI and the following instruction. Real Z80 defers
acceptance by exactly one instruction: EI:DI is atomic and EI:HALT can
never take the INT in between (an ISR ending EI:RETI would otherwise be
re-entered before RETI, leaking 2 stack bytes per frame).

Capture eiDelay before step() and clear it only if it was already set,
matching the pattern cpc-machine.ts already used.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: a2065: drop frames that cannot fit receive ring
events.message:
a2065: drop frames that cannot fit receive ring

The receive queue can stall forever if the packet at its head is larger
than the current descriptor ring can accept. Check the full frame size,
including padding and FCS bytes, before trying to drain the queue.

Drop packets that can never fit and reject packets that would overflow
the temporary frame buffer when the emulated FCS is appended.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: slirp: harden restart and DNS handling
events.message:
slirp: harden restart and DNS handling

Reset transient SLIRP state when the backend is restarted, and make
DHCP DNS advertisement depend on an available resolver.

Keep host loopback resolvers unchanged instead of rewriting them to the
virtual host address. The guest still talks to the SLIRP DNS proxy, but
the proxy must query the resolver configured on the host.

This keeps the emulated network usable after reconfiguration and avoids
advertising a DNS forwarder that cannot answer.

events.title: Comment the endgame chain; settle the Competence Rating formula
events.message:
Comment the endgame chain; settle the Competence Rating formula

Competence Rating (RatingScore, ex-'EndgameFlag') decoded exactly:
  crew term  = sum of 2 x strength over live human crew (no Android)
  room term  = +1 per room with damage < 20 (34 rooms max)
  oxygen term= 2 x leading digit of the oxygen counter
capped at 100. Which terms an ending adds distinguishes outcomes:
alien killed = crew+rooms+oxygen; escape/crew-lost/oxygen-out with
destruct armed = crew+oxygen; ship exploded = oxygen only; alien
survives to Earth = 0.

texts; PrintDeadRoster/PrintAndroidReveal/PrintRating (ASCII

events.message:
Comment the combat subsystem; fix the sprite-class fiction, verify two game bugs

The 'sprite-class identity match' story in CrewAction4_Handler /
CrewHitsAlien / CrewHitsAndroid / UpdateAlien was wrong: (IX+1) is the
actor's current ROOM, so all of these are plain room co-location
checks. Rewrote those headers; GatherSameClassSlots ->
GatherSameRoomSlots (it duplicates RecalcMorale's room-mate scan).

Decodes:
- CrewHitsAlien/CrewHitsAndroid guards are strength>=2 AND morale>=2
  (not 'pixel coords'); the weapon byte is the front-hand item id
  (not a 'corridor scan position'). Net = single-use (netting also
  destroys it); trackers shatter but still wound; extinguishers only
  scare; harpoon kills attacker+bystanders and adds 15 room damage;
  lasers add 6 room damage + 2 wounds
- TriggerAlienEvent: 29570 is the alien's WOUND counter (not a
  'corridor index') — 6+ wounds with a dormant Android sets
  AlienActiveFlag=255, and UpdateAlien then activates the Android
  (the traitor reveals himself when the alien is in danger)
- AlienStopCell -> AlienKillThreshold (wounds needed to kill = 15)
- KillActorMoraleHit/WitnessMoraleLoss: witnessed deaths are found
  instantly (+7=2, msg #20) and decay everyone's courage
- CrewAction7_Handler: the Android's attack tick on room-mates

Original-game bugs found and verified:
- AlienScareCheck's weapon bonus INC is unreachable (CP 6/CP 7 both
  required via JR NZ)
- CrewHitsAndroid's harpoon item-wipe has an inverted branch vs the
  alien-side loop: it destroys every item on the ship EXCEPT those
  lying in the room, and leaves the Android unwounded (simulator-
  verified)

Also: $7376->$737E typo family fixed (12 places), LongGameCrewInit
slot listing corrected.

events.title: Decode the 238 encounter marker: press-time RmveGrille->ATTACK swap
events.message:
Decode the 238 encounter marker: press-time RmveGrille->ATTACK swap

The stub cluster at $B2B9-$B31D is the hostile-in-room menu logic,
run by RoomModeDispatch before EVERY mode-0/1 action dispatch:

- ForceAttackRowIfHostile ($B2C0): in the room view, when the alien
  (slot 0) — or, once AlienActiveFlag is $FF, the alien-target/Android
  slot — is in the viewed actor's room, the special row (cell 13) is
  forced to 52 'ATTACK' and redrawn. If the press landed on 49
  'RmveGrille', the mirror byte is set to 238: the swap happened under
  the cursor within the same key release.
- SpecialRowAction ($B306): 238 -> restore 52 but still start the
  timed grille removal — the player's original intent is honoured;
  only the next press (row visibly ATTACK) runs StartAttack ($9275,
  action state 4, countdown 40, replaces any pending job).
- Also: row 8 (front-hand item) presses cancel the pending countdown
  ((IX+0)=0 never fires — ResetCrewTimers only dispatches on 1->0).

Verified end-to-end in the skoolkit simulator (scripted Short Game,
alien poked into Ripley's room: mirror 49->238->52, cell13->52,
state 3 timer 180; second press -> state 4 timer 40).

Also named from the same investigation: SetActionTimer's formula and
its tables (GrilleTimeBySlot $83EA, ActionTimeByStrength $83F2,
ActionTimeBySlot $83FA — 6 bytes only, slots 6-7 read into
TileTableBounds), JonesCatchBySlot $83E2, RefreshSpecialRow $B0B8,
and the InputScannerTable $A405 (was 'glyph codes?'): OptionsScreen
patches the scanner CALL operand at $874D per input device.

- 30076/$757C identified: RoomGrilleState, one byte per room (255 = in

  corner glyphs 128-131 (top-left/bottom-left/bottom-right/top-right):
  each maps the walk's incoming heading to the outgoing one while the
  arm is painted cyan; 125/142/143 end the walk (ArmEndNode).
- Item system fully decoded: ItemLocations $74F4 (22 items; value =
  room, 160/128+slot = front/back hand), RoomItemList, ItemCarryNudge,
  InitialItemRooms; menu rows 8-11 = front item / SwapHeldItems /
  GetItemMenu+GetItemPick / LeaveItemHandler. RoomDispatchTable's
  triple use documented (mode dispatch + two overlapping cursor-row

events.title: ppc: flush QEMU JIT after 68k cache changes
events.message:
ppc: flush QEMU JIT after 68k cache changes

OS3.x/WarpOS can patch PPC code and page tables from the m68k side in shared RAM. QEMU does not see those writes through the PPC softmmu, so stale translation blocks can survive until the m68k/PPC handoff deadlocks.

Import the optional ppc_cpu_flush_jit hook, mark QEMU PPC code cache state dirty on 68040 instruction-cache and MMU ATC flushes, and consume one coalesced flush at the next m68k-to-PPC handoff. Skip the flush while the m68k is halted so PPC-only OS4 execution is not forced to retranslate continuously.

events.title: Scale on-screen keyboards proportionally with the display scale
events.message:
Scale on-screen keyboards proportionally with the display scale

The 48K rubber and +/128K hard keyboards were fixed-pixel mock-ups tuned
for the ~42/48px units the 3x display scale happens to produce. A single
container breakpoint shrank only the unit pitch while every legend size,
glyph offset and block swatch stayed in absolute px, so the keyboards
only looked right at 3x and broke at 2x/1x (the pane narrows with the
canvas, firing the breakpoint and leaving the legends full-size).

Drive the key unit from the display scale via a new --display-scale CSS
variable, and express every internal metric as a multiple of a per-board
"design pixel" (--u1 for the 48K, --pu1 for the Plus/128K, including the
moulded groove gradient stops) so each face scales as one rigid block.
3x is byte-for-byte identical to the previous layout; 2x/1x now scale
down proportionally. Removes the now-dead 520px/560px breakpoints.

events.title: Fix one-scanline FLASH tear in high-accuracy renderer at column 0
events.message:
Fix one-scanline FLASH tear in high-accuracy renderer at column 0

renderLineSegment gated the display-cell draw on `xEnd > borderLeft`.
When a progressive render chunk ends exactly on the left display edge
(xEnd == borderLeft), the Ferranti +1 cell offset asks for col 0
(colEnd=1), but the strict `>` skipped the draw while
renderPendingScanlines still advanced nextDisplayCol past it. Col 0 was
then never drawn that frame and kept the previous frame's pixels — on a
column-0 FLASH cell (the editing cursor, bottom-left) this showed as a
single scanline with inverted flash bits, at flash transitions. The idle
HALT loop produces beam chunks that land exactly on borderLeft, so it
only surfaced in real time (not in headless tests).

Use `xEnd >= borderLeft`; `colStart < colEnd` is the real authority for
whether there are cells to draw. Amstrad (+0 cell offset) is unaffected.

Add tests/cores/flash-rainbow-tear.test.ts pinning the left-edge boundary.

Align toastrack rows by folding the gap into the unit pitch

Every key was already a quarter-unit and every row summed to 13.5u, but
the 4px inter-key gaps made rows with different key counts different pixel
widths, so the centred rows didn't line up.

Fold the gap into the unit: 50px pitch (46px square cap + 4px gap), zero
the row gap, and size each key to w*pitch - 4px with a 2px side margin
(left/right only, so the ENTER cell's negative bottom margin is kept).

container uses the matching 44px pitch. Also drop the unused non-quarter

The +2 reuses the 128K/+ layout but with a near-bare, light-grey face: only the RUN/CODE/LOAD keywords survive, symbol-shift tokens are kept on the number row and the single-character operator letters, and everything is one white oblique legend set on a fixed-width grid (every alphanumeric exactly 1u, every row the same width so the L-shaped ENTER stays aligned). events.title: profiler: don't silently truncate an out-of-range CFA offset in the unwind table
events.message:
profiler: don't silently truncate an out-of-range CFA offset in the unwind table

The packed emulator unwind format has only 12 bits for the CFA offset
(0-4095). A function with a large stack frame and no frame pointer can
have CFA = SP + offset >= 4096, which buildUnwindTable masked with
`& 0xfff` instead of rejecting - computing a wrong, truncated CFA and
corrupting every saved-register read derived from it (so the profiler
would attribute that function's cycles to bogus parent frames), with
no diagnostic.

Detect the out-of-range offset and skip the row instead, leaving its
slots at the existing "no unwind info" zero sentinel (the call stack
just stops there rather than continuing with corrupt data), and log a
warning so it's visible if it happens.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: profiler: don't fall through to a same-named global for an unaddressable local
events.message:
profiler: don't fall through to a same-named global for an unaddressable local

resolveNameToLValue matched a local by name, and if locationToAddress
couldn't resolve it (register-resident location, or a 'cfa' location
with no CFI for that pc), silently fell through to a same-named global
and returned its address instead. A hover, watch, or setVariable/
setExpression on such a name would target the wrong memory - read or
write hits global storage while believing it's the shadowing local.

A local name match now always shadows the global, returning undefined
when it can't be addressed rather than resolving to the global.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: profiler: exclude vasm local labels from the symbol set, not just one query
events.message:
profiler: exclude vasm local labels from the symbol set, not just one query

findSymbolOffset's excludeLocal flag fixed the flame graph's function
naming, but getSymbols/getSymbolLengths still treated `.`-prefixed
local labels (e.g. a macro's `.\@` branch target) as real symbols. The
webview's symbol list (built from these) still split a routine's
length at its first local label and could resolve addresses past it
to the wrong name — disagreeing with the flame graph for the same PC.

Push excludeLocal down into getSymbols/getSymbolLengths themselves so
buildSymbolList (and any future consumer) excludes local labels by
construction instead of needing to remember the flag, and pass it from
syntheticLabel's Kickstart path too (latent today, but the same class
of bug if a future ROM symbol set ever has local labels).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: profiler: stop flame graph splitting on macro-local labels
events.message:
profiler: stop flame graph splitting on macro-local labels

Macro-internal labels (e.g. vasm's \@ unique-id local labels used for
polling loops like BLIT_WAIT) were treated as distinct functions by
findSymbolOffset's nearest-preceding-symbol lookup, and even after
excluding local labels by name, the per-PC line-table file/line still
varied across call sites for the same function. Resolve file/line at
the symbol's own address instead of pc so every instruction in a
function (macro-expanded or not) maps to one consistent location.

events.title: od-unix: enable threaded CPU support
events.message:

Match the Windows target by enabling the shared threaded CPU path on
Unix. The port already provides pthread-backed uae_thread_id and
semaphore helpers, but sysconfig.h did not expose WITH_THREADED_CPU.

cfgfile: handle missing command line option values

parse_cmdline_option() keeps unknown command line options in the
all_lines list. A trailing option such as -G reaches this path without
a value, which passed NULL to my_strdup() and crashed before the GUI
could start.

events.title: od-unix: fix config values lost in the Qt launcher round trip
events.message:
od-unix: fix config values lost in the Qt launcher round trip

Loading a configuration file could silently change it (GitHub issue #1,
"CPU and RAM are often not the ones I set"):

- The chipset_compatible handler synced the quickstart model combo
  without blocking its signals, so loading any config with a
  chipset_compatible value re-applied the whole quickstart model preset
  over the explicit settings (FPU, compatibility flags, floppy count).
- FpuInternal was -1, which QButtonGroup treats as auto-assign and
  checkedId() returns for "no selection": the CPU-internal FPU button
  could never be selected programmatically, so fpu_model vanished from
  every 68040/68060 configuration on save, start, and each F12 visit.
- nr_floppies had no load handler, so drive-enable states never
  followed the loaded config.

Configs without a quickstart line also no longer gain a synthesized
quickstart key: quickstart mode now turns off when loading a full
configuration and is re-enabled by an explicit quickstart setting.

Verified by a new roundtrip harness: WINUAE_QT_CONFIG_ROUNDTRIP_OUT
makes the launcher load the given config, export the merged config, and
exit; unix-smoke-config-roundtrip.sh (in winuae_unix_smoke_basic)
compares CPU/FPU/MMU/memory/floppy keys across three machine profiles.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: od-unix: match Windows GUI button semantics in runtime (F12) UI
events.message:
od-unix: match Windows GUI button semantics in runtime (F12) UI

The runtime GUI's bottom button row behaved like the pre-start launcher:
Quit and Cancel both just closed the dialog and resumed emulation, Reset
reverted the UI to A1200 quickstart defaults, and Restart was hidden.
Mirror the Windows GUI (IDC_RESETAMIGA/IDC_QUITEMU/IDC_RESTARTEMU):

- Quit requests uae_quit() and exits the emulator.
- Reset applies the edited configuration and hard-resets the Amiga
  (uae_reset(1,1)), then resumes.
- Restart is shown in runtime mode and returns to the launcher through
  uae_restart().
- Start is relabeled OK while emulation is running; Cancel and closing
  the window still resume without applying changes.

The launcher result carries the new quit/restart states and a hard-reset
flag through the bridge; pre-start behavior is unchanged.

Also write floppy paths and the first CD slot into the merged config
even when empty, so ejecting media in the runtime GUI reaches the
core's disk-change detection instead of silently keeping the old image.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: od-unix: seed Qt launcher from default.uae at startup
events.message:
od-unix: seed Qt launcher from default.uae at startup

The shared core loads <configurationpath>/default.uae into the prefs at
startup (main.cpp real_main), but the Qt launcher built its state from
scratch, so the default configuration had no visible effect unless the
GUI was disabled. Pass the file as the launcher's initial config path
when it exists, matching the Windows "save as default.uae" behavior.

Configs given on the command line keep precedence: the launcher's own
argument parsing decides, exposed through the bridge so gui_init does
not duplicate it. The bridge no longer infers runtime mode from "an
initial config path is present"; gui_display passes it explicitly.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: cmake: name the Unix binary winuae
events.message:
cmake: name the Unix binary winuae

The installed Linux command, the .desktop entries, and the WinUAE.app
bundle all use the name winuae while the build tree produced
winuae_unix. Set OUTPUT_NAME on the winuae_unix target so the binary is
winuae everywhere, drop the now-redundant install RENAME, and update
the smoke script defaults, bundling scripts, and README accordingly.
macos-bundle.sh keeps a fallback for build directories from before the
rename. The CMake target names are unchanged.

events.title: od-unix: ship starter filter presets
events.message:
od-unix: ship starter filter presets

The Filter page's preset list was empty until the user saved their own
(GitHub issue #4). Add a set of bundled presets built from the portable
filter controls the Unix GLSL pipeline implements (Sharp Pixels, Soft
Bilinear, CRT Scanlines, Warm TV), installed under the shared data
directory on Linux and into the app bundle resources on macOS.

The preset combo lists user presets and bundled presets together; the
user directory wins on name collisions, saving always writes to the
user directory, and loading falls back to the bundled file when no user
preset of that name exists.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: od-unix: persist host settings in winuae.ini
events.message:
od-unix: persist host settings in winuae.ini

The Unix port had no equivalent of the Windows registry/winuae.ini
store: the Qt Paths page reverted to hardcoded defaults on every start
(GitHub issue #2).

Port the ini-file mode of the od-win32 registry abstraction into
od-unix/registry.cpp on top of the shared ini.cpp, with the same
registry.h API. The store resolves to winuae.ini next to the executable
when present (portable mode, matching Windows), otherwise
$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/winuae/winuae.ini on Linux and
~/Library/Application Support/WinUAE/winuae.ini on macOS; the
WINUAE_INI environment variable overrides the location.

The Qt launcher loads the Paths page directories and flags from the
store and saves them when the dialog closes, through new host-setting
hooks on the provider struct. The core path fetchers consult the stored
values between per-config unix.*_path overrides and the built-in
defaults, so the configured directories also apply outside the GUI.
Settings flush on dialog close and at gui_exit.

Covered by winuae_unix_registry_test (value types, subtrees,
enumeration, deletion, and persistence across reopen).

events.title: profiler: blitter line in the flame graph (reconstructed from the DMA grid)
events.message:
profiler: blitter line in the flame graph (reconstructed from the DMA grid)

Adds a second band below the DMA line — one box per blit, colored by mode (Copy/Fill/Line) — reconstructed entirely webview-side from the captured per-cycle DMA grid. No emulator change: vAmiga's default BLITTER_ACCURACY=2 stamps owner==BLITTER per cycle with the WRITE flag on the D write. Blit start = BLTSIZE/BLTSIZH write; config from WRITE-gated register shadowing (gating on DMA_WRITE avoids phantom blits from vAmiga's stale idle-cell busAddr); end = the final D-channel write (WinUAE's BLIFINALD), more accurate than the old ext's BLITIRQ+8. Validated against template.vamigaprofile: 17 blits, matching the old extension.

Full parity tooltip (size, BLTCON/minterm chips, per-channel source/dest with shift/modulo, channel-A masks, start/end/duration). Blitted-image preview deferred. events.title: profiler: synthetic [IRQ]/[Kickstart]/[External] buckets + no-CFI blob nesting
events.message:
profiler: synthetic [IRQ]/[Kickstart]/[External] buckets + no-CFI blob nesting

Bumps vamigaweb_fork (out-of-program samples emitted + [IRQ] dispatch-gap marker). Host-side syntheticLabel classifies a leaf PC: IRQ_MARKER -> [IRQ]; ROM range -> [Kick] <name> when Kickstart symbols are loaded (else flat [Kickstart]); loaded program segment -> normal; else [External]. The top-level CPU total now reaches ~100% (was ~75%).

applyContextReuse nests context-less leaves under the calling function (ports the old ext's lastCallstack reuse): out-of-program [Kickstart]/[External], and in-program no-CFI leaves (an #embed'd binary / hand-asm called via jsr, e.g. ThePlayer). The no-CFI-blob path is gated to DWARF programs (getUnwindRows non-empty) so pure-assembly captures, where depth-1 is legitimate, are unaffected. Rebuilt vAmiga.wasm.

events.title: profiler: fast webview data path (resource-fetch bulk + model store)
events.message:
profiler: fast webview data path (resource-fetch bulk + model store)

Captures took ~1s to display in dev builds. Two causes, both fixed:

1. Bulk binary (DMA grid + chip/slow snapshot) was sent via webview.postMessage, which serializes large binary slowly (cross-process, ~0.3-0.8ms/KB; a 1MB array ~820ms). Now the extension writes the bulk to a temp file in globalStorageUri (added to localResourceRoots) and posts only its asWebviewUri; the webview fetches it (~10ms for 1.6MB) and decodes it (src/profilerBulk.ts pack/unpackBulk). connect-src added to the webview CSP. Live panel and .vamigaprofile editor share this path.

2. The model (with the large typed arrays) was a React prop, and React's DEVELOPMENT build deep-serializes props every render for its performance/components track (~1s). The model now lives in a module store (modelStore.ts), read via getProfileModel() with useModelVersion() driving re-renders — never a prop/state/hook value, so it's never serialized. Production React strips that instrumentation (esbuild sets NODE_ENV=production when minifying), so releases were already fine; this fixes the dev loop (~1s -> ~20ms).

events.title: profiler: .vamigaprofile capture documents (save/load)
events.message:
profiler: .vamigaprofile capture documents (save/load)

Adds a binary profile document that is the save/load artifact, the dev fixture, and the test input through one shared pipeline. Refactors capture into a pure seam (RawCapture -> buildModelFromCapture) used by both live capture and file load.

Format (src/vamigaProfile.ts): gzip of [magic][manifest JSON][raw sections] — profile stream + optional DMA grid / chip+slow snapshot, with the program ELF embedded and the relocation (segmentOffsets/baseDir) recorded so absolute captured PCs re-symbolicate identically on load. encode/decode are pure + unit-tested (round-trip, alignment, bad-magic).

Save: a webview toolbar button posts saveProfile; the provider embeds the ELF + relocation grabbed once per session at capture time (so saving works even after the emulator/session closes), writes the file, opens it, and closes the live panel. Embedding is required and fails loud rather than writing an unloadable file.

Load: a read-only CustomEditor for *.vamigaprofile rebuilds the SourceMap from the embedded ELF + relocation and runs buildModelFromCapture (profileLoader.ts), hosting the profiler webview in file mode (Capture/Save hidden; jump-to-source works). Replay test exercises the whole chain against a committed fixture.

Session-constant data (symbols, ELF) is sent/read once per session, not per capture. mode is baked into the webview HTML so it holds even if a load fails.

events.title: CPU profiler Phase 4: DMA profiling + inline call frames + webview polish
events.message:
CPU profiler Phase 4: DMA profiling + inline call frames + webview polish

DMA profiling: captures the DMA grid + chip/slow snapshot in the same frame as the CPU profile (rides wasm_profile_start). src/dma.ts decodes the binary grid into IDmaModel; FlameGraph draws a time-aligned DMA band above the CPU rows (channelStyle colors, coalesced runs, addr/value/R-W tooltips); topDownGraph groups the TimeView under top-level CPU and DMA nodes. Symbolization moved webview-side (model.symbols + createSymbolizer); custom-register names consolidated in webview/shared/customRegisters.ts (copperDisassembler reuses it). Unwired memory/register reconstruction lives in webview reconstruct.ts; both inputs (grid + snapshot) ride the model.

Inline call frames: expandPc expands each captured PC into its physical function + DWARF inlined_subroutine chain (the unwinder can't see inlined frames), so they show as their own boxes in the flame graph and TimeView, suffixed ' (inlined)'. Line attribution follows addr2line --inlines.

Webview polish: fixed DMA channel colors (constants are 0xAABBGGRR -- red/blue were swapped); TimeView header uses the UI font + matches the old extension's swatch/divider; default time unit is % of Frame; captures now survive a webview reload (provider caches the last model and re-posts on ready instead of re-capturing).

Includes the matching vamigaweb_fork pointer (DmaProfiler) + rebuilt vamiga/ wasm. 531 tests pass.

events.title: dwarf: DWARF5 rnglists, cross-CU ref_addr, complete DW_OP table, fail-loud
events.message:
dwarf: DWARF5 rnglists, cross-CU ref_addr, complete DW_OP table, fail-loud

Fixes two parser gaps that surfaced once the CPU profiler started expanding inline frames (DWARF5 a.elf):

1. Range lists: discontiguous inlined subroutines use DW_AT_ranges, which in DWARF5 points into .debug_rnglists (DW_RLE_* entries), not .debug_ranges. The parser only knew the old begin/end format and was reading rnglist offsets out of .debug_ranges -> garbage ranges -> spurious inline frames at random PCs. Now parses .debug_rnglists with a version-aware getDieIntervals (fixes lexical-block ranges too).

2. Inline names: an inlined function's name lives on its abstract instance, reached via DW_AT_abstract_origin -- here a DW_FORM_ref_addr, i.e. a cross-CU reference. The resolver added cuStartOffset (correct only for CU0) and searched only the current CU, so names resolved to '???'. Now resolves ref_addr against the .debug_info section base + a global DIE map, and resolveDieName follows abstract_origin/specification/linkage_name (demangled).

Also corrects the DW_OP enum (dup/drop/over/pick/swap/rot/xderef were off by two, colliding with constu/consts/... and mis-sizing operands) and replaces the partial op switch with a complete, operand-accurate DW_OP table. Unimplemented DW_OP/DW_CFA/DW_RLE encodings and a missing range section now throw instead of silently desyncing/producing garbage -- preferred during development.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: CPU profiler (Phase 3): top-down TimeView + recursive unwind fix
events.message:
CPU profiler (Phase 3): top-down TimeView + recursive unwind fix

TimeView: sortable top-down function table below the flame chart,
ported from vscode-amiga-debug (React, react-window, codicons).
Filter computes filterExpanded synchronously (plain useMemo, not
useMemo+setState) to avoid the one-keystroke lag. Empty filter
guard matches FlameGraph behaviour.

CpuProfiler.cpp: fix recursive-call unwind truncation. The old
`ret == pc` no-progress guard fired when two nested frames shared
the same call-site return address (e.g. fib(4)→fib(3) and
fib(3)→fib(2) both produce RA = fib+0x22). Replaced with
`cfa <= a7` checked before updating a7, which correctly tests
whether the stack actually advanced. Adds a comment on pre- vs
post-instruction memory timing safety.

events.title: CPU profiler (Phase 2): time-ordered flame chart
events.message:
CPU profiler (Phase 2): time-ordered flame chart

Replaces the aggregated call-tree view with a time-ordered flame chart
(x = cycles in execution order) that matches the old vscode-amiga-debug
renderer at the UI/UX level:

- IProfileModel (nodes/locations/samples/timeDeltas) built extension-side
  from InstructionSample[]; per-sample stream retained for future
  coverage/disassembly enrichment (ProfilerManager.getSamples())
- buildColumns (columns.ts) ports the old stacks.tsx column layout:
  one column per instruction, adjacent identical stacks merged
- FlameGraph.tsx rewritten: 2D-canvas, drag-to-pan with pointer capture
  (robust off-iframe release), mouse-wheel zoom centred on cursor,
  double-click zoom with quadratic easing, keyboard nav (arrows/Enter/Esc),
  synced horizontal scrollbar, nice-number ruler, filter dimming
- Toolbar: filter box (text + match-case + regex toggles), unit dropdown
  (cycles / µs / rasterlines / % of frame), Ctrl+click jumps to source
  (reveals already-open editor via findOpenColumn)
- Tooltip: MiddleOut filename ellipsis, total/self/aggregate time,
  viewport-clamped positioning
- display.ts: full DisplayUnit enum + formatValue (ported PAL formulas,
  no space between number and unit)
- cyclesPerMicroSecond derived from emulator-measured frameCycles and
  isPAL flag (PAL=20000µs/frame, NTSC≈16667µs/frame); falls back to
  the standard PAL 68000 constant if not reported
- Box labels and tooltip use the VS Code UI font (not monospace)
- Debug toolbar: openProfiler at navigation@54.5 (between openStateViewer
  @54 and VS Code's built-in reverse-continue @55)

events.message:
CPU profiler (Phase 1): call-tree flame graph for m68k C/C++ programs

Adds a "VAmiga: Open CPU Profiler" command that captures one frame of CPU
execution and renders a symbolicated flame graph with per-function cycle costs.

Pipeline: DWARF .debug_frame -> dwarfParser.evaluateUnwindRows (constant-state
rows) -> unwindTable.buildUnwindTable packs a 6-byte {cfa,r13,ra} entry per
2-byte code location -> uploaded to the emulator's fork-local CpuProfiler (see
the vamigaweb_fork submodule bump) -> binary u32 stream read back over HEAPU8

call tree -> lean canvas flame graph webview (framework-neutral; the WebGL/Preact
graft and DMA/copper views are later phases).

The panel auto-captures one frame on open and offers a "Capture frame" button to
re-capture. Multi-frame and live capture are deferred future phases.

- 08_profile_fib fixture + unwindTable/profilerManager tests

events.title: demangle: fix OOM/hang on internal-linkage (static) names ending in digits
events.message:
demangle: fix OOM/hang on internal-linkage (static) names ending in digits

GCC marks static symbols with a leading 'L' after _Z (e.g. _ZL6Wait10v for
`static void Wait10()`). The parser didn't strip it, desyncing the name parse;
for names ending in digits this looped forever and exhausted memory (hit at
launch via parseELFSymbols on a fixture with such a function).

Strip the leading 'L', and add progress guards in parseArgsUntil /
parseTemplatePlaceholders / parseTypeList so a non-consuming sub-parse can never
loop. Adds regression tests for static functions and adversarial digit-heavy
manglings.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: fix(spectrum): don't contend IR on the HALT refresh cycle
events.message:
fix(spectrum): don't contend IR on the HALT refresh cycle

The frame-loop HALT path probed contend(ir) during the M1 refresh (T3-T4),
over-contending HALT whenever I:R landed in contended RAM. The Z80 core's HALT
and normal-M1 paths deliberately do NOT contend the refresh — the ULA stalls
only on the opcode fetch (PC), and azesmbog's ULA128 timing test (real-hardware
calibrated) sets I=0xFE with contended bank 7 at 0xC000 specifically to assert
this. The two HALT paths disagreed; this aligns the frame loop with the core.

PC (fetch) contention is still applied via read8(pc); only the spurious refresh
IR probe is removed, and the slow path now fast-skips when PC is uncontended
regardless of IR.

The ULA128 test does HALT (IM2 frame sync) with I=0xFE, but that contention
only ever affected the sync HALT, never the OUT-chain measurement (no HALT in
the chain), and the interrupt is frame-fixed — so the stripe result is
unchanged either way, and removing it matches real hardware. Baseline passed on
48K/128K/+3; the post-fix run is still worth a confirming look.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(z80): reset SP to 0xFFFF (power-on convention)
events.message:
fix(z80): reset SP to 0xFFFF (power-on convention)

RESET leaves SP undefined on real silicon, but the universal power-on
convention — and FUSE — is 0xFFFF, which some test ROMs assume. zx84 reset it
to 0. Align with the convention (the Z80 test harness already initialises
sp=0xFFFF, so this just makes the reset default match). Harmless for the
Spectrum, whose ROM loads SP before using the stack.

Scope limited to SP: AF/AF' are also 0xFFFF on real power-on but are left at 0
for now (the instruction-test harness doesn't override A/F, so changing them
would ripple through many tests — a separate triaged change).

Update the two tests that referenced the old sp=0 default.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: docs(fdc): note seek/recalibrate ST0 reports HD=0 by design
events.message:
docs(fdc): note seek/recalibrate ST0 reports HD=0 by design

A reading of the datasheet (where the SEEK command byte carries an HDS field)
suggests cmdSeek should latch the head bit into the seek-complete ST0. It
should not: the uPD765A returns HD=0 in the SENSE_INTERRUPT status after a seek
regardless of HDS, and SEEK and RECALIBRATE behave identically. FUSE models this
explicitly (sense_int_res[0] = status_register[0] & 0xfb, 'return head always
0'), the +3 internal drive is single-sided, and software polls SE + unit after
a seek, never HD. Comment both handlers so the omission reads as intentional.

No behavioural change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: test(fdc): pin matching-DDAM multi-sector read result; document CM choices
events.message:
test(fdc): pin matching-DDAM multi-sector read result; document CM choices

Investigating report #6 (control mark not flagged abnormal) showed the b9a93ab
refactor changed a multi-sector READ_DELETED over all-matching-DDAM sectors from
ST2=0x40 (old: last sector's raw DSK flag leaked) to ST2=0x00 (command-relative
CM clears matching marks). That ST2=0x00 is hardware-correct and consistent with
the protections' single-sector DDAM checks — verified by booting Platoon
(Speedlock 1988) and Barbarian II (Speedlock 1989), both of which use that
multi-sector pattern and load fine.

Add a regression test pinning ST2=0x00 (+ EN at EOT) for that read so the
raw-flag leak can't return. No behavioural change — comments only in the core:
why subsequent-sector flags are command-relative, and that a non-final control
mark is reported as a normal termination by deliberate choice (one behavioural
reference, FUSE, flags it abnormal; no documented +3 protection exercises a
non-final mark mismatch in a multi-sector read, so we diverge knowingly).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: fix(fdc): terminate multi-sector reads at a CRC/control-mark sector
events.message:
fix(fdc): terminate multi-sector reads at a CRC/control-mark sector

advanceSector() overwrote exST1/exST2 from each new sector unconditionally,
so a data CRC error (ST1.DE/ST2.DD) or DDAM control mark on a *non-final*
sector of a multi-sector read was erased — finishExecution only ever saw the
last sector's flags. The real uPD765A stops AT such a sector and reports its
CHRN; it does not read on to R+1.

Add a non-final-sector termination guard in advanceSector (reads only, before
EOT): a data CRC error ends the read abnormally (ST0 IC=01); a command-relative
control mark (DDAM mismatch, SK=0 semantics) ends it normally with CM set, no
End-of-Cylinder. The final/single-sector case still falls through to the
existing EOT path, and the exSingleSector / overrun protection paths are
untouched.

Extract the per-sector flag logic (undersized / unreadable-weak /
command-relative CM) into sectorReadFlags(), shared by cmdReadWrite (first
sector) and advanceSector (subsequent + MT side-1 sectors) so every sector of
a read is handled identically — previously only the first sector got the
careful treatment and the rest were taken raw.

Rewrites the SK test (it encoded the old read-through bug) to assert correct
SK=0 termination, and adds a mid-stream-termination suite (CRC mid-read,
read-through-then-stop, DDAM under READ_DATA, READ_DELETED mark inversion,
final-sector EN unchanged). Full suite green; the Speedlock/US Gold protected
+3 titles (Operation Wolf, Batman, Chase H.Q., Gauntlet, Operation Thunderbolt)
still boot.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: feat(fdc): implement 765A MT (multi-track) head switching
events.message:
feat(fdc): implement 765A MT (multi-track) head switching

READ_DATA/WRITE_DATA with the MT bit (bit 7) set were treated identically
to MT=0: the command terminated with End of Cylinder at the starting head's
EOT and never continued onto the other side. A cross-side read returned only
side 0 — a silent partial read reported as success.

advanceSector now, on reaching EOT with MT set on head 0 and a side-1 track
present, switches to head 1, reloads the side-1 track, restarts the sector
count at the command's first R, and continues; EN is only reported once side
1 also reaches EOT. Single-sided disks (no side-1 track) fall through to the
existing EN termination, so the common single-sided internal-drive case is
unchanged. Works for read and write.

Turns the old FUTURE-noted test green and adds multi-sector-per-head and
single-sided-fallback coverage.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(fdc): reject unimplemented 765A SCAN commands instead of faking a read
events.message:
fix(fdc): reject unimplemented 765A SCAN commands instead of faking a read

SCAN_EQUAL/LOW_EQ/HIGH_EQ were dispatched through cmdReadWrite() with
isWrite=false, so they streamed disk data out to the host (wrong data
direction — SCAN is host-writes-comparison-bytes) and never set ST2.SH/SN.
SCAN was effectively unimplemented but silently mis-executed as a read.

No known +3 software issues SCAN (the command was buggy on early NEC 765 /
Intel 8272 parts; +3DOS and CP/M Plus never adopted it), so rather than
implement it speculatively, reject it as an invalid command (ST0 IC=invalid),
log the opcode/unit/CHRN loudly, and latch a one-off flag the frame bridge
surfaces as a red toast: 'Unsupported 765A FDC SCAN command'. If real
software ever trips it, we'll see it and can implement it properly then.

Replaces the old test that documented the buggy passthrough with three that
pin the reject-and-notify contract.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: Add support for Nova Falcon
events.message:
Add support for Nova Falcon

The Nova VGA graphics card adapter for the Falcon has specific quirks:

- The VGA registers are mapped into cached memory in the ST-RAM range,
  thus, the CPU cache needs to switched off temporarily while programming
  these registers.
- Hardware blitting to the VGA memory causes artifacts. Thus, EmuTOS
  disables the Falcon Blitter when detecting a Nova Falcon.

Thank you to Miro Kropáček for testing the changes.

Polish: re-assess TM CRAFT_GFX render as infeasible, not deferred

The TM craft-interior renderer cannot be faithfully imaged from the
materials on hand. SHAPE_STEP/BLIT_LINE is a scanline run-length blitter
(not a self-contained vector interpreter like the DNG/SPA shape galleries
that rendered cleanly), and CRAFT_GFX is pre-rasterized hi-res byte runs,
not (dx,dy,pen) vectors. The stroker and ANIM_SETUP dereference ~13
indirect zero-page base pointers ($D6..$FA) that the resident STUPH/MI.U1
shape-actor engine sets up at runtime -- verified by grep that none of
them is initialized in any of the 16 targets.

Imaging it would require emulating that entire resident actor engine plus
reconstructing the live cell-projection state, with no correctness
guarantee, which risks shipping a broken render. Left un-imaged and
documented in prose + the verbatim HEX blob + the SHAPE_STEP/BLIT_LINE
plates. Updated TODO.md (work queue + blocked list) and the tm_subsystem

events.message:
Synthesis: the porting-notes chapter (all six synthesis types complete)

Fifth synthesis chapter and the capstone of the design layer: a catalogue
of the recurring 6502/Apple-II idioms, what each means, and its portable
replacement.

- Self-modifying code: patched-JSR/JMP dispatch (a function-pointer
  table), patched operands as variables (including the stale-on-disk
  STALE_FFFF sentinel that running code overwrites), and patched opcodes
  toggling actors (a boolean).
- Multi-entry routines: the CLC / .byte $B0 / SEC carry dual-entry and the
  .byte $2C BIT-absolute skip, both portable as defaulted parameters.
- Inline-argument calling conventions (JSR followed by data) as ordinary
  function arguments, with the disassembler trap they create.
- Numbers and tables: binary quantities with BCD displays, precomputed
  squares/perspective/row-address tables (keep the contents where they
  encode tuning, drop them where they are only speed), little-endian
  16-bit pairs.
- Machine and OS seams: soft switches, the VBL beat (and the mouse-card-
  as-VBL trick), the file library and overlay model, the hooked reset
  vector -- none change visible behaviour.

The synthesis layer now has all six section types the synthesize skill
calls for: overview/architecture, data structures, algorithms, rendering,

events.title: Synthesis: the Algorithm descriptions chapter

Synthesis: the Algorithm descriptions chapter

Third synthesis chapter, after the data-structure reference: the game's
non-trivial mechanics as platform-independent pseudocode plus design
intent -- the parts a porter cannot recover by translating instructions.

- The two PRNGs: the library lagged-additive generator (atmospheric,
  reseeded from cursor-flash timing, genuinely unpredictable) versus the
  dungeon Fibonacci seed stepper (A' = A+B+9, B' = A), deterministic so
  every dungeon level regenerates identically.
- The turn economy: food spent in BCD hundredths via TICK, faster
  transports costing less food and less time per step.
- Procedural dungeon generation: the position-derived seed, the five
  generation passes (lattice edges 6/6/8, walls+force-fields 2*level+1,
  containers, fixed cells and parity-swapped ladders, monsters), and the
  cell-byte nibble packing with its blocking rule.
- The dungeon ray marcher: stepping the facing vector, inspecting the
  ahead and two side cells via exact +/-90 integer rotation, with all the
  perspective in the DNG_GEOM table; plus the depth-scaled vector shapes.
- Shop pricing: base cost = item_index squared (a squares table) scaled
  by a charisma/wisdom/intelligence haggle factor.
- Monster spawning (tier-gated on a rising difficulty bar, hp and exp
  scaling from tier) and greedy integer-sqrt pursuit with melee-vs-armour.

events.title: MAKE.INDATA fully decomposed: the cold-start title builder, byte-perfect
events.message:
MAKE.INDATA fully decomposed: the cold-start title builder, byte-perfect

The last ORG stub is gone. MAKE.INDATA ($1E00-$5435, 13877 bytes) is the
cold-start builder U1.SYSTEM chains to before U1.INTRO: it predates the
MI.U1 engine, runs once, never touches the disk, and is discarded. It
builds the TWO TITLE SCREENS (not the world map, correcting the scout):
MI_BUILD stamps the $8700 payload + the $6000 intro art into place,
decompresses the castle-by-the-sea title onto hi-res page 1 (MI_DECOMP
from MI_TITLE_STREAM), runs the payload to unpack the ORIGIN SYSTEMS logo
to $9600, then LFSR-fizzles the logo onto page 2.

Both RLE decompressors were ported to a scoped 6502 emulator

events.title: feat(mcp): reset_trap — break on reboot to 0x0000 with culprit + stack
events.message:
feat(mcp): reset_trap — break on reboot to 0x0000 with culprit + stack

Custom loaders treat a tape edge-timeout as a fatal read error and
RET/JP/RST 0 to 0x0000 (the ROM reset); runaway crashes land there too.
reset_trap arms a hook on the per-instruction onTrap path that breaks the
instant PC reaches 0x0000 via control flow (guarded so the power-on boot
PC=0 can't false-fire), capturing the culprit instruction, the unwound
return-address chain, and the paging state. Surfaced inline in run /
step_frame / continue, and included in continue's armed-trap guard.

events.title: fix(tape): emit a terminating edge at end of tape so custom loaders don't reboot
events.message:
fix(tape): emit a terminating edge at end of tape so custom loaders don't reboot

A custom turbo/speedlock loader reading the final bit of the last block
needs one more edge after the last data pulse to terminate its pulse-
timing loop. Mid-tape that edge comes from the next block's pilot; at
end-of-tape with a zero/short pause the deck froze the level instantly,
so the loader hunted for an edge that never came, timed out, and (for
turbo loaders like Thundercats 128K) RET-chained to 0x0000 — rebooting
the machine.

enterPause now holds a ~945T terminating pause with a low-flip when no
block follows, guaranteeing the closing edge. This matches FUSE/
libspectrum end-of-tape behaviour. Mid-tape zero-pause blocks (continuous
multi-block loaders) are deliberately left untouched — their next block
supplies the edge.

Adds regression tests covering both the terminating edge on a final
pause=0 block and the unchanged mid-tape zero-pause transition.

events.message:
refactor(plus3): port +3 disk protection detection to the staged dskmanager-rust flow

Replace the flat priority-list of independent detectors with the
fingerprinting flow from dskmanager-rust: T0 ASCII signatures -> T0
geometry classification -> per-class resolver -> Track 1 -> high-track
probes -> mid-disk sweep -> stripped-FDC / unknown fallbacks.

Speedlock is now recognised by geometry (deleted-data marks, 5x1024 data
side, big weak sectors) rather than ASCII signatures; CPC vs +3 is
distinguished by the T0 sector-ID base, giving Hexagon/Speedlock (CPC)
vs +3 variants. A lone FDC error on a high track of an otherwise-clean
disk is treated as dump noise (returns '') rather than Unknown. Output
is the bare scheme name. Test suite rewritten to the new flow (74 cases).

events.title: fix(ay): anti-alias ultrasonic AY tones to kill the title-screen whine
events.message:
fix(ay): anti-alias ultrasonic AY tones to kill the title-screen whine

A channel parked at tone period 0 (e.g. Chase HQ II's title screen) clamps to
period 1 ≈ 110 kHz. Point-sampling that ultrasonic square at the output rate
aliased it down into the audible band as a high-pitched whine; on real hardware
the channel is inaudible.

Add a Sound-panel Anti-alias selector with four modes: Filter (mute an
ultrasonic period≤1 channel — the new default), Box filter (per-sample
averaging), Low-pass, and None (raw point-sampling). The AY core default stays
'none' so the VGMPlay conformance tests keep deterministic output; the app
applies the saved mode on machine creation.

events.title: refactor(tape): remove edge-loading acceleration entirely
events.message:
refactor(tape): remove edge-loading acceleration entirely

The fingerprint-based edge accelerator forged a loader's exit state (B,
carry, EAR bit) from a guessed edge length. That synthesis is inherently
loader-specific, so it loaded some titles correctly and corrupted others
(e.g. Bleepload: wrong bytes, garbled screen, game never starts) — an
unwinnable game of whack-a-mole.

Delete it wholesale: edge-loader.ts, the §4/§5 tap.ts plumbing
(onEdgeScheduled, inAcceleration, singleEdge, edge-flag categorisation),
the "Fast edge loading" toggle + setting, and docs/edge-loading.md.

Loading is now the standard, reliable model used by mainstream emulators:
 - Fast ROM loading (LD-BYTES trap) for standard blocks
 - Turbo while loading runs the REAL loader code faster — cannot corrupt
What remains is a minimal LoaderDetector (auto play/stop only) that never
touches CPU/tape data, just decides when the tape runs and exposes
loaderActive to engage turbo.

events.title: feat(ui): hold status LEDs on for 500ms past last activity
events.message:
feat(ui): hold status LEDs on for 500ms past last activity

The activity LEDs (AY-3-8912, RAINBOW, EAR, TAPE, BEEP, KEY, KEMPSTON,
MOUSE, DISK) were painted straight from a single frame's activity
counters, so bursty events (AY register writes, attribute rewrites, EAR
samples, port reads) strobed the indicators on and off.

Latch each activity LED on for 500ms past its most recent activity via a
shared ledLatched() helper: anything that touched it in the last 500ms
keeps it lit. Setters still run every frame but Solid dedupes equal
values, so an LED transitions only on an activity edge or 500ms after
activity ceases — instant-on, smooth-off, no flicker. Applied on both the
Spectrum and CPC LED paths. tapeTurbo and the transcribe-mode half of
TEXT stay immediate (sustained state, not bursts). resetLedActivity()
clears the hold on model switch.

events.title: fix(tape): make Fast edge loading accelerate standalone, not just under turbo
events.message:
fix(tape): make Fast edge loading accelerate standalone, not just under turbo

The edge accelerator did `cpu.tStates += adv`, inserting the full real
pulse length (~2168T pilot) into the CPU clock per skipped edge. At the
realtime frame cap that fits only ~32 pilot edges/frame — exactly
realtime — so Fast edge loading gave zero standalone speed-up and only
ever multiplied the turbo frame-rate. It also hand-advanced the tape AND
bumped the clock, so the per-instruction advanceTapeTo() double-advanced
the tape, racing it ahead of the loader and (via the fromAcceleration=
false edge callback) invalidating the length pipeline every other IN,
desyncing the forged-bit decode.

Make it a genuine time-skip per docs/edge-loading.md §4.5: advance the
tape across exactly one edge without moving cpu.tStates, then re-anchor
the host tape clock (new optional EdgeLoaderHost.syncTapeClock) so the
catch-up advance doesn't double-count. Fast edge loading now accelerates
on its own (~4-6x, bounded by the ROM's own LD B,$16/DJNZ per-edge
delay); turbo still stacks on top for near-instant loads.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: perf(turbo): drive turbo off a MessageChannel pump, not rAF
events.message:
perf(turbo): drive turbo off a MessageChannel pump, not rAF

Turbo execution was bound to requestAnimationFrame: capped at the vsync
rate and deliberately using only ~70% of each frame interval (overrunning
the rAF deadline makes the browser throttle rAF down). That ~30% idle per
vsync was a hard ceiling.

Drive turbo from a MessageChannel postMessage loop instead. Each burst
runs frames for a fixed wall-clock budget (TURBO_PUMP_BUDGET_MS = 8ms)
then re-arms via postMessage, which re-fires in well under a millisecond
and isn't vsync-locked — so bursts run back-to-back, using the main
thread near-continuously. The rAF loop now only renders the latest frame
and runs the 60Hz UI upkeep. Measured ~1.6x (80x -> 130x) and no longer
capped by the display refresh rate.

runTurboBurst now takes an explicit budgetMs (the pump sets cadence), so
the Spectrum's adaptive rAF-interval budget math is gone. Breakpoints hit
mid-burst are left set for the next rAF onFrame to pause on (both Spectrum
and CPC pause paths verified). Channel torn down in destroy().

events.title: fix(z80): contend internal cycles of indexed and INIR/INDR instructions
events.message:
fix(z80): contend internal cycles of indexed and INIR/INDR instructions

Indexed (DD/FD) instructions advanced their post-displacement internal
cycles with bare tStates increments, skipping the contention probes that
exec-main and exec-ed apply to every internal cycle. IX/IY-heavy code in
contended RAM mistimed.

- LD r,(IX+d), ALU A,(IX+d), INC/DEC (IX+d): 5 internal cycles now
  contend at the d-byte address (PC-1); INC/DEC's read->write internal
  cycle also now contends at the operand address.
- LD (IX+d),r: was +4/write/+4 (write@T+15); now 5 internal/write/+3
  (write@T+16), matching the read variant.
- LD (IX+d),n: was +1/write/+4; now 2 internal @ n-byte/write/+3.
- INIR/INDR: the write's completion 3T now precedes the 5 internal
  cycles, so their probes land at T+16..20 instead of 3T early at T+13.

Totals are unchanged (19/23/16/21T); only contention-probe placement and
peripheral-visible write timing differ. OTIR/OTDR already placed their
internal cycles after the I/O cycle and are untouched.

events.title: fix(z80): no contention probe during the M1 refresh cycle
events.message:
fix(z80): no contention probe during the M1 refresh cycle

Every M1 (and each prefix fetch) probed ULA contention at the refresh
address IR during T3-T4. The ULA only stalls the CPU on MREQ cycles and
the refresh is not one — FUSE models an opcode fetch as a single 4T
contended read at PC with no IR probe. The bogus probe was invisible in
normal use (I=0x3F points at ROM) but azesmbog's hardware-calibrated
ULA128 timing test runs with I=0xFE while contended bank 7 is paged at
0xC000, so every instruction in the display fetch window gained phantom
delays (NOPs 8T, OUT (C),r up to 26T), smearing the test pattern from
the paper area down. Simulating the test's full OUT chain against the
TAP bytes shows 97.4% line-to-line stripe coherence with pure I/O
contention extras and no IR refresh probe — the real-hardware model.

Internal no-MREQ cycles at IR (PUSH, DJNZ, RET cc, RST, LD A,I, ADD HL,
block I/O) are genuine and keep their probes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: fix(contention): revert 128K display origin to real-hardware value 14362
events.message:
fix(contention): revert 128K display origin to real-hardware value 14362

426feca moved displayOrigin to 14364 based on the Sinclair wiki's
63-lines-x-228 derivation, but azesmbog's ULA128 timing test (calibrated
against a real 128K) shows the paper leads contention start by 1T as on
the 48K, not 3T. Emulators tuned to pass that test agree: ESPectrum uses
TS_SCREEN_128=14361 against TS_SCREEN_48=14335 — a +26 model delta,
which in our first-pixel convention is 14336 + 26 = 14362. With 14364
the test's border stripes render 2T (4 pixels) early relative to paper.

events.title: fix(contention): 128K display origin and measured floating-bus sequence
events.message:
fix(contention): 128K display origin and measured floating-bus sequence

Two hardware-fidelity fixes:

- TIMING_128K.displayOrigin was 14362, derived by analogy with the 48K's
  contentionStart+1 relationship. The 128K has 63 lines above the display,
  so the first pixel is at 63 x 228 = 14364 (contentionStart + 3T), the
  same relationship the +2A entry already used. The old value rendered
  128K border/multicolor effects 2T (4 pixels) early.

- floatingBusRead modelled each 4T cell as pixel,pixel,attr,attr with the
  bus driven on all 128 fetch T-states. Measured hardware (FUSE, Sinclair
  Wiki) interleaves two character columns per 8T block — pixel n, attr n,
  pixel n+1, attr n+1 — then releases the bus for the idle half, which
  reads 0xFF. Tests rewritten to pin the documented sequence.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: fix(contention): anchor IN-side I/O contention at the IORQ cycle start
events.message:
fix(contention): anchor IN-side I/O contention at the IORQ cycle start

The Ferranti four-case I/O contention rule is defined relative to the
start of the IORQ cycle, but applyIOContention probed from whatever
cpu.tStates was when the port handler fired. OUTs fire at cycle start
(correct); INs fire 3T into the cycle — the late sample point tape edge
loaders need — so every IN's contention probes were anchored 3T late on
48K/128K/+2. applyIOContention now takes the caller's offset into the
cycle and walks its probes from the true cycle start, decoupling the
contention anchor from the data sample point (the FUSE approach).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(z80): I/O cycle timing, R on interrupt ack, CPxR repeat flags
events.message:
fix(z80): I/O cycle timing, R on interrupt ack, CPxR repeat flags

Four hardware-accuracy fixes to the Z80 core:

- OUTI/OUTD/OTIR/OTDR emitted the port write at T+9 instead of T+12;
  the (HL) read cycle's 3T were lumped into a trailing +=7. The OUT now
  lands at the start of the real IORQ cycle, and the OTIR/OTDR repeat's
  five internal contention probes now run at the correct T-states.
- IN r,(C) and INI now tick 3T before portIn so the sample lands late
  in the IORQ window, matching the IN A,(n) convention that tape edge
  loaders depend on (ED 78-based loaders previously sampled 3T early).
- interrupt() and nmi() now increment R: the acknowledge is an M1 cycle,
  so R advances like any opcode fetch (bit 7 preserved).
- CPIR/CPDR repeating iterations now take F5/F3 from the high byte of
  the rewound PC (Banks/hoglet 2018 block-flags research), matching the
  LDIR/INIR/OTIR repeat paths. zexall cannot catch this; z80test does.

Instruction totals are unchanged (12/16/21T); only intra-instruction
placement and flag/R state changed. New regression tests pin the sample
points, OUT placement, per-iteration totals, R behaviour, and the
repeat-flag override.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(tape): accelerate ROM-trap loads of oversize blocks
events.message:
fix(tape): accelerate ROM-trap loads of oversize blocks

The LD-BYTES trap declined any block whose payload length didn't exactly
equal DE, so tapes carrying blocks one byte longer than requested fell
back to real-time loading. The real 48K ROM reads exactly DE bytes plus
a parity byte and ignores trailing bytes, so such blocks load fine on
hardware — e.g. the Paperboy (1989, MCM) re-release ships an 18-byte
header read with DE=17, and data blocks one byte over their declared
length. Decline only when the block is shorter than DE; copy DE bytes
and consume the whole block otherwise. Looser than FUSE's exact check,
but the trap doesn't verify parity anyway so fidelity is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: test: acceleration reliability regression tests
events.message:
test: acceleration reliability regression tests

Coverage for all four acceleration fixes:

- dt=0 edge boundary: verify that when tStatesToNextEdge() returns 0,
  the acceleration still crosses the edge and advances phase.
- Single-edge advance: verify singleEdge=true stops after one edge
  while singleEdge=false crosses all edges within the advance window.
- Post-acceleration auto-stop suppression: verify synthetic B=0xFE
  does not poison auto-stop — lastBRead fix keeps bDiff in-shape.
- Pipeline reset on play-state change: verify onTapePlayStateChange
  clears all four length pipeline fields plus accelMode.
- Per-signature auto-stop thresholds: verify Speedlock (threshold 4),
  Alkatraz (threshold 3), and unknown/default (threshold 2) all stop
  the tape only after the correct number of out-of-shape reads, and
  respect per-signature gap tolerances (2000T for Speedlock, 1500T for
  Alkatraz, 1000T default).
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: tape deck single-edge advance for surgical acceleration
events.message:
fix: tape deck single-edge advance for surgical acceleration

Add a singleEdge parameter to TapeDeck.advance(). When true, the method
processes at most one edge boundary and returns, preventing the surgical
loader accelerator from crossing multiple pulse boundaries in a single
step. Without this, dt can span across short sync pulses into the data
phase, causing the two-slot length pipeline to receive the wrong edge
category and desync the accelerator.

The edge-loader's accelerate() now calls tape.advance(dt, true) so each
acceleration step processes exactly one edge.
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: edge loader acceleration reliability
events.message:
fix: edge loader acceleration reliability

Three fixes for the edge-based tape acceleration system:

1. Handle dt=0 in accelerate(): when tStatesToNextEdge() returns 0 (the
   edge is exactly due), the old code skipped tape advancement but still
   mutated CPU state — the loader would re-read the same edge. Now
   advance at least 1 T-state so the edge fires and earBit toggles.

2. Fix lastBRead after acceleration: the old code set lastBRead to the
   synthetic B value (0xFE or 0x00), which poisoned auto-stop — the
   next real IN would compute a wild bDiff and, combined with any
   >1000T byte-processing gap, auto-stop would pause the tape mid-load.
   Now predict the expected B at re-entry (+1 for INCREASING, -1 for
   DECREASING) so the first bDiff after acceleration stays in-shape.

3. Reset edge pipeline on tape play-state change: onTapePlayStateChange
   now clears lengthKnown1/2 and lengthLong1/2, preventing stale edge
   data from a previous block contaminating the pipeline after stop.
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: ROM tape acceleration defensive start-gate
events.message:
fix: ROM tape acceleration defensive start-gate

Use !tape.playing instead of tape.paused for the start-playback gate in the
ROM trap. The tape loads as paused=true (media-manager, emulator) so the old
gate always fires on first trap, but !playing is more correct when the tape
reaches a stopped-but-not-paused state via stopPlayback() or other paths.

events.title: fix(tape): replay consumed block's trailing pause after ROM trap
events.message:
fix(tape): replay consumed block's trailing pause after ROM trap

After a ROM-trap instant-load, run out the loaded block's trailing gap
in real time before the next block's leader tone, mirroring real
hardware and the ROM edge loop. Loaders chained after a ROM block —
Speedlock installs its turbo loader from a BASIC bootstrap during the
gap — desync if the tape jumps straight to the next block's tone. For
pure-ROM multi-block tapes this costs nothing: the next LD-BYTES trap
fires and instant-loads long before the pause elapses.

events.title: feat(cpc): CRTC frame-restart on live R4 enables rupture/split-screen
events.message:
feat(cpc): CRTC frame-restart on live R4 enables rupture/split-screen

The CRTC now re-reads R4 (vertical total) at each character-row boundary and
restarts its internal frame when reached — resetting the row/raster counters
and reloading the memory address from R12/R13 live. Reducing R4 (or R7)
mid-frame therefore restarts the frame early with the current screen base,
which is how hardware rupture / split-screen works: the lines below the
restart are re-based to a new address. R5 vertical-total-adjust scanlines are
also now sequenced before the restart.

This is transparent to standard programming: for R4=38/R9=7/R5=0 the restart
coincides with the host frame loop's 312-line count, so MA progression and
frame timing are identical (verified: real os6128 boots pixel-perfect,
tStatesPerFrame=79872). R12/R13 stays frame-latched (correct 6845 behaviour;
per-frame hardware scrolling already worked) — a mid-row R13 write does not
shift the current row.

Adds tests for the restart point, R5 adjust, mid-frame R4 rupture with
R12/R13 reload, and the no-mid-row-reseed invariant.

events.title: docs(cpc): correct CAS READ trap scope to headers-only
events.message:
docs(cpc): correct CAS READ trap scope to headers-only

Verified the instant-load trap against a real CDT (2048.cdt) + real os6128
firmware via headless boot. The record layout and CRC convention are
correct (extracts the real filename + full 2K data records). But only the
64-byte file HEADER actually instant-loads: making the header instant
shifts the firmware's cassette timing so the following data block pulse-
plays past before its own CAS READ is reached, and the trap then declines
on the drifted block. Bulk file data still pulse-loads via tapeTurbo.

Corrects the previously overclaiming comments (which said the layout was
unverified and implied full-load coverage) in cpc-tape-loader.ts and
cpc-machine.ts. A true data instant-load needs the pulse engine and trap
to share tape position without starving the firmware's inter-block edge
sync — a deeper rework, attempted and reverted (see project notes).

Adds spec-derived tests for the previously-untested CPC raster core:

events.title: fix(cpc): cassette motor is PPI Port C bit 4, not bit 5

fix(cpc): cassette motor is PPI Port C bit 4, not bit 5

The CPC 8255 PPI assigns Port C bit 4 (0x10) to cassette motor control;
bit 5 (0x20) is cassette write data. We had the motor on bit 5. Confirmed
against Caprice32 (cap32.cpp: `tape_motor = val & 0x10`, read back on
bit 4). Low blast radius — tape advance is cadence-gated, not motor-gated,
and the 6128 firmware never spins the motor relay — but tapeMotorOn (UI
LED, snapshot Port-C readback) was driven off the wrong bit.

events.title: feat(cpc): instant firmware tape loading; unify tape-loader naming
events.message:
feat(cpc): instant firmware tape loading; unify tape-loader naming

CPC instant load: a normal BASIC `RUN"` never executes the &BCA1 RAM
jumpblock — the firmware reaches its cassette block-read routine
internally (CAS IN CHAR refilling its buffer). Trap that internal routine
instead, located by a version-independent signature scan of the lower OS
ROM (os464/os664/os6128), re-scanned when ROMs change. On a successful
load, resume in the routine's teardown tail (entry + 0x0D) with the
post-read register state (IX = buffer, DE = page-adjusted count, carry =
success) so the firmware runs its own motor-off / PPI restore.

Naming: unify the three tape acceleration features across CPC and ZX as
Fast ROM loading / Fast edge loading / Turbo while loading. Rename the
settings signals (tapeFastRom/tapeFastEdge/tapeTurbo) and the machine
field (tapeInstantLoad → tapeFastRom); persisted setting keys are kept
stable so saved prefs survive. Surface all applicable toggles per machine
(wire up the previously-orphaned edge toggle; expose Turbo on the CPC).

events.title: fix(tape): instant loader corrupted stack on partial LD-BYTES entry
events.message:
fix(tape): instant loader corrupted stack on partial LD-BYTES entry

The ROM-trap instant loader fired at 0x056C and unconditionally popped
two words, assuming the 0x053F (SA/LD-RET) filler that LD-BYTES pushes
at 0x0561 is always on the stack. Loaders that CALL into LD-BYTES after
that push (e.g. Solseed enters at 0x0562) never stack the 0x053F, so the
top word is the caller's real return address. The extra pop discarded it
and jumped PC to garbage, unwinding back to the BASIC main loop which
then HALTed with interrupts disabled -- a permanent hang.

Pop the 0x053F only when it is actually present, matching FUSE (sets
PC=0x05E2 and lets the ROM's bare RET pop once) and ZEsarUX (single
pop_valor() at its 0x0562 trap). The normal LOAD path is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(plusd): add MGT +D disk interface (WD1772 + G+DOS)

Adds the MGT +D disk system for the 48K/128K/+2 (and, per models.ts, +2A/+3):
a WD1772 FDC, the 8KB G+DOS shadow ROM, and 8KB +D RAM overlaid into slot 0.

- src/cores/wd1772.ts: WD1772 controller (Type I-IV commands, read/write

events.title: fix(cpc): make Multiface Two Return survive mid-session enable
events.message:
fix(cpc): make Multiface Two Return survive mid-session enable

Two related fixes to the MF2 freeze cartridge's I/O shadow (the snoop of
write-only chip registers the toolkit's Return replays to restore state):

- Freeze recording while paged in. The shadow must hold the *interrupted
  program's* chip state, captured at STOP. Recording continued while the
  toolkit ran, so its own OUTs (UI mode/colours/ROM paging) clobbered the
  shadow and Return restored the toolkit's state — wrong mode/RAM config,
  crash. The real MF2 PAL gates capture the same way (cf. Caprice32).

- Seed the shadow when the cartridge is enabled mid-session. The PAL only
  captures while fitted, so switching MF2 on after boot left the shadow
  blank and Return crashed. seedShadow() reconstructs it from the live
  Gate Array / CRTC / ROM-select / PPI state by replaying the equivalent
  OUTs through recordOut, so STOP->Return restores the running program
  without a reboot.

events.title: refactor: extract shared frame driver into BaseMachine
events.message:
refactor: extract shared frame driver into BaseMachine

Spectrum and CpcMachine held two near-identical copies of the rAF frame
loop, wall-clock pacing, audio back-pressure, start/stop/destroy/tick/
runUntil lifecycle, and the MCP debug-surface fields. That scaffolding
now lives once in BaseMachine; both machines extend it.

Each machine supplies only what differs via hooks: runFrame(),
framePixels(), inTurbo(). The turbo path legitimately diverges, so it is
an overridable method — the base default is the CPC's fixed budget, and
the Spectrum overrides runTurboBurst()/exitTurbo() with its adaptive,
rAF-cadence-aware budget and accuracy/contention swap. Behaviour is
preserved verbatim.

Also dedupe the three emulator.ts mouse helpers behind one activeMice()
accessor instead of repeating the asSpectrum/asCpc branch.

Note: the live rAF frameLoop is not covered by the test suite (tests
drive tick()/runUntil()), so turbo/audio pacing wants a dev-server smoke
check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: feat(cpc): add Kempston and AMX mouse support
events.message:
feat(cpc): add Kempston and AMX mouse support

Reuse the existing Mouse pane for the CPC. Hardware port maps from CPCWiki.

Kempston: ports differ from the Spectrum (X=&FBEE, Y=&FBEF, buttons=&FAEF;
decoded on A10/A8/A4/A0, clear of the FDC) and the button bits are swapped
(bit0=right, bit1=left, no middle). KempstonMouse gained a ctor button-bit
map so the shared class serves both machines.

AMX: a different device from the Spectrum's Z80-PIO AMX — it rides keyboard
matrix line 9 (joystick 0), pulsing a direction bit LOW per mickey and
retiring one mickey per line-9 deselect. New CpcAmxMouse + a CpcKeyboard.amx
hook. The per-direction backlog is capped at one frame's drain so the pointer
stops promptly instead of coasting (the AMX's ~300Hz poll rate otherwise
leaves queued movement draining for ~0.7s after the mouse stops).

Machine-aware emulator mouse helpers; MOUSE LED wired for CPC.

Tests: tests/cpc/cpc-mouse.test.ts (button layouts, pulse/consume semantics,
keyboard integration, port decode, backlog cap).

events.title: feat(cpc): add Multiface Two (freeze cartridge + STOP/NMI)
events.message:
feat(cpc): add Multiface Two (freeze cartridge + STOP/NMI)

Add the Romantic Robot Multiface Two to the CPC, mirroring the Spectrum
Multiface: a Hardware-pane toggle and a red STOP button (NMI to 0x0066).

The cartridge is an 8K ROM + 8K RAM in one persistent 16K buffer overlaid
into slot 0 (ROM 0x0000-0x1FFF, RAM 0x2000-0x3FFF) via new CpcMemory
setSlot0Overlay/clearSlot0Overlay. Paging is OUT-decoded (&FEE8 in / &FEEA
out). The ROM (cpc-multiface2.rom) is fetched from the CDN and cached.

Crucially the cartridge snoops every OUT into a RAM shadow at the hardware
offsets (GA/CRTC/upper-ROM/PPI), because those chips are write-only and the
toolkit's Return reprograms them from that shadow; without it Return
restored garbage and crashed the CPC.

printable ASCII: the boot-banner © (0xA4), £ (0xA3), §/¶/±/÷, the ↑/^ swap
(↑ at 0x5E, caret displaced to 0xA0), Greek letters, box/block graphics and
arrows. ASCII codes are matched first so letters/digits always win a glyph
collision with a high-range graphic, leaving real text uncorrupted. Codes
with no Unicode equivalent (blank mosaic, DEL checker, 0xEF, 0xFC/FD) are
left unmapped so they read as spaces.

Source for the mapping: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amstrad_CPC_character_set,
cross-checked against the 6128 lower-ROM font glyphs.

Drop text-panel from SPECTRUM_ONLY_PANES so the Text (OCR) settings pane is
available in CPC mode — its font/size/offset/scale settings already feed the
CPC overlay path in Screen.tsx.
