events.title: feat(cpc): add mode-aware screen OCR / TEXT overlay
events.message:
feat(cpc): add mode-aware screen OCR / TEXT overlay

The CPC renders text through a fixed 8x8 font in the lower OS ROM
(&3800, 256 glyphs MSB-first), so OCR is deterministic rather than the
Spectrum's heuristic font hunt. New CpcScreenText decodes each 8x8 cell
mode-aware (mode 0/1/2 -> 4/2/1 bytes/col -> 20/40/80 cols; pixel decode
mirrors GateArray.plotChar, addressing mirrors renderScanline), treats
any non-zero pen as ink, and matches the ROM font normal + inverse.

Wires it up end to end: CpcMachine.ocrScreenForMcp (real, was a stub),
ocrScreenStyled (text + coloured HTML + match mask) and blankCells for
the framebuffer; the frame-bridge CPC branch drives the TEXT LED and the
transcribe overlay; Screen.tsx positions the overlay over the CPC active
area (border-crop viewport + pixelAspectX); the TEXT LED click guard is
relaxed from spectrum to machine. OcrGridName splits into SpectrumOcrGrid
and CpcOcrGrid so OCR_GRIDS/detectGrid stay Spectrum-only.

Verified against real OS6128+BASIC+AMSDOS: the boot banner OCRs cleanly
at auto grid 40x25. Tests paint glyphs via the documented CPC address
formula + per-mode pen packing and assert recovery in all three modes,
inverse video, and row stride.

events.title: fix(fdc): fail reads of undersized bad-CRC weak protection sectors
events.message:
fix(fdc): fail reads of undersized bad-CRC weak protection sectors

Ocean's "Game, Set and Match" +3 loader pairs a perfect filler sector
(T0 R=130, 512x0xA7) with a deliberately-unreadable weak sector (T0
R=121, 128-byte N=0, ST1/ST2=0x20) and wipes RAM (reset to 48K BASIC)
unless the weak-sector read FAILS. The FDC was reading it as a clean
success - the undersized-sector exception even stripped its CRC-error
bits - so the protection's must-fail check inverted and fired the bomb.

Report No Data + abnormal termination (and keep the sector's own error
bits) when an undersized sector also carries a genuine data-CRC error
and is not DDAM. Undersized DDAM payload sectors and full-size weak
sectors are unaffected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(media): re-mount persisted disks and tapes after a page reload
events.message:
fix(media): re-mount persisted disks and tapes after a page reload

init() skipped restoreMedia() whenever createMachine() restored an HMR/SZX
snapshot. That snapshot only captures RAM/CPU/AY state, not the mounted disk
and tape images (which are persisted separately, one blob per drive/tape in
IndexedDB). The snapshot is saved on every beforeunload, so a hard reload
restored the machine state but silently dropped the media.

Always restore media now: restoreMedia() loads the FDC image and tape blocks
plus UI state without touching the restored RAM, so a reload keeps both.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(fdc): READ_TRACK transfers sector data fields, not the raw track
events.message:
fix(fdc): READ_TRACK transfers sector data fields, not the raw track

READ TRACK (Read Diagnostic) on the uPD765A transfers the sectors' data
fields in physical order from the index hole, reporting the last sector's
real CHRN — not the gap/sync/ID/CRC bytes. We returned a 6250-byte raw track,
so loaders reading offset-sector tracks (Alkatraz tracks 7-31, R177+) got
0x4E gap filler where they expected data and failed with a disk error.

Now reads the sectors' data fields, honours EOT as a sector count, and reports
the true R so the loader learns the offset. Removes the now-unused raw-track
builder and CRC helpers. Fixes Alkatraz +3 (California Games).

Also simplifies the 0.4.1 changelog entries to one-liners.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(fdc): abnormal termination on data CRC error; keep deleted-data sectors stable
events.message:
fix(fdc): abnormal termination on data CRC error; keep deleted-data sectors stable

The uPD765A signals abnormal termination (ST0 IC=01) on a data CRC error during
READ_DATA. We returned ST0=0x00, so Hexagon-protected +3 disks read their
CRC-flagged sector, saw a clean read, and rebooted/hung. Now matches the
datasheet and Fuse's upd_fdc.c.

Also stop randomising a sector that carries both the control mark (deleted-data
address mark) and a data CRC error: that data is stable and meaningful (used by
Hexagon as a decryption key), so randomising it corrupted the key. Only a bare
CRC-error sector (weak, Speedlock-style) still varies per read.

Fixes the unreleased Ultimate compilation (Pssst, Tranz-am, etc.). Bumps to 0.4.1.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: memory: guard indirect autoconfig RAM allocation
events.message:
memory: guard indirect autoconfig RAM allocation

mapped_malloc() uses labels starting with "*" for indirect allocations.
Those allocations require a fixed start address.

Only enter that path when the caller opted in with canbang. This keeps
ordinary mappings from following that path because of label text alone.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: ppc: avoid QEMU IRQ lock inversion
events.message:
ppc: avoid QEMU IRQ lock inversion

QEMU 10 and newer take the BQL inside ppc_set_irq(). The external
interrupt path can call into QEMU while still holding the UAE PPC
spinlock.

That can deadlock if the main thread waits for QEMU BQL while the
QEMU CPU thread waits for the UAE spinlock.

Use the release-spinlock path for external interrupt injection. This
matches the ordering used for QEMU memory mapping and state changes.

events.title: ethernet: defer NIC receive injection to hsync
events.message:
ethernet: defer NIC receive injection to hsync

A2065/Ariadne injected packets directly from the host network
callback. With SLIRP or pcap this callback can run on a helper
thread, so receive DMA and interrupt updates could race PPC I/O
callbacks.

Queue received frames and drain them from the device hsync
handler, where the rest of the emulated card state is updated. Also
stop the NE2000 host callback from draining its queue, leaving that
work to the existing hsync path.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: slirp: avoid Unix thread sentinel in shared code
events.message:
slirp: avoid Unix thread sentinel in shared code

Track whether the builtin slirp helper thread was started. Do not
write BAD_THREAD into uae_thread_id from common code because Windows
uses HANDLE thread IDs and does not define that Unix sentinel.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: slirp: forward ICMP through datagram sockets
events.message:
slirp: forward ICMP through datagram sockets

Enable datagram ICMP forwarding, keep the host sockets nonblocking,
and strip host IP headers before delivering ICMP replies back to the
emulated Ethernet device.

events.title: slirp: check TCP connect completion with SO_ERROR
events.message:
slirp: check TCP connect completion with SO_ERROR

The nonblocking connect path treated a writable socket as connected
and then used a zero-length send as the failure probe. That is not a
reliable completion check and can mis-handle failed or pending guest
TCP connects.

Use getsockopt(SO_ERROR) when select reports the socket writable. Keep
pending connects pending, and only clear SS_ISFCONNECTING after the
host socket has no pending error.

The embedded bridgeboard glue provides its own file-local CPU tables
and model_init() helper. The public PCem header declarations are not
used by the UAE integration, and some of the names collide with those
local definitions when compiled as C++.

Disable the unused declarations in the imported headers instead of
removing individual entries. This avoids mixed-linkage conflicts while
leaving the original declarations visible in the source for reference.

events.title: pci: forward-declare bridge memory banks internally
events.message:
pci: forward-declare bridge memory banks internally

The PCI bridge code maps the config, I/O, memory, and bridge banks
before their definitions later in pci.cpp. Clang requires declarations
before those uses.

Keep the declarations and definitions in an anonymous namespace. The
objects remain private to pci.cpp even though the forward declarations
use extern syntax.

events.title: pcem: pass MIDI parser a byte buffer
events.message:
pcem: pass MIDI parser a byte buffer

Midi_Parse() takes a BYTE pointer. Store the uint8_t input in a local
BYTE before passing it on so the call does not depend on uint8_t and
BYTE being the same typedef on every host.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: pcem: select Voodoo codegen by host capability
events.message:
pcem: select Voodoo codegen by host capability

The imported Voodoo code only enabled its x86 code generators through
Windows-oriented preprocessor checks. That left Unix x86 builds with
the recompiler disabled even when the matching generator was compiled.

Derive explicit PCEM_VOODOO_CODEGEN macros from the host CPU and use
those macros for init, close, rendering, and the default recompiler
configuration.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: pcem: avoid dynamic offsetof in Voodoo codegen
events.message:
pcem: avoid dynamic offsetof in Voodoo codegen

The Voodoo x86 code generators compute offsets into array members
with offsetof(type, field[index]). Some compilers reject that
expression form.

Add helpers that derive the offset from field[0] plus an element
stride. That preserves the generated offsets without relying on a
runtime-indexed offsetof expression. This matches the same cleanup
merged upstream in 86Box.

events.title: pcem: fit graphics sources into C++ builds
events.message:
pcem: fit graphics sources into C++ builds

WinUAE builds the imported PCem graphics sources as C++ files.
The MGA source includes C atomics directly, and the BT482 RAMDAC
source uses C allocation declarations through C++ headers.

Use C++ atomics when compiling MGA as C++, and include the C++
cstdlib wrapper where the BT482 RAMDAC needs those declarations.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: pcem: make MGA high-bit masks unsigned
events.message:
pcem: make MGA high-bit masks unsigned

MGA defines several bit-31 masks from a signed int literal.
Shifting a signed 1 into the sign bit is undefined behavior in C.

Use UINT32_C(1) so the masks are built in unsigned arithmetic.
This matches the same cleanup merged upstream in 86Box, with the
extra OPTION_POWERPC mask that exists in this imported copy.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: pcem: fix helper thread handles
events.message:
pcem: fix helper thread handles

The PCem compatibility layer returned a raw uae_thread_id as a
thread_t pointer and then waited on that value through the semaphore
API. That was pointer-shaped on some targets, but it was not a valid
wrapper around UAE's thread API.

Store the uae_thread_id in an explicit PCem handle object, join it
with uae_wait_thread(), and free the wrapper after wait or close. Reset
and signal PCem events through the existing semaphore object instead of
passing the address of a local pointer copy.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: gfxboard: rewind Picasso IV flash before autoconfig
events.message:
gfxboard: rewind Picasso IV flash before autoconfig

Picasso IV autoconfig is read from the flash image, but the
initializer can run more than once while the expansion list is
scanned and sorted. loadp4rom() leaves the flash zfile positioned
later in the image, so a later dry scan read all-0xff data and the
board looked like it had no autoconfig block.

Seek back to the beginning before reading the Picasso IV
autoconfig bytes so repeated scans see the same board data.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: isofs: avoid undefined timezone sign extension
events.message:
isofs: avoid undefined timezone sign extension

make_date() sign-extends the ISO9660 timezone byte when the high
bit is set. (-1 << 8) shifts a negative signed value, which is
undefined behavior in C++.

Use ~0xff to build the same extension mask without relying on
that undefined shift.

events.author: tonioni

events.title: jit/x86-64: fix FPU FLDCW codegen crashes on 64-bit hosts
events.message:
jit/x86-64: fix FPU FLDCW codegen crashes on 64-bit hosts

The x86-64 JIT could crash when compiling FPU rounding-mode changes
(FLDCW with an indexed operand) via two defects in codegen_x86.cpp:

1. x86_64_rex() dereferenced its 'b' (REX.B) pointer unconditionally and
   ignored 'r'/'x'. raw_fldcw_m_indexed() passes its index register in the
   'x' (REX.X) slot with b == NULL, so the function read through a NULL
   pointer; an index register in r8-r15 would also have been mis-encoded.
   x86_64_rex() now null-guards each pointer and emits REX.R/X/B (and W).

2. raw_fldcw_m_indexed() loaded the 64-bit base of the x87 control-word
   table into RAX. RAX is allocatable (not in always_used[]) and may hold a
   live m68k value mid-block, and a LOWFUNC cannot declare a register
   clobber, so the allocator's view of RAX was silently corrupted; a later
   access through that register (e.g. MOVEM.L ...,-(An)) then dereferenced
   the table pointer as an m68k address and faulted. The base is now
   materialized in a push/pop-preserved scratch register chosen to differ
   from the index register.

Only x86-64 is affected; the 32-bit path uses a direct FLDCW [reg] encoding
and ARM64 uses different codegen.
events.author: midwan

flowchart: add movement action handler diagrams

Four per-routine decision-tree flowcharts for MAIN_LOOP's phase-3 SMC
slots: DO_ASCEND ($6378), DO_DESCEND ($63B4), DO_MOVE_RIGHT ($6409) and
DO_MOVE_LEFT ($646D, the structural mirror of right). Branch structure is
exact; multi-instruction blocks (floor-index propagation + hit-slot wipe,
descent self-stop SMC patch + ZP_LAST_DIR refresh, stance walk-cycle) are
summarized. Includes a shared notes block on floor mirrors, the stance
gating, and the DESC_LANDED_CLEAR shared tail. Derived from the movement
action handlers chunk in main.nw.

events.title: flowchart: add MAIN_LOOP per-frame expansion diagram
events.message:
flowchart: add MAIN_LOOP per-frame expansion diagram

Second Mermaid diagram expanding MAIN_LOOP ($67CB) into its ~25 ordered
per-frame subroutine calls, grouped into 9 phases plus a Game-entry box.
Entry point (GAME_START_INIT -> JMP MAIN_LOOP) is pinned to the top; the
per-frame loop returns to the $67CB frame top, not through GAME_START_INIT.

Subgraphs are declared in reverse order so dagre renders them top-to-bottom
(last-declared floats to the top; see mermaid-js/mermaid#2789); an inline %%
comment documents this. Single-line subgraph titles + subGraphTitleMargin
avoid the multiline-title overlap (#3806).

Splits the last large raw HEX blob in the level1 target (the 3072-byte
$6700-$72FF game-engine/attract window) into per-routine L1_ chunks,
each mirroring its drol.bin twin: FLOOR_ENEMY_ADVANCE tail, FLOOR_ENEMY_DRAW,
SFX_TONE, MAIN_LOOP, DRAW_ENTITIES, LEVEL_INTRO_TICK, the special
tick/draw/step/inactive group, COMPANION_UPDATE, RESCUE_UPDATE,
DIFFICULTY_UPDATE, LIFE_LOST_HANDLER, ATTRACT_LOOP, START_ATTRACT, the
table pad, and SCREEN_ROW_ADDR_HI. Adds a Pages 67-72 subsection with an
L1-label/drol-twin/span/bytes/role table. level1 stays 100% byte-perfect.

events.title: perf(z80): inline fetch8/fetch16, trim step+runFrame hot paths
events.message:
perf(z80): inline fetch8/fetch16, trim step+runFrame hot paths

CPU-internal cleanup chasing the post-flat-memory profile (read8 is now
3.6% self; the cost sits in the dispatch infrastructure).

- Inline fetch8 and fetch16 at all 41 call sites across exec-main/ed/
  index/cb and step(). Eliminates one Z80.prototype.* call per opcode
  byte fetch — Firefox can't reliably inline through that boundary, so
  the call-frame overhead was dominating fetch8 self-time at 12.5%.
  Delete the now-dead fetch8/fetch16 methods from core.ts.

- Drop postStepHook from step() and core.ts. It was assigned only to
  null and ceremonially restored by the MCP trace tool; pure dead
  weight on every instruction. Strip the corresponding save/restore
  from mcp/tools/trace.ts.

- Drop the elapsed<=0 defensive bump and step()'s return value. Nobody
  reads it; it was a guard against opcodes that don't bump tStates,
  which we'd treat as a real bug now.

- runFrame: cache watchActive once per frame. The post-step
  portWatchHit/memWatchHit null-compare ran on every instruction even
  when no watchpoints were set. Caching collapses the common case to
  a single boolean.

- runFrame: hoist advanceTapeTo's playing/paused early-exit into the
  loop body, skipping the method-call frame when tape is idle. Add
  a synchronous ula.tapeActive = false in onPlayStateChange so the
  hoisted check doesn't strand a stale tapeEarBit when the tape stops
  mid-frame.

events.title: fix(memory): write-through for aliased bank slots
events.message:
fix(memory): write-through for aliased bank slots

When two slots map the same RAM bank (e.g. port 0x7FFD currentBank=5
puts bank 5 into both slot 1 and slot 3, or currentBank=2 into slots
2 and 3), real hardware sees both windows as the same physical chip.
The previous flat-memory commit only synced the slots at map-in time
(source-fallback in _switchRam); subsequent CPU writes to one slot
silently failed to appear at the other.

FUSE handles this naturally because its hot path is pointer-based
(memory_map_read[page].page[offset]) and two slots can point at the
same bank. Our flat model needs explicit write-through.

Implementation:
- slotAlias: Int8Array(4) — slot index of the mirror, or -1. Refreshed
  via _refreshAliases() after every paging change.
- io-ports write8 (CPU hot path) and memory.writeByte (debug/snapshot
  path) check slotAlias and store to the mirror when non-negative.
- setBankFromSnapshot already iterated all slots holding the target
  bank, so it was already alias-correct.

Hot-path cost: one Int8Array load + a predictable-false branch in the
common no-aliasing case. The branch is dead-cheap for SpiderMonkey to
predict.

Adds four tests in memory.test.ts covering the live write-through case,
the alias-break case (data preserved on the still-mapped slot), and
the snapshot path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: perf: flat 64KB memory + contend closure swap for Firefox turbo
events.message:
perf: flat 64KB memory + contend closure swap for Firefox turbo

Three related changes that target the per-instruction hot path Firefox's
JIT couldn't optimise through the previous closure indirection:

1. contendN early-out on accurateTiming. The wrapper now bails before
   the loop in turbo mode instead of dispatching the closure N times.

2. Swap cpu.contend between accurate impl and no-op on turbo enter/exit.
   _contendAccurate holds the cycle-exact implementation; NOOP_CONTEND
   is a module-scope empty function. SpiderMonkey can inline the no-op
   at the hundreds of bare this.contend(addr) sites across exec-main/
   ed/index/cb instead of indirecting through an assigned closure with
   an interior accurateTiming branch.

3. Flat 64KB memory model. SpectrumMemory now backs the Z80's address
   space with a single Uint8Array(0x10000); RAM banks become cold
   storage for unmapped banks. The hot read path collapses from
   slots[addr>>>14][addr&0x3FFF] (two array loads) to flat[addr&0xFFFF]
   (one). Bank switches do 16KB memcpy back to cold + 16KB memcpy in
   from cold; the same-bank short-circuit keeps no-op switches free.

   getRamBank(n) returns a live flat.subarray view if the bank is
   currently mapped, cold storage otherwise — so screen rendering,
   snapshot save, debug tools, and frame-bridge all work without
   explicit flush calls. setBankFromSnapshot writes to both cold and
   any live mapping for consistency. Bank aliasing (currentBank=5
   putting bank 5 into slot 1 and slot 3) is handled via source-
   fallback on load: the new slot copies from the live aliased slot
   rather than stale cold storage. Cross-slot write-through is not
   modelled — real software almost never relies on it.

Profile chain on Firefox turbo: contendN 28.7% -> 0, runFrame self
22.1% -> 5.6%; cpu.read8 should drop substantially in the next pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: perf: cache slot contention + inline memory hook hot path
events.message:
perf: cache slot contention + inline memory hook hot path

Two related optimisations to the per-instruction memory access path:

1. Per-slot contention cache. Contention now owns a Uint8Array(4)
   slotContended, refreshed on every paging change via a new
   memory.onSlotsChanged callback. isContended(addr) collapses from
   bankAt() + variant.isContended() (virtual dispatch through the
   strategy object) to a single array load. Verified that every variant's
   isContended depends only on (slot, bank), never the in-slot offset,
   so the cache is exact. Helps accurate-timing mode too (MCP, tests).

2. Capture stable references in installMemoryHooks. memory.slots and
   contention.slotContended are now exposed and captured as closure
   locals, and read8/write8 index them directly instead of going through
   memory.readByte / contention.isContended method calls. Same change
   for cpu, replacing s.cpu.* chains throughout the hot path. This
   should let SpiderMonkey monomorphise the read path the way V8 already
   does (Firefox lagged Edge by ~1.7x before).

memory.bankSwitch and bankSwitch1FFD mutate _slots directly without
going through updateSlots, so onSlotsChanged is fired at the end of
each method to keep the cache exact.
events.author: damieng

events.title: perf(turbo): skip ULA contention via cpu.accurateTiming flag
events.message:
perf(turbo): skip ULA contention via cpu.accurateTiming flag

Per-instruction ULA contention is the dominant non-CPU cost in the hot
path: every memory read/write/IR-refresh runs isContended -> bankAt ->
variant.isContended (virtual dispatch through the strategy object) plus
a contentionDelay() with a floating-point division when contended.

Add cpu.accurateTiming (default true) and short-circuit the contention
chain in read8/write8/contend/portIn/portOut when it is false. The UI
turbo path in frameLoop toggles it off on enter and back on exit, in
the same block that saves/restores scanlineAccuracy.

MCP (mcp/tools/trace.ts, mcp/tools/machine.ts) and the test suites
never set spectrum.turbo, so they keep cycle-exact timing. The default
path is unchanged; only the explicit UI turbo opts out.

Measured ~3x speedup in Firefox and ~5x in Edge on a 240Hz display.
events.author: damieng

events.title: perf(turbo): adaptive rAF budget, skip audio, throttle UI
events.message:
perf(turbo): adaptive rAF budget, skip audio, throttle UI

Turbo mode previously capped at a hard 14 frames per rAF with full audio
generation and per-rAF UI reactivity, which left a lot of CPU on the table
and did not scale to high-refresh displays.

- Replace the fixed frame cap in frameLoop with a time budget adapted to
  the measured rAF interval (70% EWMA-smoothed, clamped 1.5-14ms). Avoids
  overshooting the cadence and triggering browser rAF throttling on
  240Hz displays.
- Force scanlineAccuracy='low' while turbo is active and skip the bulk
  renderFrame() on intermediate frames in a batch -- only the final frame
  produces displayed pixels. Convert scanlineAccuracy to a getter/setter
  so external writes (e.g. applyDisplaySettings after a renderer swap)
  update the saved user choice instead of clobbering the forced 'low'.
- Skip per-instruction mixer.accumulate/generateSamples in turbo (the
  buffer fills faster than realtime and the sound is unrecognisable).
  Cache the turbo flag once per frame so the hot loop does not re-read
  two properties per instruction.
- In frame-bridge onFrame, throttle the heavy Solid.js batch() block
  (LEDs, registers, sysvar/BASIC, transcribe/OCR) to ~10Hz during turbo.
  Speed readout, breakpoint check, and floppy sound updates still run
  every rAF.

events.message:
refactor(mcp): split src/mcp-server.ts into mcp/ module tree

The MCP server is a Node-only entry point with no place in src/ (which is
browser/Solid code) — Vite and tsconfig both had to special-case it. Move
it under a top-level mcp/ folder and split the 1705-line monolith into
focused modules so tools are easier to read and become unit-testable.

Layout: mcp/server.ts is the entry, mcp/tools/*.ts groups tool handlers
by topic (machine, memory, breakpoints, traps, io, media, trace,
peripherals, symbols), shared helpers (state, format, loader, traps,
fdc-log, rom-fetch, hex) sit at the mcp/ root. installTrapHook and
wireFdcLog now take spec as a parameter instead of closing over module
state, which removes a circular-import risk and makes them directly
testable.

Also drops the tsconfig exclude so MCP code is finally type-checked, and
moves the ROM cache from src/.cache/ to mcp/.cache/.

events.title: refactor(tape,audio): make cpuClock a required constructor arg
events.message:
refactor(tape,audio): make cpuClock a required constructor arg

TapeDeck and AudioMixer previously defaulted cpuClock to Z80_CLOCK_48K
as a class-field fallback, requiring callers to remember a post-
construction assignment to get the right clock for non-48K machines.
The misleading 'Z80_CLOCK_48K' import made these subsystems read as
hardcoded to 48K timing when in fact every production caller already
supplies the variant's clock. Drop the default, make the arg required,
and let the compiler catch silent miswiring.

events.title: feat(tape): edge-loader subsystem with surgical accel, fixed auto-stop, split UI toggles
events.message:
feat(tape): edge-loader subsystem with surgical accel, fixed auto-stop, split UI toggles

Replaces the LoaderDetector + loader-signature pair with a unified EdgeLoader
that handles §2 auto play/stop, §3 structural fingerprinting, and §4 surgical
edge acceleration (see docs/edge-loading.md). Fixes a clutch of issues that
showed up while loading Speedlock 1:

- accelerate(): refresh lastTStatesRead/lastBRead to post-accel CPU state.
  Without this, advancing tape by a full pulse (~2168T for pilot) left the
  next IN A,(\$FE) computing a huge tDiff and a synthetic bDiff outside
  {0,1,0xFF} -- auto-stop fired two reads later and the leader bars flapped.

- Auto-stop: require BOTH wide tDiff AND unexpected bDiff (was OR). The 48K
  ROM's LD-MARKER reloads B,\$B0 between every bit, so under OR a couple of
  close bit boundaries stopped the tape mid-block during sync->data.

- loaderActive: set on in-shape polling while already playing, not just on
  the §2 'start' event. The instant-ROM trap and manual Play both unpause
  the tape without firing 'start', so spectrum.ts's per-frame tapeLoading
  check never saw a signal to engage tape turbo on the post-trap stage.

Two real bugs surfaced while writing the tests:

     over overlapping bit ranges (A<<24 collides with DE<<16, F<<16
     with DE<<16, BC with HL). It also ignored IX/IY/SP/I/shadow/
     memptr entirely, so a loop driven by IX (e.g. INC IX ; JR -4)
     silently collapsed to a single iteration in the trace. Replaced
     with a combining hash over A/F/BC/DE/HL/IX/IY/SP/I via Math.imul.
     R and memptr stay excluded because they tick on most instructions
     and would defeat dedup.

  2. formatPortTally nulled _portTallyIn / _portTallyOut at the end

events.title: refactor(tape): align ROM trap with FUSE — trap at 0x056C, paging-aware
events.message:
refactor(tape): align ROM trap with FUSE — trap at 0x056C, paging-aware

Move the LD-BYTES trap from 0x0556 to LD-START at 0x056C (FUSE's trap
point, just past the EX AF,AF' and BREAK check). Two reasons:

  1. A handful of protected loaders CALL 0x056C directly to reuse part
     of LD-BYTES without the entry preamble. Trapping at 0x0556 misses
     those; 0x056C catches both entry paths.
  2. The trap now jumps PC to 0x05E2 (POP AF; RET) on success and lets
     the real ROM clean up the stack — no manual SP pop, no IFF
     fiddling. The POP AF loads F=0x3F from the 0x053F pushed at
     0x0561, giving carry=1 = "load succeeded" naturally.

Replace the byte-sniff (memory[0x0556]==0x14) with a proper paging
check on memory.isBasicRomActive(). The 48K BASIC ROM is always
romPages[length-1]; the helper also rejects specialPaging and
externalRomPaged (Multiface/VTX-5000) states. Previously a custom RAM
bank with 0x14 at 0x0556 would have mis-fired on +2A/+3.

Add a FUSE-style block-length sanity check: if block.data.length !==
DE the trap declines and the real ROM runs LD-BYTES at full fidelity.
This lets custom-speed turbos and protected blocks coexist with the
trap — the heuristic only fires for exact-match standard blocks.

To support the decline-without-side-effects contract, split
nextDataBlock() into peekDataBlock() (advances over cosmetic blocks
but leaves the data block in place) + commit. The trap peeks, checks
flag/length, and only commits on success.

Drop the unconditional 2168 T-state injection; the real LD-BYTES
preamble accounts for those T-states naturally, and the POP AF; RET
cleanup at 0x05E2 covers the rest.

Tests rewritten to pin the new contract: decline on no-block /
flag-mismatch / length-mismatch / short-block / long-block; on
success copy bytes, set PC=0x05E2, leave SP and IFFs untouched.

Cross-referenced against FUSE tape.c (Philip Kendall, GPL-2.0),
ZEsarUX storage/tape.c, and JSpeccy Tape.java.

events.title: refactor(plus3): split disk-format/protection detection out of dsk.ts

refactor(plus3): split disk-format/protection detection out of dsk.ts

Extract detectDiskFormat, detectProtection and all 15 detector helpers
into src/plus3/disk-detect.ts. dsk.ts shrinks from 745 to 417 lines and
imports the two public functions.

Bug fixes uncovered while expanding test coverage:

- serializeDSK now aligns each track's allocation to a 256-byte multiple.
  The EDSK per-track size table at 0x34 stores size/256, so unaligned
  totals (from short protection sectors etc.) caused the writer's offsets
  and the table to disagree, corrupting every subsequent track on read.

- Detector ordering: detectDiscsys now runs before detectPlayers
  (DiscSYS's CHRN-all-equal-index is a strict superset of Players'
  r-and-n-equal-index, so the reverse order misclassified every DiscSYS
  disk as Players). detectStudioB now runs before detectPms for the
  same reason -- Studio B / DiscLoc layouts also match PMS's unsigned
  heuristic.

- detectFrontier rewritten. The signed signature was truncated to
  "W DISK PROTECTION..." (worked only as an accidental substring of
  "NEW DISK..."); the unsigned heuristic looked for T0/S0=4096b + T9
  1-sector -- the opposite of the real disk layout. Confirmed against
  a CPDRead dump: T0 = 9 x 512b PCW sectors, then >=10 subsequent
  tracks each a single 4096-byte sector with R=1.

Test coverage grows from 69 to 157 (91 in dsk.test.ts + 95 in the new
disk-detect.test.ts), covering every format-detection branch, every
detector with positive + guard-rejection cases, all 10 Speedlock signed
variants, all 4 P.M.S. variants, and the new Frontier real-disk layout.

events.title: fix(ocr): un-pin shifted-coincidence font scan bug
events.message:
fix(ocr): un-pin shifted-coincidence font scan bug

scanBanksAtOffset's per-glyph "does any character slot in this 768-byte
window match?" question doesn't care WHICH slot matches, so any window
overlapping the real font by a multiple of 8 bytes scores 100% by
matching every screen glyph against the wrong character slot. With
zero padding ahead of the font those shifted twins all clear the
existing space-slot prefilter, and the byte-by-byte sweep hands the
earliest 0.95+ scorer to the early-exit — silently returning a window
that decodes screen 'A' as some other code entirely.

Add a structural prefilter: slot '!' (window bytes 8..15) must be
non-empty. Every real font (ROM, CHARS, +3 editor, the Nicety fixture
added here) populates '!' as a real glyph; every shifted-down twin
ends up with either the real font's empty space-slot OR pre-font
padding in '!', so they fail before scoring.

The previously-pinned screen-text cases get re-fixtured around the
Nicety 8×8 font (public-domain, 768 bytes, every printable slot
populated) so the test surfaces the bug under the conditions a real
font would meet — the synthetic sparse GLYPHS map only defined 6
letters and would itself fail the new prefilter.

events.title: fix(spectrum): un-pin AY sample-rate and eiDelay-INT bugs

the AY from `audio.sampleRate` and resyncs it (plus cyclesPerSample and
the DC-blocker alpha) via a new `AY3891x.setSampleRate()` once
`audio.init()` reports the AudioContext's real rate. `Audio` stops
forcing 44.1 kHz on the context and defaults to 48 kHz so consumers
reading the field before init() see a representative value.

eiDelay INT: `intPending` was `intT === 0 && !iff1`, treating DI as the
only reason a frame-boundary ack could fail. When `eiDelay` was the
blocker, the retry never armed and the INT was silently dropped. The
INT line is held LOW for the model's window regardless of which flag
blocked the ack — gate `intPending` on `intT === 0` alone so the
existing retry covers both cases.

Both pinned `it.fails` cases in tests/spectrum.test.ts are inverted to
positive assertions. The AY test also pins `cyclesPerSample` to the new
rate so a future partial fix gets caught.

events.title: tests(spectrum): add headless coverage, pin 3 real bugs
events.message:
tests(spectrum): add headless coverage, pin 3 real bugs

44 tests against a real headless Spectrum (no display, no AudioContext)
covering IOActivity, construction per variant, reset chain,
tick/runUntil, breakpoints, port and memory watchpoints, flushBeam
dispatch, tracing modes, portio tally, HALT fast-path, frame boundary
T-state stability, portLabel routing, and load* delegation.

3 it.fails pin real bugs surfaced during the audit:
- AY sample rate hardcoded to 44100, ignoring the eventual audio
  context rate (slight mistuning on 48kHz contexts).
- Tape cooldown auto-pauses the tape even when tapeTurbo=false:
  the cooldown counter is set on any tape activity, not gated on
  turbo having engaged.
- An interrupt blocked by eiDelay at frame boundary is silently
  dropped: spectrum.runFrame tracks intPending as
  `intT === 0 && !iff1`, missing the eiDelay-blocked case.

events.title: Replace strncat() with Str_Copy()
events.message:
Replace strncat() with Str_Copy()

gemdos.c uses strncat() as a replacement for the non-portable strlcpy()
in a couple of places. While the usage looks correct here, strncat() is
generally quite a bad function (since the length parameter does not
directly specify the size of the destination buffer, and you always have
to remember to take the additional NUL character into account in your
calculations), so we should rather completely ban it from the Hatari
sources. Let's use our own Str_Copy() function instead, that way the code
is much easier to understand.

events.title: Bootstrap Godot project + adf/rnc/team decoders + variant abstraction
events.message:
Bootstrap Godot project + adf/rnc/team decoders + variant abstraction

Three CLI tools and a Godot project that proves the PC/Amiga variant
abstraction works end-to-end:

- tools/adf-extract: pure-C# Amiga DD ADF reader (OFS + FFS). Verified
  against both SWOS Amiga floppies (125 files extracted, OFS Standard,
  volumes "SWOS" and "SWOS2").
- tools/rnc-decode: RNC ProPack v1 decoder. Both Amiga SWOS executables
  (165735 and 168061 bytes packed) decompress with CRC OK to 351596 and
  357226 bytes respectively. Implementation follows aybe/RNCUnpacker's
  model: 2-byte init, eager refill (bitcount < 16), p starts at offset 0.
- tools/team-decode: SWOS PC/Amiga TEAM.* parser. Verified team header
  (coach offset +0x24 not +0x26 as some specs claim), 3-bit-nibble skill
  packing, decimal nation-code filename suffix. ARSENAL TEAM.008 yields
  ARSENE WENGER as coach and Bergkamp with all-8 P/S/H/T/C/Sp/F.
- game/: Godot 4.6.2 + C# (.NET 9) project with IAssetSource interface
  and concrete PcAssetSource + AmigaAssetSource implementations. Game
  builds + runs headless, loading 1730 PC teams and 1616 Amiga teams from
  the local reference data — both yielding identical first team
  (ALBPETROL PATOS / FATMIR DOGANI / LEONARD HASA) which proves the
  format truly is shared across variants.

Tooling itself is held in .tools/godot/ (portable, gitignored). Original
SWOS data dirs stay gitignored. CLAUDE.md and READMEs updated to match
working build/run commands.

events.title: Emit chaos_creatures from gen_chaos_data_c.py in real piece-code order via the $E3E0 lookup table, matching the actual game's piece-code mapping rather than chaos.py CREATURES display order.
events.message:
Emit chaos_creatures from gen_chaos_data_c.py in real piece-code order via the $E3E0 lookup table, matching the actual game's piece-code mapping rather than chaos.py CREATURES display order.

Previously the generator iterated chaos.py CREATURES (sorted by name_addr for the HtmlWriter's display table) and emitted entries in that order, with the implicit assumption that chaos_creatures[i] = piece code (i+1). The chaos.ctl annotation at $E3E0 ("39 two-byte pointers ... indexed by piece code minus 1") is the actual source of truth for the piece-code-to-creature mapping, and that ordering is completely different - e.g. Bat is real piece 22, Ghost is 29, Magic Fire is 35.

Now: the generator reads the $E3E0 entries, pairs each name_addr with the chaos.py CREATURES tuple by name_addr to inherit the undead/flying/mount flags, and emits chaos_creatures with one entry per piece code 1..40. Piece 1 is the corpse placeholder at $E440 (empty name); piece 40 is Wall (special case at $EA16, not in $E3E0).

Also emit named piece-code constants in chaos_data.h: CHAOS_PIECE_GHOST=29, CHAOS_PIECE_WRAITH=31, CHAOS_PIECE_MAGIC_FIRE=35, CHAOS_PIECE_BLOB=34, plus the structure codes 36-40, so port code can refer to them by name.

events.title: Resolve the BA77 scan_line_squares annotation: confirm and document that piece codes 29 (Ghost), 31 (Wraith), 35 (Magic Fire) plus corpse-flagged tiles get overpainted with the empty highlight sprite at $EB51 immediately before the Bresenham line walk in $98DB. This is the LOS transparency mechanism - empirically verified by user testing 2026-05-02. Removes the 'needs further verification' caveat that was on the original annotation.
events.message:
Resolve the BA77 scan_line_squares annotation: confirm and document that piece codes 29 (Ghost), 31 (Wraith), 35 (Magic Fire) plus corpse-flagged tiles get overpainted with the empty highlight sprite at $EB51 immediately before the Bresenham line walk in $98DB. This is the LOS transparency mechanism - empirically verified by user testing 2026-05-02. Removes the 'needs further verification' caveat that was on the original annotation.

Update $BABE annotation to make explicit that the highlight sprite at $EB51 is empty (32 zero bytes) and that calling $BABE on a transparent piece's tile ERASES that piece's pixels for the duration of the LOS check.
events.author: Lewis Lane

events.title: Add tools/trace_los.py and tools/debug_los.py for investigating the LOS transparency mechanism.
events.message:
Add tools/trace_los.py and tools/debug_los.py for investigating the LOS transparency mechanism.

The harness currently fails to reproduce the live game's LOS-blocking behaviour - even Wall and Giant Rat (which empirically block in-game) come back clear under trace. A sanity check that pre-paints framebuffer pixels confirms $98DB itself works, so the bug is that the IM 2 ISR / MPRINT-driven board-render path doesn't actually paint sprites under trace.py interrupt simulation. Left in tree as a starting point for further investigation; see chaos-c docs/los.md for the empirical state.
events.author: Lewis Lane

events.title: Extend tools/gen_chaos_data_c.py to emit the AI piece-weight table at $C6D4 as chaos_ai_piece_weights[49] for the chaos-c port.
events.message:
Extend tools/gen_chaos_data_c.py to emit the AI piece-weight table at $C6D4 as chaos_ai_piece_weights[49] for the chaos-c port.

Correct the $C6D4 annotation: indexing is direct piece_code (the Z80 code at $C858 does ADD HL,BC with C = piece_code, no offset), not piece_code - 2 as the previous prose claimed. Replace the imprecise example values with the verified values from the snapshot in ROM order, and note that the score loop filters at piece_code >= 38 so wizard-shaped lookups (which would otherwise overrun into bytes 47-48 holding 34 and 5) never happen.

events.title: Add verified combat bonus magnitudes to the wizard buff annotations.
events.message:
Add verified combat bonus magnitudes to the wizard buff annotations.

Document at $AC16 that the combat-resolve routine reads Shield/Armour as a packed 2-bit number from bits 7|6 of wizard_status, so Armour intrinsically gives +3 to defender B162 (not +2 plus +1 from Shield) and the +2-alone case is unreachable in normal play.

Add explicit bonus magnitudes to $836A Magic Armour (+3 effective), $839C Magic Sword (+4 to B161), $83D0 Magic Knife (+2), $8404 Magic Shield (+1) and $84D3 Shadow Form apply (+3 to B162, additive with Shield/Armour so Armour+ShadowForm gives +6).

Correct the $AC16 cross-reference for the Shadow Form spell address (was '#R$8400+', now points to the actual apply routine at #R$84D3).

events.title: Annotated all 127 remaining untitled routines, taking the disassembly to 100% c-routine coverage (335 of 335 routines now carry titles, descriptions and labels).
events.message:
Annotated all 127 remaining untitled routines, taking the disassembly to 100% c-routine coverage (335 of 335 routines now carry titles, descriptions and labels).

Wave 3 covered 62 routines: the magic-weapon common-paths ($837D-$8486), the Subversion / RaiseDead / Turmoil sub-routines ($851B-$872B), the spell-orchestration helpers ($9324-$97BB), the board / range / cursor helpers ($BE86-$C0D8) including the chessboard-distance predicate at $BEE8 (formula: 2*max(dx,dy) + min(dx,dy)), and the AI movement and target-evaluation helpers ($C9D4-$CDB8).

Wave 4 covered the remaining 65 routines: the game-load preamble ($5B00-$5BB3), the working-memory stubs ($7700-$7D52), the summon / placement / line-of-sight helpers ($9856-$9DAA), the inter-turn animation block ($A0FE-$A956), the pre-movement state init cluster ($AB0A-$ABDC), the IM 2 sprite-cycling interrupt service routine and its inner helpers ($DF0C-$DFB9), the board-to-pixel converter at $E005, and the entire orphaned dead-code block at $D588-$D8C4 which is never called from live code (per the existing $D52E annotation).

Speculative entries are clearly marked with "exact role not yet verified" rather than over-claiming. The Wave 3 / Wave 4 dispatched read-only research agents had varying confidence on the deeper helper routines; conservative wording reflects that.

events.title: Documented the seven utility, attack and alignment spell handlers - Disbelieve, Subversion, Raise Dead, Turmoil, Shadow Form, Law/Chaos shifters, and the four alignment attacks - with the dice predicate, validation chain and post-success state changes verified against the Z80.
events.message:
Documented the seven utility, attack and alignment spell handlers - Disbelieve, Subversion, Raise Dead, Turmoil, Shadow Form, Law/Chaos shifters, and the four alignment attacks - with the dice predicate, validation chain and post-success state changes verified against the Z80.

Flagged Subversion's dice direction as inverted versus the alignment attacks: same offset-19 stat, opposite comparison, so high-stat creatures are easier to subvert and harder to alignment-attack. Left in the doc as a note since it could be deliberate or a flipped-comparison bug.

Fixed the Decree / Justice naming swap in the alignment-attack human cast loop. The multi-shot rule is 1 shot for spell indices 45-46 (Vengeance, Decree, bias +/-1) and 3 shots for 47-48 (Dark Power, Justice, bias +/-2).

Confirmed the Law / Chaos shifters are a thin wrapper around the standard dice routine - the world-balance shift happens inside spell_casting_check on success.

Confirmed Raise Dead has no separate magic-resistance check despite earlier descriptions implying one.

Confirmed Disbelieve consumes its slot whether or not the target was an illusion. Single BIT 4 test on the target's +481 byte decides whether to destroy.

Documented Turmoil's bit-7 marker mechanism that prevents pieces being re-shuffled within the same pass.

events.message:
Reorganised the repo into sources/, tools/ and reference/ folders, with the root holding only README.md, CLAUDE.md, update.sh, requirements.txt and .gitignore. Updated update.sh and the build-active scripts to resolve paths relative to the project root.

Removed orphaned trace outputs chaos.map and magic_wood_trace.z80. Untracked skoolkit-instructions/ from git. Added Pillow to requirements.txt.

Identified spell-record byte 4 at $7D60 as the spell-book and cast-order sort key. Added a Sort column to the rendered Spells page and corrected the earlier docs' sort direction from ascending to descending.

Fixed the casting-chance display for spell-placed objects (Gooey Blob, Magic Fire, Dark Citadel, Magic Castle, Wall) so it reads from the spell table rather than the unused creature stat record.

Documented the AI scoring chain at \$C825 / \$C858 and corrected the existing routine description's owner-mismatch error. Labelled \$C6D4 (piece_weights), \$CC55 (ai_scoring_modifier), \$CC56 (ai_ranged_target_select), \$96F3 (cast_player_spells) and \$8D7A (fill_spell_hand).

Added three custom memory-map pages grouping the engine into thematic chunks: Computer AI, Movement and combat, and Spell selection and casting.

Disabled bold rendering throughout the site since the bundled Chaos web font has no bold cut. Added font-synthesis: none on body and explicit font-weight: normal overrides for every selector skoolkit.css makes bold.

Added a "Source on GitHub" footer link in the rendered output and a link to the live https://www.archaos.co.uk/chaos-disassembly/ build at the top of the README. Rewrote the README and updated CLAUDE.md to match the new layout.

events.title: Decompose level-1 $1300-$18FF HEX blob into 15 L1_-prefixed sub-chunks
events.message:
Decompose level-1 $1300-$18FF HEX blob into 15 L1_-prefixed sub-chunks

The <<level1 pages 13-18>> raw HEX blob (1536 bytes) was a byte-exact
mirror of drol.bin's $1300-$18FF window but carried no structure.
Split it into 15 labelled sub-chunks matching drol's decomposition:

  L1_BEAM_TARGET_DRAW_TAIL   $1300-$1309 ( 10 bytes)
  L1_BEAM_UPDATE             $130A-$13A3 (154 bytes)
  L1_GAME_START_INIT         $13A4-$13D5 ( 50 bytes)
  L1_ENEMY_A_ADVANCE         $13D6-$1422 ( 77 bytes)
  L1_ENEMY_A_DRAW            $1423-$1535 (275 bytes)
  L1_ENEMY_B_ADVANCE         $1536-$1590 ( 91 bytes)
  L1_ENEMY_B_DRAW            $1591-$1645 (181 bytes)
  L1_ENEMY_C_ADVANCE         $1646-$16AB (102 bytes)
  L1_ENEMY_C_DRAW            $16AC-$17A5 (250 bytes)
  L1_ATTRACT_ANIM_1          $17A6-$17E0 ( 59 bytes)
  L1_ATTRACT_ANIM_2          $17E1-$1812 ( 50 bytes)
  L1_ATTRACT_ANIM_3          $1813-$1843 ( 49 bytes)
  L1_ATTRACT_ANIM_4          $1844-$1889 ( 70 bytes)
  L1_FLOOR_BASE_ROW_PAD      $188A-$188E (  5 bytes)
  L1_FLOOR_BASE_ROW_HEAD     $188F-$18FF (113 bytes)

Two artifacts of the swappable-page boundary: L1_BEAM_TARGET_DRAW_TAIL
is only the final 10 bytes (routine entry at $1297 is inside the
persistent drol.bin window) and L1_FLOOR_BASE_ROW_HEAD is only the
first 113 of 256 entries (tail 143 bytes $1900-$198E live in
persistent pages 19-1F).

Added a prose subsection with cross-reference table; updated the
level1.asm collection chunk to list the 15 chunks in ORG order.
All 5 targets verify byte-perfect.

events.title: Decompose level-1 $7500-$7AFF HEX blob into 10 L1_-prefixed sub-chunks
events.message:
Decompose level-1 $7500-$7AFF HEX blob into 10 L1_-prefixed sub-chunks

Split the 1536-byte raw `<<level1 pages 75-7A>>` chunk into:
  L1_SPRITE_POINTER_TABLES_LO/HI   ($7500 / $7600, 256 bytes each)
  L1_PILLAR_SPR_DATA_0..6          ($7700-$7AD3, 7x140 bytes)
  L1_HIT_SPR_NEG_DATA_0            ($7AD4-$7AFB, 40 bytes)
  L1_HIT_SPR_NEG_DATA_1_HEAD       ($7AFC-$7AFF, 4 bytes)

Bytes are byte-identical to the corresponding drol.bin range (a known
loader invariant), so the L1_ labels mirror drol's SPRITE_POINTER_TABLES
and PILLAR_SPR_DATA / HIT_SPR_NEG_DATA decomposition.  Using the L1_
prefix follows the same pattern established for page 02 seeds and
avoids symbol collisions with the authoritative drol symbols.

HIT_SPR_NEG_DATA_1 spans the $7AFF/$7B00 swappable/persistent boundary:
the first 4 bytes live here (in level1.bin) and the remaining 36 bytes
live in drol.bin at $7B00-$7B23.  That boundary is an actual in-game
artifact, not a disassembly mistake --- made explicit via the
L1_HIT_SPR_NEG_DATA_1_HEAD label.

Also adds a prose \subsection to chapter "Level 1 swappable data"
documenting the byte layout and the boundary cut.

All 5 targets (boot1 / loader / rwts / drol / level1) still verify
byte-perfect against the reference binaries.

events.title: Decompose SPRITE_PIXEL_DATA_RESIDUE_2 into player/hit/grid sub-frames
events.message:
Decompose SPRITE_PIXEL_DATA_RESIDUE_2 into player/hit/grid sub-frames

Split the remaining undecoded 1716-byte HEX blob at $854C-$8BFF into
30 labeled per-frame chunks:

  - PLAYER_SPR_IDLE_DATA_0..8 ($854C..$87F7) --- 9 unique 76-byte
    idle-path player sprites (entries 1 and 3 of the pointer table
    both reference PLAYER_SPR_IDLE_DATA_1).
  - PLAYER_SPR_ACTIVE_DATA_0..8 ($87F8..$8ABF) --- 2 idle-sized
    frames at 76 bytes, 7 at 80 bytes. Entry 1 of the active pointer
    table aliases back to PLAYER_SPR_IDLE_DATA_8 at $87AC.
  - HIT_SPR_POS_DATA_0..6 ($8AC0..$8BD7) --- 7 positive-parallax
    impact-sprite frames, 40 bytes each (W=7 H=5).
  - PLAYER_GRID_SPR_A_DATA_0..4 ($8BD8..$8BFF) --- first 5 of 7
    grid-A frames; the remaining 2 live in the swappable bank.

Key discovery: DRAW_SPRITE runs W+1 = 4 bytes/row for the player,
so many frames have a 4-byte leading or trailing zero row as
alignment pad --- bytes between frames are NOT uniform padding but
part of the frame data. Active frames 0-1 are unused at runtime
(pointer live range is [3..9]), explaining the size mismatch (76 vs
80 bytes) relative to DRAW_PLAYER's fixed H=$14.

The SPRITE_PIXEL_DATA_RESIDUE_2 label is removed from @ %def; three
new \\section{} blocks document the idle+active, hit-pos and grid-A
tail sub-tables. All 5 assembly targets remain byte-perfect.

events.title: RE GAME_OVER at $BDA0 (level1.bin end-of-game handler)
events.message:
RE GAME_OVER at $BDA0 (level1.bin end-of-game handler)

Break GAME_OVER out of the <<level1 pages 8C-BD>> HEX blob into a
labelled code chunk with symbols.  Routine: MAIN_LOOP's exit path
when ZP_GAME_OVER underflows.  Phases:

  1. Wipe (SCREEN_ROW_COPY) + reload (RWTS_RELOAD).
  2. Reseed score digits, HUD column bounds, ZP_PLAYER_Y, ZP_GAME_OVER
     (same writes as GAME_START_INIT, minus the lives/score-BCD trio
     which the conditional GAME_RESTART reaches below).
  3. 192-row page-2 -> page-1 dissolve via SCREEN_ROW_ADDR_*/MON_WAIT/
     ROW_COPY_CLICK.  The routine uses ZP_HGR_SRC as the page-1 write
     pointer and ZP_HGR_DST as the page-2 read pointer -- opposite
     roles from START_ATTRACT's orientation.
  4. Three-way continuation dispatch on ZP_RESTART_FLAG:
     - == 0 -> JMP LIFE_LOST_RESUME
     - < 0  -> JMP MAIN_LOOP direct (joystick path)
     - > 0  -> JSR GAME_RESTART (resets lives/score/flag -> $FF), JMP MAIN_LOOP

Introduces <<level1 defines>> shared alias block so the level1
assembly target can reference drol.asm / rwts.asm symbols
(SCREEN_ROW_COPY, RWTS_RELOAD, INIT_LEVEL_STATE, PLAYER_MOVE_TICK,
MAIN_LOOP, LIFE_LOST_RESUME, GAME_RESTART, HUD_SCORE_COL,
HUD_LIVES_COL, ZP_SCORE_*, ZP_HGR_SRC/DST, SCREEN_ROW_ADDR_*,
MON_WAIT) without pulling the full code chunks.

events.title: RE cold-start zero-page image at $5700-$57FF
events.message:
RE cold-start zero-page image at $5700-$57FF

Upgrade the ZP_SAVE chunk in loader.bin from a flat 32-line HEX blob
to a labeled, row-annotated table. Each 8-byte HEX row now carries an
inline comment identifying the named ZP symbols that receive non-zero
seeds in that span -- making the cold-start value of every ZP
variable visible at a glance.

Add a new prose section "Empty page and zero-page image" documenting
both UNUSED_PAGE ($5600, dead padding) and ZP_SAVE's dual role: cold-
start ZP image copied byte-by-byte into $00-$FF by FIRST_BOOT just
before JMP (ZP_GAME_ENTRY), AND save/restore backing reused by
SAVE_ZP / SEEK_AND_RESTORE_ZP across level swaps.

Key findings documented inline:
  $4E/$4F = $A3 $72 -> ZP_GAME_ENTRY = $72A3 = START_ATTRACT. This is
    why attract is the first live code to run after boot.
  $36/$37 = $30 $C0 -> ZP_SFX_CLICK low + its implicit high byte.
    The $C0 high byte at ZP $37 has no runtime store anywhere; it
    comes from this cold-start copy (see prior drol-zp-37-assumption
    memory).
  $52/$53 and $54/$55 seed ZP_INPUT_1/2 with C061/C062 (push-button
    soft switches), so default input is joystick-button-polled.
  $5E = $04 seeds ZP_LIVES_BCD = four lives.
  $D4/$DC/$E0 = $01 each -> enemy A/B/C slots initially active.

perfect. PDF builds cleanly (502 pages, same 195 pre-existing LaTeX
errors as before the change -- no new errors introduced by this pass).

Split $7500-$8BFF sprite data region into 3 labeled chunks

Replaced the single 5888-byte <<screen data tables>> HEX blob with three

  - <<sprite pointer tables hi>> at $7600 (256 bytes)
  - <<sprite pixel data>> at $7700 (5376 bytes)

The two pointer-table halves now expose 37 parallel LO/HI labels
(PILLAR_SPR_LO, HIT_SPR_NEG_LO, FLOOR_SPR_LO, WALL_L/_SPR_LO,
PLAYER_SPR_IDLE/_ACTIVE_LO, HIT_SPR_POS_LO, PLAYER_GRID_SPR_A/B_LO,
ENEMY_C_TAIL/_PUFF_LO, ENEMY_B_PUFF_LO, SPECIAL_PEEK/_BODY_POSE0..3/_GRID_SPR_A/B_LO,
FLOOR_ENEMY_SPR_S0..3_LO, COMPANION_NEG/POS_POSE1..3/_GRID_SPR_LO,
ENTITY_GRID_SPR_LO, RESCUE_SPR_NEG/POS_END/MID_LO, PROJ_SPR_R_LO

declare these symbols scattered across other defines chunks, and added

events.title: Assignment-form comments: use "<-" and "#\$" for values
events.message:
Assignment-form comments: use "<-" and "#\$" for values

User caught "STA ZP_SPRITE_H ; \$57 = \$1C":
- \$57 is the symbol's own address (should be ZP_SPRITE_H)
- \$1C is the value being stored, not an address (should be #\$1C)
- "=" loses direction information

Correct form: "; ZP_SPRITE_H <- #\$1C". The "<-" makes destination/
source unambiguous; "#\$" mirrors the 6502 immediate-vs-absolute
distinction (LDA #\$1C is a value; LDA \$1C is a ZP read).

Added to CLAUDE.md "### Chunk annotation" as a new bullet under
"Don't restate the instruction". Illustrates the three fixes
together (symbol, direction, immediate marker).

Cleanup this pass: 23 assignment expressions rewritten across the
document. Form "\$XX = \$YY" → "SYMBOL_XX <- #\$YY" (or
"SYMBOL_XX <- SYMBOL_YY" when RHS address has a known symbol and is
high-page). Skipped EQU-definition citations ("SYMBOL = \$ADDR"
describing a symbol's own address — those are documentation, not
assignment).

All 5 targets byte-perfect.
events.author: XekriRedmane

events.title: Strengthen "purpose not mechanics": delete pure restatement comments
events.message:
Strengthen "purpose not mechanics": delete pure restatement comments

User flagged "LDA RESCUE_DIR,Y ; RESCUE_DIR[Y]" — the comment just
echoes the operand in bracket notation. Zero new information. Should
either be an actual explanation of what the row means, or nothing.

New CLAUDE.md bullet in "### Chunk annotation":
  Don't restate the instruction. LDA RESCUE_DIR,Y ; RESCUE_DIR[Y]
  and STA ZP_SPRITE_Y ; ZP_SPRITE_Y both carry zero information.
  Replace with a real explanation or delete.

Cleanup: 42 bare "; SYMBOL[X/Y]" trailing comments deleted. These
were a side-effect of the earlier automated "\$XXXX,Y → SYMBOL[Y]"
conversion: original "; \$XXXX,Y" comments were also pure
restatements but went unnoticed because they looked like they were
adding information (the raw hex). Now that the automated conversion
surfaced them as "; SYMBOL[Y]", they're visibly empty and can be
cleaned up.

All 5 targets byte-perfect.
events.author: XekriRedmane

events.title: Extend address-in-comments rule to 2-digit (zero-page) hex
events.message:
Extend address-in-comments rule to 2-digit (zero-page) hex

User caught "STA ZP_SPRITE_Y ; \$5B" — the comment's bare \$5B is the
symbol's own address, same violation as \$XXXX but my earlier
cleanup regexes used [0-9A-Fa-f]{3,4}, skipping zero-page hex.

CLAUDE.md rule now explicitly names all widths: "The rule applies to
addresses of any width — 2-digit zero-page (\$5B), 3-digit (\$1FF),
4-digit (\$629E)."

Cleanup this pass (all with 2-4 digit regex):
- 73 "SYMBOL at \$X" strippings
- 32 "SYMBOL (\$X)" apposition strippings
- 122 verb/noun-context "\$X" → SYMBOL rewrites
- 51 bare "; \$X" trailing comments deleted (where X has a symbol)

All 5 targets byte-perfect.
events.author: XekriRedmane

events.title: Rule: compiled branch targets use labels, never assembled addresses
events.message:
Rule: compiled branch targets use labels, never assembled addresses

User flagged comments like:
  ;   delta == \$00           ->  \$629E branch (1-col wide)
  ;   delta == \$01 (via BEQ) ->  \$6296 branch

The numeric PCs are compiled addresses. The programmer never knew them
— the assembler chose them. Such references should use the local
label (.delta_zero, .delta_one, etc.) or be dropped entirely if the
behavioral description suffices.

Rule added to CLAUDE.md "### Chunk annotation" as case (c) of the
numeric-addresses-in-comments rule: compiled branch targets are a
third forbidden case, alongside (a) instruction own-address and (b)
symbol-redundant hex.

Cleanup this pass:
- REFRESH_LEFT_WALL header plate (lines 9799-9808): replaced
  \$629E/\$6296/\$62AC references with .delta_zero/.delta_one/
  .shared_tail local labels; dropped the shared-tail address range.
- REFRESH_RIGHT_WALL header plate (lines 9645-9652): same treatment
  with .edge_2B/.general/.shared_tail labels, plus upgraded
  "LDY \$4C" reference to "LDY ZP_SPRITE_XREF".

All 5 targets remain byte-perfect.
events.author: XekriRedmane

events.title: Upgrade $XXXX → SYMBOL in verb-context code comments
events.message:
Upgrade $XXXX → SYMBOL in verb-context code comments

User caught another miss: "loaded from \$7519/\$7619" where both
addresses have symbols. The prior apposition regex only matched
"SYMBOL at \$X" and "\$X <noun>" forms; it missed prepositional
phrases like "loaded from \$X", "points to \$X", "writes \$X".

This pass broadens the rewrite to any \$X / \$X/\$Y where a context
word within the preceding ~3 words strongly implies a memory
address: from/to/into/at/of/in/via, loaded/stored/points/writes/
reads/jumps/calls, indexed/table/pointer/routine/buffer/page, etc.

Touched 138 comment lines. \$XXXX values without a known symbol or
without a memory-context preceding word are left alone (they're
literal values like comparison thresholds, bit masks, constants).

All 5 targets remain byte-perfect.
events.author: XekriRedmane

events.title: Strip symbol-address duplication in code comments
events.message:
Strip symbol-address duplication in code comments

User caught "WALL_L_SPR_LO/HI at \$7519/\$7619" — a symbol name with
its own address as an apposition. Same rule the prose side already
enforces: if a symbol exists for the address, don't also write the
hex.

Cleanup in this pass:
- 300 lines where the pattern "SYMBOL at \$X", "SYMBOL (\$X)", or
  "SYMBOL_LO/HI at \$X/\$Y" had the address duplication stripped.
- 20 phrases like "\$X <noun>" / "\$X/\$Y <noun>" where <noun> is
  table/pointer/entry/routine/etc., rewritten to use the symbol.
- Manual fix for the exemplar line in REFRESH_LEFT_WALL:
    \$4C          -> ZP_SPRITE_XREF
    \$7519/\$7619 -> WALL_L_SPR_LO/HI

The broader sweep caught "SYMBOL ($X)" patterns that my earlier
prose-side script only touched outside code chunks.

All 5 targets remain byte-perfect.
events.author: XekriRedmane

events.title: Enforce ASCII-only code comments: no LaTeX commands, no Unicode
events.message:
Enforce ASCII-only code comments: no LaTeX commands, no Unicode

Noweb copies code-chunk content verbatim into the PDF via \Tt{},
so LaTeX commands like \Delta / \to / \S{...} and Unicode chars like
em-dash, →, ≥ render as literal backslash-text or missing glyphs.
The user spotted this in REFRESH_LEFT_WALL where "\Delta == \$00
\to \$629E branch" appeared as garbled text in the rendered PDF.

New rule in CLAUDE.md "### Chunk annotation": code comments are
ASCII-only. Use ASCII equivalents: delta, ->, >=, <=, <->, *, +/-, --.
Also: no \\$XXXX escapes in code comments; use plain $XXXX (dasm
ignores comments anyway). LaTeX commands are fine in prose chunks.

Cleanup this pass:
- 54 LaTeX commands replaced (\Delta → delta, \to → ->, etc.)
- 125 non-ASCII chars replaced (— → --, → → ->, etc.)
- 3 remaining \S{...} cross-refs cleaned up manually
- 59 \\$XXXX → $XXXX escapes stripped in code comments

All 5 targets remain byte-perfect. Prose (doc chunks) untouched —
LaTeX math and Unicode remain fine there.
events.author: XekriRedmane

events.title: Generalize the "addresses in comments" rule
events.message:
Generalize the "addresses in comments" rule

Previous phrasing only forbade \$XXXX as a ":" or end-of-line prefix,
so "\$629E (A was 0)" slipped through — the parenthesized form wasn't
caught and the address is still noise (it's the instruction's own PC).

The underlying principle: an address in a code comment must serve a
purpose beyond identification. Two non-purposes: (a) repeating the
instruction's own PC (.lst has it); (b) repeating a symbol's address
(use the symbol).

Rule in CLAUDE.md "### Chunk annotation" rewritten as a general
principle with both sub-cases explicit, plus examples. Keeps the
"addresses may stay when the reader needs the number" out (unlabeled
address, memory-region span, opcode byte value).

Cleanup this pass:
- 7 instruction-PC prefixes stripped (e.g. "; \$629E (A was 0)" →
  "; (A was 0)").
- 22 symbol-address prefixes rewritten to use the symbol.
- 1 other numeric-prefix comment left alone (serves a purpose).

All 5 targets byte-perfect.
events.author: XekriRedmane

events.title: Use SYMBOL[Y] in comments instead of \$XXXX,Y
events.message:
Use SYMBOL[Y] in comments instead of \$XXXX,Y

Flagged by the user: on a line like
  LDA WALL_L_SPR_LO,Y    ; \$7519,Y -> ZP_BLIT_SRC
the comment repeats the instruction operand in raw-hex asm syntax —
both redundant (the asm is right there) and a hex-where-a-symbol-
exists violation.

New rule in CLAUDE.md "### Chunk annotation":
- In comments, refer to indexed tables as SYMBOL[Y] (not \$XXXX,Y
  and not SYMBOL,Y). The [Y] bracket form is unambiguously prose, not
  asm, so it reads as annotation rather than duplication.

Mechanical cleanup: 67 comment rewrites where the instruction operand
used a known symbol and the comment used the raw-hex form with the
same index.

All 5 targets remain byte-perfect.
events.author: XekriRedmane

events.title: Tighten style rules: no instruction-address comments, no redundant [[SYM]]([[\$X]])
events.message:
Tighten style rules: no instruction-address comments, no redundant [[SYM]]([[\$X]])

Two rule additions flagged by the user during review:

1. Assembly comments must never prefix the instruction's own address.
   Pattern that was creeping in:
     STA \$3CA8,X  ; \$05B4: row 79
   Correct form:
     STA \$3CA8,X  ; row 79
   The .lst file has instruction addresses; repeating them in source is
   pure noise.
   - CLAUDE.md "### Chunk annotation" gets a new bullet.
   - Cleaned 492 "; \$XXXX:" prefixes in main.nw.
   - Cleaned 341 bare "; \$XXXX" trailing comments (carried no info).

2. Prose apposition [[SYMBOL]] ([[\$XXXX]]) is forbidden — the
   parenthetical hex adds no information over the symbol itself. Only
   range appositions conveying extent ([[SYMBOL]] ([[\$A]]--[[\$B]]))
   remain allowed.
   - CLAUDE.md "### Prose rules" principle 2 tightened.
   - reveng.md standing rule principle 2 tightened.
   - Stripped 125 redundant appositions in main.nw.

All 5 assembly targets remain byte-perfect (boot1, loader, rwts, drol,
level1). No semantic changes to code.
events.author: XekriRedmane

events.title: Carve REFRESH_FLOOR_LINES and FLOOR_LINES_P1/P2
events.message:
Carve REFRESH_FLOOR_LINES and FLOOR_LINES_P1/P2

Retires the 24-byte <<game engine A middle>> stub at $62CA and the
46-byte ROW_PAINT_P1_38/P2_38 helpers at $08C8/$08DF as the fourth
and final playfield-refresh subsystem.

REFRESH_FLOOR_LINES ($62CA, 24 bytes): per-frame repaint of four
reserved hi-res rows (67, 107, 147, 187) from a 12-frame animation
table indexed by ZP_WALK_FRAME ($4B).  Called from PLAYER_TICK_IDLE
between REFRESH_RIGHT_WALL and REFRESH_PILLARS; page-flag gated
tail-call to FLOOR_LINES_P1 or FLOOR_LINES_P2.

FLOOR_LINES_P1 ($08C8, 23 bytes) / FLOOR_LINES_P2 ($08DF, 23 bytes):
broadcast a 40-byte source row at (ZP_BLIT_SRC),Y to four hi-res
row-base addresses on pages 1/2 respectively (source reversed:
byte 0 lands at column 39, byte 39 at column 0).  The four rows
are the only bytes in drol.bin written to those row bases.

Shipped behavior: the 12-frame 480-byte source table at
$7BEC..$7DCB is all-zero in every level, so the routine
functionally spot-cleans the four reserved rows each frame.  The
animation-indexed hook is a generic level-data extension point
never populated by the shipped levels.

New EQUs: ZP_WALK_FRAME ($4B), FLOOR_SPR_LO/HI ($750E/$760E).

Prior-doc corrections: playfield-refresh overview now lists four
callers (was three); the sprite-table enumeration includes
FLOOR_SPR_LO/HI; the "Unknown state A/B" comment on the
$4B/$4C init in INIT_LEVEL_STATE is replaced; three
% TODO-SYM: $4B markers dropped from PLAYER_TICK_MOVE_LEFT/RIGHT
prose.

No PNG rendered: all 12 animation frames are $00 in every shipped
level, so the sprite art is blank.

Verified byte-perfect against reference/drol.bin (35584 bytes,
100% documented, no gaps).

events.title: Carve three INTERLACE_BLIT callers as playfield-refresh routines
events.message:
Carve three INTERLACE_BLIT callers as playfield-refresh routines

REFRESH_RIGHT_WALL ($61F0, 122 bytes), REFRESH_LEFT_WALL ($626A,
96 bytes), and REFRESH_PILLARS ($62E2, 59 bytes) are the three
INTERLACE_BLIT callers previously buried inside <<game engine A>>.
All three share the BIT ZP_PAGE_FLAG / BMI gate to select P1 vs P2
twins of INTERLACE_RESTORE + INTERLACE_BLIT; the wall routines also
update HUD_LIVES_COL/HUD_SCORE_COL (playfield bounds read by
BEAM_UPDATE). REFRESH_PILLARS skips the restore step since
CLEAR_DRAW_PAGE has already cleared the background; its 6-slot
loop over ZP $60-$65 is effectively a no-op in the shipped game
(those ZP addresses are never written by any code in drol.bin or
level1.bin).

The game-engine-A HEX is now split into six chunks (prologue +
three new source chunks + middle slice + tail), retiring 277 bytes
from HEX. Zero raw-hex JSR $054E/$070B/$09FE/$0B4B references
remain in main.nw. Added PNG rendering frames $02-$07 of the
PILLAR/WALL_L/WALL_R sprite tables (classical-Greek fluted
columns + T-shaped wall torches with palette-bit animation).

events.title: Fix various bugs related to spell mechanics and creature interactions
events.message:
Fix various bugs related to spell mechanics and creature interactions

- Addressed issue where Turmoil never appears in starting hands, ensuring it can only be obtained through Magic Wood.
- Resolved game freeze when Turmoil is cast on a nearly full board, preventing indefinite loops.
- Fixed RNG behavior that skips values A-F, causing bias in spell and stat generation.
- Identified and documented duplicate spell records leading to uneven draw probabilities for certain spells.
- Marked Troll as unreachable content, clarifying its dormant state in the game.
- Corrected unused corpse sprites for Vampire, Spectre, and Gooey Blob, ensuring consistency with undead behavior.
- Implemented Ghost's intended ranged attack mechanics, which were previously untriggered.
- Fixed an exploit allowing players to escape engagement through the info key, detailing the technical workings behind it.
- Updated spell documentation to reflect changes and clarify mechanics for alignment-based attack spells.

events.title: Enshrine prose address rules as three explicit principles
events.message:
Enshrine prose address rules as three explicit principles

The earlier prose-rule section implied the wrap-in-[[ ]] requirement
but didn't state it crisply. A reader could read "use [[SYMBOL]] when
a symbol exists" and conclude bare \$XXXX is OK when no symbol
exists. That's wrong — the rule is universal: every numeric address
in prose gets wrapped, period.

Restated as three principles:
1. Wrap every address in [[ ]]. Bare \$XXXX in prose is never correct.
2. Prefer [[SYMBOL]] over [[\$XXXX]]. When numeric adds info, write
   [[SYMBOL]] ([[\$XXXX]]).
3. No backslash inside [[ ]]. weave.py strips them as a safety net,
   but the source stays clean.

Exceptions list narrowed and clarified. Added "if unsure, wrap it"
escape valve.

reveng.md's standing-rule section mirrors the three-principle
structure and points at CLAUDE.md for the full policy.

events.title: Identify $4713-$47FF as dead sector-image residue (not the DROL logo painter)
events.message:
Identify $4713-$47FF as dead sector-image residue (not the DROL logo painter)

The 237-byte HEX blob previously labelled GAME_INIT_EXTRA and stubbed
as "screen-init routines that paint the DROL title logo" has been
confirmed to be statically unreachable dead code.  Three independent
lines of evidence: (1) zero JSR/JMP/JMP-indirect in any of the five
reference binaries targets $4713-$47FF, and no immediate load of $47
into any pointer appears either; (2) the "code" at $474E is a
truncated copy of STRIPE_COPY_PAGE1's prologue and first 13 iterations,
cut off mid-instruction at $4800 followed by 5120 bytes of $00; (3)
the 237 bytes are a byte-exact copy of $0513-$05FF (CLEAR_PAGE2 tail +
CLEAR_PAGE2_TEXT_ENTRY body + start of STRIPE_COPY_PAGE1), with the
leading $0B at $4713 being the high byte of JSR INTERLACE_FILL_P2's
operand at $0512-$0513 --- mid-instruction residue, not a constant.

Mechanism: PAGE_TABLE maps track 2 sector 15 to page $47 and track 1
sector 3 to page $05; those two disk sectors happen to contain
identical bytes (build artefact).  GAME_INIT's packed stream
terminates at $4712 and nothing else calls in, so the residue has no
runtime effect.  Corroborated by level1.bin (built by replaying the
loader's reload-phase track read which targets different pages): it
has $00 throughout $4700-$47FF.

Changes:
- Renamed chunk <<game init remaining>> to <<sector residue 47xx>>
  with label SECTOR_RESIDUE_47XX (retires the GAME_INIT_EXTRA misnomer).
- Added \section{Sector-image residue at $4713--$47FF} with the
  three evidence lines documented.
- Corrected the HUD-frame prose: the DROL logo is drawn by the
  attract sprite routines ATTRACT_ANIM_1..4 at $17A6/$17E1/$1813/$1844
  compositing sprite pointer tables into hi-res page 2 during the
  animated title sequence --- not by any code at $47xx.
- TODO.md milestone documents the investigation.

No PNG rendered: the bytes are neither executable game logic nor
displayable art.  The existing images/drol_logo.png caption already
correctly identifies its subject as the "(c) 1983 Broderbund"
attribution strip at $BCF1, so no rename is needed.

All five assembly targets remain byte-perfect.

events.title: RE $0C98 as RESCUE_DRAW: per-frame draw+collision sibling of RESCUE_UPDATE
events.message:
RE $0C98 as RESCUE_DRAW: per-frame draw+collision sibling of RESCUE_UPDATE

The 441-byte $0C98-$0E50 routine previously stubbed as PROJECTILE_HANDLER
is now fully RE'd as RESCUE_DRAW.  The misnaming was historical: the
routine has no relation to general projectile handling --- it is the
draw-side sibling of RESCUE_UPDATE ($6F9C) for the 20-slot rescue-child
entity subsystem.

It iterates Y=$13 down through the same seven parallel slot tables
RESCUE_UPDATE uses, and per slot:

  * pre-computes the perspective screen-X residue $AF (via sub-entry
    RESCUE_DRAW_PERSPECTIVE_CACHE at $0D8C);
  * picks one of four body sprite variants ($75DB/$75E2/$75E9/$75F0
    + $76xx hi pages) based on RESCUE_DIR sign and RESCUE_ANIM phase
    (mid-step h=$1C vs. end-step h=$1A);
  * draws via DRAW_SPRITE, with the SMC_SPRITE_MASK_OP slot patched
    to AND #imm in drift mode for one frame of flicker;
  * runs three independent collision/spawn checks for active slots:
      (1) floor-enemy mutual kill (clear $9B,X, +$0035 BCD);
      (2) player pickup (centre X-band [$40,$50) + Y window around
          ZP_PLAYER_COL; sets ZP_HIT_FLAG=$FF, +$0035 BCD, NO life
          loss);
      (3) hostile projectile-spawn into $C5/$C9/$CD slots when the
          rescue is on the player's floor at an odd row.

The third gate is the surprise of the session: rescue children are
NOT pure friendlies.  When the player joins their floor, every odd
row they emit a hostile projectile that HAZARD_CHECK then animates
on subsequent frames.  The +$0035 BCD pickup reward is for catching
them before they keep firing.

New defines:
  * RESCUE_DRAW_PERSPECTIVE_CACHE ($0D8C) sub-entry
  * ZP_PERSP_OFFSET_LO/HI ($0F/$10) --- the 16-bit pre-compute
    scratch pair (was previously unnamed scratch).
  * RESCUE_SPR_NEG_END/MID + RESCUE_SPR_POS_END/MID label pairs
    for the four sprite tables.
  * RESCUE_DRIFT_PITCH ($0213) --- the 4-entry drift-state pitch
    table.

Plus one prose correction: RESCUE_UPDATE's prose now refers to the
sibling as RESCUE_DRAW rather than "still inside the $03A8 HEX
blob".

drol.bin remains 100% byte-perfect; pre-existing chunk-placement
violations dropped from 10 to 9 (the now-removed PROJECTILE_HANDLER
reference is the one fixed).

events.title: RE $6F9C as RESCUE_UPDATE: 20-slot rescue-child tick; drol.bin now 100%
events.message:
RE $6F9C as RESCUE_UPDATE: 20-slot rescue-child tick; drol.bin now 100%

Final carve of the "game engine B tail" blob (retires the
LEVEL_LOGIC = $6F9C EQU stub and eliminates the last 513-byte
HEX region that was game-engine-B-derived).

RESCUE_UPDATE is the per-frame tick for the 20-slot rescue-child
entity subsystem --- Drol's actual scoring objective.  Iterates
Y=$13..0 through seven parallel tables and runs a five-state
machine per slot:

  $00     -> inactive: PRNG-gated (1/256) spawn combined with a
             $4D-counter-residue-3 phase gate, plus a one-shot
             player-floor override (when RESCUE_FLOOR,Y equals
             ZP_PLAYER_FLOOR_CUR $0C and $1F < $10).  The
             one-shot is implemented by a BIT/JMP opcode patch
             at $705F that fires at most once per pass.  Spawn
             direction alternates by slot parity (+dir at
             world-X $003E, -dir at $035C); row reseats to
             FLOOR_THRESH[RESCUE_FLOOR] - 7.
  $01..$7F -> active walking: step +/- 3 world-X per frame with
              a row bobble from the 7-byte signed RESCUE_BOBBLE
              ($BD) table; 1-in-32 PRNG gate triggers the
              no-hit drift path.  When the player is on the
              slot's floor, a chase AI compares the entity's
              perspective-space X against ZP_PLAYER_Y ($4A) and
              flips direction toward the player.
  $FE     -> exit animation: INC floor-col, deactivate on wrap.
  other - -> drift countdown: DEC RESCUE_COUNTDOWN every 2
             frames (gated on $FD bit 0); on 0, reseat floor-col
             from ZP_DIFF_THRESH_A ($34) and transition to $FE.

Sibling draw + collision at $0C98 (still inside $03A8..$0C97 HEX
blob) awards +$0035 BCD (35 decimal) on player-pickup and sets
ZP_HIT_FLAG $1E=$FF.  No DEC $39 --- pickup is not a life-loss
event.  DRAW_ENTITIES phase 5 at $694E renders the perspective-
grid marker sprite using only the four shared tables.

New labels:

  RESCUE_UPDATE          ($6F9C) routine
  RESCUE_DIR             ($0394) walk direction
  RESCUE_ANIM            ($03BC) step anim counter
  RESCUE_FLOOR           ($03D0) assigned floor index
  RESCUE_COUNTDOWN       ($03E4) drift countdown
  RESCUE_BOBBLE          ($BD)   7-byte signed step-Y delta
  ZP_RESCUE_SPAWN_CTR    ($4D)   free-running slot counter
  ZP_PLAYER_FLOOR_CUR    ($0C)   per-frame player-floor copy
  PERSPECTIVE_XOFF_BYTE  ($B9)   byte-domain perspective offset

gaps).  All four targets byte-perfect.

RE $6CFE as COMPANION_UPDATE: two-slot hostile-walker tick+draw

Carves the 670-byte companion subsystem (tick + 3-pose SMC walk cycle
per direction + drift/climb handler + player-catch hit-box) out of

$682F now points at the named routine directly.

Key findings:
- The "companion" slots drawn as tiny markers by DRAW_ENTITIES phase 4
  are actually hostile walker-creatures (monsters).  Each slot
  patrols a floor with a 16-bit world-X at $11/$13,X, 5% per-frame
  PRNG direction flip, damages player on contact (sets $1E=$FF in
  $40..$4F x $1A-row catch box).
- Drift trigger: when on same floor as a rescue-entity
  (ENTITY_HIT_ROW $72,X match) AND screen-X in [$40,$47), enter
  drift mode ($B3,X = $FF).  Drift climbs 4 px/row/frame until
  hitting a floor-anchor ($63/$8B/$B3), then re-arms to active on
  a new floor with row = FLOOR_THRESH[player_floor] + $0B.
- 3-pose SMC walk cycle per direction, trampoline JMPs at $6E30/$6EA9,
  operand bytes $6E31/$6E32 and $6EAA/$6EAB rewritten by each pose
  handler.  Per-level sprite pointer tables at $75A2/$75A9/$75B0
  (-dir) and $75B7/$75BE/$75C5 (+dir).
- Gate $33 (ZP_COMPANION_GATE) is set $01 on all non-minimum
  difficulty tiers (DIFFICULTY_UPDATE), so companions activate
  once score >= 4000.  Both slots auto-activate every frame gate
